Current stability is at: [?ROOT.IBRIberiaStability|Y0%%]

The Iberian Union remains united and strong in her resolve. The government is well-prepared to handle any threats, be they external or internal. While more work can be done, most generally agree that Iberia is a relatively stable country.
strings.IBR_State_MedStrong_desc:
Current stability is at: [?ROOT.IBRIberiaStability|Y0%%]

The Iberian Union has seen better days, but the current situation shows signs of normality. The Iberian government maintains the semblance of balance, but many have spoken, saying there is room for improvement.
strings.IBR_State_Med: State of the Union - Moderately Stable
strings.IBR_State_Med_desc:
Current stability is at: [?ROOT.IBRIberiaStability|Y0%%]

The Iberian Union seems to be going along steady... for now. Many have placed concerns that leaving things as is will result in a worsening state, and that the government should increase their efforts to fix it while they still have the chance.
strings.IBR_State_MedWeak_desc:
Current stability is at: [?ROOT.IBRIberiaStability|Y0%%]

The Iberian Union is undergoing some internal turmoil. The nation is falling apart at the seams, and many call for immediate action by the government, lest the country suffers more than it is right now.
strings.IBR_State_Weak: State of the Union - Critically Unstable
strings.IBR_State_Weak_desc:
Current stability is at: [?ROOT.IBRIberiaStability|Y0%%]

The Iberian Union heads towards a state of total collapse. Thousands have taken to the streets to protest against the government's inefficiency to combat the growing problems, and some even fear continued pressure may tear the entire peninsula apart.

Only a deus ex machina could save the Iberian people now.
strings.IBR_January_Yet_Again_desc:
Another year passes us by; another January begins. Officials and officers alike join their civilian counterparts in shaking off the fatigue of the usual year-end festivities. Solemnity returns and the weight of duty is felt once more; while the holidays fade, the warmth and wassail of Christmas and the New Year serves as a fond memory to keep them warm.

As the Iberian people return to work, the Government of Iberia - under the rule of the Caudillos - does so too, perhaps with somewhat greater aplomb than a hungover office worker. Franco and Salazar have a goal to pursue, after all. Presiding over the chimerical apparatus that is the Iberian Union, their ambition is to see that effort rewarded by having the nation become truly important on the world stage.
strings.IBR_January_Yet_Again_tt:
We shall begin drafting the budget for our colonial possessions.
As these plans come to fruition, decisions will be unlocked to invest in these regions.
strings.IBR_Vimieiro_Professor_desc:
In his youth, our Caudillo Salazar in fact wanted to be a priest. To that end, he started his studies at the seminary in Viseu - but as time wore on, he found law and economics better suited him. The Caudillo eventually graduated from the University of Coimbra as a lawyer, and became in short order a lecturer and a professor. Fifteen years later, he was Minister of Finance and in that role was the first custodian of the nation's purse to preside over surpluses instead of endless deficits. This was one of the first ways in which he showed forth his prudence ...

... These days, the Caudillo is as restrained and contemplative as ever. He lives as frugally as he always has, shuns all publicity. His preference is to serve Iberia in relative silence, only making decisions after deep thought.
strings.IBR_Very_Visible_Hand_desc:
We do not need total control over the economy - we are not Bolsheviks. We also are not flighty Americans or Japanese, to be so addicted to the profit-motive as to let any old business run amok. No, we are someplace in the middle, which we have found is a safer, far more stable place to be.

It follows, then, not all businesses need to labour under an iron rod of state. Instead, this government will promote the creation of public-private partnerships and also approve measures that will support the private sector. Obviously the key players will remain under government supervision or control, but we see no real need for nonstrategic sectors to undergo scrutiny so long as they adhere to the rules.
strings.IBR_Friendship_Flights_desc:
The Portuguese airline TAP currently runs a series of flights between Lisboa and Rio de Janeiro in Brazil. This is a good start but is clearly insufficient for our needs. Brazil is a major focus of Iberian diplomacy in Latin America, and there is still more opportunity for us there. Much untapped potential is to be found in the fact that many Brazilian politicians have made no secret of their affinity for Caudillo Salazar and the modern Portugal he has built. We need to capitalise on this potential.

A good start in this direction would be to take two actions: to expand beyond the current, rather restricted base of flights, and to invite a prominent Brazilian politician to Iberia. We heard that Governor Carlos Lacerda of Guanabara has been distinguishing himself in conservative, anti-Varguist circles. He would make for a most suitable guest.
strings.IBR_Dust_in_Books_desc:
We have been too lenient regarding the formation of student associations in recent years. This led to chaos once already, when the university system in Madrid was thrown into chaos in 1957 due to Falangist toughs brawling with other student groups in a bid for control over student life. That chaos was suppressed by the security organs and resulted in the resignation of the then-Minister of Education. Now we see that the lull is ending and the students are acting up again.

Naturally, this cannot be borne any longer unless we want our institutions of higher education to be more reminiscent of bombed-out buildings in Russia. Directives will be implemented and laws promulgated which will both make it harder to form student associations and easier for preexisting student associations to disband.
strings.IBR_Dust_in_Books_tt: We will adopt measures to ensure our youth receive a proper and moral education.
strings.IBR_New_Garrison_Equipment_desc: The colonial army was where a great number of today's High Command developed their early career, Franco himself included. It was also a key element in crushing the Communists during the Spanish Civil War, and it fought bravely against Mauritanian rebels in the 1950's. To this day it is the first line of defense against any possible invaders that may strike the colonies first and is also in charge of keeping peace in our territories beyond Gibraltar. As such, it should be well equipped at all times. While it has been lacking in the last few years due to budget mismanagement, the colonial officers will be happy to hear their boys are getting some brand new toys, just as good as those the peninsular troops use.
strings.IBR_Officer_Training_Programs_desc:
Everyone in Iberia recognizes the Spanish Army of Africa as the army where Francisco Franco made his name as a military leader in Morocco, leading it all the way through the '36 Civil War into his current seat of power as Caudillo. Decades of relative stability on the peninsula has left Franco's old contingent lagging behind most of the now united Iberian army.

The Army of Africa of today is staffed mostly by North African Arabs as a means to escape poverty, peninsular Europeans looking for a kind of retirement destination or a vehicle for basically anyone looking for a position outside of continental Iberia. The officer corps in Morocco is a pale imitation of '36 now, new training will be required to raise the Army of Africa up to standard...
strings.IBR_Ferrol_General_desc:
Caudillo Franco has, since his time as an officer and later a general in the former Republican army, focused above all else on the ordered and stable governance of the Iberian nation. To the Caudillo, talk about 'freedoms' and 'rights' is of no value compared to the strength, dignity, and stability of the Nation. At the same time, the Caudillo has been cautious not to go off the deep end like the brutish regimes found in Germany and Japan...

...restrained, stern, and surpassing in prudence, the Generalissimo has served our Nation for decades, first as the bane of rapacious Bolshevism and republicanism, and latterly as the final arbiter and balancer of our politics. Surely it is thanks to his efforts that Spain remains strong even as other countries fall to pieces.
strings.IBR_Con_Fraga_Hasta_Braga_desc: The current Minister of Information, Gabriel Arias-Salgado, is a good- no, great man who has worked with Franco since the civil war. However, his health has been deteriorating over the years, quite dramatically even. It would be the best for him to retire and for a younger man to take his place. Manuel Fraga would be a fine replacement for him. A diligent man from the Instituto de Cultura Hispánica, he could help Iberia's image on the world stage.
strings.IBR_Fighting_Void_Hunger_desc:
The National Institute of Colonization in Spain is a government organization that creates villages to revitalize the agricultural sector. As people slowly leave the countryside for the cities, its funding will be increased so that they can keep building settlements good enough to attract people to them so farming doesn't bleed away workers.

“When the Industrial Revolution arrived in Spain, a seemingly infinite hunger for labor came with it. Despite technological advances, the machinery's appetite for human operators has not subsided, and so thousands of villagers leave their ancestral towns behind to find work in the overcrowded urban centres of the country, depopulating the countryside and leaving harvests to rot in the field and land to go unused.

By increasing funding for the National Institute of Colonization, allowing the improvement of rural infrastructure and the creation of strategically-placed towns to maximise efficient land-usage, we can keep the countryside alive, and the bellies of Spaniards full.”
strings.IBR_Iberian_Atomic_Age_desc: The power of the atom lies with the grasp of those with the bravery to seize it and the knowledge to understand how. Spain and Portugal have been investing in the nuclear sciences since before they united, and the Iberian Union has only continued that trajectory. Iberia has accomplished much in those decades, with a second experimental reactor about to go active and plans to develop the first commercial nuclear reactor nearing completion. While the primary focus is civilian power generation, members of the armed forces, especially the Air Force, are deeply invested in the secondary teams researching nuclear warheads to establish an Iberian nuclear deterrent.
strings.IBR_Plantations_Guine_desc:
Several prominent businessmen have approached the government with a plan to start building orchards in Guiné. They say that the climate in the colony is perfect for it and that it would provide jobs for most of the population there. To further try to convince us to accept, they have pledged to do all the necessary work to clean up the dense jungle there, create the necessary infrastructure to transport the goods and run the orchards; so that the government would only see profit.

While it seems this plan is perfect, the people behind it are infamous in the high circles of Iberian society for having frequent contacts with Siegfried Müller, the Reichskommissar of Zentralafrika. Zentralafrika has been revealed to submit the natives to a state of near slavery when working in their plantations, but this won't happen in Guiné, right?
strings.IBR_Connect_Islands_desc:
Besides the Azores, Madeira, the Baleares, and the Islas Canarias, Iberia also owns several archipelagos far from the peninsula; namely, Cabo Verde, São Tomé and Príncipe, and Fernando Pó.

These islands have a very small population and are mostly agrarian, therefore the attention they have received from the central government is almost non-existent. Infrastructure is weak and they depend on naval shipping to supply modern essentials such as medicine or machinery.

To alleviate the often-mentioned logisitical concerned, port infrastracture will be expanded in the islands to better integrate them into our Union. While the goodwill gained with our brave settlers certainly makes the project worthwhile by itself, the added efficiency and revenue it will provide the Union is a welcomed boon as well.
strings.IBR_Fund_the_DST_desc:
Control of the Iberian colonies has always been shaky at best. Thankfully, we have yet to witness an armed rebellion within our holdings, and God willing, we never will. However, insurgent numbers grow with each passing day, and Iberia's geopolitical enemies grow bolder in challenging us and weakening our position in the world.

Fortunately, we are prepared and well-equipped, and we are not interested in being humiliated in the one area our pride shines brightest: the offshore territories. Growing tension and unrest have plagued the Moroccan protectorate for decades, and our response has been sorely inadequate. This cannot continue.

The Moroccan Secret Police (DST) has severely lacked funds, in part thanks to the economic turmoil Iberia experienced throughout the turbulent 1950s. Now that economic matters have calmed down, we are ready to revisit our neglected colonial policy and reinvest in the security of the colonies. With adequate funding and training, the DST will play an indispensable role in countering subversives and insurgents within the Moroccan protectorate while ensuring the loyalty of the Moroccan leadership to Iberia. Let this be the first step in increasing our colonial investments!
strings.IBR_Electrify_Eqguinea_desc:
The southern frontier of our empire, Equatorial Guinea has been part of Spain for almost 100 years now. Expanded in the late 1940's with the chaos in Africa, it now stands as our first line of defense against German aggression in the continent. However, just like the rest of the southern part of the empire, the state that Equatorial Guinea is in could be much better.

While the colony is developed quasi-adequately, it lacks proper electrical infrastructure throughout most of its territory, as do the majority of our African settlements. To resolve this, a special commission of the electrical company ENDESA will be sent there to pioneer and oversee the electrification of the region.

It will be a landmark development, a victory for Spain, as well.
strings.IBR_Bureaucratic_Reinforcements_desc:
The nature of a colonial empire demands the establishment and maintenance of a proper bureaucratic administration. Sadly, bureaucrats are lacking across many of our regions, something which must be addressed sooner rather than later. This causes reports to be scarce, numbers to be wrong and most of the time causes problems with properly applying the law.

To help the region prosper, we will send a groups of civil servants where needed. Soon, we shall know all that occurs within our borders.
strings.IBR_Summer_Haze_desc: With over half the year gone by, we are quickly heading towards summer break. But we cannot rest on our laurels just yet. Before the break begins, our government will start planning for larger, more ambitious projects that will preserve the safety and prosperity of our Union.
strings.IBR_Summer_Haze_tt: It is time for us to set our sights on grander plans.
strings.IBR_Triumvirate_Fell_desc:
Any last acts in order to save the European anti-German alliance have ultimately come short. The bulwark against northern tyranny has fallen, and now, all former member states stand alone. Their distrust for each other has triumphed over the previously strong call for unity. In the face of German economic collapse, and, thus, a decline in the Teutons' ability to enact Machtpolitik, this call has lost its power, and all that remained was unresolved tension between the members of the Triumvirate.

Ideology and imperial ambitions tore at the seams of alliance but it was really the lack of unified purpose that kept Iberia, Turkey, and Italy together.
strings.IBR_Triumvirate_Fell_tt: With the Triumvirate gone, we must now decide our new course for foreign policy.
strings.IBR_Picking_Up_Pieces_desc:
Diplomacy, empire, economics... all spheres of Iberian governance rested on the Triumvirate's fragile framework. Now that the alliance has irreparably broken, each has crashed down.

In this hour of need, Spain and Portugal have only the firm hand of the Caudillos to lift them back up. Francisco Franco and António Salazar will begin a series of private meetings to arrange affairs of state, addressing both the urgent task of securing the peninsula amidst a Mediterranean aflame and the laying of a more durable foundation for this Union.

May they move with speed and decision - the peseta weakens each day and fearful whispers are on every lip.
strings.IBR_Picking_Up_Pieces_tt:
We will begin our recovery from the Collapse of the Triumvirate. New Decisions will be unlocked to aid in this matter.

The Iberian Economy is unlikely to survive another such collapse, we best work to avoid it.
Additionally, it is highly recommended we keep a close eye on our growing Deficit and Debt values.
strings.IBR_Who_Needs_Friends_desc: Times have changed, but the ways to show our greatness have not. Standing alone on the backs of our own achievements on the international stage while attempting to improve internal matters to further strengthen our position is all our great Union needs. Our fraught recent history has taught us that we simply cannot trust those who claim to have the same interests as us.
strings.IBR_Who_Needs_Friends_tt: This “backwards” stance may affect have unintended consequences.
strings.IBR_Economist_Meetings_desc:
The collapse of the Triumvirate has been, as all are well aware, an economic disaster for Iberia. Steps must be taken to promote recovery, and to identify these steps the Government in general, and the Caudillos in particular, must meet with the nation's leading economists.

There will no doubt be ideas both conservative and radical presented, but a course of action must be discussed and decided upon. A decisive response is required.
strings.IBR_Economist_Meetings_tt: We will unlock more decisions to help with our Economic Recovery.
strings.IBR_Gentle_Departure_desc:
The end of the Triumivrate does not need to also be the end of the ties we established with other Mediterranean countries.

Whilst Iberia's interests will shift back to the Peninsula, cultural endeavors and many other social pograms will be permitted to continue, albeit with reduced funding. This will permit us to continue reaping the benefits of trade and tourism, a necessity for our already struggling economy.
strings.IBR_Fund_Iberian_Alternatives_desc:
While basic research ties will ideally be preserved, remaining dependent on Italian designs and production for weaponry would be catastrophic in the case of conflict with our former ally. We must develop adequate R&D capacity domestically to compete in an ever more stormy Mediterranean.

Targeted funding and other state support will be made available for the necessary upgrades. Luckily, the Basque region has a strong tradition of arms manufacturing - though mostly for hunting and sidearms. Salazar has also proposed elevating the state-owned Portuguese light arms company Fábrica Nacional de Munições de Armas Ligeiras, or FNM, into an Iberian institution. Whatever we aim for, it is time to take our shot.
strings.IBR_Redefine_Intelligence_Collaboration_:
The collapse of the Triumvirate has cast our intelligence networks into disarray. Some agents, in hopes of retaining the support of Italian or Turkish colleagues, continue to share information as if nothing happened. Others have sealed off all channels of communication, unwilling to risk the wrath of superiors if sensitive details are laid bare.

We will issue new guidance to all our relevant personnel. The era of the Triumvirate is gone, and with it, the assumption that our peers are operating in good faith. Channels can be kept open to cultivate sources or to build trust so that we can leverage any prepared misinformation later. But fundamentally, Iberia is now on its own.
strings.IBR_Reaffirm_Science_Agreements_desc:
Out of the Triumvirate's wreckage, there remain a few gems to be salvaged. Particularly in areas that address long-standing weaknesses of our Union.

We will summon the Italian, Turkish, and Argentine ambassadors to clarify that all scientific accords reached under the Triumvirate continue to be binding. While we can expect some resistance from security officials in our former partners, their universities and businesses should be sufficiently enticed to force a settlement. Above all, we must ensure steady access to Italian nuclear research assistance, whatever hidden addenda or guarantees are needed.
strings.IBR_new_friends_tt: We will expand our ties with the £TNO_game_rule_flag_FRA_vichy  French State.
strings.IBR_New_Times_New_Friends_desc:
The Pyrenees are not so high that we can stand in hostility to all of Europe and expect security and prosperity. No, with our former friendships wilting under the heat of the Mediterranean sun, it is time to patch up relations with the continent's undoubted hegemon.

To keep our head held high and deal with mounting economic disarray, we will begin by ending our trade embargo against the Pakt. It may not be as dramatic as meeting at the border in a railway carriage, but the reopening of trade will be a powerful step toward restoring ties with Germania.
strings.IBR_Reorganize_African_Deployments_desc:
As tensions across the Mediterranean heat up, we will take the prudent step of repositioning our troops out of Italian colonies and into our own. Arranging for the transportation and housing of these scattered forces will be a significant logistical effort, but we must adapt to geopolitical realities.

Spanish and Portuguese troops should be used to enforce our own colonial rule from restive natives and avaricious powers alike - not take bullets in the name of a failed partnership.
strings.IBR_Put_Them_Good_Use_desc:
The bonds between the Triumvirate were tenuous and transactional. We do not speak the same language, and Lepanto looms larger in our history than any shared victory. Nevertheless, our collective bureaucracies were able to weave a thicket of agreements: work programs, facilitated migration, and mutual scholarships with even these most transactional of allies.

With the Triumvirate's fall, it is time to reorient these tools and our foreign policy more broadly, toward our kin across the Atlantic. Their bright minds and calloused hands will flock to Iberia's universities, factories, and farms. We will begin with like-minded governments in the region, both because these will be the easiest with which to reach agreements and to remind Latin America the benefits of aligning with Iberia.
strings.IBR_Help_Turkey_desc:
With the collapse of the anti-German alliance, the tensions between the Mediterranean nations have risen to a dangerous level. One source of tension, the Italian colonial holdings in the Middle East which border the Turkish state, has sparked an international crisis which truly shows the extent to which former relations have entirely broken down. Turkey has threatened to use direct military force to seize the lands it claims to be rightfully part of its nation. Italy has vowed to resist the aggressive invaders, invoking comparisons to German diplomatic tact.

Our choice on whether we should get involved has been decided. We need to support the Turkish invasion in order to greatly weaken the Italian Empire. This could mean that in the near future we may be able to assert our own claims on disputed land. The intervention will however not involve troops and direct intervention, rather we shall subversively funnel equipment to the Turks who seem capable of fighting their own war.
strings.IBR_Help_Turkey_tt: We will aid Turkey in the Italo-Turkish War.
strings.IBR_Help_Italy_desc: The tensions over disputed territory between the former Triumvirate members has exploded into a political and military crisis with the Turkish statement of intent on territories in the Middle East. The regime has threatened to directly invade the Italian colony which holds the land the Turks claim is their own. We must choose how to react to this, if at all. Were we to intervene on the Turkish side, or to withhold entirely, we may be able to benefit off of Italy's weakness... However, with the vitriolic rhetoric and aggression that the Turkish state has shown, we cannot, with good conscience, support them either through benign neglect or intervention. Hence, instead, we should seek to indirectly support the cause of the Italians who still hold the internationally recognized legitimate mandate over the territory. With this, we may be able to draw closer to the Italians and possibly seek diplomatic solutions to our own tensions with them in Algeria.
strings.IBR_Help_Italy_tt: We will aid Italy in the Italo-Turkish War.
strings.IBR_Good_Morning_Enough_desc:
With the collapse of the Triumvirate alliance, many hawks within our government have gained the impetus to claim that we now need to take an entirely hostile stance with those who have chosen to betray our trust.

Yet, in reality, our decision making can not be left to such simple emotional responses. Italy and Turkey will remain our neighbours in a Europe that is still largely dominated by the Germans. We must maintain some semblance of diplomatic ties with both Mediterranean nations to best suit our national security needs.
strings.IBR_Focus_on_Us_desc:
In the wake of the great Triumvirate betrayal, we have chosen to drive our Union into relative diplomatic isolation. Considering the state of international relations this may not have been such a terrible idea. The opportunity to begin to entirely focus on domestic issues and hence bring structural improvements to our society and economy is now open to us. There are many issues which still require attention due to the hurried unification of Portugal and Spain into Iberia.

At the end of this, however, we will stand proud again, this time not shoulder to shoulder with the fellow Mediterranean countries but alone. In this way we will prove the worth of our nation without relying on others, a greater boon to our prestige.
strings.IBR_Foreign_Mistrust_desc: We Iberians have long traditions of statehood and acceptable diplomatic actions. It was not our fault that the fools abandoned the mutually beneficial anti-German alliance. The lesson learnt, however, was almost equally beneficial. The clarity by which we cannot afford to blindly trust other nations anymore is blinding. Instead we shall pursue a diplomatic policy of healthy skepticism. Foreign influences will have to prove that they are well intentioned.
strings.IBR_Bare_Minimum_Interaction_desc:
It is clear that we cannot simply trust foreign actors anymore. In trusting the Italians and Turks we have already compromised a considerable amount of national security in terms of military, intelligence and economic secrets to our new Mediterranean rivals.

However, it is equally true that being entirely isolated from the international sphere can have very dire consequences. The need to maintain trade ties and finding new ones is paramount for not damaging our economy. Equally important is the acquisition of intel on international politicking and alliance building. We absolutely cannot find ourselves alone and unprepared if the Germans resurge or other powers decide to intervene in Iberian affairs. The building of some relations to a select number of foreign actors is hence required. We will leave the option to terminate them open, in case anything should happen.
strings.IBR_Bare_Minimum_Interaction_tt: This move will have far-reaching consequences.
strings.IBR_Minimum_Interaction_f: We have began pursuing a policy of Isolation.
strings.IBR_Greater_Secrecy_desc:
The collapse of the Triumvirate has not only brought about great ramifications in the economic and military sectors but also intelligence. With previous information sharing and combined training exercises now being gone, our intelligence sector is lacking some vital infrastructure and direction to be truly effective.

We therefore must push for more allocated funds and a general expansion with more recruits and equipment. In particular we have to ensure that our counterintelligence is functioning as intended in these times of great uncertainty. The possibility of foreign spies being able to pin down our weaknesses cannot be allowed.
strings.IBR_Trade_Necessity_desc:
The downgrading and outright shutting down of many diplomatic ties, in the wake of our understanding that the actors in the foreign sphere simply could not be trusted, has been criticised by some as an act of domestic economic sabotage. The internal markets of Iberia require foreign goods and capital to function normally, so the nation is not dragged down an economic abyss.

The Caudillos have for this reason decided it would be necessary to carry on trading for vital resources with their most trusted providers. This will be done once they have undergone sufficient scrutiny to ensure that not a single trading contract compromises our national security.
strings.IBR_Trade_Necessity_tt:
Turning back on our plans will come at a cost, but it may save us further embarrasments. Nonetheless...
This move will have far-reaching consequences.
strings.IBR_Military_Parades_desc:
Many in our nation initially saw the collapse of the Triumvirate as a great tragedy. Detractors of the regime subversively spread information that it had been us who had failed to uphold the Iberian standing on the world stage through weak diplomacy.

In our pursuit to eradicate these treasonous rumors, the idea that the split with our former allies should be celebrated was born.

It has therefore been decided that we will host a grand military parade to celebrate the regaining of our independence and sovereignty from the Triumvirate. In addition to rallying the population to our side will be able to show off our strength to our neighbours.
strings.IBR_Emphasize_Union_desc:
The dissolution of the Triumvirate and our subsequent split with our Latin partners has been a great ordeal for the Iberian Union. It has not only caused difficulties in our foreign policy but also given a considerable boost to the various separatist and nationalist movements that continue to plague our great Union.

We must emphasize that we are a unified Iberian nation. We are no longer simply citizens of Portugal or Spain with separate identities and heritage. A common purpose unites us. It gives us strength. We should not hesitate to embrace this ideal of unity, especially in these harsh times.

More propaganda to this effect has been requested.
strings.IBR_Arriba_Iberia_desc:
The regime in its enlightened position of guidance has decided that it would be greatly beneficial to the morale of the masses and unity of the Union to hold large scale celebrations of Iberia and its ideals. We have endured hardships and pain together, faced off with the existential threat of German dominance and weathered the underhanded conniving of our former sly Triumvirate allies. Standing alone in the Mediterranean should not be seen as a curse but rather as a great opportunity to further forge the history of our nation. We have many reasons to be proud of our people and their accomplishments.

Perhaps a new national holiday in order to celebrate our Union should be introduced.
strings.IBR_Great_Masses_desc:
We are fortunate that our population still upholds good traditional values and the one true faith. Iberia has been a bastion of pure Christianity for centuries. Too many heathens across German occupied Europe and further beyond have chosen to reject Catholicism in favor of dangerous ideological dogma and meaningless nihilism.

The Iberian people can be rallied around service of the Lord if necessary. Faith is still proving to be more effective for drawing the population together than any government directive. We should make use of this to further bolster unity and trust in the regime in these trying times. Large, broadcasted public masses in various cities around the Union could be used for this purpose.
strings.IBR_Praise_Caudillos_desc:
The two equal leaders of Iberia have directed both of their respective nations and later the Union through turbulent times of harsh change. Whether it be brutal civil conflict, endless colonial rebellion, or adapting to the powerpolitiking of the great powers, the Caudillos have always stood strong in the face of it all. Both men have hence developed a good image in the eyes of the majority of the Iberian people. This image has been used to create an effective cult of personality that critics say mirrors the reprehensible ways in which the Germans idolised their Führer.

What that slander does not mention is that Iberia's Caudillos do not have to rely on distorting propaganda, as they have entirely proven their worth as leaders. If we were to expand on the symbolism of the Caudillos and allow it to further seep into popular culture we may be able to better influence our population and promote unity in the face of adversity.
strings.IBR_Fortify_Colonies_desc:
The Iberian colonial holdings are of vital importance to the national economy, especially now that trade and economic cooperation between the former Triumvirate partners has broken down. It is therefore of vital importance that we guarantee their continued territorial integrity and existence within our empire. In the same vein as the Germans had laid their eyes on former Portuguese holdings in Mozambique and Angola.

We must not allow our remaining colonies to follow the same fate as the Portuguese holdings did. A plan to fortify various strategically important regions has for this reason been proposed.
strings.IBR_Fortify_Colonies_tt: We will construct Forts and Military Bases across our colonies.
strings.IBR_Post_Bombing_Council_desc:
The stalled debates on essential reforms in Cambados illustrated just how deadlocked Iberian governance has become. And the attempt on our Caudillos' lives suggests the dangers of any further secluded negotiations.

We, therefore, desire to create an Iberian Council to help the government and the Caudillos better rule the country. Devolving some of the duties on people of the Caudillos' choosing should be a perfect measure in that direction. The nature of the Council is the last question that the Caudillos face. It is left to them to decide whether it should play a purely advisory role or serve in a limited legislative capacity.
strings.IBR_Advisory_Council_desc:
The government, due to overextension, has struggled to make necessary decisions. The Caudillos suffer from information overload, and at times have to resist responding to it with unproductive mass vetoes. This situation is far from optimal and ought not to be borne any longer.

Suggestions of a legislative council, though notionally appealing, run the risk of giving too much influence to forces opposed to the legitimate rule exercised by the Caudillos. Instead, what the government needs is a Council to advise the Caudillos and the Iberian cabinet about the situation to help them make more effective decisions and prevent further government deadlock like what led to the disaster in Cambados.
strings.IBR_Provisional_Legislative_Council_desc:
Salazar's baroque vision, honed amidst the mists of Galicia, now comes into view. A legislature, one built on corporatism rather than liberal democracy. An empty vessel to fill with loyalists from across Iberia, gathering together the Caudillos' organizations to advance the legal framework of the Peninsula step by step. And always in accordance with their will.

Franco and Salazar will make joint, carefully synchronized, announcements of the new body from Madrid and Lisbon. At their word, UN-FET y de las JONS and the Estado Novo will begin the tireless work of materializing a Legislative Council from the aether.
strings.IBR_Amend_The_Constitution_desc:
While the Caudillos' word is sufficient to conjure up the Legislative Council as a political body, its full integration into the Iberian body politic requires legal grounding. Lawyers will be summoned to draft a new Fundamental Law, carefully scoping the powers of the Council.

Salazar, of course, will review them in minute detail. And so will Generalísimo Franco. For as much as he takes a hands-off approach to governance, the Caudillo maintains the tightest conceivable grip on power.
strings.IBR_Determine_Legal_Parties_desc:
As our Legislative Council takes shape, we must fill it with thoughtful, public-minded servants of Iberia and its Caudillos. Elections will serve to select most of them.

Polling places will be needed, yes, but only a minority of the Council's seats will be chosen by Iberian households. Instead a grand array of organizations, from the mighty Vertical Union to provincial governments and universities, will elect their own Council Members. With all this voting taking place, firm order will be needed. To prevent any unseemly disputes, but more importantly, to make sure that every single ballot is cast in favor of men loyal to their Caudillos.
strings.IBR_Codify_Powers_desc:
Relatively few of the Legislative Council's seats are set aside for Members directly appointed by Professor Salazar and Generalísimo Franco. But, paradoxically, this only strengthens their voices.

Those Members, anointed by the hand of the Caudillos, have both the personal prestige and the political experience to rise to formal and informal leadership roles within the Council. They will wield the gavel and the whip to ensure laws are passed efficiently and debates remain within appropriate bounds.

For, to question an appointed Member, is to question the will of the Caudillos.
strings.IBR_Permit_Legislative_Oversight_desc:
The Legislative Council will be permitted to conduct oversight over the government, with designated committees allowing specialized review of agricultural, educational, or commercial-industrial activities among others. The gathered information will support them as they craft the finer details of laws. Naturally, there are some areas, such as the military or internal security offices, that Caudillo Franco is averse to opening to too many eyes, no matter how loyal they may be.

But for less sensitive matters, we must decide how deeply the Council will be allowed to pry, and what tools they will have to do so.
strings.IBR_Regional_Veto_Limitation_desc:
Professor Salazar's plans for the Legislative Council included a feature to force the reconsideration of legislation impacting a region if it fails to attain sufficient votes among the Members of that region. The intention to secure Portugal's position within the Union is clear, but the language was left vague to obfuscate precisely that.

The provision is now attracting some furtive criticism whenever the Caudillo is out of earshot: can Galicians stall the Union's fishery policies? Will the Canaries can the latest cannery regulation?

A proposal to tighten this regional veto to specify Portugal and Spain is gaining traction. But this challenge to Salazar's design must meet his approval.
strings.IBR_Ensure_System_Mutability_desc:
One thing must be made absolutely clear. The Council serves at the pleasure of the Caudillos. If it ever ceases to be a useful tool to them, it has no purpose.

It would behoove us to establish formal procedures for adjusting the Council's remit, subject to unanimity between the Caudillos. Keep the tool sharp, and honed to the problems of the day. And if absolutely necessary, prepare to discard it entirely.
strings.IBR_Discourage_Leftist_Involvement_desc:
As the election results roll in, we know who will be entering into the Legislative Council: a diverse slate of modernizing technocrats, Falangist unionists, military men, and conservative politicians united in their loyalty to the Caudillos' political project and duty to Iberia.

But. There is always the possibility that a wolf lurks among the sheep. If not in this flock, then future ones. Communist sympathizers, Judeo-Masons, aging Republicans all hunger to infiltrate the Council, to learn the secrets of our regime and secretly steer it toward collapse.

This must be prevented at all costs.
strings.IBR_Puppet_Legislature_desc:
With the institution's foundation carefully laid by our benevolent Caudillos, the first session of the Legislation Council is called to order. And order it shall bring, taking on day-to-day lawmaking so that Generalísimo Franco and Professor Salazar can efficiently address the grand affairs of state.

To a long and prosperous future, three cheers for Iberia!
strings.IBR_By_The_Caudillos_Will_desc:
Our Caudillos have absolute power over legislation. As such, their will shall be done, no matter what. The representatives will advise only in the Caudillos' interest, and never against the Caudillos.

Their advice will not be considered as imperative orders, merely as suggestions, to which the Caudillos will consider, at their own discretion.
strings.IBR_Ensure_Fair_Representation_Not_desc:
Contrary to Republican delusions, the absence of a democratic system does not mean the absence of meritocracy or a denial of its usefulness. Though the Caudillos will of course prefer that their close allies serve on the Council, they are not so foolish as to seek out toadies and praise-singers that merely spout affirmations of the Caudillos' wishes and whims.

The Caudillos have set up this Council to help them and the government function. For this, they need advice, not sycophancy. The Council will have as members only the best people that the Caudillos can find within the government and their networks of loyalists to ensure their advice is as useful as possible.
strings.IBR_Alter_The_Constitution_desc:
In the interests of furthering sound governance and ensuring the stability of the government and the nation, we will now add to the Fundamental Laws of Iberia to reflect the changes that are currently being implemented. This will of course be a suitable opportunity to add in other laws to the collection— but the most important one will of course be the newest law about the Council, its membership, and its responsibilities.

Fortunately, this should not be too difficult of a measure, given that we will not have to alter any existing Fundamental Laws to bring this about — an advantage to having this system, instead of some witless liberal constitution.
strings.IBR_Watch_Them_Closely_desc: It is evident from recent chaotic proceedings of the Reich Senate and the Imperial Diet, or indeed of the Council itself, that bodies that meet regularly for political purposes have to have rules and enforce those rules if they wish to function properly. But we do not need the sort of rah-rah vigorous energy that the Americans or the Argentines have in their legislatures; nor indeed do we need elaborate pageantry and ritualization as if it was a sacred consistory. What is sufficient for us is to have rules regarding i) when meetings happen; ii) how they happen; and iii) how the Council should present its advice to the Caudillo and the Government.
strings.IBR_Strengthen_The_Illusion_desc:
Opposition factions will go on and on about how the Council is just a show, merely reflecting the wishes of the Caudillos back at them. Well, we are not going to deny that. Are the Caudillos not responsible for the welfare of the Iberian people? Exactly why will Iberia prosper by doing as these subversives propose and setting up some kind of “full democracy”?

Meanwhile, the regular citizenry of Iberia are simply indifferent. This is no issue to us, so long as that indifference does not crystallize into some manifestation of revolt. Our propaganda on the subject should merely be to publicize the Council as being part of the government and working to serve the interests of the Nation.
strings.IBR_Maintain_Common_Sense_desc:
There will be no gain from the Caudillos assembling advisors around them if said advisors can be credibly accused of taking bribes or supporting subversive movements whenever the Caudillos' backs are turned. As such, the Council members will be subject to “rigorous” vetting to avoid corruption.

Of course, what we mean is that we plan to nip any potential corruption scandal in the bud by filing away anything that smacks of corruption. We do not have any moralistic goals in doing this, aside from the welfare of the state being the primary goal—a goal that will not be met by corruption scandals and discreditation operations.
strings.IBR_Controllable_Representatives_desc:
We need a formula to determine replacements of council members. It is true that a member of the Iberian Council will have the right to serve for life. But the Caudillos know all too well, given how many advisors and friends have predeceased them, that none of the candidates can do so forever: the ones that do not step down or resign will die or lose their mental faculties. A suitable methodology of naming replacements has to be devised and implemented in the laws about the Iberian Council so that the body will not just die off after the first members leave.

Perhaps a shortlist of replacements, continually updated per member, may be the right way to go about it.
strings.IBR_Representatives_In_Name_Only_desc:
We have done it. A properly advisory Iberian Council has been set up, assembling the best and brightest authorities in the Iberian nation to govern it and taking a real load off of the government's plate. Everything has been put in place for them to carry out their tasks as normal, properly advising the Government of Iberia in accordance with their assessment of what is necessary for the future of our country.

Even more advantageously, since the Caudillos were the ones to select them, they will be in close alignment with our concerns—there is no need for any of us to bother with any illusions of democracy. So let us celebrate a job well done.
strings.IBR_germany_in_flames_desc: Germany has exploded into civil war! While factions within Iberia bicker about the new legislature, we must consider various ways to ensure the situation comes to our advantage. We may be bruised and ill right now, but we are still a major power!
strings.IBR_germany_in_flames_tt: Germany has fallen into civil war, we should decide what to do about it.
strings.IBR_matter_of_national_security_desc: Much as we hate the Germans, many in our government recognize that Albert Speer, should he take power, is the least likely to be aggressive with us. It may put a bitter taste in our mouth to do so, but it might be worth it in the long run to aid Speer's faction. Plus, sending over volunteers is an easy way to rid ourselves of some diehard fascists in our own country.
strings.IBR_reformist_tt_13: Supporting Speer and therefore his ideas will expand reformism in the Council.
strings.IBR_light_in_the_black_desc: Speer's faction needs soldiers. We have lots of dissidents in our army who have covert or open fascist sympathies, something a bit too extreme for our government's liking. Perhaps we can kill two birds with one stone by sending over these radicals as “volunteers” for Speer. They'll be out of our hair, and Speer will be grateful for the support.
strings.IBR_get_rid_of_radicals_desc:
Word is being run through the corridors and backchannels that the government is forming a secret group of military advisors to aid Albert Speer's attempt to restore the Reich. Only the most capable and competent military officers, who coincidently happened to be all hardline Falangists, are recruited through private meetings and ordered to bring five of their most trusted aides.

Famous Old Guard General Agustín Muñoz Grandes was honored to have been trusted with this special task and is leaving Madrid on a plane heading for Germany. We can only pray their journey will be without respite and their time in Germany short.
strings.IBR_influence_tt_GCW_1: Getting rid of hardline Falangists will increase the Council's influence.
strings.IBR_reformist_tt_GCW_1: Getting rid of hardline Falangists will increase reformism in the Council.
strings.IBR_new_blue_division_desc:
Even after many of its more vocal members left for Germany the Old Shirts still hold significant influence in our Union, especially among the armed forces. We should expand the scale of our volunteer program, creating a new form of the Divisíon Azul, much cherished in Falange lore.

The Old Guard will receive the calling with enthusiasm, eager to prove their worth and restore the prestige they once had, as will many young recruits who grew up hearing their father's war stories and now seek their own baptism by fire. They will march their way through the port of Bilbao, where they will sing “Cara al Sol” and kiss their wives one last time before they embark on what hopefully will be a one way trip.
strings.IBR_send_over_guns_desc: The start of the German Civil War is an outstanding opportunity for our nation. By sending weapons to Albert Speer, the tamest of the German warlords, in the best case scenario we can make amends and turn a page in history, while in the worst case we'll keep our enemies fighting amongst themselves and their attention away from us. It is also seems like a great opportunity for Iberian weapons corporations such as Astra, Star, and CETME, whose executives are proposing that they send weapons of their own to supplement our shipments, provided the Germans are willing to pay.
strings.IBR_thoughts_and_prayers_desc:
In a private meeting the Archbishop of Madrid plead the Caudillos to implement his plan of massive Iberian intervention in the German Civil War with aims of assuring Speer's victory, after days of deliberation and revisions the bold plan was finally accepted.

By decree, every Iberian priest is now obligated to donate, be it funds, clothing, food or clean water, and to instruct their flock to do the same in order to help the civilian population in Germany through this tough times. Though they may not make as much of a difference in the short term, such actions will surely win us support with the Germans, which might make them more willing to aid us in return later.
strings.IBR_Extraordinary_Council_Meeting_desc:
Finally, the so-called “Battle of Barcelona” has reached its conclusion. The separatists lay dead or under arrest, demonstrating without a doubt the ability of the armed forces to quell rebellion. However, there is something else occurring. The Caudillos are worried, not because of the battle itself but of the idea that it could have happened at all. If something this large was able to slip under their noses, then what else could have?

They do not have the grip they used to maintain. For the sake of the Union, that must be rectified. In order to do that, however, they must know where to start. That is why an extraordinary meeting of the Council will be called, so that a decision may be met on how to fix this mess.
strings.IBR_Extraordinary_Council_Meeting_tt: This focus will start the process to upgrade the Iberian Fundamental Laws through which the Union is governed.
strings.IBR_New_Fundamental_Laws_desc:
It is an indisputable fact, by anyone who understands reality, that things change. The world is not fixed, and one of God's favorite pastimes is striking down those arrogant enough to presume it is. We must not be counted among the fools who are caught unawares by the tides of change, so sure that things will stay as they always have.

Therefore, the best way to reassert our control is to change with the times. The Fundamental Laws must be updated, with brand new provisions and revisions designed to allow us more power. Additionally, it would likely be a very good idea to make sure the people themselves are content, since if they see that they are cared for, then they will be less inclined towards rebellious thought.
strings.IBR_Rights_of_People_desc:
It has become evident, as the process continues, that nowhere are the explicit rights and obligations of the Iberian people codified. This causes no end of legal issues, and so it will be corrected, through the establishment of a Fundamental Law for that very purpose.

Such a law will also, of course, include proper provisions for its suspension, when necessary, in order to ensure public safety. And it will be specific - further rights can be elaborated upon in later laws.
strings.IBR_Religious_Freedoms_desc:
Iberia is, and always will be, a Catholic state. But it is - we are - not a theocracy, and public suppression of other religious practices is an archaic concept not befitting a modern state. We will recognize this, and permit that practice, as long as they do not impugn public morality.

Rabid discrimination based on religion is not in keeping with the compassionate teachings of Christ, or of Christian doctrine, and we will enshrine this in the laws of our state.
strings.IBR_Maslows_tt: The Caudillos will explore ways to ensure this pyramid is catered and respected.
strings.IBR_Speak_Your_Mind_When_Allowed_desc:
We will, of course, enshrine freedom of speech in the appendices to the Fundamental Law. But it is critical that we learn from the disorder seen in America and elsewhere, and ensure that its exercise does not cover insurrection against the lawful state.

Sufficient checks and balances will be inserted to allow the state to provide proper oversight, of both the people and the press.
strings.IBR_Colonial_Citizenship_Question_desc:
While it may seem that Iberian citizenship is a very simple thing, it is not. However, the definition of a citizen is very simple. If a parent is an Iberian citizen, then the child will be an Iberian citizen. The location does not matter, nor the parent - only that one is really a citizen. A new question has come up recently as to a potential addendum to this rule:

Natives from our African holdings do not count as citizens. Therefore, they have limited rights and are not eligible for many privileges that a regular citizen would have. A political movement around this has grown, as a few politicians argue that the natives should be granted citizenship. They find that, since they live in part of Iberia, they should be treated as Iberians, or at least given some form of limited citizenship. We must consider this question carefully.
strings.IBR_Colonial_Citizenship_Question_tt: The time has come to answer this subject...
strings.IBR_Collaborate_State_desc:
It is very important that certain values are instilled into the population. They are not ideology, and in fact they are far from it - every good state has a good culture, the sort of which must be carefully cultivated. While it is difficult to introduce these values at a mass scale, an important step towards such an outcome would be to emphasize them in the Fundamental Laws.

First and foremost, parties with significant disputes should not turn to violence. We must pound this into their heads, at every turn, to prevent another Battle of Barcelona. We need to encourage these groups to work with the state, rather than fight it. After all, it is much easier to create change within the system rather than trying to overturn it.
strings.IBR_Collaborate_Each_Other_desc:
One of the most fundamental - and one of the most flawed - ideas of Bolshevism is the idea of class struggle. They would pit the wealthy against the poor, dividing mankind along arbitrary lines because of the words of some dusty manuscript. For Iberia's stability, we cannot allow anything of the sort to come to exist. The best way to discourage the idea is to enshrine the opposite in the Fundamental Laws.

We must explicitly denounce class struggle for what it is - pointless division and conflict. Every class must recall that they are Iberians, and that in the end they are of the same country, and so share a common destiny. They must collaborate with one another, so that the state works as well as possible.
strings.IBR_Charter_Iberians_desc:
The draft of the Fundamental Law has been delivered for inspection, and at first glance it appears to completely accomplish the goals of the state. Fundamental rights given to the people are identified, as are their conditions for suspension in the name of public order.

A far superior choice to the chaotic model of so-called 'intrinsic' rights seen in less stable polities, and a choice that will ensure the safety of the state against actors who would misuse these grants.
strings.IBR_Obligations_of_State_desc:
For far too long, the fundamental processes of state have been scattered across laws, executive orders, and simple norms of convention, and this has caused disorder, confusion, and constant difficulty. It can no longer be tolerated.

And it will not be. A new process will begin, and we will draft a new foundational law to correct these deficiencies - and introduce new strengths.
strings.IBR_Diarchy_Question_desc:
The Union was itself born out of Peninsular compromise in a time of great need. The concessions made then in order to permit its formation - especially regarding the executive - while workable in a general sense, continue to rely upon ill-defined spheres of influence and rules of convention.

It has been a long time since then. Times have changed, as has the world, and the diarchy will likely need some changes as well. Neither Caudillo would lose their power, of course, but the system requires at least a cursory review. We must make sure it is up to the times.
strings.IBR_Diarchy_Question_tt: An age old question must still be answered.
strings.IBR_Justice_Issue_desc:
It is no great revelation that the Union's judicial system is in need of great repair, especially if it is expected - as it is - to work to support the actions of an efficient and modern state. Action must be taken to ensure this. To revise the current frameworks, dispense with duplicative efforts, and codify the intentions of the state within the pages of judicial power.

Both the Caudillos and the legions of offices below them will work to ensure this. To ensure that the laws are properly organized, properly supportive, and properly capable of being applied quickly and correctly in the interests of both public stability and state security.
strings.IBR_Justice_Issue_tt: Justice and the Rule of Law are key to any state. We must work to ensure the Union enjoys the benefits of both... as its does not clash with the Caudillo's influence.
strings.IBR_Regime_Families_desc:
Even though any perfect government has no factions or cliques, every regular government has plenty. We are definitely no exception. Internal factions have been a constant presence ever since both regimes were established, and they have remained through the founding of the Union. We have deemed the groups the “families” of the state, and there are many - the party itself, the army, church, and so on.

Every group has their own power and influence, and while they are all ultimately subservient to the Caudillos they can still cause incidents in the government. Even though they are non-official, it would do some good to interfere with them, ever-so-slightly. If we balanced their power, and broke up a few of the less useful cliques, it is a definite possibility that more could be squeezed out of exploiting them.
strings.IBR_Regime_Families_tt: Every Family has its black sheeps...
strings.IBR_Administration_Pyramid_desc:
The system of governance devised by the Caudillos is very peculiar. Unique might be a better word. Each province of the country is represented equally, and they are part of two constituent countries - Portugal and Spain. They are both represented equally in the Union itself, which has the final say in many regards.

However, there are issues with the system. A lack of adequately clear provisions, as well as some uncertain edge cases, have turned the administrative system into a hydra that is more inclined to smack its heads together; a distinct lack of the harmony required to run a Union like ours. Were we to clearly define what each level can and cannot do in relation to itself and the others, we could have the country run much better.
strings.IBR_Bureaucratic_Audit_desc:
Bureaucracy is, and always will be, a precarious balancing act. If you have too little, the state will be paralyzed and cease to function. Should you have too much, you will have a bloated monster who is only capable of profiting off its own suffering. Eventually, both will collapse in on themselves. For everyone's sakes, we cannot be either.

We are, however, the latter. When the Union was first created - the root of all evil, it seems - the compromises made led to what we have now, a bloated monstrosity that chokes the life out of everything it touches. As part of our recent governmental reforms, it would do no harm to give the bureaucracy its long-overdue audit. There are many superfluous parts, certainly, we simply have to find what needs rooted out.
strings.IBR_Organic_Law_Of_State_desc:
The various in-process drafts of the Fundamental Law have been reviewed, compared, and edited - and the final draft has now been presented to us. It is complete. This new law will preserve the basis of the state, delineate and regulate obligations and responsibilities, and will ensure the stability of its future.

Now we need only ensure its acceptance.
strings.IBR_Approved_Exclamation_desc:
It is done.

All within the Union rejoice not only at the skill of those who drafted its many particulars, but also at the thoughts of what is to come for Iberia. At long last, the Fundamental Law has passed all necessary steps, and now exerts its authority over the state - for the betterment of it. And of its people, naturally and of course.

But above all, they thank the vision of the Caudillos, they who guided the long and difficult process, remaining always focused on the future. On the people. On what was needed for Iberia. Who refused compromise, refused submission, refused to place Iberia's needs below others. Who have then, now and always, guided Iberia towards progress. And with them continuing to do so, that future is bright indeed.

Forwards!
strings.IBR_assessing_the_economy_desc:
The Iberian economy has been crippled and stagnating for ages, now, and there seems to be no end in sight. From the lack of GDP Growth to the outright uphill struggle to course-correct the twisted administration half-stuck in Spain, half-stuck in Portugal, and entirely stuck in the past. If the Iberian Union is ever to move forward, we must find a solution. Fortunately, three options have presented themselves.

Addressing the problems which plague Iberia shall be our first objective. As our other immediate issues have at least begun to stabilize somewhat -save for perhaps the question of the separatists- we may now begin to focus on the immediate challenges of the Union.
strings.IBR_assessing_the_economy_tt: We will decide the Union's plan for putting an end to the Economic Malaise.
strings.IBR_approve_stabilisation_plan_desc:
In 1959, the Opus Dei and several Portuguese intellectuals came together to propose a plan to save the economy. Through purging the nation of corporatist elements, and embracing capitalism, while also sanitizing the economy through investments in industrial, civilian, and agricultural advancements. Ultimately, however, the plan was shelved, as the government had yet to realize the importance of reforming the economy into a cohesive body. Now, however, we have sound reason to look into the plan, as we fall deeper into our malaise.

As we plot to expand the economy greatly through this plan, our involvement in the economy will inevitably increase, as we will need to dirty our hands to strangle the corporatocratic elements of the economy, though if we manage this crisis well, we may very well find ourselves on the top of the world.
strings.IBR_stabilisation_plan_tt_1: Empowering the Opus Dei will strengthen reformism in the Council.
strings.IBR_stabilisation_plan_tt_2: Empowering the Opus Dei will increase the Council's influence.
strings.IBR_stabilisation_plan_tt_full_warning: Due to the Present State of the Iberian Economy, the drastic measures this plan proposes will almost certainly backfire.
strings.IBR_stabilisation_plan_tt_warning: Due to the Present State of the Iberian Economy, the drastic measures this plan proposes may or may not backfire.
strings.IBR_establish_peseta_conversion_rates_de: The Iberian Union has always found itself in a unique state of affairs in terms of foreign affairs, and with the collapse of the Triumvirate, that fact stands stronger than ever. Between the cooling -if still strong- tensions with the Germans, to the stabilizing -if still heated- relations with the Italians, not to mention the Americans across the pond always trying to get their foot in the door, we find ourselves in the company of many opportunities to trade. The problem, however, arises in converting the humble Peseta with the comparatively stronger currencies of the German Reichsmark, Italian Lira, and American Dollar. If we ever hope to trade with these powers on fair grounds -and perhaps establish firm enough relations to take out a loan, if need be- we will need to stabilize the Peseta, and establish that we are more than capable of dealing with the hegemonies at our door.
strings.IBR_freeze_salaries_plan_desc:
One of the many contributors to our spiraling inflation challenges would be that of the salary. A clear source of financial inflation, an option is to temporarily freeze the salaries, in an effort to not only control the ever-worsening inflation but also aid the struggling businesses of Iberia. Of course, consumption will temporarily dip, and growth may temporarily decrease as a result of this measure, therefore the public must remember that this is a provisional solution, and will be lifted in due time. After all, once the salaries are reinstated, consumption will skyrocket, and make up for the shortfall.

While many will be unhappy with this measure, we must remind the people that what we are doing now is all for the greater good, and will provide them great riches, in the long term.
strings.IBR_raise_interest_rates_desc:
The word “debt” is practically synonymous with the Iberian economy among foreign and even local economists, and for disturbingly good reason. While Iberia finds itself in the common circumstance of too much money chasing too few goods, there is always an unorthodox solution to such a dilemma as inflation.

Through increasing the rates in which banks can charge those that take out loans, we will be able to decrease the amount of money which the average Iberian owns, which will mean less products are being bought, which means that businesses will have no choice but to decrease the cost of their goods and services, thus increasing the value of the Iberian Peseta once more. While we will have some minor blowback to this decision, there will always be angry people, no matter what we do, thus they are best ignored.
strings.IBR_out_with_coal_desc:
We cannot expect for the economy to grow through only addressing the challenges and vices which have it gripped so tightly- we must also begin to shed the inefficient aspects of the economy. Among these issues in need of modernizations, that of power is in need of addressing, in particular, the inefficient use of coal as a power source. While plentiful, it is simply not worth the time and effort, not when other more efficient, cheaper power sources exist.

Pulling our investments from coal and switching them into oil-based industries can only help future growth, provide us with a greater reach of our natural resources, and ensure further growth once the economy can be kicked back into high gear.
strings.IBR_out_with_coal_tt:
We will gain 25 £oil_texticon oil.
We will gain 10 £tt_power grid power.
Building Speed effects of the {ibr_economy_modifier} will increase by 5%.
Industrial efficiency gain effects of the {ibr_economy_modifier} will increase by 5%.
strings.IBR_new_iberian_household_desc:
If you were to ask anyone what an “Iberian household” was before today, they may very well tell you one of any dozen of answers, be it a family which speaks Portuguese and lives in the upper echelons of society, or a Basque family speaking their regional language. It is high time we give a definition to the countless, proper Iberian households across the Union. No matter what language they speak, they will all abide by the same mannerisms, all in the means of increasing consumption.

A new propaganda campaign will be implemented across the Union, asking a simple question. The Iberian household is a happy family, which possesses a full set of appliances, a TV set, a car, lives in a proper suburban residence or apartment, and travels in the summer.

Is your household an Iberian household?
strings.IBR_limit_credit_concessions_desc:
One of the countless myriad of problems besieging our economy today is that of debt, more specifically, the inability of the government to increase the value of the Peseta. Through a lack of proper options, little action has been taken against this contributor to the Iberian economic tragedy.

Now that we have the economy in the forefront of our minds, we can finally address this issue. Something which we do have the capability of changing in favor of decreasing inflation would be to limit credit concessions to the general populace. While we will be decreasing consumption through allowing only limited credit, we will also be ensuring that the value of the Peseta does not decrease. While we will inevitably receive some blowback for this decision, it will be for the greater good of the Iberian economy.
strings.IBR_first_development_plan_desc:
The few regions which Iberia can properly claim as being industrial powerhouses are unsurprisingly few and far between, as countless mountain ranges cut through the nation, greatly limiting economic expansion. To remedy this issue, we must expand the reaches of the industry from a sparse collection of cities to a monolith of progress and achievement for the Iberian people!

We shall commence a series of 3-year plans known as “Economic and Social Development Plans”, dedicated to the industrial expansion of several otherwise sporadically industrialized regions. Once these plans fully come to fruition, Iberia shall become an industrial powerhouse like no other!
strings.IBR_first_development_plan_lock: Present Circumstances prevent us from pursuing this part.
strings.IBR_burgos_industrial_zone_desc:
The city of Burgos has always been a considerably agrarian one. Bearing limited infrastructure at best, the region is not contributing nearly half as much as it could should it be given a push in the right direction.

The government will take on this task in the form of constructing some much-needed infrastructure in the region in the form of highways and roads, and greatly industrialize the region through opening up an industrial zone, and invite private industries to invest in the city. Through exploiting the greatest advantages of the private sectors, we can properly turn the city into an industrial haven, all while profiting in doing so!
strings.IBR_alentejo_chemical_zone_desc:
A sparsely industrialized city, a unique opportunity has found itself in the once Portuguese city; the chemical industry. While the Iberian Union's industries are largely underequipped as a rule, that which we find ourselves particularly lacking is the chemical industry. As Évora finds itself a blank canvas, we shall paint it with the great many chemicals which the economy so needs to both diversify and expand, in equal measures of necessity.

Through opening up a unique industrial zone in the city and inviting the experienced private industries, we will once again benefit from the industries at our fingertips, and find ourselves with another prosperous city to add to the list!
strings.IBR_new_automotive_plants_desc:
An unfortunate side-effect of our current predicament is a considerable decrease in consumption, and a drop in employment, as the terrible cycle of less profits for companies leads to mass layoffs, and thus consumption decreases further, and the cycle repeats. If we ever hope to put an end to this state of affairs, we must act, and soon. A proposed solution to tackle this twin challenge would be to increase employment and decrease the price of products in one fell swoop- namely, in opening several new automotive plants across Iberia.

Through the renewed production of automobiles, we can not only provide the people of the Iberian Union a new opportunity to work, but also strong, affordable automobiles. In time, these investments will prove invaluable.
strings.IBR_end_portuguese_conditioning_desc:
Following the slow progression of founding the Iberian Union, countless old laws and systems continue to operate just as they had around a decade ago. This can not stand. As we strive to pull our economy from the dysfunctional state it has found itself in for the past several years, so too must we modernize and improve upon old laws.

For a start, the corporatist systems in the region continue to operate, making it impossible to move, open, or close factories, or invest into new machinery without the government's permission. Through ending this system of endless bureaucracy, we can facilitate a fair, free competitive market.
strings.IBR_end_portuguese_conditioning_tt: All industrial effects of the Economic Malaise will be nullified.
strings.IBR_end_portuguese_conditioning_lock: Present Circumstances prevent us from pursuing this part.
strings.IBR_subsidise_agricultural_mechanisation:
Not unlike much of our outdated, aging legislation concerning industry, our agricultural strength across the Union is waning. Forced to maintain their crops with ages old equipment, far too many of the children of far too many farmers continue the legacy of their parents. Working for their children to repeat the cycle, and fail miserably to accomplish anything of note. Should work on the farm be profitable enough to send those children to be properly educated, they are liable to break that cycle.

Through providing these farmers with subsidies in an effort to increase their profits, the cycle can finally be broken, and countless of the children once relegated to a lifetime of toil in the fields of Iberia can now benefit society through a proper education, and through entering the great cities across the Union.
strings.IBR_invest_new_technologies_desc:
As the economy has slowed and investment into modern civilian technologies has slowed in tune, we must take action to revive these decaying industries. As the government maintains a strict hold over the industry of innovation, we must lead the private sectors in the pursuit of cheaper, more reliable methods of industrial production within the civilian sector. Be it through research into metalworking, chemistry, plastics, or synthetic materials, we will lead the industries in research, and not only kickstart development in these regions, but also profit from revolutionising the industries!

Through investing in the industries which have otherwise gone under notice, we can greatly benefit from the improved technologies. While we will have the thankless job of kickstarting an industry, we'll be rewarded for our labors with a great countless advancements in the fields of industrial production.
strings.IBR_invest_new_tech_tt: Industrial capacity effects of the {ibr_economy_modifier} will increase by 10%.
strings.IBR_rise_of_iberia_desc:
Not long ago, the Iberian Union was a dysfunctional, broken mess of a nation, at least fiscally and administratively speaking. While we once hardly scraped by under the weight of countless projects only serving to slow down the economy, as inflation and tired systems strangled what growth we managed to benefit from, we can now say with confidence that the age of inefficiencies has ended in Iberia. Through allowing the government's participation in the economy to bolster the greatest aspects of the circumstances which we find ourselves in, we have well and truly improved upon the state of the economy, and therefore Iberia.

Across the Iberian Union, things are getting substantially better, and faster than it has any right to be! The stabilization plans have already begun to rake in profits, and the buying power of the Iberian Peseta has skyrocketed in spectacular fashion! People are moving into the cities en masse, and consuming high-quality products like never before! The Iberian Union is no longer a joke, no longer a case study in poor economics already behind the times, but a statue of just how far a nation can go when it plays its cards right.

Iberia is strong again. May we keep it as such forevermore.
strings.IBR_rise_of_iberia_tt:
GDP Growth effects of the {ibr_economy_modifier} will increase by 0.50%.
Miscellaneous Income of the {ibr_economy_modifier} will increase by $$0.1 B.
strings.IBR_open_for_business_desc:
One of the many advantages which Iberia benefits from in its non-committal relationships with nations across the world is that of trade. As few see the Iberian Union as an enemy, we have been able to benefit from smaller trade deals with most all hegemonies which surround us. Even still, however, we have found ourselves unable to reap all the benefits provided by further pursuing these relations.

Through redoubling our efforts to cooperate with foreign powers and open up Iberia to foreign investments and even foreign companies coming into the Iberian Union. With this change, Iberia shall become a new testament to international cooperation, as foreign tourists and business magnates come to visit the beaches and factories of Iberia looking for pleasure and for profit, benefitting Iberian industries as a whole as thanks to the increased investment into the burgeoning new industries of the Union!
strings.IBR_open_for_business_tt: Trade Relations with Every European Country will be increased by 15.
strings.IBR_allow_foreign_investment_desc:
If we ever hope to exploit our ties to foreign nations, we must first allow for these ties to be exploited in the first place! As it stands, the economy of the Iberian Union is entirely unprepared for foreign interaction, at least in a legal sense, as foreign investment has been outright banned for several years, thus putting a considerable roadblock in the way of growth within Iberian private industries.

The first step towards ensuring growth in the private sectors, then, is to allow for foreign investments to invest where the Iberian Peseta cannot. Through passing new legislation ensuring this foreign investment, we will be sure to not only benefit greatly from untold amounts of wealth being poured into the private industries but also stronger relations with the powers across the globe, as we find ourselves bound closer and closer with foreign powers.
strings.IBR_heavily_reduce_tariffs_desc:
One of the many aspects strangling the Iberian economy is a lack of trade, which has greatly decreased the Iberian Union's ability to keep pace with the competing world powers, at least technologically speaking. This limited trade has most certainly been the result of countless tariffs placed on both imports and exports, making it nearly impossible to trade with foreign nations with any genuine profits. As a result, the Iberian Union has been practically disconnected from the rest of the world, and it has shown the lack of growth in recent years.
