Now that we've gotten the chance to address this problem, however, we must do everything in our power to nullify the mistakes we have made in the past, and prepare to tackle the future. Drastically cutting down on these tariffs -if not abolishing them outright- will do wonders for the economy. This development will not only allow for a new source of revenue for the various private industries across Iberia, but it also allows for the average Iberian to purchase countless more products of international origin, for a much lower price than they may have had to otherwise. With this change, Iberia will be able to breathe a sigh of relief from the economic challenges which had once troubled it.
strings.IBR_reform_the_tax_system_desc:
As is known within and without Iberia, the taxation system of the Union is outright incomprehensible at best, and unusable at worst. Such a deeply rooted issue cannot be torn up over the course of a month, though we may be able to reform some aspects of the system to make it at least feasible in the short term.

One of the many changes which can be made to streamline the system or at least improve upon its efficiency has been decided to be increasing taxation upon the people and businesses to increase state revenue, while also slashing spending wherever we can. While this decision may not be the most popular decision which we will make in fixing the economy, we can at least improve upon the system, and that is more than worth it.
strings.IBR_iberia_is_different_desc:
It seems that the Iberian Union has found itself fomenting the perfect storm for an odd sort of industry which the peninsula is far from unfamiliar with; tourism. While the notion of inviting foreigners over to spend their money and see the sights of Iberia has died off in recent years as thanks to the Cold War and Iberia's own isolationism, it seems that with the rolling back on the latter aspect, there are a brave few which have decided to stage their vacation in Iberia. The new challenge, then, is how we get everyone else to visit Iberia.

The solution? An advertising scheme of unrivaled scale, across the globe. The Iberian Union consists of countless beautiful landmarks and sets of scenery alluring enough for any tourist to add it to their list, though the varied cultures of the peninsula are surely to attract just as many who would look for a unique experience.

With every passing day, Iberia is becoming more beautiful, as its problems have been all but solved, at least in terms of foreign involvement in the economy. Truly, the peninsula is beginning to heal.
strings.IBR_trust_the_ministries_desc:
In recent years, the approach of the Iberian government to resolve the current economic crisis has been one of slow liberalization, ensuring a steady pace is taken to prevent any economic destabilization. This plan has been decided to be the right way to take the economy from the advice of our ministries, though they offer a unique piece of advice- to begin accelerating this process, and to increase our involvement in the recovery process.

Through this economic plan, we will find ourselves greatly liberalizing our current economic system, which many prominent economists believe to be the better path to trek. All we can do is hope these assumptions are proven right, and Iberia can be clawed out of this economic quagmire.
strings.IBR_deficit_management_tt: Our Ministries have been adequately performing their duties and our Debt-to-GDP ratio is lower than 75%.
strings.IBR_deficit_management_b_tt: We possess the necessary budgetary lee-way for large-scale investments, that is to say, our Debt-to-GDP ratio is lower than 75%.
strings.IBR_deficit_management_c_tt: We possess the necessary budgetary lee-way to pursue Autarky once more, that is to say, our Debt-to-GDP ratio is lower than 75%.
strings.IBR_deficit_management_d_tt: The State of Our Economy has worsened sufficiently to reconsider our Economic Strategy
strings.IBR_new_industrial_legislation_desc:
The current industrial conditioning within Portugal is greatly hampering the progress of industrial development, as many potential investors in the region are greatly discouraged as a result of the tightly regimented system in place. Through clearing out this dysfunctional system, we will revamp investment in the region, and install new legislation to work to the best of the region's benefits.

The first step to resolving the flawed legislation will be to replace it entirely- implementing reformed industrial limitation legislation will allow us to benefit from the pre-existing system of industrial limitation, though will also be toned down enough to reap the rewards of a liberated market. Before long, investments in Portugal will increase beyond comparison, and benefit the Iberian Union beyond belief.
strings.IBR_new_industrial_legislation_tt: All industrial effects of the Economic Malaise will be nullified.
strings.IBR_bring_ini_to_portugal_desc:
Since the foundation of the Iberian Union, there have been several stipulations and caveats which have maintained a division between the former lands of Spain and Portugal. One of the more troublesome exceptions to the unification of Iberia has been the INI; the Instituto Nacional de Industria, a Spanish public organization dedicated to the creation and financing of public companies. As a result of Portugal's more restrictive form of governing, the INI has never allowed for the expansion of some industries within Portugal. As the Iberian Union grows closer and closer, however, it may be high time to remove this troublesome caveat and allow for the INI to support public businesses across Iberia.

While this decision will inherently be unpopular with some within Portugal, they will soon come to know the benefits in keeping a leash on the people's ambitions.
strings.IBR_sponsor_new_companies_desc:
Now that the INI has been established across all of the Iberian Union, we can begin to make the most of the strengthened organization. While the roots of the organization still settle into Portugal, however, we would be only failing to seize the initiative. As the INI organizes itself across Portugal, we will provide funding to the INI across Iberia to finance the creation of new companies, as well as ensuring the expansion of already existing companies, be they private or public.

Through exploiting the existing organizations within Iberia and using them to expand the fledgling companies across the Union, we will soon find our economy to only stabilize and improve in the coming years.
strings.IBR_build_apartment_buildings_desc:
As the economy has slowly improved, opportunity is finally beginning to return to the cities, and countless Iberians are returning to urban centers. The problem is, far too many Iberians are making a run for the cities, and the value of housing in these regions has skyrocketed as a result, to the point that few -if any- can afford to move into the cities, and many find themselves sunken into poverty as a result.

To remedy this unfortunate problem, we can begin building apartment buildings around the outer rims of the city. While these apartment blocks may not be the biggest or most efficient buildings, they will give Iberians jobs, and they are capable of holding an Iberian family, and for Iberia, that will be enough.
strings.IBR_federal_consumption_tax_desc:
As the Iberian government finds itself funding more and more of the public and private industries, the necessity of a new source of revenue is making itself clearer and clearer with each passing day. While the investments made thus far will inevitably turn a profit down the road, the government needs funds, and fast.

A proposed solution is to implement a federal consumption tax, where the rates will affect each and every product on store shelves proportionally to their necessity. Essential products, such as food, tools, and the like will be taxed the least, while luxury products will be taxed the most. As a result, the government will receive new funds, and the people will experience the least amount of financial discomfort.
strings.IBR_revitalise_senpa_desc:
In ages past, the state organization of SENPA -the Servicio Nacional de Productos Agrarios- has managed the production and distribution of agrarian products as well as their derivatives. With this grand responsibility, SENPA has also regulated the prices of these products, though this organization has fallen from grace since the Iberian Union has begun trading with other nations once again. This has made it harder and harder for SENPA to manage the prices of these products, as price and production have returned to obeying natural demand. The question, then, is how do we tackle the question of SENPA?

One potential solution would be to totally reorganize SENPA and to shed the notion of total control over the agrarian market of Iberia. The Iberian Union is changing. It's high time that SENPA change with it. While we provide the organization with new funds, its directive will change- from an organization set to monitor and regulate the markets, to an organization set to represent the interests of the Iberian government in the realm of agrarian matters.
strings.IBR_new_agricultural_methods_desc:
It is an unfortunate fact of life in Iberia that the overwhelming majority of farmers operate with ancient equipment, and hardly modern techniques. The reason for this is quite simple- the farmers are incapable of purchasing these new technologies for lack of funds. As a result, our agricultural output is a far cry from what it could be.

Our solution to this glaring issue is rather simple- we will purchase vast amounts of these new technologies and equipment, and sell them to the poorest farmers. By allowing the best aspects of government participation to strengthen the people, Iberia will become the gold standard for capable governing practices.
strings.IBR_promote_consumption_desc:
At present, consumption within Iberia has greatly sunken, which has meant fewer goods are in circulation, and production has not had to put in much effort to keep up with demand. While a thrifty population is a hardy one, we must bring the mindset of the people up to speed with the needs of economic growth.

Through an advertising campaign dedicated to the notion of a happy family, as well as a compulsory sales season surrounding Christmas, consumption will greatly increase. While this will also increase economic growth and prosperity for industries across the board, it will also pad the wallets of the Iberian government by taking advantage of the federal sales tax.
strings.IBR_a_federal_economy_desc:
While many would laugh at the notion of the Iberian Union becoming an economic powerhouse not a few months ago, it seems that just that has been managed. Through the sheer tenacity and ambition of the Iberian government, we have successfully reversed the economic downturns of years past, and have even considerably federalized the economy.

The past years of humiliation and degradation have been buried. The future now lays open, with unlimited potential in store. With our economy firmly dealt with, we can now look onwards, towards not only recovering from the past but building off of it. Today is a proud day for Iberia. May it last forevermore.
strings.IBR_Economic_Crash: The current economic plan has been scrapped
strings.IBR_a_national_expansion_desc:
Should Iberia ever hope to become a legitimate regional power, a considerable industry is going to be an inherent necessity. Unfortunately, this is something which Iberia finds itself considerably lacking. Any other nation might call it quits at that, and declare their economy dedicated to another resource, perhaps to better adapt to their natural resources.

Iberia does not bend the knee to nature.

From this point onwards, the Iberian government will fund a wide variety of large-scale industrial projects, and will not stop until Iberia can count itself as an industrial power.
strings.IBR_prospect_new_mines_desc:
The lands of Iberia have proven rich in resources, enough to fuel our economy over the past centuries into the modern-day. If we hope to live on for centuries more, we must look into greater resources for the economy. While in the past, coal and steel have been the fuel to the fires of industrialization, today the foundations of the future are built around a new fuel; uranium. Between the two forms of fuel, we must first find it, however.

Through opening up a variety of investigations across the Union, we may soon find the Iberian Union to sit upon a treasure trove of resources. All we need to do is look. Through opening up prospecting, we're liable to dig up fuel for our new industrialization programs. Hopefully, the Union will live to make good use of them.
strings.IBR_new_mines_tt:
GDP Growth effects of the {ibr_economy_modifier} will increase by 0.15%.
We will gain 30 £aluminium_texticon aluminium.
We will gain 30 £chromium_texticon chromium.
We will gain 30 £tungsten_texticon tungsten.
We will gain 5 £uranium_texticon uranium.
strings.IBR_national_infrastracture_plan_desc:
The Iberian Union is considerably well connected in terms of transportation, at least concerning the fact that the Union is an odd fusion of two nations fused through little beyond circumstance and determination. In fact, the infrastructure is above average, rivaled only by Germany's Autobahn. Even still, we find ourselves capable of further uniting the nation.

Not only will a closely connected nation decrease commuting costs for products, but laboring to improve upon the infrastructure will also open up countless jobs to Iberians, decreasing unemployment. The National Infrastructure Plan will do much more than build new train stations, airports, naval ports, and roads, it will also bring the Iberian Union closer together, in far more ways than one.
strings.IBR_national_infrastracture_plan_tt:
Every European state with an airport will receive another one.
Every European state without an airport and more than 700000 people will receive one.
Every European state with less than 5 infrastructure will get one more.
Every European state with a port will receive another one.
Multiple new Railway Lines shall be constructed on the mainland.
All states receiving improvements will also receive a boost to their GDP!
strings.IBR_expand_heavy_industry_desc:
One of the great resources within Iberia has always been iron deposits. Even today, iron has been a massive contributor to the Iberian war machine and international market. Of course, we can also melt and cast this useful material into countless products which can be sold abroad. While even now we greatly benefit from this resource, we can always improve our margins, and further exploit these profits.

While there is a considerable amount of blast furnaces and other metallurgy across the Union, we will build several new establishments to further exploit this natural resource, as well as provide the Union with a stronger revenue stream. All it will take to make the most of these resources is some legwork, and we will find ourselves rich in iron beyond our wildest dreams.
strings.IBR_meet_with_the_big_fish_desc:
Within the Iberian Union's economic battlegrounds, there are always the select few within the countless private and state corporations which are known to be the fatcats of the markets; our own Abs, Flick, Siemens, and Geilenbergs. Many would laud these individuals within the Union as too powerful for their own good, even if they are massive contributors to the economy. Even still, the Iberian Union is a well-mended state by necessity. Likewise, we will need to reel in these fatcats should we hope to collaborate for a greater future.

If the Iberian Union is to not only survive, but thrive, we must take the necessary measures to align the big fish of the industries to ensure economic growth. It is by our grace that they do not have their heads on pikes outside the French border. So long as they continue to obey our whims, it will stay that way for ages to come.
strings.IBR_reapply_the_old_desc:
Corporatism and Falangism are far and above the best direction in which the economy can be taken, as the relative economic stability and prosperity of the '40s have been interrupted by the worst excesses of liberalizing a perfectly functional system. With the degrading status of the economy, we find ourselves condemned to but one solution: a return to the system of days past, of state intervention, total economic control, and a return to Autarky.

This return to traditional economics will inevitably infuriate many of our liberal colleagues, though it is the only way forward. Liberalism has failed Iberia, and a change in course must be established, lest the Union collapse altogether.
strings.IBR_nation_wide_conditioning_desc:
A system originating from Portugal, the notion of “Industrial Conditioning” consists of the government checking over every single application to open up any sort of establishment; anything from a mom-and-pop shop to an industrial complex, all would need the seal of approval from the government when purchasing any piece of industrial equipment, which would allow for the government to accurately catalog the needs of the industries across Iberia.

This system of organizing the economy, while certainly bureaucratic, will be expanded upon through necessity, not only beyond the borders of Portugal but will also have its total outreach expanded to a great many more categories of industrial equipment. Of course, this will slow down the process of economic expansion, it will be worth it to keep a tight grip on the economy.
strings.IBR_empower_national_unions_desc:
Legally speaking, the only unions permitted within Iberia are the Sindicato Vertical, which has served the people of Iberia for years, though there has been a sort of underground revolution since the mid-1950s. These Communists founded several of their own unions, which have caused a considerable headache for the businessmen across Iberia. Unfortunately, many of these businessmen have collaborated with these Communists, citing finding it easier to negotiate with rather than the Sindicato Vertical through less paperwork.

These acts of disloyalty have greatly hindered our economy, and something must be done. Crackdowns and punishments will be unleashed across Iberia, and those caught collaborating with these illegal unions, not to mention the total obliteration of these Communists. We will expand the powers of the Sindicato Vertical, and we will ensure it stands as the sole organism in charge of worker-boss relations. May it last forever.
strings.IBR_seize_private_assets_desc:
To begin, it is obvious that private property is an unquestionable right. Even still, there are several powerful industries and businesses which can be considered of “national interest” as they consist of one essential aspect to the economy or another. While these industries are technically controlled by private individuals, who are technically autonomous in the sense that they can do with their property what they want, they are also below the state. As a result, we can pass a law that will allow for the state and its organism to seize and nationalize any assets which are of national interest. Through this new legislation, we will find ourselves capable of expanding the reach of the government.

While the people will inevitably become angered at this cracking down of the private industries, it is an essential step to take towards a brighter future for Iberia.
strings.IBR_rise_the_tariffs_autarky_desc:
The Iberian Union is surrounded by enemies. The backstabbing Italians, the spiteful Turkish, the imperialist Germans, and the corrupt Americans have all left us to suffer. If we hope to become a regional power, we must become fully autonomous from the influence of others. If we hope to escape the influence of others, we will need to completely and totally sever our international trade. Through rising import and export tariffs, external nations will have no choice but to not trade with the Iberian Union, and our own businesses will have no choice but to sell locally.

While this may harm the economy, this initiative will prove essential once the backstabbing ways of the other powers across the globe come to light.
strings.IBR_total_senpa_control_desc:
As more and more power is shifted towards the government, we must address the organization of the SENPA. Created several years ago to manage the prices of agricultural products, we now have sufficient cause to transfer all power to the SENPA. Everything from prices to products will be put within the jurisdiction of the SENPA, everything. Be it the tools, harvest schedules, production, or the very prices of the product, all will be expanded into the realm of the SENPA's jurisdiction.

Of course, this will only centralize the powers of the SENPA, and while it will temporarily slow down economic growth, it will prove worthwhile in the long term.
strings.IBR_consume_national_desc:
So much as we try, it always seems as though there are some foreign products that have made their way into Iberian territory. Unfortunately, these products haven't come here off the back of a select few intrepid businessmen looking to bear the price of the countless tariffs. They have instead come here under the black market, a cancer which has only grown since our protectionist measures. Even now, the black market expands in influence, and more and more Iberians turn towards it in favor of Iberian goods. This is going to change.

Through beginning a propaganda campaign, to encourage the consumption of national-produced products, as opposed to any kind of subversive foreign goods. Of course, this is not the only way to root out the black market. Through cracking down on these black markets, we'll do more than enough to get rid of these insubordinate thieves.
strings.IBR_economic_disaster_desc:
The factors which came together to cause the Iberian economic disaster are greatly varied. Foreign powers conspiring against us have forced our hand, and we find ourselves suffering because of it, on top of our past economic troubles which have gone unaddressed due to higher priorities. There is no use crying over the past when there is still so much to do, however. We have already addressed the root of the problem- the simple challenge lies in determining the symptoms.

As our government has already identified the exact statistics which plague the economy, we can now safely say that the worst has yet to come to pass. Brain drain, agricultural unrest, and a capital flight have all contributed to a sharp incline in prices, high unemployment, and the general side effects of an economic crisis. Already, our government is mobilizing to combat the crisis, though some lament that it is simply too late.
strings.IBR_economic_disaster_tt: The experiment has failed, and now we have to pick up the pieces.
strings.IBR_kill_the_legislation_desc:
It is now clear that the corporatist legislation which we were forced into implementing has not worked to fix the economy, and has only dramatically worsened our situation. While not all of this is entirely up to the government, there is certainly a degree of responsibility in the falangists and corporatists who recommended the plan in the first place. The first step in remedying these mistakes is to remove the causes completely. Uprooting the corporatist policies is the first step to our recovery, though it certainly is still a long way to stability.

Reinstating the economically-liberal policies of slow-burn liberalization is without a doubt the best option to take right now, even if at the cost of a great humiliation of the government's ability to select successful policies.
strings.IBR_kill_the_legislation_tt: All industrial effects of the economic miracle will increase by 10%.
strings.IBR_shame_the_corporatists_desc:
Taking a moment to identify the cause behind the disastrous policies which put us in this position, we can easily track down that belief which has placed us in this terrible position; corporatism. The ideology is long past its prime, and certainly has no place in the Iberian Union. Thus, its advocates have no place in the Iberian Union, either. No matter how long it takes, we will root out those politicians and economists who have brought Iberia down to this level, be they in the Council or really any position in the government. Putting any corporatist into a position of power is nothing but a death sentence, and we would be fools to fall for their tricks again.

With the progenitors of this crisis out of the government, we can only hope they never have a hand in Iberia, and that we can recover from their disaster.
strings.IBR_god_fix_this_mess_desc:
The situation within the Iberian economy is not improving. In fact, it seems to be deteriorating at an unimaginable rate, and our actions thus far have done little -if anything- to quell the waves of economic downturn. Unemployment is increasing, and the value of the Peseta has decreased to catastrophic levels. It is time to make some decisions.

We know of the horrific condition of the economy, and we are running out of options to fix it. Our only choice is to take all of these options at once. Whatever it takes, we will pull out all the stops to fix this mess, and heave Iberia out of the ditch. This flurry of new legislation may not be enough to completely solve this crisis, though it will be enough to stave off the collapse.

God willing, it will be enough.
strings.IBR_god_fix_this_mess_tt: Inflation effects of the Economic Malaise will decrease by 2.0%.
strings.IBR_rise_the_salaries_desc:
Since the economy fell from grace like a brick falls from a skyscraper, many of Iberia's best and brightest have left the nation to pursue more fruitful careers abroad. While we would typically find nothing but spite for those that would flee from Iberia in its time of need, now is not the time for senseless hatred. In an effort to bring these talented individuals back home, we will increase their paycheck, and raise their salaries.

With some luck, getting even some of these skilled personnel back into the economy will prove vital. Not only that, but with these greater paychecks, it is hoped that consumption will be encouraged.

God willing, there will still be goods worth buying by the time they get back.
strings.IBR_business_tax_cut_desc:
While business tax is a fantastic form of profit for the Iberian government, now is not the time for short-term benefit; if this crisis will persist into tomorrow, then so must our policies. Through cutting these excessive taxes, we will find our national businesses to grow, as they no longer need to worry about spending half their budget on taxation.

While we may miss out on some of this profit, it will allow for the businesses of Iberia to begin to grow again, or at least weather the storm.

While this legislation may not be in the best interest of the government, it is becoming increasingly clear that perhaps that is not what should come first.
strings.IBR_business_tax_cut_tt: GDP Growth effects of the Economic Malaise will increase by 0.10%.
strings.IBR_increase_civilian_spending_desc:
As consumption decreases, and businesses are forced to let go of more and more Iberians thanks to dropping business, unemployment has grown substantially, with little signs of slowing down. With this in mind, we must act to aid the Iberian people, and to ensure their well-being.

Through increasing civilian spending, more businesses will be able to hold onto their employees, thus decreasing joblessness, and those employed will be able to increase consumption, thus decreasing the total amount of jobs on top of stifling job loss.

While this is far from a fix for the horrendously destabilized economy, it may be enough to bring the diving numbers back out of the deep red, and keep Iberia afloat.
strings.IBR_back_to_square_one_desc:
In spite of just how far the Iberian economy has faltered, it would seem as though through the combined efforts of the nation in its time of need and absolute desperation, has pulled the economy from out of the depths of where it once laid, and back into where it was before the terrible decision was made to return to corporatism. Unfortunately, that is exactly where the economy lays; exactly where it was before we attempted to fix it. Between the extreme amounts of unemployment finally being reigned in, to the corporatists being forced out from the government, nothing has changed.

Within Iberia, the economy has combusted for no good reason. While it has been repaired, the economy has achieved the concerning merit of “no longer the least of our problems.” Across Iberia, there is unrest growing at our handling of the economy. Things may very well get worse before they get better, though only time will tell.
strings.IBR_economic_tragedy_focus_desc:
Hubris lies at the root of countless tragedies. And so it is here.

The technocrats proposed a radical path for Iberia's economy. One of temporary pain, for divine rewards in the hereafter. But their daggers plunged too deep. Production was curtailed, investment was slashed, and their target was ultimately missed. Those thin savings the populace built up after the collapse of the Triumvirate allowed them to keep spending, maintaining demand. However, with store shelves emptying and the same amount of pesetas passing through the till, prices could only go up.

And so temporary pain became divine retribution for the technocrat's pride: inflation, unemployment, shuttered factories, foreclosed homes. Iberia must repent before downturn becomes crisis.
strings.IBR_economic_tragedy_tt: The experiment has failed, and now we have to pick up the pieces.
strings.IBR_salvage_the_legislation_desc:
The liberalizing features of the Stabilization Plan were sound. Predictably, however, our about-face on its macroeconomic precepts has given Iberia's corporatists a perfect opportunity to counterattack.

The leadership of the Vertical Union is demanding the rollback of our streamlining measures. In the name of 'consultation,' it is pushing for tighter control over wage policy and even influence over state developmental investments.

We'll look to 'consult' them in a series of tepid, seemingly unorganized meetings. Anything to keep them from slathering Iberia's businesses in red tape once again.
strings.IBR_saving_face_desc:
To the uninformed, the Stabilization Plan caused nothing but instability for an economy that was doing well, if not well enough. Such beliefs could reflect negatively upon Iberia's leadership... such as on certain Portuguese Caudillos famed for their financial and economic acumen.

A two-part strategy must be employed. First, we must claim that this crash was inevitable, and that the Stabilization Plan relieved some of the symptoms. Second, blame must be assigned. Navarro Rubio's ilk must be thrown out for causing this mess, for failing to oversee the successful implementation of the Plan. Together, that should ensure those we need to protect are protected.
strings.IBR_god_fix_this_mess_sp_desc:
We've protected the most valuable elements of the Stabilization Plan and, more importantly, of the Iberian government. But we have not managed to protect the Iberian economy. Unemployment and inflation continue unabated, with old factories remaining closed and untouched, overgrown fields in place of our planned industrial parks.

We must take whatever measures necessary to resume production in Iberia. To put tools in workers' hands and cans on their shelves. Only then will the Union be truly protected once again.
strings.IBR_rise_the_salaries_sp_desc:
Freezing the wages of the Iberian worker failed to stop inflation or spur business growth. Now, with inflation roaring higher and families' savings depleting quickly, it is both politically and economically untenable to keep salaries stuck.

To rousing cheers, we will cancel the most hated element of the Stabilization Plan, allowing pay packets to grow once more. Of course, with inflation raging, salaries have still decreased in real terms, so we can pray more firms will not buckle under the added strain.
strings.IBR_business_tax_cut_sp_desc:
The failed Stabilization Plan pursued a complex economic liberalization. One that ultimately proved too abstract for businesses' needs.

As we navigate forward, we will recover Iberia's productive capacity in the most simple way possible. We will slash firms' tax bills. Let them keep their profits, add zeros to their bottom line, whatever it takes to get them investing, hiring, and above all, producing again.

Critics will point to the Union's yawning deficit, and say that we cannot afford these giveaways. But nor can we afford to do nothing.
strings.IBR_increase_civilian_spending_sp_desc:
Factories and farms lie dormant, casualties of the Stabilization Plan's shocks. If production is to resume, if prices and unemployment are to be lowered, Iberia must take decisive measures to see them reopened.

With consumer spending increasingly precarious as savings are run down, the Union itself must take up this duty. The state shall guarantee bulk purchases in key industries, giving firms the confidence to reopen assembly lines and facilities. We shall back loans to those same companies, ensuring they have the capital required to do so. We shall stuff Spanish sectors with INI subsidies, and prop up Portuguese production with pesetas. We shall spend, spend, spend, until the economy is moving once more.
strings.IBR_changeless_change_desc:
Stability. We sought it, and in our pursuit, cast what little we had away. Now, after wasted, painful months, we have clawed our way back to where we began. Our treasury emptier, the peseta weaker, and the Church far shorter of alms.

No one would claim the Iberian economy is healthy. But nor is there any further appetite for the radical measures needed to rehabilitate it, not after the failure of the Stabilization Plan. We must keep moving, look beyond the economy for other approaches to strengthen our Union.

Especially after this failure, we do not have the luxury of standing still.
strings.IBR_reformist_tt_econ_1: Empowering the Opus Dei will strengthen reformism in the Council.
strings.IBR_influence_tt_econ_1: Empowering the Opus Dei will increase the Council's influence.
strings.IBR_reformist_tt_econ_2: Removing these entrenched elements will strengthen reformism in the Council.
strings.IBR_influence_tt_econ_2: Removing these entrenched elements will increase the Council's influence.
strings.IBR_reformist_tt_econ_3: Returning to autarky will weaken reformism in the Council.
strings.IBR_influence_tt_econ_3: Returning to autarky will decrease the Council's influence.
strings.IBR_reformist_tt_econ_4: Empowering the Old Guard will weaken reformism in the Council.
strings.IBR_influence_tt_econ_4: Empowering the Old Guard will decrease the Council's influence.
strings.IBR_antisep_start_desc:
The Battle of Barcelona will go down as a defining and traumatizing moment in Iberian history. Everyone remembers what they were doing when they heard Barcelona was burning.

The government decision to allow TV crews to follow the advancing troops and broadcast live from the front in hopes of a propaganda victory horribly backfired. Caring Iberian mothers had to cover their children's eyes when the television showed a Leonardo Vulture pecking the eye of a dead DI member underneath the marble façade of the Sagrada Família Cathedral, and the footage of a Guardia Civil Colonel executing a handcuffed militiaman became the centerpiece of heated arguments at Sunday family lunches throughout the whole Union. Our citizens are starting to question if the State is really capable of protecting them.

Caudillo Franco has made a reassuring speech explaining that the Barcelona Uprising was a complete failure and the Reds lost both the military and the political battle, but behind closed doors everyone in the regime knows that this Barcelona was only the beginning of the violence. Our fragile Union will not be able to withstand another Barcelona, and everything in our power must be done to stop the terrorists.
strings.IBR_antisep_mobilize_AAS_desc:
RESERVADO/SÓLO LECTURA/SECRETO/APENAS LEITURA:
Definitive Plan for reform and expansion of the AAS:

1) Create exception ordinances permitting the AAS to release prisoners for use as informants, preemptively detain suspects without charges, perform enhanced interrogation techniques, commandeer local law enforcement and produce and use compromising materials against terrorism supporters. Also grant their officers immunity from prosecution under Iberian law while performing their duty, allowing undercover work in terrorist organizations.
2) Funding will increase drastically, and the selection process for new officers will begin immediately. The Agency's current reach is insufficient to deal with the expected terrorist threat.
3) Recruit and train teams of loyal officers from minority backgrounds and embed them as local citizens in terror supporting neighborhoods, use them for full surveillance of the physical and telematic spectrums.
4) Create the GEO, a specialized counterterrorist unit capable of swiftly dealing with high-risk arrests, bomb threats, and hostage situations without the need of help from the Army or the Guardia, guaranteeing operational security.
strings.IBR_antisep_mobilize_AAS_tt:
This focus will add AAS Resources for use against various separatist organizations in the decisions menu.

Open the decisions menu to begin counter-terrorist operations - Iberia's stability will depend on this!
strings.IBR_antisep_blank_check_desc:
A series of reforms are being made to the AAS to ensure what happened in Barcelona will never happen again. However, intelligence is only the first step in our fight against terror. We will turn the terrorists' arms against them and just as they laid waste to our living, we shall lay waste to theirs.

Our most loyal AAS officers will form the GAL, Grupos Antiterroristas de Liberación. These groups primarily composed of “former” police officers, “patriotic” mercenaries and “concerned” criminals will participate in blank check operations without formal connection to the Iberian State.

These brave men will carry out missions that our official state security forces cannot: The preventive neutralization of terrorist cadres inside or beyond Iberian borders, the kidnapping, interrogation and extortion of valuable members within the hierarchy of various terrorist groups, and the realization of false flag operations against civilian targets as a form of armed propaganda to undermine sympathy for the terrorist cause. “Para grandes males, grandes remedios”.
strings.IBR_antisep_break_them_desc:
Popular music songs are loudly emanating from residential and commercial buildings alike on the outskirts of every major Iberian city. Onlookers are probably thinking there are bunches of rowdy teenagers, but the truth is much more sinister.

Behind those walls torture chambers are being run at full steam by the AAS, who are employing exotic interrogation methods to gather as much intelligence as they can get to support our next move. Every phone is being tapped while every small hint and every anonymous tip is being followed with zeal.

If a person is deemed suspicious by intelligence, he is then kidnapped by GAL and secretly brought to these facilities, ironically named “Checas” by their agents, the name the Soviet barbarians gave to premises just like ours during the Reconquista. In a few more days our Checas will have gathered enough information to enable our forces to begin our grand counter-terrorist offensive and nip this evil in the bud.
strings.IBR_antisep_break_them_tt: We will begin a campaign to strike back against the separatists as quickly as possible.
strings.IBR_antisep_batons_desc: After weeks of planning, investigation, and analysis we finally can strike back at the terrorist threat. Using information gathered from informants, Checas and wiretaps the AAS has identified hundreds of key terrorist elements and is ready to execute mass arrests on command. In the dead of night, the Falangist anthem “Cara al Sol” will be played on radio stations throughout the country. That will be the signal to start the arrests. GAL operatives will take care of the most dangerous targets, while the lesser risk warrants will be served by AAS officers. This move will show them that this land is ours and that we will wipe clean the scourge that has sullied our peaceful Iberia.
strings.IBR_antisep_batons_tt: This will add more AAS Resources to combat separatism. If they can be neutered quickly, perhaps we can prevent more horror.
strings.IBR_antisep_trials_desc:
The “Trial of the Century” will be hosted in Madrid, with two dozens of the vilest terrorists on the planet standing in front of the Supreme Court at a Special National Security Session. More than 150 witnesses encompassing government officials, bombing victims and the so called “Soplones”, terrorist turncoats who will cover their faces and testify against their former comrades in exchange of immunity, will be ready to give their testimony on the prosecution side. News outlets from all Europe and beyond will be covering the event, including a team from the New York Times led by famed reporter Hanna Arendt. Cameras will be placed around the pulpit transmitting the full session with live commentary by loyal journalists.

The defendants will be held in a soundproof glass cage in the middle of the courthouse, responding their questions using a microphone which can be muted if the plaintiff tries to use the trial as a soapbox. Most of the suspects will be sentenced to life imprisonment, and the worst of them all being given capital punishment. With this show of force we aim to deter further terror attacks.
strings.IBR_antisep_trials_tt: We will begin trials of suspected separatists, giving them the harshest possible punishments. This should present an effective deterrent.
strings.IBR_antisep_radios_desc:
A car bomb went off in the all-girls Sacred Heart School in Bilbao, murdering 19 schoolgirls who were playing in the yard and wounding many more. Forensic experts quickly analyzed the scene and discovered that the explosive used was the famous Goma-2, ETA's signature weapon.

The nightly news was fully dedicated to the bombing, interspersing footage from the victims with the image of Doña Maria del Carmen, Caudillo Franco's lovely wife, crying when she received the terrible tidings. The closing segment depicted two men in white masks in front of an Ikurriña flag reading a statement: “The ruling classes refused to socialize their power and wealth and because of their avarice and short-sightedness, the ETA is beholden to socialize suffering”.

On the next day vigils honoring the dead children were spontaneously made throughout our whole Union, even in the Basque neighborhoods, and many mourners chanting “¡Asesinos! ¡Asesinos!” A photograph taken by El Correo of a Guardia Civil hugging a wounded schoolgirl touched the world and was even nominated for the Pulitzer Prize.

With this operation we scored our first major propaganda coup against the terrorists. We need to keep up with these actions to further erode the enemy's support among the local populace.
strings.IBR_antisep_radios_tt: We will spread propaganda and false claims through affected regions, lowering the support of separatists for a short period of time.
strings.IBR_antisep_snafu_desc:
Everything will be alright in Iberia. Our workers toil away in their offices and factories, safe and assured in the knowledge that the state is there to protect them from the terrorists. Their sons and daughters sit happily at their school desks, the guards outside the school gates there to keep them safe. The viejitos enjoy the warm weather, sitting placidly about park benches watching the birds sing, and no longer think about Barcelona. And above them all, perched on every lamppost, the roaming eyes of the AAS watch them, ready to call upon the gentle hand of the Guardia Civil at the first sign of trouble.

The events in Barcelona have put fear into the hearts of many Iberians. But it is time to move on from worrying about the phantom of terrorism. Iberia is safe and secure, locked tightly and lovingly in the hands of our adored Caudillos.
strings.IBR_antisep_snafu_tt: We have done all that we can for now. Council members are beginning to draft domestic reforms to improve life in Iberia.
strings.IBR_death_of_salazar_desc:
António de Oliveira Salazar, Caudillo of Iberia, ruler of Portugal, economist and statesman, has died. His death signifies the ever-changing times Iberia finds itself in. It serves as a reminder of our own mortality that a figure such as Salazar must also answer to the call of death. He will be remembered as a brave man, who staved off the Communist threat and who helped guide Iberia down some troubling times. He may never be forgotten.

After his passing, we've got to make sure Salazar's death doesn't cause any undue instability. If his passing ends up causing harm here in the living, his memory will surely be sullied. There shall be a parade in his honor, and then finally we will ensure this all goes ahead as a smooth transition. The Caudillo must be given his due, and that begins with a worthy funeral.
strings.IBR_worthy_successor_desc:
It is only fair, right and proper that the highest being in Iberian political society be given the important responsibility of choosing a new successor. And how thankful are we that this being is none other than General Franco himself. The Portuguese people shall be ever so grateful that a man such as Franco is picking their new representative.

There may be a few concerns that Spain's own Caudillo Franco is to pick the successor rather than some shambled together committee of various bureaucrats from Portugal, but there shouldn't be any reason to fear. This is a union of equals and Franco knows this all too well. He has Portugal's best interest at heart, much more so than any pencil pusher. Rest assured, a worthy successor shall be chosen.
strings.IBR_choose_caetano_desc: One candidate for the new Caudillo is one, Marcelo Caetano. A career politician who has long since held various forms of power under Salazar, he is seen by Iberian political society as a mild reformer. This may raise a few eyebrows amongst some hardliners, after all a reformer's a reformer, but this has been offset by his service to Iberia. He appears to truly believe in Iberia and wishes for nothing more than its longevity and success. We will likely know what to expect of him in this respect and may be able to outflank him if need be. He seems to be a safe choice, first and foremost. Or at least that's how he appears for the moment. It will always be important for us to remain vigilant in today's times.
strings.IBR_influence_tt_salazar_1: Choosing the moderate Caetano will increase the Council's influence..
strings.IBR_reformist_tt_salazar_1: Choosing the moderate Caetano will strengthen reformism in the Council.
strings.IBR_go_with_da_motta_desc: An option available to us is the man known as António da Motta Veiga. Like Caetano he is a highly educated career politician who has also served his time under Salazar. Unlike Caetano though he is much more ruthless in his endeavors. He would certainly be an effective force, but if we ever found ourselves needing to outflank him then we could face some difficulty. He may also have greater ambitions than that of Caetano, but reform is simply not in his playbook. His reputation amongst Iberian political society is mixed, but he may be just what we need at this crucial moment.
strings.IBR_influence_tt_salazar_2: Choosing the conservative da Motta Veiga will decrease the Council's influence.
strings.IBR_reformist_tt_salazar_2: Choosing the conservative da Motta Veiga will weaken reformism in the Council.
strings.IBR_out_with_old_desc: “So that's it, goodbye and good luck?” The soon to be former yes-men of Salazar will say to Franco as he announces their timely replacement. “I don't recall saying good luck.” Franco will reply with a ruthless callousness. Salazar's time is over, and thus so is the time of his lackeys. Great changes are beginning to occur here in Iberia, and these new times we find ourselves in do not need useless careerists such as these flunkeys. Franco has a grasp on a great political broom with which he is sweeping up any incompetence from the old stooges of Salazar. The next phase of the political process does not need these men nor does it particularly want them. We're sure they'll get by just fine, after we replace them with men of a finer political standing.
strings.IBR_the_grand_inauguration_desc: A momentous day such as this requires a lot of preparation. It is the first time in the Iberian Union's history that we have had a transitional period from Caudillo to Caudillo. The people will need to be aware of the importance of this occasion, so a rather grand ceremony is bound to take place. The public can expect to see all the regular displays of Iberian prowess, unveiled for the entire nation to bare witness to and hold dearly in their minds. It shan't be a day that is forgotten about for quite some time. An illustrious affair is deeply needed, even if it's just to hammer home the greatness of this landmark decision. It is sure to be quite the spectacle, which should hopefully settle the new Caudillo right in his place side by side with Franco.
strings.IBR_a_lone_caudillo_desc: The rest of them could never truly understand how vital this decision was. It is a necessary one, that is for certain, but not everyone is quite as enlightened as dear General Franco. He could not afford to, once again, put the fate of his glorious homeland in the hands of another man. To put it in the grasps of an outsider, an opportunist and an obstacle would be an act of treason. It would doom the nation to another age of bureaucratic infighting, stagnation and instability. No, he will go it alone. Just as he had done once before, Franco shall take the reigns as the singular head of state. It is truly for the best, yet for the time being he must keep his cards close to his chest. God knows what the hidden fifth column would be up to if he disclosed everything to everyone all of a sudden. Franco would bide his time but let there be no doubt of his intentions. He alone will rule Iberia, indivisible and eternal.
strings.IBR_cauinfo_lonecaudillo_tt: Salazar's popularity upon his death may influence the outcome of this decision.
strings.IBR_influence_tt_salazar_3: Franco's decision to become Iberia's sole Caudillo will greatly decrease the Council's influence.
strings.IBR_reformist_tt_salazar_3: Franco's decision to become Iberia's sole Caudillo will greatly weaken reformism in the Council.
strings.IBR_rouse_old_guard_desc: The old guard of Falangists, who were once cast aside as the Iberian project lifted off the ground, can now rejoice with the rising power of General Franco. They were once a disgruntled bunch but who could really blame them, as they were left to stew in irrelevancy with Salazar's cronies gaining prominence. Their disgruntlement made them desperate and dangerous which had led to some unfortunate incidents in the past. But this is now the present, and in this present Franco is ready to reassert himself and the Falange along with him. The frets, worries and anger of the old guard is to come to an end. In its place, will arise a rejuvenation of the fledgling movement. Franco will not forget what the old guard will do for him now in these key stages and he has no intention of letting them down.
strings.IBR_empower_the_loyal_desc: It is unfair to pen all of Portugal with Salazar's cronies and the various bureaucratic stooges that have somehow managed to hold office over there. Some in Portugal see how we do things in Spain with glowing enthusiasm. These officials look to Franco and his message wholeheartedly and are amongst the most loyal of the various officials in Iberia. They shall be rewarded for their loyalty with the empowerment of their offices. Promotions are in order and some reshuffles are certain. After all, it's only fair that hard work and great devotion is properly compensated.
strings.IBR_francoist_propaganda_desc:
The people need to be reminded of Franco's accomplishments if they are to accept him as their sole guiding principle Caudillo. They must be reminded of his great campaign that saved Spain from the ills of foreign communism. They must be reminded of him standing up the German threat, against all odds of the all-powerful Nazi war machine. It is intrinsic that all learn what Franco has done for them and how he has impacted their everyday life.

To do so, we shall give the important job to our greatest propagandists capable of spreading this message far and wide. Every man, woman and child is to be bombarded with appraisals of the Generalissimo, if they are to truly place their trust in him. And trust in Franco is trust in the nation, so this thought process will be an important task to accomplish for everyone. We're sure the vast majority of Iberians aren't traitors, and thus they will humour us in agreeing that Franco is representative of the nation. They needn't worry though, it'll become all too clear for everyone soon enough.
strings.IBR_francos_speech_desc: It's time to let the masses know what is truly occurring behind the scenes and what better way to do so than a glorious speech. Franco shall use his ever-broadening platform to disseminate his new plans for the Iberian political process. The reaction may at first be mixed and some may be confused, even angry, but we're sure tempers will reside once minds become clear. Franco is the best option for all of Iberia future and the masses will come to know of that son enough. We're sure a bit of persuasion from the charming Franco and our propaganda services will soon put the minds of the people at a calming ease. Anyway, it will soon become apparent to us all what the reactions will be as Franco's speech starts and officially makes history.
strings.IBR_caetano_first_day_desc: Caetano will soon begin his first day as Portugal's new Caudillo. It will more than likely be mostly a formal affair, greeting his new staff and winning hearts and minds, but it will be something Caetano will need to get used to. We're sure he'll excel in the role, and will get a good feel for what needs to be done in his new office. It's his first day so it's likely we won't be seeing any dramatic moves but an eye is still best kept on the new Caudillo. Vigilance is key in these difficult times and we can't rest easy for no-one these days. It's for the best though, that Caetano feels warm and welcome in his job. We'll make sure he becomes a fine Caudillo for Iberia.
strings.IBR_making_new_appointments_desc: Salazar's former yes men will likely be in for a surprise when they hear of Caetano's plans to rejuvenate his office with his own men. Caetano clearly has no need nor use for the bureaucratic vestiges of a dead man. Instead he looks to the future, his future more precisely with his own people. All will know that Caetano is not just some carbon copy replacement of Salazar. He is his own man, with his own ambitions. These ambitions will hopefully be delivered with this influx of new staff. Iberian political life will no doubt be impacted by these latest changes as the era of Salazar slowly fades from memory.
strings.IBR_tour_of_iberia_desc: A Caudillo should know his people. A new one especially, will need to grasp the people's needs and demands as he rules over them with great oversight. In order to satisfy this particular need of his new office, Caetano shall go on a grand tour of Iberia to meet the masses face to face. Some in Iberian political society have turned their noses up at the idea, seeing it as stinking of Caetano's alleged reformist mindset, but many more see it as a welcoming take on the role of Caudillo. It will certainly cause a bit of a stir and shall show off the Caudillo role for the public to gawk at, face to face. Hopefully, some form of rejuvenation through being in the public light shall come from all this preparation.
strings.IBR_for_the_good_of_the_union_desc: All can rest easy in the safe and sound knowledge that Caetano was almost certainly the right pick for the role of Caudillo. He has, thus far, graced the office with this professionalism and has reinvigorated it with a welcoming freshness. Kicking out Salazar's cronies, and the various other stooges and lackeys that made up the crux of the office, and going on a grand tour of Iberia has certainly put Caetano in our good books. The Union looks to be strong, sturdy and stable with Franco and Caetano ruling over the nation as dual Caudillos. It is a welcoming sight to see the maintaining of the Union's stability with this choice of Caudillo now seemingly entrenched. For the greater good of Iberia, Caetano will hopefully prove himself to be a more than capable Caudillo.
strings.IBR_for_the_good_of_the_union_tt: As the new Portuguese Caudillo, Marcelo Caetano must now work to expand his influence in the government as well as his faction's, known as the A Choupana Group.
strings.IBR_portugal_in_disarray_desc: For the moment, there is scarily little information coming from Portugal. What we are hearing though, is not good news. Rumours of fighting, riots and looting have been thrown around but we can confirm very little for the moment. What we are not hearing though, is any sort of calm and lack of disturbance. This can only mean that some form of trouble is starting to arise at an ever-quickening pace. This trouble seems to be spiralling out of control at an uncontrollable rate, and we can only hope to get a grasp on the reality of the situation soon. For something will have to be done sharpish, before whatever situation is arising comes to a head and it becomes too late to do anything about it. If we don't keep a handle on this soon, the consequences could be truly devastating for the whole of Iberia. Containment, it seems, will soon become key. For if these incidents are not contained, they threaten to swallow Iberia in destruction and terror.
strings.IBR_containing_protesters_desc:
The protestors are soon becoming a menace. They're spiralling out of control and will soon besiege the nation with their violent rhetoric. It's become apparent that containment is the message of the day and this will need to be implemented sharpish or we will face unforeseeable, but likely terrifying, consequences. Something must be done, that we can all agree on. The question though remains, how uncompromising shall our response be?

One side recommends we take a firm hand but not one that overdoes it. Control will be hopefully established, but our forces will not be allowed to run rampant in order to put down the insurrection by any means. In response, another side recommends going the whole 9 yards with our reaction and let the protestors know we mean business. No chances can be taken with this situation, we cannot afford to look weak in the face of a challenge such as this. Control of the situation must be established as soon as possible by any means before the protests gain enough momentum to become near unstoppable. It's a tough decision, and one that will definitely have consequences not just for Portugal but for all of Iberia.
strings.IBR_convincing_politicians_desc:
If we are to truly grasp the situation and take control of what is occurring over in Portugal, then we will have to deal with the local politicians, and even some of their supporters in national politics, who are currently adding fuel to the growing fire that threatens to swarm us all. They are partly responsible for the current crisis and thus, it is only right for us to hold them accountable. We will need to decide though, just how much we're going to hold them accountable for and how harsh we will be with our justice.

One option would be to send a message with our righteous justice that these actions will not be tolerated. It will certainly put off any other would be two-bit politician who thinks they can stand up to the Iberian Union's central government. Others though have expressed doubts as to whether this option will not have lasting ramifications that could create a deep-rooted atmosphere of future distrust and bitterness over our handling of these events. Instead, the situation could be resolved with a more forgiving hand in order to settle the situation. It may just calm the situation, but it could also be interpreted as a sign of clear weakness that the fifth column and other opportunists may pounce upon. Whatever decision is made, it will have to be done quickly in order to settle this ever-growing crisis.
strings.IBR_the_dust_settles_desc: Our efforts have been enforced and it can only be hoped that the unrest will now be quelled. We have certainly done our very best to quash this crisis and stop it from escalating out of control. What may be more troubling now though, is what the aftermath of all this shall be. The atmosphere, the very memory of what occurred here may have a lasting legacy we cannot hope to escape from. As people ponder what happened here and what could possibly occur again, it is our job to steer the nation through these tormenting times. If not, we will have to face something even bigger and much worse than the previous incident.
strings.IBR_out_with_salazar_yesmen_desc: Salazar's untimely departure has cleared the way to remove his bureaucratic lackeys. Under Franco's supervision, the current administration will be swept and reorganized, with Franco himself selecting more capable and compliant officials to replace those who will be relieved of their positions. According to Franco, Iberia is headed in a new direction, and these incompetent fools are not part of the bigger picture.
strings.IBR_legcouncil_unlock_vcon_tt: The Iberian Council is Strongly Conservative
strings.IBR_legcouncil_unlock_vref_tt: The Iberian Council is Strongly Reformist
strings.IBR_advcouncil_unlock_vlow_tt: The Iberian Council's influence is Very Low
strings.IBR_advcouncil_unlock_low_tt: The Iberian Council's influence is Low
strings.IBR_advcouncil_unlock_neutral_tt: The Iberian Council's influence is Medium
strings.IBR_advcouncil_unlock_high_tt: The Iberian Council's influence is High
strings.IBR_advcouncil_unlock_vhigh_tt: The Iberian Council's influence is Very High
strings.IBR_the_state_of_the_union_desc:
The Iberian Union is a nation inevitably held in contrast with the fascist nations of Europe, a point of fact that the Caudillos were more than happy to play into at times; Psychomania reigns supreme in Germania, as it does everywhere else touched by Nazi rule. Frightened mothers and despondent fathers looked upon Europe in tatters, until eventually the word spread: 'It's safe south of the Pyrenees.'

Then António Salazar met his end, and the security and stability of Iberia were cast into doubt.

Even with Caetano firmly in power in Lisbon, the foundations of the Union have proven far rockier than anyone thought. The new Caudillo might have ideas to address this, but he is a new player in an ever-shifting game. Iberia's future now hangs in the balance, we will see what happens next.
strings.IBR_the_state_of_the_union_tt: Iberia stands at a crossroads, one that will determine the fate of the Union as a whole.
strings.IBR_friendly_introductions_desc:
Anxiety abounds over the state of affairs in Iberia, perhaps resulting in a more immediate desire on the part of Spain and Portugal to strengthen relations between their leadership. Franco and his supporters represent an old order while Caetano's bloc leads a new one, but there are those in either camp that believe that both can be made to co-exsist.

Portugal's new Caudillo happens to be good friends with Laureano López Rodó, a high ranking member of Spain's Technocrats. A great number of Caetano's allies in A Choupana Group have similar ideals to men like Rodó among others, establishing a network of connections between either sect will reform a bedrock between the Spanish and Portuguese right. Reconsolidating the Iberian Union may take some time, but these efforts are certainly a decent place to start.
strings.IBR_first_dip_desc:
Caetano's first foray into greater Iberian politics will obviously prove the most vital, which is precisely why the new Caudillo has opted for the most surefire method of securing popular support, as well as proving himself a capable leader to the Iberian Council. Like many European rightists, Caetano intends to push forward some laws for minor improvements to social security. A well-tested, if somewhat unoriginal, form of populism that few are likely to argue against.

Although the Iberian Council is obligated to pass any law proposed by Portugal's leadership as a matter of course, the real test lies within the chambers of the Iberian Council themselves. Should the Council deem it necessary to water them down in any way, it will not speak well to the confidence they have in Caetano as Caudillo.
strings.IBR_caetano_hour_desc:
The heady and turbulent days where fascist rulers spoke to the people from balconies are rapidly becoming a thing of the past, soon to be replaced by more modern methods of popular demagoguery now that Caetano is in charge. The Caudillo intends to be among the first to properly use the medium of television to accomplish this, launching a new program titled 'Family Conversations' in an effort to properly ingratiate himself with the Iberian nation.

The program will utilize a teleprompter to aid the Caudillo in public speeches. This first in Iberian television production will to add to an already growing list of achievements for the Portuguese dictator. Franco remains unconvinced of the program's effectiveness, yet the show's pleasant reception from viewers seems to be a step in the right direction!
strings.IBR_other_half_desc:
With the Iberian continent seemingly coming around to the new Caudillo, Caetano now turns his attention to the colonies where a new series of public speeches are scheduled. He will make sure to toe the line on any plans regarding Ibero-African development, keeping whatever promises to this end comfortably vague. The real reason for this venture is far more realpolitik.

Caetano intends to make clear Iberia's commitment to defending its African holdings, indirectly sending a message to the integrationists and especially the military to prepare them for increased activity in the region.
strings.IBR_graduation_cap_ministers_desc:
Caetano can be forgiven if one of his early proposals received blowback, even for one as proven and capable as he. The Caudillo proposed a small cabinet reshuffle to appoint a few Reformist ministers in second level positions, a minor affair to showcase his aptitude for administration.

The odorous headlines that read 'Graduation Cap Ministers' were not a particularly subtle mockery of Caetano's choice of appointments, with most articles taking umbrage with the young age of the new appointees as if they simply walked from university straight into Caetano's office. More fool them, as far as Caetano is concerned, for they have proven more than up to the task of managing the Portuguese side of the Union's day-to-day governance.
strings.IBR_hunting_with_general_desc:
Caudillo Franco has of course met Caudillo Caetano on previous occasions, but with his elevation to a position of co-equal power, it is critical that the relationship deepens. Caudillo Franco has, to that end, invited his new peer hunting in the countryside.

He hopes to confirm that Caetano is, despite previous overly-liberal statements to the contrary, committed to the idea, stability, and continuation of the Union as a political entity. If that can be so confirmed, a fruitful partnership is assured, regardless of whatever personal political differences may exist.
strings.IBR_hunting_with_general_tt: The time has come for Franco and Caetano to meet.
strings.IBR_call_of_spring_desc:
With the formal confirmation - and informal political consolidation - completed, Caudillo Caetano has decided to formally propose his central policy initiative for the immediate future - the solidification and combination of the Union's Fundamental Laws into a true unitary Constitution, and in so doing simplify and improve the organs of state.

Caudillo Franco has agreed with his proposal, assuming that Caetano's often too-liberal language be toned down, and the proposal has therefore been forwarded to the Council. It should move through the process quickly - the Caudillos demand it.
strings.IBR_the_unexpected_turn_desc:
It would appear that the issues plaguing the Iberian Union's interior were more pronounced than first thought, a stark reality that has revealed more of the internal dysfunction in government than anyone in power wanted to see; Franco and Caetano are united in rage at the Council's rejection of the new constitution, the first major rejection of the Spanish/Portuguese establishment since the Spanish Civil War.

The Council has been working to provide another means to create a new constitution, but the damage is already done; Clearly the Iberian Council represents a less compliant bureaucracy than the Caudillos are willing to tolerate, enough that both man are embarking on their own missions to see its influence curtailed.
strings.IBR_democracy_unlock_tt: Reformism in the Council is 40/100 or above
strings.IBR_teamwork_always_works_desc:
It is not unsurprising that an inner-government resistance to the Caudillos' rule has developed overtime, for the deeply veiled and closed-door nature of the Iberian Council means there was very little inter-council dialogue on the assumption that loyalty to Madrid and Lisbon was assured.

Allowing the creation of Parliamentary Groups with the Council will do the heavy lifting on enticing fence-sitters to align with the reformists, while also providing an echo chamber for the far right within the Council to keep the belligerents on the defensive while we work on ousting them.
strings.IBR_power_of_red_tape_desc: The best way to fight fire is fire, which is precisely how the Council will target the resistance of the Caudillos from within. Occam's Razor suggests that time has been allowed for Franco and Caetano's influence to become bloated, enough for them to get ideas beyond their standing of who Iberia 'belongs to'. By reorganizing council committees and placing pro-reform people in charge, any defiance from the Caudillos' Yes-Men will be rendered dead-on-arrival as their initiatives wither on the vines of committee bureaucracy.
strings.IBR_pink_pointes_desc:
Sensitive information regarding the leadership in Portugal, enough that may well rock the establishment of the Estado Novo, has suddenly wormed its way back into the public eye.

The Ballet Rose, an infamous name for a series of sex scandals that rocked Lisbon in the early 60s, has resurfaced again. Once upon a time, Salazar was able to hush things up pretty quickly at the time. Now Caetano's regime has been implicated in involvement with prostitution rings, sex trafficking, and a lot worse. With Lisbon in an uproar, Caetano's efforts to topple the Iberian Council will face delay as he is forced to run damage control and confront the fallout of the controversy.
strings.IBR_pink_pointes_tt: This move will have grave consequences for the Portuguese side of Union, but it will buy us much-needed time.
strings.IBR_smile_hold_fort_desc:
With the dual regimes of the Caudillos increasingly becoming embroiled in multiplicative scandals, efforts to upend the gridlock in the Iberian Council will fall upon a select few; the reformist councilors are to become the lifeline for their plot to gain control over Iberian affairs.

With some assistance from more veteran politicians, the reformers will take up the lion's share of air time through public speeches and appearances to spread the word of their mission, emphasizing their achievements to win over the public's trust.
strings.IBR_family_matters_desc:
Caetano will not be the only Caudillo facing turmoil from public backlash, for the family of Francisco Franco are source of entirely separate series of scandals. A number of third party entities have secretly audited the holdings of Franco's brother and his allies among the Technocrats, revealing a long and deeply unflattering history of corruption directly tied to the administration in Madrid.

The Spanish capital is seething as Franco is forced to consider difficult questions regarding his brother and his private dealings, enough that Franco's own crusade against the Iberian Council will be set aside while he and his family are in the crosshairs.
strings.IBR_family_matters_tt: This move will have consequences for the Spanish side of the Union, but it may cause Franco to step aside in the chase.
strings.IBR_just_good_business_desc:
Since the unification of Spain and Portugal, the whole of the private sector of Iberia has been intrinsically beholden to the whims of the Vertical Union. Even though businesses already have the CNE as their representative organization, it has been powerless to deliver anything beyond reporting on big business' opinions on current events. Most of which, to no one's surprise, tend to revolve around their dissatisfaction with the Vertical Union.

Having Iberia's peseta-makers in our pocket is certainly never a bad thing, particularly if they are feeling under the gun. By brokering with the private sector to maintain workers' rights with promises of abolishing the Vertical Union and opening up the economy, we will secure a large swath of support for the Iberian Council in the campaign against the Caudillos.
strings.IBR_shield_and_sword_desc:
With the attempt by the Iberian Council to corral the Caudillos already underway, we can now turn to their allies within the Council itself. As many as there are who stand in antipathy to reform, there are high ranking officers on the Council who can be convinced otherwise.

Costa Gomes, Botelho Moniz, Spínola, Vega Rodríguez, Díez-Alegría. These are the men, among many others besides, who recognize the importance of ensuring that the Iberian Union endures. These men will have the political capital to specially manage the more conservative members of the Council, an effort for which they will be gladly compensated.
strings.IBR_third_wheelers_desc:
With the Iberian Council throwing up questions as to the current health of the dual-regime, it is vital for the populace to be reminded that there are plenty in the government that are as livid with the Caudillos as they are the Council. There remain many voices within the Judicial branches of Spain and Portugal that are happy to proclaim their support for the new reforms, enough for the press to run with it in painting our cause as the rightful one.

In the meantime, we shall take the opportunity to establish clandestine connections with the sympathetic lawyers and judges in the Iberian courts, bolstering their commitment to rule of law as one with our own.
strings.IBR_law_political_reforms_desc:
After months of working tirelessly to contain them, the Iberian Council has made their move. They have drafted the Law of Political Reform, a provision to give the Council greater power and the authority to call elections to a proper constituent council. The Caudillos and their allies have done all they can, now a vicious fight for the future of the Iberian Union is set to proceed.

What comes next may well prove transformative for Western Europe's political conduct in the Cold War, all of it hanging in the balance of who emerges victorious. The conservatives on the Council are defanged, but by no means defeated. Franco and Caetano are on the warpath, but their plan of attack has the potential to backfire. All the while, the committed Reformists on the Council are torn between aligning either side or striking out in the name of real, positive change.
strings.IBR_law_political_reforms_tt: As Iberia approaches a true representative system, the influence of different political factions within the regime is no longer a useful way of tracking the politics of the nation.
strings.IBR_road_is_clear_desc:
Administrative and legislative work on the proposed Constitution has begun. The needed subcommittees have been established and the Council is well-aware of the demands both of the state and of the Caudillos themselves. Now begins the core process - organizing and clarifying the Fundamental Laws in reasonable articles.

This will take time and care, but it will be completed, with only minor impositions from the agents of the Caudillos, who have been tasked with ensuring 'needed insertions' where applicable.
strings.IBR_setting_the_foundation_desc:
The most important aspect of the Fundamental Statute is its consolidation of all of the various Fundamental Laws into one cohesive document. For far too long the overlapping, contradictory, and confusing sets of Laws caused no end of trouble within the Union, and this will be decisively ended with the Statute's finalization.

The new supreme law of the country will be clear, it will be consistent, it will be supportive of the functions of government, and - when necessary - it will be applicable to the goals of the Caudillos, which cannot but be supportive of the Union.
strings.IBR_nothing_by_the_people_desc:
It is of course critical that the new Fundamental Statue be inspected by the public - after all, it will be encapsulating their rights and entitlements - and criticized where needed, so that improvements can be made. No such procedure could ever be overlooked if the Statue's legitimacy is to be ensured.

It is, however, similarly expected that virulent criticism will originate from opposing regionalist and separatist presses. The extensive work put in by the Council committees should limit most mainstream critiques to technical and bureaucratic matters, rather than any real concern with the substance of the articles.
strings.IBR_a_matter_of_semantics_desc:
A small roadblock has been encountered in the drafting process of the Constitution. Caudillo Franco has raised numerous concerns - emphatically - about the fundamental usage of the term 'Constitution.' It is far too easy, he says, for anti-Union elements to compare such a document to those in other states, and thereby call for autonomy or even independence.

Resolution of this has taken quite some time, and more than one very long all-night meeting, but an acceptable compromise has been reached. The consolidated document will, from here on, be referred to as the 'Fundamental Statue of the Union,' and encapsulate the special considerations of Iberia.
strings.IBR_new_decade_new_education_desc:
Any attempt at long-form state building must begin on an educational level, for from it flows everything else. To this end, Caetano has begun designs on a series of education reforms to expand existing schooling curriculums and increasing support for children already in attendance.

This may merely be a first draft, but it will provide a framework for more once the new Constitution is ratified.
strings.IBR_continental_reorganization_desc:
Although the process is largely a formality, the Iberian colonies are to be restructured and administered as 'overseas provinces'. While this is nominally a name change to distance contemporary Iberia from Spain and Portugal's imperial legacies, it will include a few minor reforms to reflect Iberian modernity.
