Chief among these initiatives will be making the Portuguese Colonial Act defunct via legal technicality, essentially absorbing the regional laws of the Portuguese colonial authority. Government officials in Madrid and Lisbon make this to be a larger affair than it actually is, but the means and methods themselves are perfunctory than anything else.
strings.IBR_the_peoples_choice_desc:
It is not exactly an unknown quantity that the new Constitution is little more than a figleaf to endorse anything and everything fronted by the Caudillos, as enabled by their proctors in the Iberian Council. In particular, the included clause for referendums as an act to be used at the government's discretion. Despite the grandiose wording, it too is just another pretense to rubber-stamping in a regime more or less built around it.

The Iberian system of rule might be a parade of yes-men under the thumb of the Caudillos, but it is still incumbent on such yes-men to entertain a facade of nuanced administration. The New Constitution will be ensured to be applauded by the Iberian regime as an extravagant affair, even if people know little of just how little it truly means.
strings.IBR_decorporitization_desc:
While not explicitly enshrined by the constitution, it is still of import that Iberia maintains a healthy relationship with the labor movements of Spain and Portugal. In a move that will surely win over support from the Old Guard, the new initiative will make inroads with the working class by cutting down on red tape for trade unions and loosen restrictions on running for union elections.

While the dual rule of the Caudillos and the Iberian Council remain at the top of Iberia's natural order, indulging in some labor populism never hurt anyone, no matter how much the Nazis grouse.
strings.IBR_organic_democrats_desc:
With Caetano's initial reforms railroaded through the Iberian Council, eyes now turn to the Modernist clique within it. In an attempt to remedy the aging institution, the Caudillos seek to use the Modernists as a stopgap measure on the government's behavior and reduce the seats of the Reformist factions across the aisle.

This will have the added benefit of heavily defanging the Reformists in the next election, to the convenient exclusion of - and benefit to - the Modernists who stand to make great gains come election day.
strings.IBR_evolution_in_continuity_desc:
The New Constitution is to be a triumph of Iberian statecraft, a monument to the ideals of progress and reform! The Caudillos Franco and Caetano will be heralded as true men of vision and egalitarian virtue, for whose legacy in providing the Iberian peoples a true bulwark of national polity shall endure the test of time!

The many lies man tells himself are as capricious as they are hilarious.

The Constitution will be submitted via referendum, a forgone conclusion in a rigged vote to ensure a great shift in the politics of Iberia not at all. It will prove an ample excuse to pop some champagne and ponder on the folly of those who actually buy into any of this tripe, what else is there to do on an election day?
strings.IBR_dont_get_into_politics_desc:
Let the geopolitical shell hole in Madrid, the one in where the Iberian Legislative Council used to be, serve as an example of just who the real power brokers in Hispania are; It was Franco and Salazar who built the Union, just as it was Franco and Caetano who maintained it. The Caudillos' rivals on the Council sought to carve out their own little fiefdom from below, now it falls to the Caudillos' to reconstitute the fractured interior of Iberia once more.

Franco and Caetano have jointly acted and suspended the Iberian Council, creating a vacuum in the Spanish/Portuguese legislature that will need filling. It will be quite the mess that the Caudillos will have to clean up here, but who are they if not the ideal men to get things up and running again?
strings.IBR_dont_get_into_politics_tt: One should never try to fool their betters.
strings.IBR_monochrome_cabinet_desc:
First measure of reconsolidating the interior will involve a major restructuring of the cabinet, so as to ensure any bleed-over from the Council belligerents does not infect anyone else. All Reformist ministers and senior members of government will be promptly removed, soon to be replaced by loyal bureaucrats to ensure a smooth transition in administrative affairs.

This is not exactly going to go unnoticed by the general population - it's not exactly a subtle move to make - but then again, this is assuming public opinion has any effect in matters of state.
strings.IBR_monochrome_cabinet_tt: The Government Cabinet will be changed to account for our new direction.
strings.IBR_forever_barred_desc:
The time has come, and action must be taken against the 'radical' members of the Council. So it will. Their names are known, and though there will not be any overt movements made against them, it will be made understood that they are not to be 'elected' to any further office or achieve advancement in any branch of government.

In doing so, their influence on state direction will be curbed, ensuring Caudillo Caetano's vision is pre-eminent. Though there will of course be a cost in curbing the usefulness of so many skilled young officials, it is a cost that must be paid.
strings.IBR_save_yourselves_desc:
The campaign against 'radical' members of the Council continues, and the focus is now to turn against those with more conservative associates - who have begun to suspect the fates that are rapidly approaching them. It will be communicated that should they testify against certain individuals, both they and their friends will be spared removal.

Of course, neither will ever be permitted to advance further, but they will maintain their lucrative positions, and it is likely that some will even see Caetano's light, and embrace the position of efficiency above all.
strings.IBR_warning_shot_desc:
The radicals must now be isolated from their external associates within Iberian business and legal circles, and so they shall be. Those so associated will be audited for corruption, which will of course be found, and suitable charges will be brought against them. Along with equally swift, and harsh, convictions.

This action will be well-publicized, and every person who matters will understand - these are not men to be friends with, to associate with, or to support politically in any fashion. Isolation will be guaranteed.
strings.IBR_caetanos_mistake_desc:
While character judgements can be harsh south of the Pyrenees, one should be reminded that Caetano's a new player in an ever shifting game. The Caudillo can be forgiven for his naivete in his dealings with the Iberian Council, if nothing else, it will be a learning experience for the young ruler. Franco himself is bound to reassure him on this as the two meet to debrief on the fate of the Council.

The meeting is not to punish Caetano for what happened per se, indeed, he is much too powerful to be so flatly condescended to. Rather, his position in the dual rule of the Union is to be reassessed to better protect him and Franco both, shifting Caetano's image to be that of a moderate (albeit not explicitly reformist) counterweight to Franco. Moreover, with the balance of power now back in the Caudillos' camp, Caetano will have an even easier time pushing his own agenda than before. God willing, this should smooth over relations between him and Franco for the duration.
strings.IBR_nothing_to_see_here_desc:
It is not the end, but it is the beginning of the end for the Council, and it is now time to sweep away the obstructionist measures that they have introduced over the years. With the radicals now isolated and unsupported, the Council itself can be suspended operationally, and the Caudillos can finally move towards its removal.

Of course, to calm the Iberian public the Caudillos will make a public statement regarding the Council's currently subversive nature - regardless of its origin - and thus frame its new state as a response borne of national security.
strings.IBR_a_new_old_law_desc:
It is finally time. Both the support and the legal structure now exist for the repeal of the Council Law, allowing the bloated and obstructionist organization to finally be disposed of. With its repeal, the Caudillos can finally assume the power they should have always maintained, and can exercise it for the betterment of Iberia.

To further ensure this, the Organic State Law itself will be amended simultaneously, codifying the powers that the Caudillos have exercised in practice through influence and maneuver into official law.
strings.IBR_the_state_of_the_union_ac_desc:
It cannot be denied that the death of Caudillo Salazar caused great unrest throughout the Union, exposing structural weaknesses that may need to be addressed - in good time. For now, however, we must work to support Caudillo Caetano in solidifying his position, and in ensuring that he returns stability to Iberia.

There are many who remain skeptical of his abilities and his influence, and much resistance to the few agenda items he has so far brought forward. These must be rectified - and they will be - in time and as the Caudillo grows more secure.
strings.IBR_friendly_introductions_ac_desc:
The state benefits greatly through the personal relationships of Caudillo Caetano. One of these in particular is Laureano López Rodó, a major figure within Iberia's technocratic circles. Many of the new functionaries who have entered the administration alongside the Caudillo share such technocratic sentiments.

As such, this friendship can benefit the state while also growing the Caudillo's influence. Introductions will be made and connections formed, and both Caetano and the Union will benefit.
strings.IBR_caetano_minute_desc:
Through both our actions and those of others in our government, the Iberian people are growing to increasingly accept Caudillo Caetano. Some of them, at least. Others are more hesitant, and state officials have explained that this is largely a problem of visibility.

This will be corrected. We will arrange a lengthy interview on television for the Caudillo, where his positions, perspectives, and personality can be shown to the people - so that they can properly support him.
strings.IBR_revamp_recycle_desc:
With the ascension of Caudillo Caetano, it is paramount that the members of the Council are as loyal to him as they were to his predecessor. For many this is the case, but unfortunately it is not for all, and this must be corrected, one way or the other.

We will work to support the Caudillo in his efforts to rectify the situation. Some council members will be replaced with known supporters, and the loyalty of others will be obtained either through reward or through more 'persuasive' methods.
strings.IBR_our_commitment_desc:
One would not have noticed it from the broadcasts shown across the Union that night, full of smiling crowds as they were, but the reception to Caudillo Caetano's speeches across the African colonies, numerous as they were, was not universally positive.

Popular opinion was, of course, positive. The Caudillo had been very clear as to the status of the colonies as Iberian territories. As Iberian possessions. That the settlers there were Iberians, and that the Union would pay whatever cost was needed - monetarily or militarily - to defend them. Any true Iberian would agree with this, and so they did. It was a strong response for the new Caudillo, and the influence that the settler lobby transferred could not be denied.

Those not counted among them, however, were much less positive. Nowhere in the broadcasts could be seen the sea of native faces set in stone, or the ranks of native administrators and officials rendered despondent at the lack of any mention of their own welfare. Or even any mention at all. Many of them had hoped that Caetano would bring some form of change, and they found themselves increasingly uneasy that no such change would be coming.

Primetime ratings were excellent, however.
strings.IBR_Merits_Not_Money_desc:
Astute observers, who noticed the cars lining the streets of the government office blocks that morning, and the figures loading boxes into them, were the first ones outside the government to realize what was happening.

The large-scale removals of staff meant the similar removal of high-level officials, and as the day progressed it became more clear. Caudillo Caetano, as part of his transition, had engineered the dismissal of a number of highly-placed and long-serving bureaucrats, replacing them with new ones. Officially, the new arrivals possessed skills that were highly in demand, and those departing were ones who had largely gotten their positions through favoritism and connections.

This was, of course, at least partially true. But those same observers who had first noticed the cars also quickly noticed that many of the new officials were those who had, at one point or another, worked directly with or for Caetano before his elevation to Caudillo. Though some argued that this would make the working relationship that much easier and more productive, others countered that it meant a shift in loyalty of many government departments to the new Caudillo.

On this point, few raised objections.
strings.IBR_hunting_with_general_ac_desc:
Caudillo Franco had once again escaped the annoyance of the city, taking pleasure in one of his favorite activities - hunting. Unfortunately, however, today was not all relaxation.

No, he had to gain the measure of Salazar's replacement, and so soon after the succession it would not have been possible for Caetano to refuse the invitation to spend the day with his co-executive. Caetano was, as far as Franco knew, very much not Salazar, and the first impression had not been good. A 'liberal in disguise,' the reports had said. He was not looking forward to the day, and if his fears were confirmed, there would be letters going out that evening.

Luckily, however, that was not needed. The hunting had been very good that day, indeed, but what was more Caetano had surprised him. Not in his ability to hunt, but in his words and tone. He had been adamant that he supported the core values of the union - and the fundamental conservatism that Franco himself considered critical. And all in a much less confrontational package than Salazar.

The day had ended well, and as far as Franco was concerned, if it meant that business could be completed without a regular shouting match? All the better.
strings.IBR_Special_Meeting_desc:
The efforts of the past days and weeks by various government organs to solidify Caudillo Caetano's position in the Iberian executive had gone well. There were few who would argue, whatever their opinion of the man, that he was not mostly secure in his authority. Others still noticed how quickly he was now moving to implement his various agendas.

Such as the 'suggestion' that had just been made by his office to call a special meeting of the Iberian Council. The agenda was vague, and the points upon it individually unremarkable, but taken together it was noticed by more careful observers that it amounted to a general evaluation of the Council's 'performance,' though the metric it was to be evaluated upon was unclear. Any examination of performance, however, necessarily meant suggestions as to improvements. Or, others feared, for reorganizations.

There had been whispers that the Caudillos thought the Council unneeded. Outdated. Threatening. That they were planning to abolish it. It was a worrying thought. It was true that the Council was not perfect, no organ was, but it had proven critical during the Crisis, and there were many who saw it as a necessary check, however effective one could claim it to be, on the power of the Caudillos. Those in the know waited with apprehension.
strings.IBR_cutting_dead_weight_desc:
The creation of the “Iberian Council” had good intentions at its root: a legislative body meant to guide and carry out the wishes of the Caudillos, providing input along the way with their invaluable insight.

The reality has been far from that - a waste of money, time and resources, it has done nothing except slow down the administrative process and, at times, even worked against the Caudillos' best wishes. Why keep this institution? We have learned from our mistakes. It is now time to correct them.
strings.IBR_supremacy_of_the_caudillos_desc:
It is clear to all that Iberia owes its stability - and continued existence - to the presence, skills, and governance of the Caudillos. It is they who rescued the Union from the weak and corrupt states that preceded it, and they who possess the foresight to lead it, now and forevermore.

This axiom must remain true, and we must take the steps needed to ensure that such is so. There are those, of course, who would say otherwise, and so we will act to remove them, whether in terms of influence, position, wealth, or otherwise.
strings.IBR_Tissues_Knives_desc:
While the Council itself is an obstacle, it is not necessarily true that all those upon it are opposed to the Caudillos. There are those sitting upon it who possess the correct loyalties to remain in positions of influence and authority. As well as those who do not.

We will preserve the former while divesting ourselves of the latter, and those who have proven themselves friends of the state will be permitted to move to other positions of importance. Suitable sinecures will be provided to the others - image is critical, after all.
strings.IBR_Not_Miscalculation_desc:
The formation of the Council was a major event, and so too is its dissolution. The public narrative must be controlled, and the idea that the Council itself was a mistake must be dismissed. This will be accomplished, and the Iberian press will assist in this.

The message is and will be clear: The Council was established in response to a critical need, and performed excellently in that capacity. However, the corrosive political environment around it, together with the passing of the emergency it addressed, resulted in the precisely correct time for dissolution.
strings.IBR_Dont_Get_Used_desc:
Dissolving the Council will necessarily entail the repeal of one of the Fundamental Laws, and the response has been more hysterical than was expected. Many press outlets are claiming that the government plans to repeal additional Laws, and this narrative must be ended.

It will be made clear that no other Fundamental Laws are to be touched at this time, and that one is only being repealed as a corollary to the Council's obsolescence. This is an initiative to improve the Union's governance, and the press must be made to understand this fact.
strings.IBR_peace_at_last_desc:
With the half-baked solution known as the Iberian Council gone and out the way, a new ray of clarity shines on the mechanisms of state. Without endless bickering and bureaucratic slog, our government can now work toward the goal it was always meant to achieve; the prosperity of the Iberian Union as determined by the divine hand of the Caudillos, guided by Christ and experience.

The poison of politics and the danger of indecisiveness has finally been swept away in favor of a new, more peaceful system that will work in the interests of the country, and not just politicians.
strings.IBR_National_Defence_Council_desc:
The defense of the state is paramount, and we must have a cohesive strategy among all military branches in order to ensure that such defense is prosecuted effectively. This will be ensured through the creation of a National Defense Council, bringing together the respective chiefs of staff of those services.

They will advise the Caudillos on matters of defense and security, and in so doing will both reduce the workload placed upon the Cabinet while also ensuring that those who make decisions regarding defense matters know something about them.
strings.IBR_New_Decade_New_Education_ac_desc:
It is essential that the education of the future generations are prioritized if Iberia is to be competitive in the years to come. Unfortunately, the current laws and structure surrounding the education system are woefully outdated - and this must be corrected.

We will take action to do so. We will draft a new framework that allows for the needed support of the system, and while it may not be completely sufficient as of yet, it will be a suitable first step. Once the Constitution is completed, we can then return, and complete our process.
strings.IBR_New_Decade_New_Sins_desc:
It is the absolute duty of the Iberian government to ensure stability throughout the Union - and that means taking decisive action against the elements that would undermine said unity. One such element is that of the various antisocials - homosexuals, drug traffickers, vagrants, and the like.

Their depravity and deviance will no longer be tolerated, and through the Law on Dangerousness and Social Rehabilitation they will be brought under control. It is the strength of our traditions that keeps the state safe - and they must be protected in turn.
strings.IBR_A_Special_Message_desc:
Attention, Iberians!

Your Caudillos speak, for the first time together as one nation. Many of the neighbouring powers have regarded our nation as insignificant or otherwise unworthy of recognition that other nations are given. This conception is misguided. In this ever-developing and changing world, Iberia can truly face God with a stern face and pronounce ourselves a bulwark of tradition proven to work.

In the coming decade and the decades that succeed, Fate will be cruel and have even nastier surprises for us. It would be foolish to proclaim victory and resign ourselves now, but to neglect any of our accomplishes would too be a mistake. Let us take a moment and recognise the sweat and toil that was expended to build this new united Iberian nation. Every day our economy grows, the military stands on guard, and a new generation of Iberians grows up and gets ready to bring forth a new set of achievements to the country.

Yes, dear Iberians, many challenges await us in the future, but we simply could not have reached as far as we have without your sacrifices. We thank you all...
strings.IBR_Improvements_Needed_desc:
Troublesome as it has been at times, it cannot be denied that the Council has been useful on occasion. The learned men upon it provided helpful advice to the Caudillos on more than one occasion, and certain crises have been better resolved than would have been the case otherwise.

It similarly cannot be denied that flaws do exist within its structures and procedures, however, and these will be corrected. The Council served, serves, and will serve Iberia and the Caudillos, in ever better form.
strings.IBR_Exclusive_List_desc: The Iberian Council is the highest legislative body in the Union, and with such power, there must be checks on its members. To ensure the quality, and more importantly the loyalty of the Councillors, we must set up a tight system of requirements. Appointments to the Council will be thoroughly vetted and held to the same standards that the Caudillos themselves are. Through this system, we can allow for the leadership of Iberia to be a group of skilled statesmen, and more importantly, figures with loyalty to the government, and to the Caudillos themselves.
strings.IBR_Rite_of_Entry_desc: To lessen the load of responsibilities on the two Caudillos, they have decided to extend the right of nomination of additions to the Council to fellow Councilors. While the nominees still have to go through the extensive vetting process established by the Caudillos, it allows for a greater degree of autonomy from the two main leaders of the country, or so it seems. But all nominees must be vetted and confirmed by the Caudillos, something that leaves the more reform minded members of the council disappointed.
strings.IBR_Nondisclosure_desc:
A perfect Council is a loyal, subservient Council.

The idea of Council members voicing dissent or making unapproved statements is utterly unacceptable. To ensure absolute perfection within the Council, the content of all meetings shall remain secret until the government grants approval for their release.This fair measure will erase internal discord and fortify unity and efficiency. The Council is supposed to show an image of unwavering consensus, approval and resolute leadership.

And after all, would any Council member wish to disappoint the people and the Union?
strings.IBR_Trapdoor_Clause_desc:
Within the endless halls and labirynths of governance that is the Council, swiftness and quick decision-making should stand as a priority for all procedures committed within it, that including the member removal process. Neglected for too long, henceforth, any Caudillo, minister, or the President of the Council should possess a unequivocal, straightforward right to initiate a petition for the expulsion of a member.

Once the petition is in motion, a simple majority of the cabinet is enough to promptly free a seat within the Council. This streamlined process will assist in purging the incompetency and unloyalty within the Council and ensure that the most steadfast and capable voices guide the Council.
strings.IBR_Council_Perfected_desc:
The Council finally stands ready for an era of uninterrupted perfection. With our recent reforms successfully sweeping the Council, it has been transformed into an institution of upmost loyalty to the government, swift decision-making and efficiency.

The days of the institution being a burden, only slowing the government down with its conflicts and incompetency are long gone. It can finally stand as a strong pillar suppoting the nation's prosperity, and will help drive the nation's progress, embodying the long-standing unity and strength necessary for a prosperous future.
strings.IBR_Change_Begins_Upstairs_desc:
Any man with even a drop of Iberian blood knows of the heavy hands and oppressive eyes that have been trained on us since the end of the Republic. While claiming to serve us, our Caudillos have failed to provide time and time again, all the while plundering the treasury for lavish vanity works. Trusting them or their lackeys to truly change is as foolish as pelting a thundercloud with rocks. We, the Reformists, will bring the country into the modern era and create a nation of truly free citizens. To do so, we must trek the first of one thousand steps.

Our opponents have just taken a fall, and we will not throw this golden opportunity away! We will shift the balance of bureaucratic power towards our faction. Ministers, judges, managers, and all others who worship our country's pitiful present will be dragged from the spotlight. In their place will come fresh faces with bright ideas like “democracy”, “freedom”, and “the rights of man”. It will be slow, but it's a start.
strings.IBR_Change_Begins_Upstairs_tt:
The Caudillos are long away from being defeated.
For democracy to take its first breath, we have a lot of work ahead.
strings.IBR_Sins_Of_The_Father_desc:
The illusion of our Caudillos as pure and competent men has been shattered. However, an unacceptable number of power-players in the government, business, legal circuits, and church retain their allegiance to the dictators and what they represent. Some of them are die-hards, and will remain a thorn in our side for the foreseeable future. Just as many, if not more, might be amenable to rethinking their loyalties.

Our members, allies, and contacts will start to chat with those who we suspect are pragmatic enough to face facts. Franco is old and nearing his deathbed. Tying themselves to his legacy will be assisted career suicide in the best case. We will subtly (and overtly) suggest that, if they move towards a reform-minded approach, they might still cling to their career. In doing so, we anticipate their new “change of heart” will inspire their followers to follow in step.
strings.IBR_Thank_You_Pilar_desc:
With the Caudillos and their support base on the backfoot, we turn our attention to the vehicles of their respective regimes, to the corrupt and vacuous institutions of the FET-JONS and UN. Fortunately for the Reformist cause that either party has been in decline since the early 60s, with popular interest slipping through the Caudillos' grasp like sand through their fingers. The time is upon us to begin depowering the two parties to seed their abolishment in the near future.

As much to send a clear message as for an earnest moral impetus, the Spanish Sección Femenina will be formally abolished to signal the trend of Iberia shift away from the nationalist right. As much as the Lady de Rivera may deserve far worse than being dismissed via a brief letter of thanks from the government, It is somehow fitting that the public face of the Falange and all their lofty ambitions should then be brought so low with the coup de grace of a rubber stamp.
strings.IBR_Political_Party_Registry_desc:
As the reorganization process continues, it is critical that the state maintain reasonable oversight over the entities that can be expected to represent the permitted expression of the people. As such, the Political Party Registry will be created - and registration made mandatory in order for any entity to operate legally.

In such fashion, managed democratic particulars can continue to expand in general, but the state will be granted the ability to prevent disruptive and destabilizing parties (of specific orientations) from conducting legal political operations.
strings.IBR_Political_Party_Registry_tt: With a legal avenue established, an avalanche of organizations are expected to begin registering as political parties.
strings.IBR_Reshuffle_the_Officers_desc:
Our movement continues to grow discreetly, just as we hoped. Yet, like a sprouting seed beneath a boulder, we find ourselves restrained. The armed forces have grown into a rat's nest clinging on to the ancient past. They fear being stripped of their near-limitless authority, and hate our dreams of democracy. Worse yet, they remain the only opponent to our legitimacy with the arms and men to stop us!

If we ever dare to dream of a democratic future for our nation, we must push out the reactionaries and elevate their conciliatory peers. Reformists such as ourselves would be ideal, but men simply content to do their job and stay out of politics will do just fine for our purposes. The older ex-soldiers will get very generous severance packages, while the younger ones will be given “special” promotions to perfunctory and powerless titles or shoved off to the colonies. This will cost us, but it's a price well worth it for a loyal soldiery.
strings.IBR_Censorship_What_For_desc:
As much as we desire for a freer Iberia, there is only so much we can do to force the issue within our system, such as with the matter of censorship in the Union. As much as the apparatus of Franco and Salazar's oppression of dissent is repugnant to us, enough influential conservatives in the regime would rather risk open mutiny rather than let the tools of the government's censorship slip from their control, something that can not occur if our reforms are to be successful.

As a gesture to the hardliners in our government, the regime's censorship apparatus is to be kept in place, but only after significant restructuring to see it defanged and enforced only in select cases. The organization in charge of government press and newspapers is to be similarly reformed, selling off large swaths of it to more liberal and reform minded private news outlets.
strings.IBR_First_Contact_desc:
In preparing for the new election, we have come upon a political masterstroke to secure our position against the opposition - we will formally establish open contact provided that they create a unitary body to serve as their official and formal representation. While this notion might have been considered heresy, the benefits are multi-faceted. By creating a formal body, the opposition will no longer be able to claim persecution and their unifying message will be countered.

The opposition is too large and too divergent to establish a unitary body, which means the opposition's hardliners and extreme fringes will refuse to join, fracturing them. Finally, our rule will appear more benevolent, continuing to gain legitimacy in the eyes of the people.
strings.IBR_Synchronize_Your_Watches_desc:
After much work on the part of nearly every major organ of state, we are now ready. Iberia will have a constitution in short order, following the elections that will permit the selection of a politically acceptable body with which to generate it. The Council is to be informed of this decision and, in order to ensure that the rate of progression continues at an acceptable pace, the date will be aggressively set.

One hundred days. The process begins now.
strings.IBR_Synchronize_Your_Watches_tt:
The Time has come. 100 days from now, the Iberian Union will have its first elections.
You can now check the polls for the election in the decisions tab.
strings.IBR_Correcting_Mistakes_desc: With our announcement of a timetable for our new constitution, we must look to secure the popular goodwill of the people. Our prisons are full of countless non-violent political prisoners, arrested for protesting the policies of the Caudillos or detained for petty offenses as a pretext for long-term incarceration. To show our commitment to bettering the country, we should approve a political amnesty program; freeing prisoners who have only been arrested for political offenses without a violent crime or major property damage component. This will breathe life into the Iberian reform movement, enrich the body politic with civically-minded individuals, while keeping the truly dangerous criminals behind bars where they belong.
strings.IBR_Police_Dial_desc: Political demonstrations are cropping up all over the country. Every major city sees multiple assemblies every day, and even minor villages see small crowds with signs gathered outside their courthouses and city halls. The police will be instructed to allow demonstrations to take place as long as they remain peaceful and controlled. The old headlines about police violence and pictures of protesters with bleeding skulls and broken bones will be a thing of the past, and our initiative will demonstrate that we are ready to enter a new age for Iberia. The opposition will no doubt feel emboldened by our softer stance on political assembly, but the benefit in showing our new humanitarian stance will be worth the opposition's extra vigor.
strings.IBR_A_Bridge_Not_A_Tightrope_desc:
The opposition speaks of a full rupture with the past, completely wiping out the previous structure of the government in order to start fresh and build a new country. They state that any association or relation to the old regime must be weeded out to prevent any regression and that any new government that stems from it will be irrevocably tainted.

This is complete nonsense, and a recipe for anarchy. We will not eliminate what came before in the hopes of growing something new from a fallow field, but rather reform Iberia from within, using the existing systems in place within Iberian law to establish new democratic safeguards and robust civil protections. In this way, we maintain legitimacy for our state and conduct ourselves with coherence and transparency, and ensuring that our democracy stands on strong foundations.
strings.IBR_The_Continent_in_the_Room_desc:
In truth, the public is largely apathetic to our African holdings, and that means that there is flexibility for our government to dictate a new colonial policy.

However, there is no need to rush with a poorly-considered policy; the apathy that the citizenry feels for the colonies is as much an argument for the status quo as it is for reform. We shall establish a committee of moderate native leaders to study the situation and make policy suggestions so that we may be ready with an effective solution to address the Africa issue. These leaders can turn into effective allies, secure our influence and access to resources, and perhaps trim the colonial budget to focus upon other concerns.
strings.IBR_Bring_Them_Home_desc:
As the Iberian Union moves away from the heavy-handed dual rule of the Caudillos, the need for sending Iberian soldiers to die in the colonies grows even more unappealing. While we have no intention of relinquishing our grip on Africa anytime soon, the native-staffed Africa Corps represent an example for sparing Europeans from dirtying their hands and cast the Reformists' colonial policy in a better light.

Couched in the language of 'devolution for posterity', usage of native Africans in colonial garrisons is to be expanded while Iberian soldiery is returned to Europe, the largest rotations of returning Iberians and African recruits reserved for Guiné and southern Morocco, where guerilla activity has spiked in recent years. As ever, colonialism is a numbers game and one must measure how to balance negative press from military casualties with the negative press from partisan terrorism.
strings.IBR_Rip_the_Bandaid_desc:
Reform is a certainty, and that distresses the military quite significantly. Many of the military fear what will come afterward and have become knee-jerk opponents to any form of reform whatsoever. A discontent military could potentially be a problem, and so we need to find a way to ensure that the military remembers their oath to Iberia as it transitions into its next new era.

Fortunately, the military has many anxieties from the old regime. Budgets were often wildly unpredictable and changed on whim, cronyism and corruption were rampant, and there was no unified Ministry of Defense that could manage the military's many myriad needs. We will call a meeting of the top brass, and there we will suggest a single defense ministry with consistent and secure funding and a reform of promotion examinations and cadet recruitment. With these reforms, we can ensure that the military will back our plans for reform and ensure that Iberia can remain strong and secure in the years to come.
strings.IBR_Still_Tough_Though_desc:
We are not a pro-terrorism government, we have made that abundantly clear in our arrests of terror leaders. Yet we know that torture and extrajudicial killings do not solve the problem - formal arrests and public trials do. When those who cause harm to others are brought into the light, the public turns away from them, and the fervor for their cause dries up.

However, this message has not permeated into our police departments. Several overzealous officers have mistaken our calls for reform as weakness and softness, there has even been rumors of blanket amnesty for all violent offenders.

Despite our denials, these lies have led anti-terror officers to act on their own accord, conducting their own raids against terror groups without approval or sanction. We need to get our people under control before they destroy what we hope to accomplish.
strings.IBR_Yes_In_My_Backyard_desc: In a bold and controversial move, we are allowing a congress of socialist parties to assemble within our borders—a rare concession to political pluralism unprecedented in the Iberian Union. These socialist factions have long lobbied for individual congresses to advance their causes, but we shall only grant permission for a single, all-encompassing assembly. This congress will be framed not as a platform for political maneuvering but as an academic symposium on theory and doctrine. By presenting it as a high-minded discussion rather than a political forum, it is hoped that we can give off the impression of genuine discourse while also mitigating potential dissent that can pose a direct threat to our authority.
strings.IBR_Red_Return_desc: Legalizing the Communist Party of Spain (PCE) and the Portuguese Communist Party (PCP) certainly represents an audacious leap into uncharted political territory. This move, intended to integrate these underground but still formidable parties into our electoral system, carries profound implications. We are opening the door to ideologies that once lay dormant in the shadows, allowing them to vie for a place in our newfound democratic process. However, such a bold gesture comes with substantial risks; if not meticulously managed, the potential for backlash and instability looms large. Our challenge is to implement this transition with strategic precision, ensuring that the inclusion of these parties strengthens rather than destabilizes our fragile reforms. The stakes are high, and the path forward must be navigated with both caution and resolve.
strings.IBR_ABC_of_Communism_desc:
While the restoration of democracy in Iberia has allowed the moderate left headed Carrillo and the PCE a chance to resurge, the agitation of the far left remains an issue, as embodied by Cunhal and the PCP. We can not risk backtracking on our promises of pluralism by illegalizing the Communist Party, not without risking throttling our renewed parliamentarianism in the crib.

With this in mind, a more tactful approach to discredit the PCP will be employed. Covert targeting of the PCP will stunt their growth as an organization while press outlets run articles and opinion pieces to make sure average people associate Communism with the Cunhal and his bloc and not the parliamentary socialists of Carrillo and the PCE.

As the old line goes: 'Which side are you on?'
strings.IBR_Freedom_to_Bicker_desc:
There is a grave and growing threat lurking in the halls of organized labor. The Comisiones Obreras, the CCOO, a trade union founded and administered by Communists, has been growing rapidly and is seeking to monopolize all labor activity under their rule by proposing what they call an “intersindical,” essentially unifying all of the trade unions into a single entity under their control. This would be a disaster of unfathomable proportions - every worker receiving propaganda from their union.

We must counter this by ensuring that other unions are stronger than the CCOO. We shall embark on a covert funding initiative of labor unions, both those with political leanings and those that focus more upon working conditions and collective bargaining, have better funding than the CCOO.

This way, these unions appear to be a more robust and attractive option for the average Iberian worker, and the CCOO will wither on the vine.
strings.IBR_The_True_Faithful_desc:
It's been known for decades that the Catholic Church in both Spain and Portugal have played major roles in backing up the Caudillos' regime in either nation. Yet for all the hardline conservatives or repulsive sycophants who turned a blind eye to Franco and Salazar, there were still good and decent human beings among the clergy, whose piety and benevolence remain untainted.

These men of the cloth have often faced punishment for refusing to dance to the Caudillos' tune, which can now be remedied now that the Reformists have come to power. By inviting the exiled Bishop António Ferreira Gomes of Porto to return, he can work with the Bishop Vicente Enrique y Tarancón of Toledo to encourage the church and its supporters to back the Reformist government. Measures to further separate church and state will still be enacted however, lest unfavorable comparisons to the Caudillos be invoked.
strings.IBR_Another_Tour_desc:
We're setting off on a new diplomatic tour of Latin America, echoing the high-profile journey the Caudillos undertook in the early '60s. This tour is more than just a ceremonial visit; it's a strategic opportunity to solidify our connections with democratic nations across the continent. Our goal is to rebuild and strengthen ties, particularly with Mexico, where our relationship has seen better days.

However, there's a more subtle layer to this move. While we publicly focus on fostering cooperation and goodwill, we'll also use this chance to discreetly engage with opposition figures and emerging leaders in these countries. This behind-the-scenes diplomacy aims to give us deeper insights into the political climate and position us favorably for future developments. It's a careful balancing act—enhancing our international partnerships while quietly preparing for the shifts ahead.
strings.IBR_Liberty_Other_House_desc:
The United States is the most powerful democratic nation in the world; it is not boasting, it is simply a fact. With our nation democratizing, it is only natural that we would pivot our foreign policy along with our methods of governance.

However, this must be done delicately. There is a great deal of concern that both the Iberian government and the Iberian people have with the OFN that need to be addressed. If we bring this up with the American diplomats, we can work to see what areas of common interest we have while we strive to maintain a palatable foreign policy for our citizens. At the same time, we must stress to the Pakt that we are not becoming a OFN bastion on the European continent.

We are an independent nation capable of pursuing our own foreign policy, but we are not looking to plunge the European continent into another war. Like Franco before us, we shall strive to keep Iberia out of any conflict between Germany and the United States.
strings.IBR_Popping_Up_Like_Mushrooms_desc: Granting our citizens greater freedoms in gatherings and organization has led to an explosion of new groups and movements—like mushrooms springing up after a rainstorm. The once-muted voices of women's rights advocates, youth activists, sexual minorities, students, and reformists are now clamoring for attention. Neighborhood improvement societies and prison reform campaigns are burgeoning. While this vibrant outpouring of civic engagement reflects a society on the cusp of transformation, it also presents a complex challenge. We must vigilantly monitor these developments, ensuring that radical elements do not seize this opportunity to undermine our hard-won progress.
strings.IBR_Hopeful_For_The_Future_desc:
“Therefore, this new era will seek, first and foremost, to create, a new Iberia that holds every citizen in equal regard. As Spain and Portugal united to form something greater than themselves, so too will Iberia recognize that together, we are so much greater than the sum of our parts.”

Overtly, the Council and the President are neutral on the election and are wishing to ensure solely that the election is conducting transparently and fairly. Covertly, however, the President supports our centrist coalition and wishes to conduct a limited campaign to boost our results in the next election cycle. The President will give a speech stressing equality and the need for a coalition that incorporates all of the various peoples of Iberia governed from the center of all.
strings.IBR_Coalition_Rollcall_desc:
We have fielded a wide variety of candidates, and many are widely known to the public, either through their experience in the Iberian government as a whole or in major provinces such as Barcelona, Lisbon, or Madrid. This benefits us well in the larger, urban provinces, but our appeal to smaller towns and rural areas is very limited.

We must begin a campaign immediately to showcase members of our coalition that come from these regions, so that these regions can believe that their concerns will be heard with our government, along with policy intellectuals who can explain exactly how our government will directly and positively benefit these areas.

Simultaneously, we should look to famous public figures who can drum up significant popular support through their fame alone, and seek out their endorsements to get the public excited and talking about our coalition.
strings.IBR_The_Butcher_Friends_desc:
Our principal rival in this upcoming election, the National Conservatives, have many prominent figures associated with the caudillos on their electoral lists, giving them broad recognition among the public.

However, many of these figures were associated with some of the more unsavory aspects of the previous era, having been a part of, having authorized, or having helped arrange massacres of political dissidents or those suspected of being a fifth columnist. The NatCon's have been trying to obscure these figures' involvement in order to win over moderate voters.

We must not allow them to hide such vital information to the public, and publish details about the truth of these candidates so that the voters can make a truly informed decision.
strings.IBR_election_play_cc_f: We will play as the Centro Democrático.
strings.IBR_Social_Christianity_desc:
One of the most persistent accusations against our coalition is that we are nothing but a bunch of godless atheists, just like the Communists who murdered priests and looted churches during the Civil War with a veneer of respectability and decency. It is not true, but the scars of that war linger on even now. We cannot allow this vile falsehood to take root and potentially cost us the election.

Therefore, we must press upon our Christian Democrat coalition partners to stress their Catholic roots, along with members of our coalition that belong to Catholic societies, to emphasize our commitment to our faith and our desire to maintain our Christian values in our government even as we press for reform.
strings.IBR_Bittersweet_Independents_desc:
One of the greatest weaknesses of our coalition is that the political parties that make it up are very new, and as such they don't have many members. This has led to a wide electoral list with some parties fielding only a handful of candidates. While this has helped attract niche votes, this has made our roster quite shallow.

Independent candidates have potential to fill out the ranks of our roster, potentially giving us a more robust list to offer the Council and the voters. Some members of our coalition support this idea, as it burnishes our centrist image and shows that we're willing to listen to a variety of different ideas to best govern Iberia. Others oppose the idea, stating that bringing in independents will dilute our core reformist message. The time has come to settle the matter.
strings.IBR_Our_Better_Half_desc:
Women fought hard for their right to vote in the Second Republic, and while they could not vote for decades after they had earned it, they have retained the ability to vote. Now, the women of Iberia have reached another milestone. For the first time, women will be permitted to hold public office, to much fanfare and press coverage.

We should capitalize on this new trend by showcasing the women who have decided to stand under our coalition banner. We should showcase that these women are not only newsworthy, but capable of leading Iberia in their own right.

Some are lifelong bureaucrats, capable of working within the structures of government to achieve political goals. Others are fearless self-made businesswomen, capable of navigating the business world and earning a livelihood for themselves and their families.

These candidates can appeal to men and women across the country, and will demonstrate our commitment to advancing women's concerns in the next Iberian government.
strings.IBR_The_Rose_Favorites_desc:
Several moderate social democrats from the opposition have sought to join our electoral lists, some expressing dissatisfaction with the opposition, others believing that the centrists have a better chance of leading the country to a prosperous future.

Whatever the reason, we have been presented with a golden opportunity to help strengthen our centrist credentials. They are capable of drawing votes from opposition marginal voters, as they make our coalition appear to be truly governing from the center.

We should immediately begin outreach using these candidates to speak in areas where the opposition holds slight advantages, in large industrial centers, in impoverished and neglected regions, to get the people to know that among all their choices, the centrists are the ones who are capable of creating a prosperous and free Iberia for each and every one of them.
strings.IBR_Proud_Of_Iberia_desc:
“Iberia, since its foundation, has been nothing short of a tremendous accomplishment. As we transition into a new era, we must never forget the successes of the past, and keep them close within ourselves, so that we might continue on the path and create a future we can all be proud of.”

As we look toward this new election, we must not forget the things that have made Iberia truly great. Manuel Fraga shall be front and center, ensuring that we do not forget our past as we look toward our future. By taking the best of Iberia's past and discarding the worst parts of it, we shall make ourselves a new, greater Iberia, that surpasses the sum of its parts.

Only one coalition, the National Conservatives, has the clarity of mind to take that from the past which makes us strong. Like a weaver, we shall take the best of the past and blend it with the ideas of the future to create something robust, that neither forgets its past nor is unable to adapt to the future.
strings.IBR_election_play_rc_f: We will play as the Alianza Popular.
strings.IBR_The_Vigor_Of_Youth_desc:
“You are an old movement led by old men.” That has been a constant refrain against our movement, that we are stuck in the past; the last generation without any sense of the present or the future. Our opposition will tell everyone that will listen that experience is meaningless and youth is energy.

The best defense is to place our young people front and center, ensuring that they are giving speeches and holding rallies, particularly in areas with high youth populations. Some of our young candidates have worked with the Youth Front, which has given them invaluable experience in policy writing, speech delivery, and holding campaign events, which will combine the vitality and energy of youth with the wisdom of experience, and put any accusations of outdated mentality to bed.
strings.IBR_Red_Danger_desc:
Spain remembers her injuries well. In the 1930s, the Communists and anarchists brutalized the people of Spain, from farmers being murdered because they refused to allow the Communists to strip their larders bare without compensation to priests murdered for their faith. That instinct lurks within every member of the left; they may cloak themselves in rhetoric, but there is a terrorist in every left-wing heart.

We must remind the people that the left brutalized Spain and her people when they broke bread with the Communists. We must state firmly and with conviction that these were the people that terrorized Spain thirty years ago, and should they come to power, we would see the same results. Only we can protect Spain from those who would see her suffer.
strings.IBR_Hide_the_Boogeymen_desc:
Victory in this next election is paramount, and our decisions should not be made as if we believed that our victory was assured. Membership within our coalition cannot be afforded to those whose views would serve to draw negative attention and turn voters away from us at the ballot box.

We must let them know, through backchannels, that they may indeed have an influence on coalition structure and policy-writing, but they must remain in the smoke-filled backrooms rather than front and center - even if that is not what they would prefer.

We can cajole them with positions if they cooperate, but if necessary, we must stand firm and be willing to blacklist them from policy positions if they refuse to cooperate with us.

Victory is paramount, and we must not hesitate to act like it.
strings.IBR_The_Moneybag_Goons_desc:
The center coalition represents a significant electoral threat, they are capable of pulling in a wide number of votes and have appeal across a variety of different demographics. Their relatively moderate positions also appeal to moderates and uncommitted voters, which prevents us from attacking on wedge issues.

However, their pro-market reforms offer us an opportunity by accusing them of being in the pockets of big business. We should run radio spots and give speeches talking of the danger of the centrists eroding workers' protections and labor rights for their corporate paymasters.

While there is some danger of treading too close to the old Falangist attack model by being too anti-capitalist, we can undermine that problem by keeping the focus on labor rights and protecting the livelihood of factory workers and other honest Iberians hoping to protect themselves from predatory corporations and foreign firms.
strings.IBR_A_Feminine_Touch_desc:
If there is one thing that has captivated audiences both domestically and worldwide, it's that so many female candidates are running in the Spanish elections. Our opposition says, quite vocally, that our coalition is anti-woman and sees them as second-class citizens. Our own female candidates handily rebut that assertion, but simply denying that claim will not win us an election.

We must go on the attack, give our female candidates the room to declare how proud they are that they can sit in the seats of power for the nation, and also care for their children. That they can keep a home and also keep a political office.

Not only will this defang our opposition, but it will inspire women across the country, housewives and mothers, to cast their votes for women who embody the strength that they live everyday.
strings.IBR_Our_Law_Our_Order_desc:
Other coalitions may pretend to believe in law and order, but when their people cause disorder, the platitudes dry up. We are the only people that truly stand for the sound health of our nation and defend those who have sworn to protect it.

We must launch an aggressive campaign, together with our allies in the police, and let the people know that when we are in power, we will protect them from everything from the heights of terrorism to the lowliest petty theft. There is no compromise with those who have decided that innocents are simply targets and tools to be used to demand political change.

We are the only coalition that stands firmly with the police and against terror, no matter its message, no matter its form. Once we highlight the hypocrisy of our opponents, we can count on the vote of the Iberian citizen who desires nothing more than security for their family, their home, and their livelihood.
strings.IBR_our_place_on_the_world_stage: Our Place on the World Stage
strings.IBR_our_place_on_the_world_stage_desc: We are now ready to return to the world stage after having been absent from it for so long. The paths we took prior to the establishment of Iberia and the ones since uniting may have been difficult, but we are finally ready to look to the world once again. There are multiple options for us to take, depending on the status of our nation and those around us. Across the Atlantic lay the Americans, a reasonable group. To the north, perhaps there is a like minded person in Berlin. And in the Mediterranean, maybe we could meet with our old friends once again.
strings.IBR_side_with_ofn_desc: Europe is full of deceit and betrayal. An enemy in Berlin, liars in Rome and Istanbul. We cannot trust anyone around here to work with us, to potentially have our back. Across the Atlantic however, in Washington, perhaps there is somebody who we can trust, or at least work with. The OFN is our best option here, and our position in Europe provides a strong bargaining chip, so we should open discussions with them immediately.
strings.IBR_mediterranean_reconciliation_desc: The Italians and the Turks were our only friends in this dangerous world. The Germans want complete control over the world, and the Americans are a threat to our national sovereignty, aligning with either of them would only add us as another member of their spheres, another piece for them to throw at the other. While the Triumvirate was around, we had actual influence in the world, free from the orders of some larger nation. Maybe our old friends weren't as bad as we thought, perhaps we should start talking again, and see if we can get past our differences.
strings.IBR_under_the_shadow_of_the_hegemon: Under the Shadow of the Hegemon
strings.IBR_under_the_shadow_of_the_hegemon_desc: The Germans have been a dangerous enemy. Seizing Portuguese Africa, strangling our former trade partners, and then leaving us to deal with it, the Germans have not treated us well. That said, perhaps the pain we went through was necessary. The sheer determination they gave us by doing this has led to greatness in carving out our destinies. Now we can marshall our resources properly. A stronger nation has been born from these trials, strong enough to deal with the Germans directly. It is time to send a diplomat to Berlin on our terms.
strings.IBR_above_the_world_desc:
We have learnt our lesson from the rather unequal “partnership” we had with the Germans and Italians in our past, and any man who lived through the Civil War and all the decades that followed could tell you what everything meant for Iberia behind the bombastic “friendship” parades and vibrant posters celebrating the “partnership”.

No longer will we allow ourselves to become dependent on any Great Powers or even Superpowers in the region. We are an empire in our own right and an economic power holding great leverage over European finance! Let us assert ourselves as a neutral power which pledges allegiance to Iberians and Iberians only.

Though total autarky and isolation would certainly score a nationalistic propaganda victory for us, we know better than to believe the most exaggerated parts of our own propaganda. Total isolation is clearly off the table, but even building our own economic sphere and strengthening ties with our neighbours - even the Great Powers around us, are not mutually exclusive. Perhaps it is even the only true way to cement ourselves as a neutral power - that is, through good and plentiful trade agreements coupled with a formidable economic force.

In the end, the choice is clear - Iberia will not bend backwards for any superpower, though we will not assert ourselves in a destructive, self-annihilating manner.
strings.IBR_above_the_world_tt: Opting for Neutrality will allow us to pursue increased trade with both Superpowers.
strings.IBR_neutral_diplomacy_bonus_tt: Thanks to our neutral foreign policy this investment decision will have additional benefits!
strings.IBR_visit_to_washington_desc: Considering our shared common heritage with the Americas and our current standing in Europe it has been decided to draw closer to the USA and its allies in the OFN. In order to do this we will have to show them our willingness to open new diplomatic channels and capacity to trust, therefore a number of senior civil servants for the foreign office will be sent as envoys to Washington.
strings.IBR_OFN_import_designs_tt: This will unlock decisions to import modern military designs.
strings.IBR_import_modern_designs_desc: The Iberian Military as it stands today is horribly outdated. Our old Verdeja tanks are jokes, our old Messerschmitt and Heinkel copies are jokes, our military is a joke... technologically speaking, at least. Unlike the OFN armies. Standing at the forefront of technological advancements, the United States is capable of quickly raising our military from the gutter into modernity, through imports of new equipment that we badly need: guns, missiles, aircraft, ships, tanks, and so much more. All we need now, is a lot of signed checks, and from then on, Iberia will be a lot more menacing to the eternal Hun.
strings.IBR_american_military_advisors_desc: Given the improvement in diplomatic relations between the OFN and our great Union, we are finally able to share knowledge to further advancements in all sorts of different matters of state. After all what are good friends who do not share? Despite our army being a force to be reckoned with, at least in the eyes of some, it can always use a keen, knowledgeable foreign eye to point out further areas of improvement since perfection is not a concept rooted in reality. The experience the Americans have had in recent conflicts could be a great help in modernising our army further. Whether we then follow their points of advice is another question entirely.
strings.IBR_OFN_military_advisors_tt: This will unlock decisions to reform the Iberian army using American advice.
strings.IBR_expand_atlantic_trading_desc: There are many benefits to having good relations between two state actors, or rather in our case between an alliance of states and our Union. One of these is an increase in trade, hence economic growth and specialization. With such opportunities now in short reach of our eager fingertips we must make sure that our infrastructure is capable of maintaining the transport and storage requirements of Atlantic trading. An upgrade is in order.
strings.IBR_invest_in_latin_america_desc: South America, once the combined jewel of Iberian imperial conquest and colonization, now firmly under the thumb of freedom, is a great target to invest into. As former colonial masters it is our duty to help these young nations thrive, despite our fraught past. It also would help to show the OFN that our intentions in approaching them are pure and for the good of both actors involved. In the future our investments may even return a good flow of dividends helping our economy in turn as well.
strings.IBR_OFN_invest_latin_america_tt: This will unlock decisions to invest in Latin America.
strings.IBR_deal_with_la_canadiense_desc: La Canadiense, now a Canadian state utilities company with offshore capital in our country, used to be in European hands before the great slump provoked by the German madness of the '50s. Were we to purchase this equipment and the sites we could further electrify the peninsula and deepen ties to the Canadian government. We should raise the issue with the Canadians at the next summit.
strings.IBR_attract_industrial_investors_desc: The USA and its numerous allies may have suffered financially tremendously 30 years ago causing long term structural damage to their tottering economy, yet they did not have to follow German whims into certain ruin during the last decade like we did. Rather they were able to use the peaceful years to build up an industrial base we could only enviously admire from afar. With us drawing closer to the OFN this may change however. We can use our improved relations to try advertise our economy to the investors of the Free World.
strings.IBR_OFN_attract_investors_tt: This will unlock decisions to attract investors from OFN countries.
strings.IBR_the_next_step_desc: While we aren't ready to commit to joining the OFN in the present, having some sort of formalized association with them should serve our needs in this vast world. Besides, if we get too close to them, then we'll get dragged with them should anything bad happen overseas. Therefore, it would be better for us to simply ask for an observer status in the OFN, not chaining us to them, while also not leaving us stranded without any prospect of foreign assistance should we need it.
strings.IBR_revive_regional_trading_desc:
The end of the Triumvirate alliance not only severely damaged political ties between the nations situated on the Mediterranean Sea, but also diminished regional trade ties. Initially it had been deemed that this would be a necessary sacrifice to endure as the ramifications of spying and unwanted foreign influence trumped the terrible financial and economic consequences in terms of national importance.

With time this view however became associated with those unwilling to accept that a healthy economy was a key building stone in securing national security. With the northern Hegemon regaining its vitality we cannot allow the southern nations to again just become simple chess pieces in a game outside of their control. Iberia must reopen trade with other Mediterranean nations again. No matter how great the betrayal had been, national security comes first.
strings.IBR_meet_with_italian_leadership_desc: The Italians were the leaders of the old Triumvirate no matter how you spin it. That being said, they weren't the worst of leaders. We'd have been left alone in Europe without them, and for that we are in their debt. Even then, they weren't the worst people in the world, and with some proper communication, we can mend our relations with them, surely.
strings.IBR_diplomacy_with_turkey_desc: The Turks are an interesting bunch, to say the least. Further away from us than the Italians, they too had to deal with the drying out of trade in the Mediterranean. While we are not sure if it is safe enough to send one of our leaders to Turkey to conduct diplomacy with them, we can't just ignore them. They were a crucial part of the Triumvirate and remain a strong player in the Mediterranean which we cannot ignore.
strings.IBR_share_military_designs_desc: We would all benefit from exchanging military designs with each other. We all have to fight in different conditions, so we have different equipment specialized for each situation. Outside of these situations however, we stand unprepared for our enemies. Iberia has had issues developing military equipment for a while now, and we would benefit from Italian and Turkish designs. This isn't to say that they are better than us by any means, but having more ideas would surely be of great value. And of course, they would be able to learn from us too.
strings.IBR_propose_free_movement_desc: We should request free movement between the nations of the ex-Triumvirate. The benefits that this would entail far outshine the negatives, such as allowing for easy access trade across borders, and as such reducing any tariffs that may have been imposed on each other's goods. Likewise, this would reduce border tension by allowing people to travel wherever they want within the Triumvirate, something that Italy and Turkey are likely to receive well.
strings.IBR_indulge_the_fuhrer_desc: There sits one man in Germany that controls all, Führer {ger_getleader} himself. While one man holding the world in the palm of his hand is a terrible picture, the truth of it may allow for a weakness that would not work with a group of people. The Führer is one man, and as such, he is subject to some sense of logic and reason. With this in mind, we can approach him with an agreement that would be illogical to reject, relations with our nation.
strings.IBR_formally_end_the_embargo_desc:
With the establishment of German hegemony over Europe, retrenchment onto our peninsula was a natural choice. One that safeguarded our sovereignty at the cost of economic ties. Previous attempts at opening proved singularly ill-timed, with our own diplomacy in disarray and a German political catastrophe shortly after. But now, with our head held high on the world stage and warming relations with Germania, we can tear down old barriers and reassert ourselves as a fundamentally European Union.

And what bigger barrier exists than the Pyrenees? Roadways that circumvent the mountains via Irun and La Junquera will be improved. And more explosively, we will reach out to French authorities to begin the decades-long process of building a joint high-speed railway tunnel directly through the peaks. The tunnelling will not begin today, but the diplomatic benefits will.“
strings.IBR_invest_in_the_east_desc:
The German sphere continues to reach far even after the terrible economic collapse of the 50s and recent devastating civil war. Stretching from the Atlantic to the Urals it however does not present a uniform picture. The east in particular is still economically underdeveloped due to seemingly failed Germanization efforts and rampant banditry.

As relations between our state and the northern hegemon continue to thaw we should ensure that our efforts in the diplomatic field are not mere gestures but active attempts to show our good will. In this it has been decided that using our reserve funds we should begin to invest in the east of the German realm. This could not only ensure that we continue to foster better relations but also yield great dividends once the eastern economic situation has improved.
strings.IBR_pakt_investments_tt: This will unlock decisions to invest in Eastern Europe.
strings.IBR_secure_the_border_desc:
We may be called many things on the international stage, but never shall we be known as a nation not capable of drawing from the lessons of our own history. The National Socialist hegemon had trampled our national interests under their jackboots in order to play at being gods. In the process they had lain waste to important parts of our economy. We have not forgotten.

Despite both of our states now drawing closer again we must not allow there to be the possibility that our trust can be abused again. The Germans notoriously have a short temper and are viciously determined to seek out their goals no matter the cost. We must hence work on preparing for the unlikely yet still possible threat of invasion from the north. Industrial and military consultants have been called to give their expert opinions on necessary actions that have to be undertaken to secure our border and state.
strings.IBR_add_1_fort_tt:
Every Mainland Border Province:
  Add 1 Land Fort.
strings.IBR_add_2_fort_tt:
Every Mainland Border Province:
  Add 2 Land Forts.
strings.IBR_visit_to_germania_desc: In an effort to continue improving the diplomatic ties between our new northern partners and our state we should plan an official diplomatic visit to Germania. In this we could garner promises of future cooperation, importantly both economic and political. It also is a brilliant opportunity to show the international sphere the strong new friendship that our states are fostering. This may not ultimately raise our standing amongst many, but it would clearly define that we could not simply be trifled with.
strings.IBR_secret_service_cooperation_desc:
The Union practically since its inception has fostered a strong tradition of bettering the quality of our secret service through cooperation with our allies. Despite the many risks this entails it has given us many new technologies and important training methods which have ensured that our secret service is a considerable force to be reckoned with.

The German diplomatic overtures are providing the opportunity to again regain this tradition which was lost with the collapse of the Triumvirate. Despite ideological differences in attaining its status we recognise the effectiveness of the German intelligence system. We would be fools to not try to make the best use of the improved relations between our two states.
strings.IBR_invite_the_corporations_desc: There already have been a great number of benefits that have come with the realignment to the German sphere. One such, which is of great importance to Iberia, is the economic support and cooperation that inevitably follows the fostering of better relations. We should strive to encourage the Reich's private and state corporations to invest in the peninsula with the argument that we could provide a greatly profitable market. Ultimately this can only help our economy as it will encourage local businesses to compete whilst also providing employment and profit. In the long run we can use the cooperation to build a strong infrastructure for Iberian business modelled on the large German conglomerates.
strings.IBR_invite_corporations_tt: This will unlock decisions to invite German Corporations.
strings.IBR_not_foes_desc: Iberian relationship with the German Reich used to be very cold and nebulous, but we have to remember that despite our strained relations, the Reich is not our enemy, they were the first one to extend their hand to us when we rose against Marxism in 1936, without the support of the Luftwaffe our Great Crusade would have been crushed while we were still in Africa, and the whole Peninsula would have fallen under the Red Menace, they also provided the much needed investments for the start of our industrialization process. Germans are not the enemy of Iberia, and even with all of our disagreements we should strive to keep a healthy relationship with them.
strings.IBR_portugal_ports_spain_tt: Portugal will lease ports to Spain
strings.IBR_spain_ports_portugal_tt: Spain will lease ports to Portugal
strings.IBR_help_both_companies_tt: Companies from both countries will be helped
strings.IBR_divorce_decision_tt:
Iberia is in a dire situation, so it may time to finally split the Union.

This can be done by £decision_icon_small Decision

Spain and Portugal have no content in this release of TNO!
strings.IBR_letting_go_desc:
Even after decades of effort and struggle, our work has proven fruitless. Every attempt to maintain our Union has failed, and finally we must acknowledge the simple reality: Iberia cannot survive. Both Caudillos have agreed, and the council is nearly united in its verdict.

The only question that remains in the council is how to implement the split in the least harmful way possible, for the long term benefit of Iberia and its people.
strings.IBR_letting_go_tt: We will begin the process that will separate the Union into its constituent parts: Spain and Portugal.
strings.IBR_sever_the_economies_desc:
Iberia has, by no means, ever been a unified nation. Even in its economic sectors, it has always been de-facto, and often by law, separated by internal divisions. In spite of this, a large number of businesses rely on labor from across the peninsula.

In order to rectify this and ensure the economic pains from the dissolution will be minimal, we must immediately establish a strict separation of each nation's economy.
strings.IBR_end_regional_tax_laws_desc: One of the major issues that have always plagued Iberia has been its conflicting regional laws and regulations, with few things representing this more than the regional tax systems. Thankfully, ending this issue will be relatively simple, as all that needs to be done is to return both nations to the pre-unification tax systems.
strings.IBR_wind_down_the_economies_desc: While it will no doubt be painful, it will be necessary to slow down the nation's economy in order to maintain economic stability post-dissolution. The economy of both nations will be brought as closely as possible to each other in order to prevent future issues.
strings.IBR_work_out_the_companies_issues_desc: During the Union's existence, companies from both Portugal and Spain operated across the border. When it was announced that dissolution would begin, companies from across the peninsula sounded the alarm over the potentially catastrophic effects that would result if they ended operations. The Caudillos are in full agreement, drastic action must be taken to prevent economic collapse.
strings.IBR_re_negotiate_port_leases_desc: Thanks to a surge in trade across the Atlantic, the western ports of both Spain and Portugal have grown in value rapidly this past decade. With the Union soon to end, we must decide whether the Atlantic ports will be leased or not.
strings.IBR_territorial_disputes_desc: Within Iberia itself, neither the Portuguese or Spanish have any major overlapping claims. However, in Africa and the Atlantic there are numerous colonies that as of now remain outside of either nations jurisdiction. In order to ensure cordial relations and effective colonial management, we must begin untangling the web of our overseas possessions.
strings.IBR_the_division_of_west_africa_desc: The first step to finally untangling our colonial territories is dividing West Africa.
