While the Kingdom of Morocco is undeniably Spanish, Mauritania remains disputed. If we are to evenly and justly solve the issue of West Africa, the Caudillos must come to agreement.
strings.IBR_split_equatorial_africa_desc: In the Equator there are several Iberian colonies, currently ruled by the federal government in madrid. In order to return Equatorial Africa to the pre-unification status quo, the Caudillos must strike a deal for the return of the colonies to their respective rulers
strings.IBR_transfer_the_islands_desc: In the Atlantic there are several island groups that are not considered colonies by our government: The Canaries, Azores, and Madeira. Previously split between Spain and Portugal, the return of these islands to their proper owners is a priority for the dissolution.
strings.IBR_the_fate_of_guinea_desc: The colonies of Guiné and Cabo Verde were Portuguese possessions long before the Union. As such it only makes sense that the Caudillos will reach a deal restoring them to Portuguese rule.
strings.IBR_disentangle_the_militaries_desc: While Iberia's armies have always been disunited and segregated along linguistic and regional lines, it will still be difficult to fully separate it into two portions. Yet this issue can not go unresolved, a solution will have to be found soon to remedy this.
strings.IBR_audit_the_stockpiles_desc: During our initial efforts to untangle the militaries, it has become apparent that the need to evenly distribute the existing stockpiles of our nation is critical. In order to accomplish this we must set about taking stock of our armaments and munitions, and distributing them accordingly.
strings.IBR_retrain_the_crews_desc: The soldiers of both Portugal and Spain must be retrained and forced to retire the old doctrines of the Union, allowing both armies to develop their own tactics from this point onwards.
strings.IBR_classified_information_desc: It's no secret that the secret archives of the military are vast indeed, and evenly giving them away will be no small task. However it is necessary that both nations receive the relevant archives.
strings.IBR_say_goodbye_to_our_friends_desc: In accordance with the upcoming separation, it is integral that both nations are garrisoned entirely by local troops. As such, Spanish military staff deployed throughout Portugal will return to Spain and vice versa.
strings.IBR_re_establish_embassies_desc: The embassies of both nations have long been dormant, serving as reminders of the past and Iberia's relevantly short existence. In order to serve the needs of the new governments, the embassies shall be reopened and put to use as soon as the word is given.
strings.IBR_dissolve_the_federal_government_desc: As part of the final phase of dissolution, we will formally dissolve the federal government, returning all power to the Spanish and Portuguese administrations.
strings.IBR_the_end_of_iberia_desc: In the final phase of the dissolution, both Caudillos have drafted and signed the dissolution law, permanently ending Iberia as a nation. From Lisbon to Barcelona, there are celebrations for the future, and thoughts of what could have been.
strings.IBR_leftlib_victory_desc: With the victory of our Unión Republicana party in the first congressional elections, the people of Iberia have stated their desire to see an end to the oppressive and backwards state of the nation imposed upon them by the Caudillos. We take this gesture of trust to heart, and will do our utmost to build a free, fair and just society for all Iberians regardless of nationhood, color or creed.
strings.IBR_stabilizing_the_country_desc: So much for the “police state” - unrest has gripped the country in the form of both terrorism and a general civil unrest for years on end. Now that democracy has been restored, the old guard are up in arms too, attempting to strangle freedom in its crib and restore the autocracy. At least the other major parties and their supporters have accepted the election results peacefully. Our first priorities must be to deploy the police (in a responsible manner), make clear our aims to the restless working class and make sure that the military doesn't get any funny ideas.
strings.IBR_the_matter_of_autonomous_communities: The Autonomous Communities - the administrative divisions of Iberia - haven't had anything resembling autonomy since the civil war. Franco and Salazar's obsession with centralisation led to any degree of self-governance they once enjoyed being stripped away in the name of “streamlining” the administration. The result, rather than a more efficient government, was a bloated and overworked bureaucracy that served as a breeding ground for corruption. Reversing the centralisation of our state is not only the right thing to do morally; it is also much more practical and will ease the burden on our administration.
strings.IBR_meet_with_the_regional_leaders_desc: Though popular unrest is the most visible kind in our nation, it rarely erupts spontaneously. There are a number of regional leaders who are usually responsible for the various protests, strikes and riots that crop up from time to time. Though they have always possessed a fair degree of plausible deniability, their names and involvement is an open secret these days. Given the current unrest, they clearly remain unconvinced by our campaign promises. The best course of action would be to meet each of them privately, so that we may clearly elucidate our plans and get them on-side.
strings.IBR_legalize_their_languages_desc: The banning of the Basque and Catalan languages was more than just an act of petty collective punishment on Franco's part. He sought to totally erase their distinct cultures after they dared to defy the Nationalists. Restoring the right of these people to speak their own language is no act of revolution, but merely a return to that most time-honored of Iberia's traditions: diversity. This injustice must be dealt with, now.
strings.IBR_new_statues_of_autonomy_desc: The old statutes of autonomy were shockingly easy for Franco to rescind. There was virtually no resistance from the government remnants of the time, likely out of spite for the perceived “failure” of the Basques and Catalans to halt the Nationalists. Though we cannot say for certain that there will never be division within Iberia again, we can take steps to soothe wounds both old and new. Not only will the statutes of autonomy be re-established, we will also enshrine them in the Fundamental Laws. Henceforth, regional autonomy will no longer be a matter up for debate.
strings.IBR_the_agrarian_unrest_desc: The peasantry and landowners were two of the few demographics not severely impacted by autarky, as the vast majority of their crop yields were purchased by the state itself or by food companies operating under state supervision, rather than being exported. The end of autarky has many of them worried about foreign competition, and some peasant communities have already downed tools in protest of our promises to make the agricultural sector more competitive. Unlike our compatriots in the PRD, however, we will be careful not to let the free market get out of hand. Reassurances must be doled out to inform the agrarian populace of our good intentions before we find ourselves facing widespread protest action and subsequent food shortages.
strings.IBR_meet_with_the_axencia_desc: The Axencia are quite rightly a force to be wary of. Their long record of successful prosecutions and tireless zeal in pursuing anyone deemed a threat to national security is both commendable and rather concerning. However, they are clearly professionals at heart, and rather less politicised than we initially feared. We think that's the case, anyway - they haven't arrested us for winning the election yet, at any rate. There may be some mutual misunderstandings that remain, so our new cabinet should meet with their leadership as soon as possible to smooth things over.
strings.IBR_find_what_were_looking_for_desc: When we set out to fulfil our promises of restoring regional autonomy, our critics demanded to know exactly what we hoped to accomplish by turning back the clock on centralisation. Many pointed out that regional unrest, most prominently in Catalonia, was a leading cause of the coup that triggered the civil war. We must admit that they were not entirely without fault - the party was, indeed, divided over what fulfilling our promises meant. Now, however, we believe we have found the answer that was demanded: a new vision of autonomy, where the constituent nations of Iberia act as faithful confederates with the assurance that their ancient rights will not be trampled upon by government overreach and paranoia.
strings.IBR_in_defense_of_democracy_desc: Iberian democracy is young and fragile. While the police and Axencia have so far proven themselves trustworthy, we cannot rely solely on them to protect the systems of government. Teething problems are to be expected, and rumours of election fraud have already reached us. Weeds in the garden are best ripped up before they can entwine their roots with their neighbours - the same approach must be applied to any miscreants and aspiring tyrants in our new administration.
strings.IBR_investigate_election_fraud_desc: Though it clearly failed to influence the election, there was undoubtedly a good deal of election fraud in vulnerable areas. In Catalonia, it was even reported that club-wielding Falangists attempted to scare away Catalan voters! Had it not been for the Guardia Civil, who knows how widespread such incidents might have been? Similarly, more than a few radical leftists were caught red-handed, their pockets stuffed with forged and filled out ballot papers! An internal investigation, headed by a reliable prosecutor and operating with the assistance of Axencia and the police, must be carried out post-haste.
strings.IBR_get_the_municipalities_on_board_desc: The municipal governments grew accustomed to taking things easy under the Caudillos. With so much authority centered in Madrid, there was little for them to do beyond run-of-the-mill paperwork. This laxity is no fault of theirs, but the era of smooth sailing is over. Their inexperience with democracy proved problematic when they were assigned the responsibility of managing polling stations. Councils and mayors must be roused to action and cooperate with our investigation, or else be replaced.
strings.IBR_investigate_the_causes_desc: The causes? Those are obvious enough to everyone. There are many anti-democratic groups in Iberia, both left- and right-wing, who loathe what we stand for and wish to see Iberian freedom destroyed. It would be folly to simply send out the police en masse to arrest everyone we think is responsible, however. Proper, thorough inquiries into each and every suspected group, individual and ideology must be carried out. Due process must win out over political convenience.
strings.IBR_protect_the_congress_desc: Securing safe and free elections is the most important item on the agenda right now, but we must also look to protecting Congress itself against direct action. Iberia has a long history of political violence. Prior to and during the civil war, leftists, fascists and the military killed one another with impunity, whittling away at the foundations of the Second Republic with every death. Nobody who votes should have to worry about going back to the polls a month later because a bloodthirsty ideologue mowed down their representative in a hail of gunfire. The Caudillos made the houses of government well-suited as fortresses - let's double down, and extend the role of the Guardia Civil to protecting the physical manifestation of government.
strings.IBR_extend_the_vote_desc: The surest way of making election fraud more difficult, short of arresting the perpetrators, is to drown out fraudulent votes. The first election had a good turnout, but the franchise was not as broad as it should have been. The voting age of 21 is far too high, and the fact that women had to qualify at all when most other major democracies have had universal suffrage for half a century is absurd. Additionally, there are many citizens convicted of petty offences who have been forbidden to vote for life. With our majority in Congress, drafting and signing into law the legislation required to address these injustices should be no problem at all.
strings.IBR_faith_in_the_people_desc: What greater expression of faith in one's people is there than to place power in their hands? The Iberian people might have chosen poorly, but they knew better - as we believed they did. They made clear that they did not wish for petty division and civil strife, but rather longed for peace and justice. For years, the Caudillos insisted that democracy could not work in Iberia for so long as the threat of radicalism persisted, but the people proved them wrong. The radicalism that was so feared amounted to little more than a few misguided souls screaming into the wind of change. The Iberians were tested, and were not found wanting. Democracy shall continue, and its principles shall never die so long as a free Iberia endures.
strings.IBR_ending_the_franquista_desc: Dismantling the old regime's extensive system of harsh laws, surveillance and brutal repression is not going to be an easy task. We can expect resistance from the old guard, Falangists and possibly even the conservatives of Alianza Popular. But it must be done. There have been too many families torn apart by baseless convictions; too many denied basic freedoms because they spoke out of turn; too many miniature Caudillos who grew drunk on the power they held over the people. Justice is due.
strings.IBR_legalize_the_opposition_desc: The idea unnerves even us a little, but the parties outlawed by the Caudillos must be allowed to operate in the political arena again. This includes the social democrats, socialists, Communists and even the anarchists (though they're not likely to care either way). There will be outrage and frothing at the mouth from the right, but we must stand up for our democratic principles. Anyone willing to participate in a democratic system and who swears not to subvert it will be welcome, so long as their party is not found guilty of any wrongdoing.
strings.IBR_audit_the_prisons_desc: The prisons have been full to bursting since the civil war. Countless political prisoners and citizens jailed for minor offences have simply been thrown in with the genuine criminals and left to rot. This state of affairs is unacceptable, especially given the horrifically high rates of assault, murder and suicide within prisons. Though the process will be long, painful and drawn-out, the only just solution is to go over conviction records, the judicial system and the prisons themselves with a fine-toothed comb. We must find the resolve to press forth until every wrong is righted.
strings.IBR_close_down_tarrafal_desc: The Tarrafal is the most infamous and brutal prison in the entire peninsula. Essentially a fortress built around a concentration camp for political prisoners, none who enter will ever leave - save for the guards and prison staff. This symbol of Francoist tyranny must be shut down immediately. Every single staff member will be thoroughly investigated and dealt with accordingly should they turn out to have been complicit in any criminal offence themselves, including mistreatment of prisoners. The inmates of the prison will be distributed among several smaller, more modern and humane prisons until reviews of their trials and supposed crimes are completed. The Tarrafal will be mothballed until we figure out what to do with it - perhaps it would make a nice museum or luxury hotel with a bit of work?
strings.IBR_we_can_be_better_desc: Merely undoing Francoism is not enough. We must replace it with something new and improved. Injustice must be replaced with its opposite number - just so for corruption, immorality and brutality. We do not wish to stick our noses in everyone's business like those obsessive moralists from the Alianza Popular, but there must be some direct intervention to stop the taint of authoritarianism finding root once again.
strings.IBR_an_objective_education_desc: These days, all school children are taught of the “glorious” and “brave” Caudillos who united Iberia, frightened off the Germans and destroyed the Marxists and liberals with their brave, faithful soldiers. Who knows how many burgeoning fascists these lies have created? This kind of despotic claptrap will no longer be permitted - from now on, our mandate on education will be that our recent history, from the early 20th century onwards, must be taught in the most objective manner possible. People must be permitted to form their own opinions instead of being indoctrinated for generations on end.
strings.IBR_investigate_military_corruption_desc: Considering its size, the military hasn't been up to much since the civil war. We know that their equipment and training could be better, yet no apparent improvements are ever made. So where, pray tell, does all that funding go? Why are so many of the wealthy bourgeoisie of our nation commissioned officers rather than bankers, businessmen, entrepreneurs and lawyers? Why is the private still paid a pittance while every second lieutenant has a house, a mistress and an Italian sports car? We must brave the lion's den and set about the military apparatus with the same rigour and decisiveness that we have applied to the bureaucracy and judicial system, lest this blatant corruption continue even in the face of renewed German aggression!
strings.IBR_find_who_we_can_trust_desc: There are enemies lurking all around us, but we are not completely surrounded. Through all the years of dictatorship, there were those who held on to the dream of a better Iberia. Even within Franco's inner circle there was always dissent, and now those dissenters turn to us for the realization of their dreams. It is not enough for there to be mutual trust between ourselves and the electorate - we must extend the hand of friendship to any who will take it in earnest. Iberia is not yet lost.
strings.IBR_the_beginning_of_our_ascent_desc: Like a gentle spring rain from on high, peace and justice now hold Iberia in their warm, soothing embrace. Wrongs have been righted, justice dispensed and grievances addressed. Where once the streets were quiet and ordered, the jackboots of the over-militarised police clicking on the cobblestones, they are now filled with life. Businesses, homes and churches alike have become places of hope and happiness. Even the halls of government peal with laughter at times, as a sense of optimism unrivalled in our nation's history sets in. Above all else, there is the sense that no matter what comes, Iberia and its people will find a way to endure. No fascist, terrorist or mad dictator will halt our ascent to heights yet undreamt of! For a free Iberia, and a better tomorrow!
strings.IBR_UR_oil_crisis_desc:
Yet again the Italian mismanagement of their colonial possessions in the Middle East has ended in disaster; only somehow titanically worse than any other blunder in their history. The revolution in Iran has sparked several other civil wars across the region that have seen some of the world's largest underground Oil reserves lost to hellish desert warfare. Every major nation's economy has been cut off and instability looms.

Iberia has not fared any better than any of her immediate European neighbors. Our chronically over bureaucratized economy has to untangle the mess of this global economic crisis. The nation must seize the initiative in limiting the damage and reforming the economy to ensure future system shocks are not repeated.
strings.IBR_nep_iberia_tt: We will approve a new economic plan to get Iberia out of this crisis.
strings.IBR_New_Economic_Program_desc:
Fernández-Miranda has decided that it is imperative that the government should implement what they dub the “New Economic Program” made especially to deal with the crisis. The reforms within the Program are focused on protecting the wellbeing of the people most heavily affected by the crisis through increased government spending, fairer taxation, and by tackling rising inflation.

If done right, Fernández-Miranda's New Economic Program could lead to Iberians being even better off than before. However, free market proponents have established vocal opposition to the program, decrying it as an intrusion on the market's ability to correct itself and as being too expensive.
strings.IBR_secure_minimum_wage_tt: The minimum wage will be secured, to keep a minimum of conditions for the workers
strings.IBR_Secure_Minimum_Wage_desc:
The first step as part of the New Economic Program, is to establish a minimum wage for all workers. The condition of workers have seen a dramatic fall since the Oil Crisis hit Iberia and after reports of pay cuts after pay cuts, the government has seen it fit to make sure that all working Iberians have the ability to provide not only for themselves, but for their families as well.

Business leaders have claimed that it'll make their costs too high to do business but this is a recession and we all have to make sacrifices.
strings.IBR_limit_oil_consumption_tt: A propaganda campaign will be released to motivate people to save oil through various means.
strings.IBR_Limit_Oil_Consumption_desc:
With wages secured, it is time to move on to the next stage of the program. A propaganda campaign will be launched to motivate the populace to do what they can in order to bring our consumption down to alleviate the pressures of the sudden loss of oil incurred by The Oil Crisis. By encouraging public transport, carpooling, and burning wood instead of gas, the hope is that these add up to reduce our dependence on oil.

Naturally, the oil companies tell us that this will only worsen the crisis by hurting their bottom lines but it was their incompetence that placed us in this situation in the first place so they will be disregarded.
strings.IBR_expanded_healthcare_tt: In this time of crisis, healthcare for our citizens must be secured and expanded.
strings.IBR_Expand_Healthcare_UR_desc: After the Oil Crisis reverberated into the economy, Iberians all over the nation saw a sudden and dramatic drop in quality of life. Our government cannot stand for that so the next action that needs to be taken is an expansion of our current healthcare facilities. This expansion will cover both the quantity and quality of the current healthcare system and will involve some minor nationalisation and joint public/private construction. Not only will this endear the people to our administration but will also allow people to get healthy quicker and get back to work quicker, therefore speeding up our economic recovery as well as our societal recovery.
strings.IBR_ps_subsidies_tt: Special subsidies will be granted for those public services that employ a certain number of people.
strings.IBR_Subsidies_Special_PS_desc:
Our healthcare scheme has seen popular support from the population which means we can press on with more government intervention confidently. The next step of our New Economic Program is to allocate special subsidies for public services that hire more than 1200 employees.

These subsidies need to be introduced in order to make sure that our public services do not collapse in on themselves and are forced to lay off too many people. We plan to trial this in the public sector first and if successful, we will eventually roll this out to the private sector as well.
strings.IBR_progressive_taxes_tt: “Those that earn more should contribute more than those who earn less.”
strings.IBR_Progressive_Tax_System_desc: While our policies in dealing with the crisis have been popular so far, there seems to be a growing sentiment that we don't have the funds to keep these policies long term. In order to combat this sentiment, we have proposed an overhaul of the tax code, replacing our current flat income tax system with a progressive one where higher incomes are taxed at a higher rate than lower incomes. While this will be popular amongst the lower income and the more left wing in our society, we can expect an uproar amongst the highest income bracket and free market proponents but it's a measure needed to weather the storm.
strings.IBR_tame_inflation_tt: We will try and control inflation.
strings.IBR_Tame_Inflation_desc: Inflation has been spiralling ever since the crisis hit and if we do not do something about it now, the worry is that it will spiral out of control. Luckily, we included policies to control inflation in the N.E.P and there is no better time to introduce them. We will raise interest rates to encourage saving and slow down the immense price rises. Additionally, we will implement temporary wage controls in order to keep both prices and wages down. This will be unpopular with the people who had supported our previous policies but at least it'll calm down the industrialists.
strings.IBR_New_Energy_Investments_desc:
We can not sit idle while the petrol stranglehold on Iberia's economy proceeds to choke the life out of it-never before has the premise of Autarky become more vital for the survival of the Union. Too much of Spain and Portugal's energy come from foreign imports, and improving on the self-sufficiency of the power grid must take priority.

The recent interest in renewable energy sources worldwide has caught the eye of the regime in Iberia for this reason, and the peninsula is a somewhat ideal testing ground for them. By investing into solar and wind power alongside further development of hydroelectric dams, we will secure the energy grid against future crises and improve Iberia's economic independence at the same time.
strings.IBR_energy_investments_tt: Investments in new energies will increase costs by $15 million and give 2 £tt_power grid power.
strings.IBR_Worldwide_Trading_desc:
The Oil Crisis was a global crisis and any economy attached to the global economy has been affected by the problems that were a result of it. However, despite this, we should seek out new trading partners to diversify our trade. Through this, we can make sure that even if one of our trading partners collapses because of future global recessions, we will at least have the others to fall back on.

Additionally, by having more trading ties with the world, it will speed up our own economic recovery because of the fact that it will give us access to a wider market for our exports and the opportunity for more foreign investment.
strings.IBR_pay_our_debts_tt: The government will start to pay its debt to ensure debtor confidence!
strings.IBR_Pay_Our_Debts_desc:
Now that we have implemented a good portion of the New Economic Program, it is time to start paying back the debt that we accrued while funding our economic recovery program. It is imperative that we do this as soon as possible to avoid defaulting on these loans and having our state debtors bail out on us.

Additionally, by paying them back, it will increase business confidence in us which allow us to pursue further loans in the future should we need to. Confidence in the government's ability to pay back it's loans is paramount to ensuring that our economic recovery can be completed.
strings.IBR_Another_Economic_Miracle_desc: Good news has been hard to come by since the start of this crisis however our internal economists have predicted that our recovery should be coming soon. As brilliant as this is, we must not become complacent and we need to make sure that we stick to the emergency measures that we put into place and carry on as we were or else risk slipping back in a recession. The New Economic Program has been mostly implemented and for the time being, sticking to what is currently in place seems to be the shortest road to recovery and our economists agree.
strings.IBR_end_crisis_tt: The crisis is almost gone, but a lot is yet to be done...
strings.IBR_End_Crisis_UR_desc: It has become clear to us that the worst of the recession is now over and we have left the trough and are heading into recovery. This means that we can relax some of the emergency measures that we put in place at the start of the crisis and things in Iberia will start to go back to normal. Our vision of brighter and fairer Iberia will soon come to fruition and the New Economic Program will be expanded and adapted to a non-crisis economy but until then we will make sure that Iberians, no matter their stature in life, have faith in their government to look out for their welfare.
strings.IBR_A_Victory_For_Democracy_desc:
For the first time since 1936, the Iberian Peninsula has hosted the first truly free election in Its history, finally bringing democracy to the peninsula for the first time in generations and sweeping away the autocratic dual rule of the Caudillos. Largely a coalition of Progressives, Liberals, Christian Democrats and Conservatives, the Democratic Center party (CD) have emerged victorious as the new government for a new Iberia.

CD now has the unenviable position of drafting a new constitution for a united Iberia to replace the outdated Spanish and Portuguese constitutions of Franco and Salazar, this on top of reforming the ailing economy and expanding the rights of Iberians that have long since been denied to them.
strings.IBR_A_Victory_For_Democracy_tt: It is time to bring Iberia into the Modern Age.
strings.IBR_What_We_Are_Here_For_desc:
There is only one overriding goal of this government and parliament: the creation of a robust Iberian constitution that will ensure an enduring Iberian democracy. We shall establish a Constitutional Commission, based upon the proportional representation of the parties within Parliament, in order to secure support for a new constitution that transcends party affiliations.

With this, we will ensure that we can build a new, democratic Iberia that politicians and citizens can both believe in, ending the legacy of abortive republics, unstable monarchies, and brutal dictatorships.
strings.IBR_Balancing_Act_desc: Our Constitutional Commission contains members from across the political spectrum, both left and right. We must ensure a proper balance of their demands to ensure that we do not write an unrepresentative constitution and force one side or the other against the very idea of a constitutional republic. We must take great care to both find a middle ground for issues where there can be compromise and offer concessions to both sides to ensure that the new Iberian constitution can retain a broad base of public support.
strings.IBR_Get_Fraga_In_desc:
Manuel Fraga has been very vocal about how he may not support the completed constitution. His party is large and even beyond it his influence is immense. If Fraga opposes the constitution, we will find it very difficult to secure Iberia's democratic legacy.

However, Fraga's ego is his weakness. We will ensure that Fraga himself is placed within the Commission and is permitted to help craft the constitutional text. He would never oppose something that he himself has had a hand in creating - his own exalted self-conception cannot permit it. If his party suffers a fracture over his participation, so much the better. It will shunt those who cannot abide by a democratic Iberia further to the fringes and further from political relevance.
strings.IBR_A_New_Concordat_desc:
Iberia has deeply Catholic roots; as such the Vatican holds great spiritual and cultural significance for the people. Therefore, the first fully Iberian concordant should be concluded with the Vatican, as a powerful symbolic gesture of continuity to the people.

However, while the Vatican and Catholicism remain a significant influence on our people, our identity as a nation must stand as a secular one. We will declare the formal separation of church and state in our constitution, and enact legislation that formally establishes freedom of religion and anti-discrimination policies for non-Catholics, to establish a legislative basis for our new liberal society.
strings.IBR_Head_of_State_Renewal_desc:
Iberia will not soon forget the contributions of the Caudillos Franco, Salazar, and Caetano, yet the Union's right to sovereignty must be molded to suit the times, lest it follow the same fate that befell the Third Reich and most of Europe. Simply put, the era of the rule of personalistic, ultranationalist strongmen is well into its twilight. The diarchy of Madrid and Lisbon must become one that is ruled by laws, not men.

'The Presidency Council' may sound benign to the sterner sect in Iberia, but the role of Franco and Caetano remains more or less the same; The official title of Caudillo will be done away with in favor of the Presidential Offices of Spain and Portugal, now formally co-existing in a joint role to and staffed by the two of them for as long as they remain alive. The provision to reorient either positions into an elected one in the event of their death may be a bitter pill for either man, but they can anesthetize themselves in the knowledge that their legacy in the national identity of not one, but three principle European nations has finally been secured.
strings.IBR_Many_Make_One_desc:
As efforts to re-codify the structure of the Iberian Union commences, the inevitable question of the peninsula's regional nationalities must be addressed at the outset; The agitation on the part of the Catalonians, Galicians, and Basque is not going to go away simply because it is asked of them, while forced suppression of regional identity, at least to the degree posited by some of the military leadership, is as much of dubious morality as it is an erroneous waste of time and resources.

Rather than risk a worse confrontation in the future, a solution in equity is to be introduced; While not quite equal in status as Portugal is, regional autonomy from the central government is to be granted to the Basque Country, Galicia, and Catalonia respectively. It will be a very long time before the leadership in La Coruña, Bilbao, and Barcelona will be considered on the level of Madrid or Lisbon, but a hardline commitment to constitutional sovereignty for each of these regions is sure to be accepted by the local populations.
strings.IBR_Tactical_Withdrawal_desc:
Many nationalists and conservatives across the Iberian Union would point to the colonies as a symbol of the continued imperial pride that the Union has inherited from the once-mighty Spanish and Portuguese Empires, though a closer analysis clearly highlights the colonies as a white elephant more than anything, with the constant presence and attention outweighing the few settlers and few resources that those lands bear.

Too expensive for the Union to continue holding in the same way it does now, it would clearly be in our best interest to begin a controlled withdrawal from the overseas territories. While we know better than to completely abandon these lands, much to the chagrin of the more conservative elements within the country, we can slowly reduce our presence by establishing local councils and allowing increased autonomy to reduce the burden of direct control over the colonies.

New governors oriented towards the creation of autonomous but loyal political groups within these colonies will be installed, replacing the more conservative old guard. With this process, we can hopefully alleviate some of the strain on our administrative resources and perhaps orient ourselves to more pertinent matters for our country.
strings.IBR_Rule_Of_Law_desc:
For many years the people have considered the Iberian judicial system to be both highly partisan and a tool of state oppression. This is not a wholly inaccurate view, and so we will take steps to correct the known deficiencies.

Separation of powers between the judicial and executive will be formalized, the pathways of arrest and trial will be moderated and the use of judicial tribunals for the prosecution of political crimes will be abolished. In this way, trust will be steadily restored.
strings.IBR_The_Villamejor_Pacts_desc:
If the most herculean mission for the Iberian Union is to draft a new constitution, the political and economic reforms for the nation are barely a foot behind it in that race. Many are keenly aware of the import the new constitution represents, as they are for the need for a general consensus for what is needed to institute these reforms.

A litany of written agreements, signed with the consent of all representative political parties and trade unions in Iberia, has been compiled to achieve this design. This collection of agreements, hereafter known as Villamejor Pacts, will delineate the agreed upon reforms in the Iberian Union once the new constitution is ratified.
strings.IBR_Forgive_and_Forget_desc:
Many have known our justice system to be one defined of political repression and kangaroo courts - hardly appropriately deserving of the name “justice”, when countless of our people have faced oppression simply for speaking out against the clear injustices committed against our own nation by those who have led. The prisons, unlike those of functioning, civilised countries, are home not to murderers and rapists, but students, professors, and laymen - guilty only of the crime of free thought and the audacity to vocalise the perceived injustices. It can be said that even each Iberian family knows of one acquaintance who has crossed paths with the Falangist political repressions, silently wishing for the return of their loved ones.

Conservatives, of course, raise valid and often alarming concerns of drawing the distinction of mere dissidence and full-blown terrorism. However, in our commitment to winning the trust of the people is forcing our hand in extreme changes, even if it may mean amnesty even for the perpetrators of blood crimes...
strings.IBR_Education_for_Democracy_desc:
Our education system, though existent and functioning actively within the state and raising its children, can hardly be called adequate in bringing about the next generation of Iberian children and the children of theirs. One good look at the current state of education in Iberia is hardly one worthy of a modern nation - with teachers forced to read from neglected textbooks and parrot politicised drivel verbatim from outdated textbooks.

The panacea for the backwardness of our systems, is of course the medicine of knowledge - and what better way to bring about this than the revitalisation of the education system. The curriculum, in dire need of updates, and the style of classes and lectures, opened up to the voices and opinions of teachers and parents, will be the first place we begin our reforms. Education will be reorganised to become compulsory for both boys and girls up to age 14, and a greater emphasis will be put on encouraging and preparing students to attend and succeed in university.

Nothing is more golden than knowledge in the human race, and instilling these values in our descendants will ensure that our future may be preserved for centuries to come.
strings.IBR_Our_Boys_in_Brown_desc:
The police forces in any civilised country are meant to serve the people and not those in charge - and as it stands, both the military and the police were oriented to serve those in charge. Though we can at the very least grant our predecessors the excuse of establishing stability in a war-torn and impoverished country recovering from civil war, the times clearly have changed and reforms must be made, lest our commitments to democracy be put into question.

The police forces are to be drafted to be put under jurisdiction of the Minister of the Interior, as the arm of civilian security rather than armed defence and counterespionage, as is the role they play now under the jurisdiction of the Army. Naturally, with the adoption of a new policing doctrine with the reorganisation the officer hierarchies and welfare practices, so too will we have to move the police closer to civilianhood, allowing women to become officers too.

Finally, the question of the political and secret police remains - such a clear system of barbarism and repression will have no place in the Iberia of tomorrow. Only a police force that serves the people and the people alone, shall be worthy to bear the badge of the Iberian coat of arms.
strings.IBR_Reshuffle_the_AAS_desc:
Although necessary at the time and during the years of crisis, it must be recognized that the immense growth and mission profile of the AAS is no longer sustainable. It possesses far too broad a mandate, with far too much responsibility, and in its bloated state it is no longer effective. Or controllable.

It is to become solely focused on counterterrorism, with its other functions moved to other intelligence or police organizations. And although we cannot replace its military leadership - yet - civilian administrators will be integrated to allow for further reform.
strings.IBR_Her_Rights_Too_desc:
Though we have the utmost respect for traditional society, it is unbecoming of a civilized nation to not recognize facts. Adultery, cohabitation outside of marriage, and contraceptives are becoming increasingly common in major cities. Iberian women are vocally demanding bodily autonomy. Even the conservatives recognize that we must compromise somewhere.

We will decriminalize adultery and premarital cohabitation, and permit the sale of contraceptives, albeit with strict regulations.

This move will remain exactly that- a compromise. Neither the left nor the right will be especially happy. With many radicals demanding no-fault divorce and legalized abortions. However, this should move us forward and address our changing society rather than continuing to blindly push against a tide.
strings.IBR_Reinsertion_Not_Isolation_desc:
Among the few points of agreement, consistent agreement no less, within the caudillist regime was that of their philosophy towards prisons: a rug under which no limit of problems may be swept—a black hole no different than that of Calcutta, wherein dissent may at last be snuffed out once and for all. Dissent such as the ideals our coalition has pledged to uphold.

It goes without saying that such a state of affairs cannot continue in an Iberia worthy of the title “just”; thus shall the ceaseless tide of change erode even this timeless institution, so that incarceration may better its subjects rather than silence its victims. The barbaric overuse of solitary confinement shall find itself restricted to pure necessity, while guards and other employees alike will enjoy a newfound work environment wherein they need not fear a vengefully drawn knife behind every corner.
strings.IBR_Damnatio_Memoriae_desc:
If Franco only knew about some of the horrors committed in his name, he could only weep. The noble desires of the Caudillos were distorted by the aggression of those who believed they were carrying out their wishes, resulting in tragedy. Mass graves, concentration camps, the murders of pregnant women in the hundreds. It is a sin to ignore it.

We cannot continue to propagandize their legacy. Any memorials that bear the names of known criminals will be taken down. Plaques will be removed, streets renamed, and pompous busts sold off from public ownership.

Some may protest, but honestly, most citizens will be glad to see this stain on our history disappear. It must be a clean break, so no counter-memorials. Those may be... excessively controversial. Our eyes remain firmly fixed on the future.
strings.IBR_Green_Book_of_Financial_Reforms_desc:
Iberia isn't a country known for economic stability. Government corruption, corporatism, and other parasites have pushed our country backward. We will whip this beast into shape by hook and by crook.

First, the hook—we will introduce a new punitive law regarding tax crimes, which will be investigated by a specialized task force. Then the crook; we will reach out to those dizzy with wealth, and gently suggest they regularize their taxes or face prison time.

New foundations must also be built. Banks will be forced to reveal their finances to build investor confidence. We will roll out some “progressive” taxes on wealth and luxury items, but not a step further. The next government can build upon this as they see fit.
strings.IBR_Tackle_the_Prices_desc:
Many products sold to our citizens have been marked up to an absurd extent. The poor pay half their day's wages for bread. Middle-class citizens haven't the cash left over to fix leaky faucets. Even the wealthy are feeling the squeeze.

Though some of our free-market-oriented allies will bemoan our next move, we cannot ignore our countrymen's plight. We will put controls on the prices of staples, and require all our country's monopolies to keep costs below a certain threshold.

These thresholds, however, are bound to change over time. To future-proof this policy, we will get company representatives and consumer association leaders on a new price control board, which will discuss future changes. After all, what is more modern and civilized than compromise?
strings.IBR_Close_The_Money_Tap_desc:
Like everything else wrong with the Caudillos' rule, the brutish approach to economic independence for Iberia has allowed inflation to seep through thanks to an over-reliance on money creation. As much as the Oil Crisis left Iberia reeling for proper spending reserves, stunting the growth of inflation takes precedence.

Reducing the output of the money printing will help to manage inflation, giving Iberia's economy some much needed room for domestic growth.
strings.IBR_High_Wages_Low_Firings_desc:
Economists are predicting a large jump in inflation. Left unchecked, this could rattle Iberians of all stripes and undermine faith in the coalition; therefore, we should be proactive in addressing it. We will increase the minimum wage along the predicted rate of inflation to maintain a roughly equivalent standard of living without triggering an escalatory price-wage spiral, as well as offer tax breaks to companies if they maintain their current levels of employment within a few percentage points.

Longer term we will need to find subtler ways to reduce inflation and lower costs, but for now this will serve to keep the people on our side and maintain their level of economic prosperity.
strings.IBR_National_Energy_Plan_desc:
Energy is critical for any nation, but especially one such as ours with our rapid growth in industrial production. Unfortunately, our nation has few fossil fuel resources that can be expanded to scale with our growing energy demand, so we must be creative with our energy generation while working with our environment.

We will create a new National Energy Plan, building new hydroelectric plants where it is feasible and diversifying our import sources to ensure that nothing can compromise our energy security. Crucially, inefficiencies in our domestic energy production will be identified and removed, ensuring that we can satisfy the demands of our citizens and avoid power rationing or blackouts.
strings.IBR_Hoy_No_Se_Fia_desc:
As much as the new Iberia has embraced the free market as a matter of course, the regime must be prudent in how much it invests in cultivating the private sector compared to the rest of the interior. It is a very tumultuous time Iberia enters as democracy is allowed to blossom once more; a time in which the people need us to support them in their business ventures, regardless of if that comes as an inconvenience to the corporate class in Iberia.

By limiting government funding allocations for larger companies, we can reinvest it into small and medium level enterprises as well as job creation across the peninsula. This might alienate some of the titans of our domestic industry, but it is only right to showcase the new Iberia as a nation that offers opportunity and prosperity for its peoples.
strings.IBR_Reign_in_the_Public_Sector_desc:
In past years, it was no secret that the various bloated and inefficient public corporations served as a source of patronage appointments, nepotistic placements, and sinecures given as political reward. Commensurate economic inefficiencies were, and are, starkly evident. This will be corrected.

All public companies will be placed under parliamentary control and subject to empowered oversight. Furthermore, in order to accomplish their public mission, they will be decentralized, with operations preferentially located in less developed areas of Iberia.
strings.IBR_Free_Iberia_desc:
After a generation of authoritarian rule across the peninsula, Iberia has resurrected the dream that died in 1936 and was long buried by 1945. The post-war regime of the Caudillos has gradually evolved into something even grander, supplanted by the first democratic government in the region since the onset of the Civil War.

With the new constitution drawn and framed, the time has at last come to send it to parliament for the vote to ratify and to the people for a referendum. Once these hurdles are passed, this Parliament will be dissolved and new elections will decide the future of Iberia, with a firmly-established constitutional democracy now ready to guide her path through it.
strings.IBR_Free_Iberia_tt: The Parliament will vote on our new Constitution.
strings.IBR_market_liberal_oil_crisis_desc:
Yet again the Italian mismanagement of their colonial possessions in the Middle East has ended in disaster; only somehow titanically worse than any other blunder in their history. The revolution in Iran has sparked several other civil wars across the region that have seen some of the world's largest underground Oil reserves lost to hellish desert warfare. Every major nation's economy has been cut off and instability looms.

Iberia has not fared any better than any of her immediate European neighbors. Our chronically over bureaucratized economy has to untangle the mess of this global economic crisis. The nation must seize the initiative in limiting the damage and reforming the economy to ensure future system shocks are not repeated.
strings.IBR_Opus_Dei_Program_desc:
It has been argued that in these times of crisis intervention in the market in some form is necessary. Even officials within our ranks are starting to be convinced by foolish economic policy. It is our luck that the loyal institution of Opus Dei has provided a comprehensive plan in order to emerge from these dark times.

The organization has promised that with certain stimulus arrangements the market would be able to recover and begin resuming a normal trend. In general, however, the emergency program is designed to uphold the market liberal ideology while alleviating the shock of the crisis. After all, the market has always proven itself to be most efficient at designating resources. Opus Dei have promised that opening the possibilities of exploiting new energy sources to investors, and pushing for tax cuts across the board, will bring back the forces of supply in order to meet the outstanding demand. Until then the market should be allowed to stabilise itself.
strings.IBR_Earn_Your_Wage_desc:
A fair number of petitions have made their way to the desks of government officials in light of the current oil crisis. One of the most disturbing however was a one complaining about a factory in Barcelona firing most of their staff unfairly in order to uphold liquidity. This is clearly unacceptable. We cannot have companies going bust and damaging the necessary market forces we need to stave off this crisis.

To remedy this issue it has been suggested that a new work culture should be introduced, one where we can insure that firms uphold required staff numbers without paying for it with unmet variable costs. Hence, we should ensure that companies know they are supported by the government in firing unnecessary workers as long as they keep those who are truly earning their pay. This should promote productivity in the long run too.
strings.IBR_Audit_SegSoc_desc: In the plan to restructure the economy the eyes of officials have fallen on the administration responsible for Seguridad Social. It has been recognized that social security is an important component of modern state organization, but this does not mean that just like with other government branches that it is immune to inefficiency. In line with arguments that have claimed that it only is a bottomless pit that continuously sucks money without giving back to the economy, we have decided it finally is time that we audit the whole operation. There certainly will be parts that are either not an absolute necessity or that are downright mismanaged. All these will be cut in order to save money for the government which can be used to stimulate the currently still tanking economy.
strings.IBR_Oil_For_Pay: Oil... For Those Who Can Pay
strings.IBR_Oil_For_Pay_desc: With the ongoing oil crisis other nations have seen drastic government overreach through direct intervention to restrict oil consumption in the economy and to artificially reduce its price for state enterprises. We on the other hand will use no such draconian regulation to harm our economy. The free market has historically proven itself to be the most effective and efficient distributor of resources through the demand and supply paradigm. Hence, we should leave it to these forces to decide what happens with the oil that our nation has access to. It surely will go to those with the most need which we can identify by how much they will be willing to pay for it.
strings.IBR_Invest_Energy_desc: The crisis has shown us above all that oil as the sole energy source for many economic sectors cannot be relied on anymore. With any lack of energy diversification, a shock could bring great ruin. We must therefore look to other energy sources that can be exploited to ensure that our economy will be on strong foundations even when those around us are suffering. Surveys of options that we have available have produced arguments for hydroelectric power generation amongst others. It is necessary that we move quickly to restore faith in the market.
strings.IBR_invest_energy_tt: Investments in new energy sources will increase costs by $6 million and give 1 £tt_power grid power
strings.IBR_Let_Market_Alone: Let the Market Sort Itself Out
strings.IBR_Let_Market_Alone_desc: Some officials and pressure groups have come to the government to argue that direct intervention to correct market forces is essential to bring the Iberian economy out of the crisis. With great difficulty and after a number of intense debates have they been rebuked. It is clear that they have been seized by an irrational panic! Do they not know that the market is the best and only tool to correct itself? Time and time again when central authority has intervened in order to bring about what it says as good change has it resulted in terrible outcomes. On the other hand, the market has always been able to efficiently correct course and stabilise the forces of demand and supply. We must once again trust its capability; it will surely lead us out of this crisis stronger than before.
strings.IBR_Find_New_Markets_ML_desc: Liberalising the internal market conditions has consistently been a priority for government policy due to the terrible conditions which the previous regime had left for us. However, with the advent of the Oil Crisis it has become clear that work needs to be done to expand our market liberal vision into the international sphere. In a similar vein to energy diversification we also must seek to expand our trading networks. Our currently weak links were damaged by the expansive economic damage that weak preparation and an incomplete restructuring of market forces had given us. Finding new markets abroad will hopefully ensure better trading capabilities in the future and ensure that future crises will not ravage our economy again.
strings.IBR_Find_New_Markets_ML_tt: Our trade relations with various countries will improve.
strings.IBR_Tax_Cut_Oil_Crisis_desc: The government has been terribly affected by the Oil Crisis, both in financial but also national security terms. A large factor in this is the economic downturn that domestic markets have faced. Both companies and private individuals have fewer funds than previously and hence are not spending or investing which are the important bloodlines our economy depends on. It is not for the government to sort out issues with how people interact with the market and more importantly how it functions, yet we should certainly facilitate an opportunity for the market to resuscitate itself. In this we have decided upon a general tax cut which will affect all interests in the economy. By individuals and firms having more money again we will hopefully see a return to a new normal.
strings.IBR_Allow_Private_Services_desc: Despite our best efforts to influence the Iberian population and culture into accepting all tenets of free market capitalism we have never been able to really breach the bastion of support surrounding the provision of what are deemed essential public services. The crisis has however given us new impetus in our mission to finally achieve total victory over those who stand in the way of liberalising all aspects of the economy. Under the guise of returning financial stability to government expenditure it has been decided to allow private versions of public services to be authorised. With those who can afford private provisions switching we are still providing a safety net to the less advantaged strata of our society. Under current legislation the change will remain under review for a good amount of time as many are still not entirely convinced by the measure, however we are sure that the efficiency the market will display will assure them otherwise.
strings.IBR_Negotiate_Creditors_desc: Since the formation of the Iberian Union the new state has relied on large expenditures to ensure a semblance of external safety and internal stability in a tumultuous Europe. This has resulted in a large amount of debt now sitting square on our shoulders. With the international economy having taken a great hit many creditors have allowed panic to set in. A number of them have insisted that Iberia pay back its debts with the most utmost urgency, in some cases even with reduced interest rates. It would however currently be detrimental to our recovery were we to pay back all of the amassed debt. We hence need to find common ground with the creditors and convince them that both our parties would be better off if the debts could be delayed for a longer period of time.
strings.IBR_Thank_Later_desc: The economic measures implemented on the behest of Opus Dei and with the clear approval of the administration are proving themselves to be successful by the necessary factors measured. They have however incurred the wrath of certain interest groups and some of the wider population. Describing the reforms as ruthless and amoral they have rallied against the government in protests and numerous petitions. Clearly when relying on technocratic advice it sometimes is difficult to make the public understand our intentions. Necessary sacrifices may be seen as negligence or even worse intentional evil. Like with so many things in history only hindsight will be able to clear the cobwebs from their eyes. In time they will thank us for what we done for them and those who follow. We have chosen the correct and righteous path.
strings.IBR_Crutial_Moment_desc: We stand now at a crossroads of vital historic importance. Iberia must choose whether to embrace and effectively work with our reforms or deny their value and fall alongside other nations entirely crippled by the economic crisis. The Union has the potential to become a leading powerhouse in Europe, towering above nations with similar demographics only due to the effective management of market forces. We have done all we can for now, our response was well orchestrated and allowed the passing of necessary legislation in combating the crisis. The foundations for a strong economic upswing hence have been set. It is for Iberians to now lead the Union further into prosperity or reject the gifts we have bestowed upon them.
strings.IBR_A_Victory_For_Iberia_desc:
While the diarchal rule of the Caudillos has now been swept away, the first free elections on the Iberian Peninsula in over 40 years has seen the rise of a coalition of ideals still familiar to those who live in it. The People's Alliance (AP) represents a multitude of right-wing political parties from Spain and Portugal who now carry the responsibility of reforming the economic and political systems in Iberia.

Many may worry over the return of a firmly rightist government to Madrid, whose comparatively moderate values are unavoidably going to evoke ugly memories of Franco and Salazar to those in the opposition. The AP, with the responsibility of crafting a new constitution and safeguarding prosperity, has a lot to prove in the coming years.
strings.IBR_A_Victory_For_Iberia_tt: It is time to live up to our name.
strings.IBR_Our_Given_Duty_desc:
Any organisation can rule a state, but what is it to rule a nation? How can a nation know itself to be ruled? By what mechanisms is ruling carried out, and what responsibilities do both ruler and ruled possess? Without the answer to such questions, ruling a nation is always a short term proposition. It is our duty, as the vanguard of a new Iberia, to ensure its longevity and to fulfill our Government's most important purpose; the creation of a new constitution.

We shall create a commission, composed proportionally of all the different parties currently represented within the legislature, to truly define what Iberia is and how it shall be governed. As a cross-party effort, this new constitution shall be a beacon not just to Iberia, reminding us of the strength of our society, but to the World. To show all that tyranny need not beget tyranny, and rationalism can always win out.
strings.IBR_A_New_Concordat_con_desc:
After much deliberation, it has been decided to decisively resolve all state conflicts with the Church. We will work to sign a new Iberian Concordat with the Vatican, securing final answers to all relevant and existing questions of faith.

We will further enshrine principles of religious freedom, finalize the separation of Church and State, and end discrimination against other faiths. Of course, Iberia is and will remain a Catholic nation, and so it is expected that this understanding will result in the Concordat having favorable terms.
strings.IBR_Executive_Access_desc:
No one denies that the aftermath of the Civil War was an uncertain time for our country, with enemies within and without threatening us. The ascension of the Caudillos represented stability and security for the country in such circumstances, when fears of Communist bombs or German tanks were high.

However, the passage of time and the efforts of the Iberian people have transformed us into a resilient and robust nation, such an inflexible system no longer suffices. We will rename the position to 'President' to better signify their new position, to be chosen by the State's representatives rather than appointed by circumstance.

In recognition of their accomplishments, and in the interest of government stability, we will name Franco and Caetano as our first two presidents. Who better to act as the first of these new Consuls for the Iberian people?
strings.IBR_Regionalism_Done_Right_desc:
Regionalism is an ever-present concern of the State and it must be definitively addressed if the state's goals are to be achieved. We will work to appease and divide the regionalist bourgeoisie, granting significant autonomy to the major regions - namely Portugal, Galicia, Catalonia, and the Basque Country. Smaller regions will receive more limited powers.

We will, however, tie these regions to the central government through the establishment of an assistance fund. Paid into by the more affluent states, funds will be dispensed to the regions in amounts identified by the State, ensuring a reasonable degree of control.
strings.IBR_Tip_The_Scale_desc:
The commission in charge of the State's upcoming constitutional changes was appointed proportionally to party legislative share. This ensured its basic legitimacy, and affords the State a plurality of representation, but does introduce a problem - there are far too many members from leftist parties, some of whom are unacceptably radical.

However, an opportunity does exist. The centrists are similarly alarmed and if they can be convinced of the extent of the left-wing threat, we can count on their support to defeat any potential extreme proposals.
strings.IBR_No_Idea_Too_Far_Fetched_desc:
As we transition to a new era of governance, we must reexamine how our territories are administered. A newly made Commission for Territorial Affairs will conduct a thorough review of current governance structures, consulting with local communities and experts. During this period, we must replace outgoing officials, of course... selected for their competence and commitment to our principles.

This is not about dismantling systems overnight, but about building governance that reflects our values while maintaining stability. The commission will propose phased reforms - always prioritizing self-determination within our constitutional framework, ensuring no community is left behind in our renewal.
strings.IBR_Rule_Of_Law_con_desc:
For many years the people have considered the Iberian judicial system to be both highly partisan and a tool of state oppression. This is not a wholly inaccurate view, and so we will take steps to correct the known deficiencies.

Separation of powers between the judicial and executive will be formalized, the pathways of arrest and trial will be moderated and the use of judicial tribunals for the prosecution of political crimes will be abolished. In this way, trust will be steadily restored.
strings.IBR_White_Book_of_Political_Reforms_desc:
Our opponents warn of chaos while ignoring the slow decay that comes with stagnation. They're not entirely wrong for history shows that reckless change brings only ruin. But neither are they right, for we must not hold ourselves down.

Ours is the steady path between these extremes. We shall reshape our nation as one works marble - knowing when to strike and when to polish, when to remove and when to preserve. Let the doubters gasp as we unveil a stronger nation, not through surrender to turmoil, but through the disciplined work of rebuilding law by law. This is how great nations renew themselves, not in the fire of revolution, but in the forge of careful reform.
strings.IBR_Families_First_desc:
We must always remember that the core of Iberian society is the family unit. Across the nation there are families facing a variety of tribulations, and it is essential that our Government supports and promotes them to the best of the State's ability.

We will issue a series of tax breaks and assistance programs for large families and rural families. To promote these new support avenues and offer general social assistance we shall establish family centers across the nation. Further, we shall reform relevant laws to not discriminate against extramarital children, ensuring that such unfortunates can be better integrated into society and prevent cycles of familial dysfunction. After all, good society begins at home.
strings.IBR_Education_As_You_Want_It_desc:
Sound policy makes our today, but what builds tomorrow? Education, Education, Education. Despite that fact, many aspects of our system remain antiquated and it is essential that we modernise, so that Iberia is properly prepared for tomorrow.

The school leaving age will be raised to 14 for both genders, with the curriculum updated to include the most up to date information for students. Teachers' pay will be raised and new funding for school resources unlocked, with subsidies for both private and public schools maintained in order to safeguard aspiration within the system. Most importantly, public universities will see their entry requirements rationalised, standardized testing ensuring our best and brightest have access to higher education whatever their background. This great programme must be remembered as a turning point in Iberia's fortunes.
strings.IBR_Enforcers_of_the_Law_desc:
It is essential that the State's approach to law shifts as realities change, and within the coalition calls for such are frequent and loud. Political policing stands as an archaic piece of the past at a time when other branches of law enforcement cry out for more resources with which to safeguard law-abiding citizens.

We shall abolish the functions of political policing from national law enforcement, abolishing every group committed to it and updating reformable forces to no longer have such responsibilities. Resources will be redistributed amongst other bodies of law enforcement, ensuring that the focus of our policing is both where it should be and properly supported in its endeavors.
strings.IBR_Reshuffle_the_AAS_con_desc:
The AAS since its inception has blurred the line between an appropriate answer to the more organised threats Iberia faces, and a paramilitary organisation employing force against groups towards whom the State harbours distrust. Such perceptions are rife within the wider public, and so for the AAS to appropriately fulfill its role in safeguarding Iberia from terrorism, it requires change.

The AAS's purview will be limited solely to counter-terrorism, with all other responsibilities diverted to forces more appropriate to their requirements. Further, the wider organisation will be reshuffled with an increased presence of civilian administrators within its operation, even if the leadership remains primarily military, allowing the AAS to avoid insular military excess.
strings.IBR_For_Her_Too_desc:
Women are the bedrock of society, for it is through their toiling that sound men and women are created. However, misconceptions continue to proliferate regarding this truth, the Law in some aspects inadvertently discriminating against those it is seeking to serve.

We will reform relevant laws to remove discrimination against women in the workforce and promote job opportunities, as many single women or women whose children have grown up are ready and willing to be productive in the economy. Further, we shall recognise being a housewife as a legal profession and issue a modest state salary, so as to recognise and support women in perhaps the most societally vital profession there is; raising our future.
strings.IBR_Crime_Punishment_desc:
There are prison cells holding men and women whose only crimes were to speak their mind and advocate for Iberia's improvement; such an injustice cannot be permitted to continue. We shall issue a wide ranging pardon to all those convicted of political crimes.

However, we must be sure to temper ourselves. Those who engaged in violence are not guilty for speaking their minds, but for endangering their fellow citizens for their own ends. Those convicted for terrorism will not receive an unconditional reprieve. Further, having moved away from one extreme, why should we permit the extreme Left freedom to subvert our young renewal by legalising extreme parties? Our opposition may cry out for trials of previous leaders and opening the gates of political radicalism, but such lack of care is why they remain as opposition.
strings.IBR_Alive_Neighbourhoods_desc:
The most stable currency of all states, more than gold or industry, is land. Usable land, able to be turned over to the needs of the State and the People. The Americans, Germans and even the Russians enjoy this; any mistake they make or advantage found is always done with a guarantee of room to expand. It is the foundation of economy, and therefore prosperity.

With our growing population and plans for economic growth, it is essential then that we utilise land owned by the Government to create new social housing, as well as establishing new community services in already existing neighbourhoods. Further, we must crack down on land speculation, a vice too often ignored, in order to free land for construction projects that might better aid the nation. To compete with our larger competitors, we must ensure our land is used as effectively as possible.
strings.IBR_Green_Book_of_Financial_Reforms_con_:
We have promised the people of Iberia comprehensive financial reform - and we will deliver on that promise. Using the advice of experts in the field, we will introduce numerous additions to the criminal code for financial crimes, and make it very clear that all entities, private and otherwise, are expected to adapt to it.

We will pierce the veil of secrecy around the banking sector. We will introduce a progressive system of taxation. We will introduce wealth and luxury taxes. In doing so, we will strongly repay the trust given to us.
strings.IBR_Economic_Reforms_Later_tt: We have sufficiently progressed with our Constitutional Reform plans.
strings.IBR_Extra_Crisis_Effects_tt: This policy may have other effects should a Crisis befall the Iberian Economy.
strings.IBR_Tackle_the_Prices_con_desc:
It is clear to all that the increases seen in the prices of both basic necessities and luxuries, have caused the people tremendous hardship - and they often place the blame at our feet. We will correct this, and introduce a system of price controls on a basket of goods.

Corporate monopolies will have their control reduced, and we will further ensure public engagement in the plan by including sympathetic companies and public associations in the determination process whenever possible.
strings.IBR_Close_The_Money_Tap_con_desc:
Although once necessary, ongoing increases in the national money supply have allowed inflation to increase to untenable levels. This must now be brought under control. Both the people and the business community demand it, and we will satisfy this demand.

We will cease the rampant printing of additional currency, and by doing so act to curb inflation. A necessary and popular action - and therefore one with little cause for objection.
strings.IBR_Ever_So_Slightly_Better_desc:
It cannot be denied that the employment situation within Iberia is not ideal, but we will work to make things better. We will take a twofold approach, increasing the minimum wage by a small amount while ensuring a significant increase in unemployment benefits.

It will be expensive to be sure but it will keep people supported during their employment search and ensure public stability - along with securing public gratitude for the state's actions.
strings.IBR_Against_Big_Finance_desc:
While the Caudillos no longer stand supreme, they were hardly wrong about the excesses of capital run amok. As much as nurturing domestic industry and commerce is needed, the average citizen direly needs protections against the avarice of Banks and the other titans of finance, especially in times of economic woe.

A firm hand is needed to ensure the banks do not attempt to play God with other people's fortunes, however unpopular disciplinary measures against the financial sector may be for fiscal liberals and corporate types. Further, small and medium-sized business ventures shall be granted greater access to the stock markets, so that up and coming enterprises are given a chance to expand and grow the private sector consecutively.
strings.IBR_National_Energy_Plan_con_desc:
How are we to achieve economic prosperity, when the ability to turn the lights on at home and machinery powered in the factories is leveraged against us through foreign dependency? The road to long-term self reliance starts now.

A New National Energy Plan will target weak points in our energy grid. Existing oil deposits will continue to be exploited, while millions will be funded into newer, more renewable energy sources that work with our environment. In the meantime, imports will be diversified so that no one country has too much of a stake in our power grid.
strings.IBR_Bet_on_Green_desc:
The agricultural sector is the lifeblood of the Iberian Union. Food prices are the one anxiety that unites all across class and region. We must support the agricultural community with comprehensive legislation designed to boost productivity across the board.

Generous loans will be offered to aid young agribusinesses and farming cooperatives. A new initiative focused on expanding irrigated land for farming use shall be established and grants offered to firms involved in agricultural investment in everything from mechanization to fertilizer production. Lastly, forests nationwide shall be rejuvenated and expanded. If the rural regions can have prosperity, all Iberia shall follow.
strings.IBR_For_Sale_Healthcare_Services_desc:
As seen clearly by even our own nation in the past decade, sometimes the state does not always know best. More than a few mistakes, bottlenecks, and bureaucracies have taken their toll on the Iberian citizenry; nowhere is that more clear than within healthcare and Social Security.

Iberia will embark on a decentralization of healthcare and social security, allowing patients to choose doctors to match their own needs, as well as allowing agreements with the private sector to handle some services allowing us to increase efficiency and lower costs at the same.
strings.IBR_Dawn_New_Era_desc:
We've finally reached the precipice. Our constitution is finalized and is being sent to Parliament to be voted upon. If and when it passes, the people will vote upon it through a referendum. As soon as it is approved, Parliament will be dissolved, and new elections called for a government to replace them - and us.

There's little we can know for sure about the future of our nation. Will it be as civilized, democratic, and prosperous as we hope? Will we still remain one strong nation, Iberian and whole? Will it be left-wing, right-wing, or some new dark horse ideology? Our citizens must decide that by the ballot. As for us, we will drink our wine, pray to God, and hope that the foundations we have laid will last.
strings.IBR_auth_union_oil_crisis_desc:
Yet again the Italian mismanagement of their colonial possessions in the Middle East has ended in disaster; only somehow titanically worse than any other blunder in their history. The revolution in Iran has sparked several other civil wars across the region that have seen some of the world's largest underground Oil reserves lost to hellish desert warfare. Every major nation's economy has been cut off and instability looms.

Iberia has not fared any better than any of her immediate European neighbors. Our chronically over bureaucratized economy has to untangle the mess of this global economic crisis. The nation must seize the initiative in limiting the damage and reforming the economy to ensure future system shocks are not repeated.
strings.IBR_Budget_Readjusting_desc:
The reality of the economic calamity we find ourselves in calls for hard decisions to be made. Revenues across the board are down; if we are to remain solvent, the checkbook must be balanced.

Deep cuts, into the double digit percentages, will be made across the board to government subsidies and sectors that are not essential, such as: tourism, higher education and others, Meanwhile, essential administrative departments and economic stimulus will be ramped up. The people shall bite the bullet, lest we take one straight to the dome of our economy. The Iberian people are no stranger to austerity, and it knocks once more.
strings.IBR_Cutting_Loose_desc:
