Anti-capitalism is perfectly sound for a political platform, but an economy in freefall is not the time for puritan autarkic ideals. While economic development in Iberia should always be supervised, we are in dire need of income to battle the Oil Crisis and the free market is the most straightforward means to source it.

But we are not blind to the treachery behind capital either. What better time for capitalists to infiltrate than when capital is sorely needed? The Government will agree to loosen restrictions on domestic companies so we can combat the crisis more efficiently, but they will know the red lines that the leadership would rather they not cross. One knows not to test Iberia's patience amidst a global crisis, after all.
strings.IBR_New_Sources_of_Energy_desc:
We can not sit idle while the petrol stranglehold on Iberia's economy proceeds to choke the life out of it-never before has the premise of Autarky become more vital for the survival of the Union. Too much of Spain and Portugal's energy come from foreign imports, and improving on the self-sufficiency of the power grid must take priority.

The recent interest in renewable energy sources worldwide has caught the eye of the regime in Iberia for this reason, and the peninsula is a somewhat ideal testing ground for them. By investing into solar and wind power alongside further development of hydroelectric dams, we will secure the energy grid against future crises and improve Iberia's economic independence at the same time.
strings.IBR_Great_National_Works_desc:
Poverty in the streets, a global economy in tatters. Iberia, much like the rest of the world, is scrambling to properly respond to the disaster. While the Iberian Council is as defiantly anti-capitalist as either Caudillo, they are not opposed to some initiatives espoused by the west as the whole of Europe presently is.

Public works programs of the kind the Americans and elsewhere enacted during the Great Depression proved a worthy model to alleviate economic woes. By starting up our own works projects across Spain and Portugal, we will provide employment programs with much-needed compensation to help lift Iberia out of the current economic nosedive.
strings.IBR_Deal_Or_Deal_desc:
As much as recent political tensions with Europe still rest bitterly on Iberia's palette, the Union can not be so stingy with pursuing trade deals with other nations in the hopes offsetting the fiscal crisis in any major way, even it means breaking bread with power blocs Spain and Portugal have long since cut ties with.

While Latin America is always a principal trade center for Iberia, Germany is still the most immediate trade partner to rekindle mercantile relations with, as are countries firmly within the Reich's sphere such as France, Britain, and Scandinavia. The ex-Triumvirate countries of Italy and Turkey have been vital commercial hubs along the Mediterranean since before Jesus Christ walked the earth and one would be foolish not to entice the economic powerhouse in Japan to aid in off-setting market deficiencies.
strings.IBR_Deal_Or_Deal_tt: We will gain increased trade relations with other countries due to the new economic treaties.
strings.IBR_One_for_Thee_Three_for_Me: One for Thee, Three for Me
strings.IBR_One_for_Thee_Three_for_Me_desc:
With the government struggling to establish a self-sufficient energy grid, much of the peninsula is still reliant on petrol to keep the economy from total implosion. The only way to keep the gears of Iberia turning is to ration the fuel supply across Spain and Iberia, forcing our regime to play triage with what little fuel reserves we have in our possession.

The Iberian Council will be quite flexible in deciding who gets what; while the government and military will retain a greater portion of it, it will be with limited and infrequent access, freeing up a decent portion of it to go towards industry upkeep, with only private use being strictly regulated.
strings.IBR_Atomic_Economy_desc:
The crippling effects of the Oil Crisis have made one thing abundantly clear - whatever the resolution today, the state must act to secure tomorrow. While other departments work to stabilize the situation, a focus will be placed upon the expansion of Iberian nuclear power generation.

This will take quite some time but, by doing so, we will demonstrate to the people that we are looking to the future. Should another such crisis occur then, we will be ready, and hopefully spared the disasters of the present.
strings.IBR_Weathering_the_Storm_ac_desc:
Although it has been difficult - in some cases exceptionally so - the worst economic effects of the Oil Crisis seem to have passed, with government initiatives working to improve supply, encourage conservation, and identify alternative solutions.

Though logistical pathways are still somewhat tenuous, none can deny that the Iberian economy is showing promising signs of improvement. Therefore, some of the most controversial emergency measures can be removed, with corresponding benefits to public order.
strings.IBR_reconciliation_with_opus_dei_tt: Perhaps it is time to allow Opus Dei to assist in dealing with the crisis.
strings.IBR_fight_inflation_tt: The situation is getting out of hand. Measures have to be taken to combat inflation.
strings.IBR_loosen_state_control_tt: It may be time to loosen state control of the economy somewhat.
strings.IBR_oil_reserves_tt: We must consider stockpiling our oil reserves.
strings.IBR_raise_taxes_tt: Raising taxes might be unpopular, but if that's what it takes to help fight the Oil Crisis, so be it.
strings.IBR_concessions_to_the_companies_tt: We may have to grant more rights and privileges to various companies if we are to survive.
strings.IBR_assist_the_farmers_tt: The simple farmer has been struck hard by this crisis. Helping them would improve our standing.
strings.IBR_pray_it_works_tt: We have done our best to contain the situation. Now we pray our efforts are successful.
strings.IBR_despunion_victory_tt: Iberia will have to balance its stability to keep the Union from falling apart
strings.IBR_desp_union_politics_desc:
The last thing that Iberia needs in times like these is to move away from the tried and true rule of the Caudillos. We should not spend our time trying to fix what isn't broken. The stern and steady hand of the Caudillos has guided Iberia through the storm of German aggression, the disintegration of the Triumvirate, and the years of separatist terrorism. There is no reason to think that this style of governance will not continue to work in the future.

Some call our system of government despotic, but they care little for the security and survival of the Iberian people. True patriots know the truth: the regime of the Caudillos is the sword and shield of Iberia, and will continue to guide her on a steady and secure course.
strings.IBR_desp_union_politics_tt: Stability, for we wouldn't permit anything else.
strings.IBR_Bulwark_of_Tradition_desc:
As much as the former Axis alliance still poses a threat to the Iberian Union, the specter of a much older enemy that lurks beyond the Atlantic. Even if Franco and Caetano have long forsaken any allegiance to the fascist powers, Spain and Portugal are both still nations of the reactionary right. Capitalism remains a principal enemy of Iberia, even as an active ally against the Einheitspakt.

While Europe is very different from what it was prior, Spain and Portugal's joint prerogative remains just as it was in '36 and before. Washington may be just giddy to run roughshod over the ambitions of the Reich, but there isn't much stopping them from pointing the cannon right at us should the Pakt's influence begin to recede. Iberia is among the last defenders of traditional culture in Western Europe and it is vital that Uncle Sam's less flattering impulses be kept at bay.
strings.IBR_The_Church_Protected_desc:
Is anyone going to pretend that the Iberian Peninsula isn't home to some of the most devoutly Christian nations in the world? The heirs to the vanquishers of the Moors, the birthplace of the Inquisition and a steadfast defender of the faith for almost a thousand years? With Germany seeking to stamp out traditional religion while political instability in Italy keeps the Vatican in a state of flux. Iberia means to preserve the status of the Church in Western Europe. Therefore, it is only fair that the clergy should respond in kind.

Through an agreed-upon commitment by the regime of the Caudillos, the government will crack down on these so-called 'worker priests' agitating against the government's policies and at a brisk pace. In exchange, the Church will continue its uncritical support of the regime, even aid us in isolating progressive officials in favor of more conservative voices.
strings.IBR_Absolute_Authority_desc:
While Franco is not the same man he was in the Civil War and Caetano represents something different from the era of Salazar, the cult of personality surrounding both remains strong. With nothing left to stand in their way, the reconsolidation of Iberia can proceed in earnest.

The Iberian Union was founded on the principle of mutual defense against the Einheitspakt, a deliberate means to ensure some bastion of rational society against rabid fascist encroachment. The Caudillos require and demand unhindered control over the apparatus of state via installing compliant and loyal administrators in positions below them, such that no one person will share authority outside of Franco and Caetano. They are, after all, the only men capable of defending Iberia, lest the forces of the Reich or the Empire seek to plunge the peninsula into further chaos.
strings.IBR_The_Universities_Neutered_desc:
Our universities and their colleges-indispensable for the functioning of our state-are home now to all manner of intellectual crime and planned insurrection, among both faculty and pupils. Perhaps those harboring silent treasonous intent have seized upon-and abused-the wide liberty of discussion allowed at academy, perhaps the adolescence of the student and the discursive nature of education make for foolish dreams, but, regardless of cause, this insolence will not continue.

Accelerated expulsion procedures, coupled with government appointment of ideologically suitable administrative officials and compliance officers, shall bring this section of the intelligentsia to heel. And if we are unfortunate enough to see these measures met with substantial and abiding resistance, we possess measures to ensure policy implementation.
strings.IBR_Lackeys_and_Sycophants_desc:
The dire failures of the Iberian Council have shown the need for Iberian governmental bureaucracy to be remade from the top down, for the last thing we need is anyone else in our government to start harboring similar ideas. Ending the Council was a decent start, but more is needed to make certain that the regime of the Diarchy is secure.

From the high offices in Madrid and Lisbon, to the low level ministries and beyond, every position of importance in the Union is to be staffed by only the most obsequious and docile loyalists of Franco and Caetano. While the administrative efficiency of the state is bound to degrade as obedience is favored over talent, such measures are needed to keep the machine of state in working order; the dancing steps of statecraft that Iberia is most adept in.
strings.IBR_Review_Local_Election_Laws_desc:
It is clear now that we have demonstrated far too much tolerance in our past dealings with the oppositions, enough for Reform-minded individuals within the government to gain more power than should have ever been allowed. In order to ensure that the diarchy of the National Front and Estado Novo reigns supreme, certain electoral proceedings will have to be restructured.

By including extensive background checks for candidates in local councilor elections, as well as requirements for running in “Family Third” and “Trade Union Third” categories, we can constrict opposition members from seizing a majority by making large endorsements a necessity to compete against either the Front or Estado Novo, effectively neutralizing opposition candidates on a ground level.
strings.IBR_Encourage_Youth_desc:
As we plan revitalization of our youth programs by means of benefits to the participant, concerns about the sincerity of engagement have been raised. While it is our firm belief that most who involve themselves with these programs will do so out of genuine political agreement, the possibility that cynical-minded careerists and misguided youth comprise a small but substantial portion of youth groups should not be disregarded outright.

These ailments share a cure: ideological practice. Youth will be encouraged to watch media favorable to our policy and commanded to demonstrate their understanding in writing. The misled youth will realize the best way for him to serve the people is through established institutions and the careerist will come to understand the true value of his labor.
strings.IBR_Choke_the_Press_desc:
As Iberia advances into the 1970s, the modus operandi of the Union remains much the same. While efforts to modernize and solidify the stately rule of the Diarchy are to be lauded and venerated, many tactics employed in accomplishing this are very familiar to those south of Pyrenees.

Case in point, consistent censorship and regulation of the press has hardly changed much since the reconstruction after '36. That said, allowing for limited enterprise in Iberia has allowed for more liberal-leaning outlets to crop up again over the interregnum.

By strong-arming these outlets to scotch some of the more intolerable portrayals of Iberian domestic affairs, we can encourage these malingers to adapt to the government's preferred style of journalism and/or shutter the ones who do not comply.
strings.IBR_Organic_Law_of_Education_desc:
Why, in the age of rockets, television, and now computers, are we still dancing the ways of old in the field of education? The children are the future, and the future generation will not live to enjoy the shade of the Iberian tree if we continue watering the seeds halfway.

The new “Organic Law of Education” will be a much-needed course correction for our academic institutions. Education will be reorganized and be compulsory for both boys and girls alike until the age of 14. The more archaic portions of the curriculum will be gutted and updated, while a strong emphasis on the benefits of our system will remain. Teachers will be supported, though what they teach will be under our complete supervision.
strings.IBR_Sacrificed_Work_desc:
The technocratic faction that has entered the state bureaucracy has many ideas. Many reforms that they want to implement. And they are very insistent about implementing them. But they are not aware of the political cost of that implementation, and so we must resist their calls.

The current economic system works fine within its political constraints, and so must remain. The technocrats claim they are the best in their respective fields, no? They can therefore act to prove it - by improving the economy within the confines we set them.
strings.IBR_Feminine_Wisdom_desc:
Even though the Iberian Union is defined as a rightist traditionalist society and culture, this does not mean modernity is something to be wholly shunned. Far from it, Spain and Portugal have made immense gains as a society without sacrificing the wider majority of their people's ingenuity the way Germany and Japan have. The growing presence and influence of women in Iberian society is a sterling example of this.

Indeed, the women of Spain and Portugal show a wellspring of ambition and cunning to be tapped by the Iberian regime. The Caudillos have laid out a program that will require women applying for University to be members of the Women's Section of either the National Movement or Estado Novo. While this might seem like a superficial change to inflate the membership of the ruling party, it will strengthen the image of Iberia as one of modernism while Europe slips further into tribalistic barbarism and decadence.
strings.IBR_Strengthen_the_Axencia_desc:
None would argue that the Axencia is not critical to the stability of the state. That it is at the forefront of our efforts to defeat the many enemies arrayed against it. Similarly, none would argue that it is unwieldy, lacking clear direction, and often working at cross-purposes to itself. This must be corrected.

We will implement such correction in a comprehensive fashion. Funding will be increased, internal pathways will be reorganized, and it will be reassigned to the Ministry of the Interior, allowing for better collaboration with police forces nationwide against the terrorists. As well as, of course, against opposition elements of different persuasions.
strings.IBR_Divide_And_Conquer_desc:
While legalistic methods of curtailing the opposition are fine and dandy, methods to ensure a more...deliberate means of stifling opponents work just as well. After all, one can only pull on the administrative or bureaucratic levers of power so many times before corruption allegations become much more difficult to explain away.

Luckily for us, the colonial empires of Spain and Portugal prove to be fertile land for planting unruly agents among the opposition. Expanding the already useful Banishment laws will be handy in dislocating rival politicians to Africa, as will impromptu conscription of suspected opposition members into the colonial military. Aiding in this will be infiltration of opposition groups by law enforcement to better identify rival agents, so that they might be targeted and profiled before being removed accordingly.
strings.IBR_The_Captain_Payday_desc:
Much of the power structure in the Iberian Union is composed of the upper echelon of the Spanish and Portuguese military brass. Many of these men hold offices of such high esteem as to assume the role of a new aristocratic class in their own right. While this certainly gives the men of the upper officer corps something to strive for, many mid-level commanders are forced to work secondary and tertiary jobs to keep their heads above water, often alienating them from the very regime they aim to serve.

Given the very personal connection the men of barracks often have with these mid-level officers, it does not take a political analyst to see this is a recipe for trouble. By improving wages and upping the living standards of the officer corps, we will make sure they remain loyal to the Caudillos' regime.
strings.IBR_New_Iberian_Military_desc:
It has been brought to our attention that certain elements of the high command have expressed dissatisfaction with the current position of the state regarding military modernization. While we may disagree, we absolutely cannot permit any opposition in the military to continue.

So we will satisfy their needs, and so improve their view of the government. Reforms will be introduced in terms of budgeting, procurement, and future development. We will prove our commitment to them, and in so doing secure their support.
strings.IBR_African_Militarization_desc:
Our colonial regime in Africa remains a point of pride for our Union. While the bloodshed sweeping the continent has caused many to question the sanity of European colonialism in Africa, Iberia still has no intention of ever leaving the dark continent, regardless of whatever danger geopolitical analysts might warn of.

With the expansion of military infrastructure across our possessions along with a doubling of manpower for the colonial garrison, our remaining outposts will be impregnable.
strings.IBR_Breadcrumbs_for_Africa_desc:
For far too long, the colonial integrationists have been railing against standing colonial policy. Their voices are loud, and with the many other challenges facing the state we must remove this annoyance in order to ensure a clear focus elsewhere. So we will placate them.

Some small concessions to their agenda will be made regarding those policies, particularly those with the most visible - and least impactful - effects. It certainly would not do, afterall, for the carefully balanced economic profile of those same colonies to be adversely affected.
strings.IBR_Stricter_Casting_desc:
The administration of Iberia is often defined by filling the offices with happy yes-men to grease the wheels of the Caudillos' regime, but there is only so far their influence can extend past Madrid and Lisbon. The Secretary of Interior's role has been to appoint provincial governors that answer to the federal government, but laxity within the office has seen the rise of governors that are either not up to the task or are found to be politically distasteful to the regime.

A new reform in provincial appointments has been formulated by the Caudillos' inner circles, one that will see that any name put forward by the Interior Minister must be approved by all members of the Cabinet. In this way, we will secure the loyalty of provincial leadership as well as better solidify the Caudillos' rule across Iberia.
strings.IBR_Remember_Where_You_Came_From_desc:
The Falange, known to most of Western Europe as the chief representatives of the Spanish Far Right, have been an integral partner of Francisco Franco and the National Movement ever since 1936. While the movement's least amiable elements have long since been done away with, they are still the face of Franco's most extreme supporters and are a useful ally of the regime.

With Caetano and his clique being the most reform-minded political force within the Union, Franco recognizes that the Falange represents an ideal foil to balance against the influence of the Lusophone moderates. By appointing notable members of the Falange to high-ranking, and conveniently benign, positions of authority, we can keep Caetano's agitators at bay and make sure the Far Right remain at our beck and call.
strings.IBR_National_Tourism_desc:
Not that it is any surprise, the history and beauty of our Union draws visitors. Visitors who we, given our gracious nature, are more than happy to host. And for gracious men obligations abound; obligations that extend beyond hospitality, obligations to our families, to our daughters, and to public moral standards. Unfortunately-but perhaps not unsurprisingly given our continued dedication to the obligations stated prior-many in this world do not share our standards and, all too often, this is demonstrated by the uncouth behavior of our visitors.

The consolidation of EyD and the FANT into one organization will allow us to refocus upon domestic tourism.
strings.IBR_National_Tourism_tt: We will gain a new source of income worth $$75 Million.“
strings.IBR_Green_Red_Yellow_Pride_desc:
Efforts to unite the peninsula into a singular national identity will not end merely at the borders of the television screen, for the greater movement to unite the cultures of the Spanish and Portuguese is only deepening and growing larger. For centuries, geopolitical wrangling conspired with foreign intrigue to keep the sister nations of Iberia divided. Now, with the decadent west in position to oppose us and the former Axis power distracted with internal problems, Iberia has been allowed to resurge, bridging the gap between two of Europe's oldest nations.

The ICH and IAC have long existed as cultural and philosophical institutions dedicated towards enlightening the societies of Spain and Portugal respectively. In accordance with government initiative, they will be merged into the Institute of Iberian Culture and tasked with preserving and proliferating Iberian culture, both in the interior and abroad.
strings.IBR_The_Green_Backbone_desc:
The rural population are the backbone of rightist authoritarians across Europe and Iberia is no exception, with the countryside of both Spain and Portugal making up a large portion of the support base of the Front and Estado Novo. This political fact is unlikely to change under the continued rule of the Caudillos, which is precisely why an expansion of government aid to Iberia's rural communities has been approved by the regime.

This will encourage young men and women to find hearty work in agriculture and prevent immigration to the cities. With the recent turmoil in Ukraine being a keen example of the dangers of food insecurity, it is most prudent to make autarkic agrarianism into a matter of course as to keep Iberia's food production as self-reliant as possible.
strings.IBR_The_Third_Channel_desc:
With the relatively recent advent of the television, governments all over the world have grown privy to utilizing the medium to help promote and entice public support of government programs and initiatives. In Iberia, this has largely been facilitated through the support of the RTVE and RTP networks, respectively representing Spain and Portugal in administering two channels in their respective languages.

As part of an effort to encourage a unified Iberian national identity, a third television channel will be created to feature programming in both languages, with support for subtitling in either language as well. This channel will feature an emphasis on cultural programming as well as shows filmed and produced in Iberia, so as to aid in finally bridging the societal gap between two of Europe's oldest sister nations.
strings.IBR_The_Coming_of_Winter_desc:
As the Council disappears into memory, so do visions of deeper reform to the Iberian Union. Of those who adhered to that false promise, at least those who have not already been swept aside for disloyalty to our Caudillos, many are willingly retiring to academia, commerce, or to their family homes. Some of their talent will be missed, even if their flawed ideas will not.

The appropriate authorities will be notified to keep a loose watch over these tired and broken men. To ensure those heresies die with them.
strings.IBR_Una_Grande_y_Libre_desc:
Although divided for centuries, Iberia has been unified - and strong - for over twenty years. This has provided stability, security, wealth, and advancement for its millions of citizens, and it is owed not to faceless bureaucrats, unknowable forces of history, or to anything else. No, it is owed to the visionary rule of the Caudillos.

While other states have suffered unfocused and divided leadership, such is not the fate of Iberia. The Caudillos will remain, they will continue to keep Iberia strong, and they will ensure another twenty, fifty, one hundred years of prosperity!
strings.IBR_despotist_oil_crisis_desc:
Much like with their former ally in Germany, it would seem Franco and Salazar's initial impetus to distrust detente with the Italian Empire was a correct one. A generation of colonial mismanagement in the Levant and Mesopotamia have sparked a global economic crisis, cutting off the industrialized world from the principle exporter of oil as revolution and civil war erupts across the sands.

Despite Iberia's previous attempts to maintain autarky, the unanimity of European overreliance on Middle Eastern oil is just as true south of the Pyrenees as it is anywhere north and east. Neither Spain or Portugal have been spared from the economic freefall gripping the world, meaning that it will take some time to properly assess and deal with the damage to restore Iberia's economy to working order.
strings.IBR_Tighten_Your_Belts_desc:
Iberia's economic sovereignty must not be sacrificed upon the altar of the Oil Crisis. With the Caudillos' grip on the minds of the masses tighter than ever, it is the duty of our fellow countrymen to aid in shouldering the burden of lifting Iberia out of the current economic nosedive.

With budget cuts clearly out of the question, strict austerity measures are to be employed across the board. With both the government and the general population encouraged to slash expenditure, the economy within and around the peninsula will retain some ballast to properly combat the fiscal crisis.
strings.IBR_Gods_Workers_desc:
Our efforts to preserve regime unity have begun to pay off in the aftermath of the Oil Crisis. With technocratic clique firmly in the pockets of the Caudillos, Franco and Caetano have access to some of the brightest minds of Iberia's industrial elite.

By bringing in technocrat advisors into the economic ministries, Iberia's fiscal recovery can begin in earnest. Furthermore, by expanding INI regional operations, we can improve industrial development in regions hitherto untapped by Iberian enterprise.
strings.IBR_The_Battle_for_Energy_desc:
While the drive for autarky has often been focused on heavy industry, energy also remains a principal component in achieving national self-sufficiency. Franco knew this, as did Salazar and laid plains to properly bring power to their respective nations. While those plans have been largely successful, a number of these development plans were mothballed over the years as other projects took precedence.

These overlooked energy programs might prove to be Iberia's salvation in the wake of the Oil Crisis, as what was initially designed as a means to secure Spain and Portugal's 'energetic sovereignty' can be used to reduce reliance on energy imports from abroad. By expanding construction of coal mines and hydroelectric dams, we can better ensure that any and all power in Iberia is locally generated and nationally owned.
strings.IBR_Protecting_the_National_Product_desc:
Continuing the trend set by the Caudillos in the years after the Second World War, the economic autonomy of Iberia must be maintained to prevent it growing dependent on the rest of Europe or lands across the Atlantic. A healthy byproduct of this policy is to protect the job market by placing domestic production over foreign products.

By placing further tariffs on foreign goods, Iberians will be encouraged to spend their money on Iberian-made products over price-gouged imports. This will ensure the supply and demand chain, including the job opportunities provided by either, remains wholly national in nature.
strings.IBR_The_Military_First_desc:
One principle object of the union between Spain and Portugal was international security. An issue that only grows more pressing amidst the interventions in the Middle East.

Regardless of the pressing need for oil elsewhere, the lion's share of Iberia's fuel reserves must be allocated for military usage. Even if it means resorting to fuel rationing for other sectors, defense and sovereignty must be paramount.
strings.IBR_Enact_Price_Controls_desc:
We cannot allow the people of Iberia to go hungry as their finances disappear into the aether, nor can we allow inflation to spiral while the rest of the economy is doing the same. Instituting price controls will doubtlessly irritate the entrepreneurial class of Spain and Portugal, but the wants of the privileged few will not come before the needs of the many. Price controls will aid in chipping away at inflation while keeping the majority of Iberians above the poverty line with a steady income to keep their families fed, something that any unruly businessman should be wise to respect.

There is no choice to be considered in this regard, not in our society anymore. One is wise not to bite the hand that feeds, a fool is one who chooses to meet the foul end of a boot heel.
strings.IBR_Expand_Nuclear_Operations_desc:
Nuclear power has been something of a marvel of the modern era, one that is as full of risks as there are benefits. With conventional energy production from coal and hydroelectricity only as viable as much as the Earth itself can provide, something with the gargantuan output as provided by the Atom perhaps offers a more long-term alternative.

While the government initiative to further construct nuclear power plants across Spain and Portugal has been greenlit, it will take some time and a hefty amount of resources to see the results. With time however, this will alleviate the power imbalance on the peninsula by further cementing Iberia's energy autonomy from the rest of Europe and future proof against any potential energy crisis down the line.
strings.IBR_Weathering_the_Storm_desc:
Let it never be said that the diarchal rule of the National Movement and Estado Novo are not consistent in their ambitions, for not even the worst economic crisis to rock the world since the Great Depression could undo the regime of Franco and Caetano. If anything, their efforts ensured that they emerged even stronger than before.

While the damage the Oil Crisis dealt to Iberia is clear to all, the worst of that damage has been mitigated and the economy more or less restored to working order. The low supply of oil remains a key issue for the duration, yet Iberia now has the fiscal stability to enact proper measures so that economic recovery can begin.
strings.IBR_Tighten_Your_Belts_tt: These actions will doubtlessly decrease the stability of our nation, but will be necessary for long term stability.
strings.IBR_Gods_Workers_tt:
This will doubtlessly worsen the conditions of Iberia's poor.
This will doubtlessly worsen the efficiency of our industries.
strings.IBR_The_Battle_for_Energy_tt:
This will doubtlessly worsen the conditions of Iberia's poor.
This will doubtlessly worsen the expertise available to our industries.
strings.IBR_Protecting_the_National_Product_tt:
This will doubtlessly worsen the conditions of Iberia's poor.
This will doubtlessly worsen the function of our agricultural industries.
strings.IBR_The_Military_First_tt: This will doubtlessly worsen the conditions of Iberia's poor.
strings.IBR_blessed_is_the_simple_man_tt: This will doubtlessly worsen the conditions of Iberia's poor.
strings.IBR_just_enough_on_the_plate_tt: This will drastically worsen the conditions of Iberia's people.
strings.IBR_crush_the_masons_tt: This will decrease the influence of the Opus Dei in the country.
strings.IBR_the_ascetics_of_jesus_tt: This will drastically worsen the conditions of Iberia's people.
strings.IBR_auth_congress_politics_desc:
Though Iberia has endured for almost twenty years, that time has not been without difficulty. We have endured numerous challenges and crises, and though we have overcome them, we must understand - using the countless examples of failed states - that adaptation is necessary.

Nearly ten years ago, the creation of the Iberian Council was one such adaptation, and it served the state well, cementing the reign of our enlightened Caudillos. We will continue to fight for their values, but we will remember the need to embrace change.
strings.IBR_Honour_the_Family_desc:
The foundation of Iberian culture, of Iberian identity, is the family. Everything revolves around that institution, from daily life to, in a representative sense, the relationship between citizen and state. There have been many voices claiming the family to be under threat by corrosive influences, but we understand the truth.

The truth that change must be embraced, as long as it does not threaten the foundation. American music, women working, and the dozen other 'evils' claimed by many are merely superficial - as long as the family exists, as long as the state exists, that change can be accepted.
strings.IBR_Unified_Authority_desc:
No one can deny the legacy Franco and Caetano have built for themselves, but no one can deny that such a legacy has not been without Its excesses. Visionary as they are, the Caudillos require a governing body to assist them in ruling the Iberian Union and it is the Legislative Council that shall fill that role, as much to curtail their less presentable impulses as to ensure their genuine ambitions to uplift Iberian society are cleanly implemented.

The Council will soon become an institution to be exhorted and venerated, with civil servants and scholarly legalists from all over working tirelessly to one day serve in Its hallowed chambers to proctor the course of the Union with justice and temperance.
strings.IBR_The_Other_House_of_Christ_desc:
The distancing of the Church and its clergy within Iberia from the state is a worrying trend. We cannot, however, take direct action against it - their pervasive influence, turned against us, would be a lethal threat. So we must be careful, and limit their turn to, at worst, one of neutral ambivalence.

We can take action against individuals who turn outspoken against the Caudillos and the Union, but we must take care to restrict action and maintain a friendly demeanor to the Church as an institution. The stability of the state demands such.
strings.IBR_Academic_Prevention_desc:
It is, has, and likely will always be the case that the universities, despite their essential purpose, remain hotbeds of anti-government activism. We can act to ameliorate this somewhat, however, by embedding agents of the Ministry of the Interior within them, allowing subversives to be identified early.

Many on the academic staff will oppose this, but they can be managed. Those so opposed can have their careers managed, have academic opportunities denied and, thus, be rendered subservient if they wish to remain in their positions. As they certainly do.
strings.IBR_Show_You_Are_Worthy_desc:
A particularly onerous example that the Caudillos are mortal men whose judgements that can be appropriately flawed as any other is ubiquity of nepotism in government appointments. Franco, Salazar and Caetano have all been guilty of placing close friends and family members in positions of power in Madrid and Lisbon, something that simply can not continue if the Iberian Union is to improve itself as a modern society.

By relocating politicized appointments to positions of much more limited authority, we can set about reorienting government appointments along more meritocratic processes. Recognition of experienced and trustworthy government employees from among the Civil Service and elsewhere are to provide a new generation of capable administrators, as well as newer initiatives to begin talent pooling from the Private Sector where applicable.
strings.IBR_New_Trade_Unionism_desc:
Despite the valuable service they provide, it is an open secret that the state-controlled trade unions are severely disliked by both workers and businessmen across Iberia, with commensurate inefficiencies resulting. We can act to correct this by allowing the formation of a small number of non-state controlled unions.

They will be apolitical, required to have state union representatives, and submit to inspections to central authorities. The state apparatus will, of course, be displeased, but they will have to accept change. Economic prosperity demands it.
strings.IBR_Youth_Investments_desc:
While nationalist youth organizations might seem passé in the new decade, they are just as valid a font for long-term nation building as they were in the 1930s. The Germans have done a truly pestilential job in alienating most European nations to the concept through the vile imagery of arm-banded children with upraised arms in Hitlarian salutes, which may indeed be a reason why Iberia's youth groups must be cultivated with care.

As part of a government expansion of Iberian youth organizations, these groups will offer job programs for their members and be granted a greater presence within Iberia's metropolitan cities. Right as rain, membership is bound to soar as they become the place to be for young Spaniards and Portuguese, which the government is sure to capitalize on in head-hunting for capable young men who may well become the men to rule the Iberia of the coming generation.
strings.IBR_Refocus_Censorship_desc:
The oppression and censorship of artists and press outlets under authoritarian regimes are well-known and longstanding. If the Iberian Union is to reorient itself as a nation of moderation and modernity, this practice must be reevaluated, lest we once again be lumped in with the worst offenders of similar policies in Germania, Rome, and Tokyo.

While overtly politicized art and press will be strictly regulated, the majority of independent artists and journalists are to be left alone. Iberia no longer wishes to waste any time or resources on petty and frivolous political witch hunts. Spain and Portugal's long-standing reputation for artistic expression should continue for centuries more, if for no other reason than the easy public relations windfall as Iberia presents itself as a Union that aims to celebrate Its cultural richness, not erode it.
strings.IBR_General_Law_of_Education_desc:
Economic prosperity does not drop into our hands like a coconut from a tree, at the mere hand wave of a politician. No, economic prosperity is decided years, if not decades in advance, in the classrooms and gymnasiums of the everyday citizen, their knowledge and expertise providing a robust foundation upon which glory will grow in the years following.

With the General Law of Education, we will take back the initiative, making school compulsory for boys and girls alike until the age of 14, in addition to streamlining university admission systems. Cutting edge trades and skills will be taught, and the conditions which our teachers find themselves in shall be improved.
strings.IBR_Experts_Know_Best_desc:
The technocrats owe their positions - and their influence - to the correctness of their predictions, policies, and plans of action. They are experts in their fields, and if we wish to encourage change, we must have expert advice.

In particular, many of them possess extensive knowledge of economics, and as we work to rebuild and expand our economy and economic health, we should, and will, leverage that knowledge, and incorporate their advice into state policy.
strings.IBR_The_New_Iberian_Woman_desc:
How can we claim to be adapting our administration to the modern age, when half our country is still being left behind in the process? How can we tout advancement, when it is only the man who benefits from our new reforms?

The Iberian Woman shall not be left behind - restrictions will be reduced, women shall be allowed to do more without the signing off of their husband, provided certain criteria are met. In order to involve them in this new process, suffrage laws will be eased as well. This “New Iberian Woman” initiative shall serve as a hallmark of the new council.
strings.IBR_Reform_the_Axencia_desc:
Though met with many roadblocks at first, the admittedly hastily organized counter-terrorism capabilities of the AAS in the past several years have given us a base of institutional counter-terrorism knowledge we must capitalize on.

With these reforms, the Axencia will become a fully-fledged counter-terrorism branch, making use of existing knowledge while further narrowing its mission, allowing it to operate at full efficiency in service of the state. A pipeline will be set up in the military and intelligence communities in order to funnel aspiring talent into the organization, clearing the way for a new generation of administrators and operatives unburdened by past inefficiencies.
strings.IBR_The_Other_Cheek_desc:
The whole object of the Iberian Union's existence as a sovereign state is to preserve a solitary enclave of rational society in continental Europe, defiantly austere against the escalating mania of Nazi rule in Germany. While the effort to ensure the Union's survival often requires a heavy hand, the regime in Iberia knows that a measured approach to the opposition is sometimes necessary to prevent counterproductive violence against political enemies.

Conservatives on the Council may blanch at the prospect of offering amnesty, but the situation in Iberia requires a deft touch. While the targeting of opposition leaders will continue, reprisals against individual affiliates will be reined in as a gesture of good faith. This will aid in defanging a lot of the criticism over authoritarian overreach, even if persecution of violent detractors and potential terrorists remains just as relentless.
strings.IBR_Happy_Soldiers_desc:
The primacy of the militaries of Spain and Portugal remains a key example of the power structure in Iberia, even under the new regime of the Iberian Council. While the men of the general staff and upper officer corps enjoy a hearty share of the Iberian Union's political capital, with all the benefits and personal luxuries that entails, the same can't always be said for the mid-level officers, who form a crucial link in the chain of command between the boots on the ground and the high command in Madrid and Lisbon.

In a gesture to ensure the loyalty of the mid-level officers to the new status quo in Iberia, quality of living standards for the barracks is to be improved along with a healthy increase to the mid-level officers back pay. This will help to quell any resentment among the bottom ranks of the Iberian military structure and grant us some welcome support and respect from the men in uniform.
strings.IBR_Rotate_the_High_Command_desc:
As we move to advance change, we must acknowledge the reality of the state of our high command. Many officers occupying higher placements have been in their roles for many years and, in some cases, decades. We must act to increase turnover, and will do so by reducing the expected retirement age.

Experts have advised that this will slowly encourage the exit of more radical elements and clear the way for younger, more politically neutral officers to advance - a strongly desired outcome.
strings.IBR_African_Militarization_ac_desc:
The ever-present whispers of defiance, and perhaps even revolt, have-as of late-intensified. Perhaps the native feels emboldened by changes in the global political climate. Perhaps foreign actors presently attempt to spur him into rebelion. Whatever the cause of the recent unrest, the renewal of our colonial commitments is a strategic imperative.

Although they may not be the most motivated or useful troops, the organization of natives into auxiliary military units will prevent their recruitment by violent opposition forces. Additionally this will allow our most effective troops-native Iberians-will be available in greater quantities where they are most needed. Military installations in fortifications will further preserve our manpower. These adjustments will enable us to fight, if need be, a protracted war against an irregular force.
strings.IBR_A_Future_for_Africa_desc:
The best opportunity the native has at achieving civilization is through continuing Iberian supremacy in his land. While this fundamental order will persevere, as the native approaches civilized status he will be allowed a greater involvement in the governance of the lands he occupies. All participants in this arrangement shall benefit; we see our administrative burden reduced and the native obtains meaningful education.

And should the relationship between our nation and those we are tasked with uplifting change, as to alter this fundamental order, a class appreciative of our interventions will be the recipients of sovereignty, enabling continued constructive engagement.
strings.IBR_Home_Grown_Governors_desc:
A frequent criticism of past policies of regional administration was the choice of choosing governors unfamiliar with the areas they were appointed to. This caused no end of problems, and is a policy that must be corrected, through the identification and appointment of governors native to or experienced with their assignments.

People who know their regions, know the people of importance, know the allowances to be given and balances to be maintained, will serve better. And, of course, their popularity will naturally transfer to the state, as well.
strings.IBR_The_Dustbin_of_History_desc:
Every previous government decision was made for a reason. Every procurement, trade deal, diplomatic gesture or political neutralization had purpose behind them, and we must keep this in mind.People who were removed from positions of influence were removed for cause, and we will not backtrack.

Current administrator cadres are perfectly sufficient to execute policy, and those who fear we may be going too far in certain respects can be reassured that those who opposed - or will oppose - state action will remain in the wilderness where they belong.
strings.IBR_Welcome_to_Iberia_desc:
Even amidst the hectic pace of the Cold War, Tourism is still a ready and reliable form of revenue for most of Europe. Both Spain and Portugal's reputations for idyllic natural beauty and historic metropole are just as relevant for attracting foreigners on vacation as any other form of mercantilism. Not one to miss out on cultivating an easy source of income, the Council has signed off on provisions to aid in developing Iberia's tourism industry.

From expansions of Iberian airline travel for the influx of visitors, to money grants for coastal towns and major cities for tourist attractions and accommodations. Iberia lives and breathes by being one of the few nations left in continental Europe existing free of the lunacy gripping our northern neighbors, therefore it makes the most sense to raise a profit for granting the people of the world a place to rest their heads in the sun.
strings.IBR_Welcome_to_Iberia_tt: We will gain a new source of income worth $$100 Million.
strings.IBR_The_Sum_of_Its_Parts_desc:
As much as the hardliners prefer cultivating a greater Iberian national identity, there is no avoiding the fact that Iberia is primarily constituted with two wholly unique societies and cultures, despite their shared history. The only sensible way forward for either constituency is continued acknowledgement of, and mutual respect for, the differences of the other; One foot in front of the next, one hand grasping the other.

Yet there is more to the Iberian Union than just the Spanish and Portuguese. Nearly the whole of the free world, From the Caribbean to Central and South America, represents over one eighth of the Earth's landmass and carries a legacy that is intrinsically tied with that of our own. Through these shared languages across the Andes and the Amazon, Iberia will rekindle her ties to the western world, once more taking a paternalistic approach to her former colonial empires.
strings.IBR_Green_Productivity_desc:
While the days of the fascist powers revolutionizing the agricultural output of Europe is looked upon with fondness in Iberia, newer advancements have surpassed even the advancements imposed by the likes of Franco, Salazar and Mussolini. Italy in particular has long been celebrated as the breadbasket of the Mediterranean, but Spain and Portugal have proven worthy contenders for such a distinction in their own right, something this new technology is sure to push forward in our favor.

As part of an agricultural revitalization program, farmers are to be provided with top-notch farming equipment and technology, alongside consultation with the Ministry of Agriculture to encourage new farming methods. This increase in production will help introduce new industry into the countryside. Iberia might be a long way off from eclipsing Italian agri-buisness, but this effort is certainly a step in the right direction.
strings.IBR_Iberian_Wide_TV_desc:
One could scarcely imagine the advent of the television a mere generation ago, but the near-ubiquity of the medium speaks for itself. In Iberia, the state-operated television networks of the Portuguese RTP and the Spanish RTVE represent nationally oriented programming for the constituent halves of the Iberian Union. While ether networks have proven their worth as national television providers, the time has come to begin consolidating the networks into a unified national program.

As part of this initiative to create a new national television program, RTP and RTVE's secondary channels are to be merged to form a test bed for a peninsula-wide channel. In addition, infrastructure to support television broadcasts in the Canaries, Azores, and Madeira will be improved to ensure the population in Iberia's peripheries have reliable access to both foreign channels and national networks.
strings.IBR_Season_Thaw_desc:
It was easy for the political class of the Iberian Union to sneer in poorly-disguised condescension at the Reformist Wing of the Iberian Council, their foolish haste to try and topple everything we have worked so hard to build only serving to upend their scheme before it even got off the ground.

Yet truth be told, reform was inevitable in the Iberian Union, it just needed a guiding hand to see it molded to the state's benefit. Many among the upper echelons of the Iberian power structure now grow pale at the notion of reforms coming to sweep away the worst of their excesses, but our methodical approach in implementing has ensured there is little they can do in resisting the change without facing reprisal. The Iberian Council is no longer just an administrative body, but a monument to the institutional virility of a new and reinvigorated Iberian Union!
strings.IBR_The_Iberian_System_desc:
In truth, it was Spain and Portugal that emerged victorious in the Second World War, the simplicity of the matter is that few in Europe were of a mind to see it clearly, however unhumble it may sound. What else can be said of the former Axis powers that has not been said already? Italy rests on a bed of nails after the Oil Crisis, Japan stares down the barrel of a resurgent China and the once mighty Germany continues to throttle itself to death amidst a mire of efficiency and decline.

Iberia stands as the sterling example of all Europe, a union that not only refused to compromise itself with Its former Axis partners or Its emmenant rivals to the west, but reforged itself into a contemporary nation that honors both modernity and tradition in just the right combination. Not one can deny us, not one can defy us!
¡Viva España!
¡Viva Portugal!
¡Viva Iberia!
strings.IBR_Storm_Next_Door_desc: There has been a vast power vacuum in Algeria for decades now, just waiting to be filled. Now, with the Burgundian invasion of France, this vacuum has grown even wider. With France's loss in the Burgundian war comes also the loss to any pretences of French legitimacy in the region. They are incapable of protecting their own European borders, never mind those of their colonial belongings. We would be fools to let this ultimate opportunity slip by us and allow Algeria to remain an official French territory, or worse yet, allow it to fall into the hands of our Italian rivals. Instead, we shall lay claim to this region as a rightful part of the Iberian Union. How exactly we go about this plan will no doubt be debated extensively in the coming days.
strings.IBR_Storm_Next_Door_tt: The Clouds over Algiers choke out the sun.
strings.IBR_Lifeline_Algiers_desc:
In order to go through with our new plans for Algeria, we will need to inform Jorge Jardim of these latest developments in our Algerian policy. Jardim is our main man over down Algeria way and shall be needed to keep up with any sudden changes to our advances over the region. Any plan, formulation or strategy will need to run past him in order to make sure chaos does not reign over Iberian controlled Algeria.

These are amongst the most critical moments in the campaign and thus, to put a step wrong now could doom the entire endeavor to monumental failure. In order to avoid such a calamity, Jardim will need to be thoroughly debriefed. He shall need the knowledge from this debriefing to keep order during this critical time. For if anarchy reigns during this demanding occasion, then all shall be lost before the intervention has even begun. Jardim will certainly need to keep on top of things and we shall do our best to keep him informed of all the latest developments.
strings.IBR_Lifeline_Algiers_tt: Contact with Algiers will be vital in determining our intervention plan.
strings.IBR_Emergency_Meetings_desc:
The situation down in Algeria is reaching a critical point. Tensions grow by the day and complete and utter chaos could break out at any second. If we wait too long, then our Italian rivals may be able to get the upper hand. In order to avoid this great tragedy, emergency meetings between the Caudillos of Iberia and the top echelons of the Iberian military will need to be arranged post haste.

The reasoning behind these meetings are simple. Plans need to be arranged, and rather quickly, in order to gauge how best to handle the ever-growing situation in Algeria. If something isn't agreed upon quickly then the opportunity provided to us will slip from our grasp. But we shall fear not, for our top men are on the case to come up with a solution for the Algerian problem.
strings.IBR_Change_in_Management_desc:
The important and crucial emergency sessions that were arranged to formulate a plan for the ever-escalating Algerian situation have reached a thankful conclusion. General Kaúlza has come up with quite the plan to tackle the Algerian conundrum and has managed to convince both the top brass and the Iberian political elite that his formula for Iberian domination in Algeria is foolproof.

The general's plan involves the following steps. The first step is an embarking of covert operations in the region, following along a strategy of tension that will help the settlers see the benefits of Iberian rule over the entirety of the region. The next step is to arm the (mostly Portuguese) settlers that inhabit Algeria and train them in the proper self defence stylings in order to stave off any would-be settler killer that dare strike out at our citizens. The final step is a surprise attack that will knock out our enemies quickly with such vigor, they won't even know what hit them. It's truly a great plan from General Kaúlza that we hope to replicate with great precision and ability.
strings.IBR_reformist_tt_32: Seizing Algiers for ourselves will make reformism weaker in the Council.
strings.IBR_Arms_to_Settlers_desc:
In order to prepare properly for General Kaúlza's plan, we will need to send some much needed supplies to our settlers in Algeria. The mostly Portuguese settlers are amongst our most rabidly loyal citizens, and are deeply committed to the Iberian dream and all of its colonial ambitions. To take on the white man's burden with such tenacity is surely something to behold.

We will need to back their idealism in the form of guns and training programs, to make sure they are properly equipped with the skills necessary to take on the Italians and their barbarian allies. However, once the settlers are equipped with the training of our most capable officers and our most modern military equipment, then they shall be turned into a truly unstoppable force.
strings.IBR_Plausible_Deniability_desc:
Any man with half his brain working can see things are going awry in Algeria. Chaos, anarchy, and sectarian violence threaten to engulf the entire region. Order will have to be kept to avert disaster and it falls upon us to deliver this order.

This is of course what we will be telling the rest of the world when our volunteers are moved into Algeria. It helps to keep up appearances these days and a certain level of plausible deniability cannot go amiss. In actuality, our brave boys will be preparing for the surprise attack against the Italians and any desert rat who dares stand up to us. They won't see it coming, even though it's staring them right in the face.
strings.IBR_Air_Bridge_Oran_desc:
Preparation in these early stages is key. Being negligent now can doom the entire project to failure and put our brave men at a serious disadvantage. This kind of opportunity does not come around often and to waste it now would be a disastrous stain on this governments record. Thus, it's time to set some proper planning into motion and get ready for the coming war.

In order to properly gain the advantage in terms of equipment over enemy forces, we have come up with a remarkable plan. Shedloads of military equipment and high-grade weaponry will be sent by plane over to Oran. Through this method, we can really start to set up the infrastructure that can handle an all-out war in the future.
strings.IBR_Mamae_Sumae_desc:
The job that is laying the groundwork for our invasion into Italian Algeria can only be handled by some of our best operatives. As well prepared as the settlers are, and as much faith we have in our normal army units, this job requires a more professional touch. For this reason, we shall use General Kaúlza's greatest commando forces to start setting the invasion plans up and putting them into an unstoppable motion.

These men are amongst our very best and they will not let us down in these vital key stages of the pre-campaign. In order to become ready and set up the commandos shall land in Algeria, ready and prepared to inflict proper damage to the enemy. The Italians and any would-be “liberator” native will be outmatched by the fearsome prowess of these commandos and the enemy is certainly going to be in for a shock when our forces hit them with everything they've got.
strings.IBR_Prepare_the_Strike_desc:
Our agents, marines, and settlers have done great work in laying the groundwork for the military strike that will allow us to take full control over Algeria. Armaments, weaponry and manpower have been strategically sent out across the colony, ready to be used to wipe any enemy presence straight off the map.

Now, some of the most important preparations are underway for the first direct strike against the sordid Italians. It is of great importance that the Italians cannot know of these preparations or we shall lose the great advantage of a surprise attack. Our men will have to be careful but we have full faith in their abilities. The Italians will soon come face to face with the surprise of a lifetime once we are finally ready to hit out against them. It will be a truly glorious sight to see our sudden victory against such a lacklustre enemy.
strings.IBR_Operation_Don_Henrique_desc:
The day of the great surprise attack against the Italian is almost upon us! Soon, the wrath of our well-prepared forces will come striking down with an almighty fury on the unsuspecting enemy. All of our soldiers are waiting and ready for the Caudillos' command and all are eager for the strike to finally take place.

The Caudillos themselves are no doubt proud of this, soon to be historic, operation. Salazar himself insisted on naming the operation after the famed Portuguese explorer Dom Henrique, in order to honor the Portuguese settlers who have become an intrinsic part of the operation. Franco, though, has also insisted on having him referred to by the Spanish title of “Don”. No doubt showing that some friendly rivalry is still alive back in Iberia.

It matters little though, for our forces are here to do one thing and one thing only: Take out the enemy in one fell swoop, thus securing Algeria all for ourselves. No French, no Italians and no native can hope to stop us in our crusade to secure Algeria. This event shall prove the supremacy of the Iberian nation and shall showcase our military prowess to the world.
strings.IBR_Returning_the_favor_desc:
Picking a superpower to work with is perhaps one of the greatest decisions Iberia will ever make. Having an international patron is very important, and their aid will allow us to assert ourselves in ways we never could otherwise. This wasn't a particularly hard choice, either - the Americans are far better than a callous government two continents away or the same bastards that stole everything from the Iberians.

Of course, the only way to show a country you want to make friends is to angle yourself correctly. The best way to get the attention of the United States is to give them some help in very important places. Since they seem to be occupied down in South Africa, perhaps the best chance to help out is wide open. Giving particular support to this plan is Salazar, who has been spearheading the effort to increase Iberia's relevance in Africa.
strings.IBR_Returning_the_favor_tt: We should help the Yankees in South Africa after they helped us deal with the Santa Maria hijacking.
strings.IBR_Music_Concert_desc:
The National Women's Movement has never ceased to be a great boon to Iberia. They are of upstanding moral character, making very good care workers, and frequent volunteers. All we need to do is so much as ask and they will be willing to help, and more often than not have someone able to do what is needed.

It is said that a good song can lighten even the darkest heart, and there are many dark hearts in wartime. The American soldiers stationed in South Africa would most likely appreciate someone to sing for them, and for a sweet melody to raise their spirits. The Women's Movement has many talented singers in it, and they can be sent to Africa to play for the American troops. The concerts will be funded by us fully, and they are sure to appreciate what we can do for them.
strings.IBR_Navy_Exercises_desc:
The American navy is very adept at what they do; It is only logical for a world power to have a great sailing force, able to dominate the waters. Since American relations seem to be improving, it may be possible that they would be willing to participate in a few mutually beneficial programs. All it will take to bring them around to it will be a small amount of persuasion, and then some competent scheduling.

It is no secret that the Iberian and American naval fleets have a world of difference between them, with different doctrines, tactics, and officers all creating a vast gap between the two. Opposites attract, and a contrast of naval styles could prove very helpful. To this end, arrangements will be made for a joint naval exercise, which will prove invaluable in providing intelligence to better improve our strategies.
strings.IBR_Lease_Sao_Tome_desc:
São Tomé. One of the only Portuguese colonies to resist German incursion, and a stable and pleasant island. The island is a darling of Portugal, not for its beauty, but for its importance. It was first colonized to serve as a waypoint in the long and treacherous journey to India. Even though it has been centuries since then, and decades since the last time the island was necessary, it is not without use. The island is in a location of immense tactical value, able to serve as a dock for ships and a point through which to filter supplies. It is for these reasons that the Americans want to use it.

As a gesture of goodwill, we can effectively rent out the island to them, and allow them to use it as they please - so long as it is given back to us in fair shape. It so happens, conveniently, that a fair sum of money can be made off the deal.
strings.IBR_Provide_the_Maps_desc:
The Germans took the Portuguese colonies from their original owners. Ripping out the pride and soul of half of the Union, it was nothing short of an act of cruelty. Worst of all were the retornados, who were forced to flee their homelands to escape the tyranny that would affect them. The heart wrenching stories of those who have truly lost everything have made a very strong case to the government.

Therefore, it is about time they got their revenge. If the Portuguese shall not have it, then the Germans assuredly won't either. Even though they seemingly took everything, there is something very important they failed to take. We still have the map of assets around Angola and it is unlikely that Germany has modified anything. It would be a shame if that map were to be given to the Americans, so that they could disable the infrastructure when they find necessary.
strings.IBR_Green_Berets_Bissau_desc:
Africa is a vast place, with many different environments. What no-one will tell you is that these environments are less different than one would think, and there is a lot of crossover between them. For example, there are many skills you can learn in one place that you could make use of in another. It is only logical that the Americans would appreciate learning some skills for their time in South Africa.

We will open up Portuguese Guinea to the United States military, and in particular invite their special forces to come train in the area. They could use the practice to fight better in the hostile environments of Africa, where Guinea could prove a valuable introduction to it.
strings.IBR_Cancioneiro_Niassa_desc:
The mission of the Portuguese in Angola, their divinely ordained duty, was to civilize the people there. Since the Portuguese were chased away by the Nazis, that job was left only half-finished. Yet still, the history of Portuguese colonialism in the region is something that can be used to our advantage. One of the first things the settlers did was teach the inhabitants Portuguese, in order to better communicate with the natives. Portuguese language is by no means universal, but a significant enough number of Africans in the former colonies know the language to make alternative operations practical.

We will deploy forces able to use the power of song and voice to strike fear into the Africans fighting under German command, turning their traditions and customs against them. These operations will harm their morale, allowing the Americans a better chance.
strings.IBR_Airborne_Nurses_desc:
Some of the Portuguese are without a doubt brave. That, or they are just thrill-seekers. Either way, their willingness can be put to good use in service of the Americans. Medics are not always on time, nor can they get to some places easily on land. What makes it worse is that they can't always get where they need to be by air, either - as they would have nowhere to land. The Portuguese airborne nurses have been created to solve that problem.

They will parachute out of helicopters and other aircraft at high altitudes, into hostile conditions, in order to save lives. Through thick and thin, no matter the risk. It is here that the bravest will shine, and those who are in it for a thrill will get exactly what they want. They will be like angels from heaven, come to bring salvation to those in need.
strings.IBR_Counter_Insurgency: The Back of Our Own Hands
strings.IBR_Counter_Insurgency_desc: Many of our retornados were natural outdoorsmen, and have never truly forgotten their old home. We shall form special advance elements utilizing their experience which will give us and our allies a notable boost on the battlefields of Mozambique and Angola.
strings.IBR_New_Viritatos_desc:
Iberia has sent quite a few Portuguese down to the south of Africa. No matter how many we send, it just doesn't seem to be enough. Clearly the mistake was prioritizing quality over quantity so highly, as we have sent barely anyone. Any advantage is quickly nullified by the total lack of people to capitalize on it. As it were, we will be sacrificing a bit of that fighting quality for numbers.

To this end we will reform the Viriatos volunteer divisions, originally deployed to Spain to assist Franco, many years ago. Many brave Portuguese men will be able to taste the honor of battle, made all the sweeter by revenge. They will not rest until Angola and Mozambique have been avenged!
strings.IBR_divorce_game_over_tt:
THERE IS NO CONTENT BEYOND THE DIVORCE TREE.

Spain and Portugal have no content in this release of TNO!
strings.IBR_duet_max_rep_tt: This Interest Group is not already at its maximum alignment with the Caudillo.
strings.IBR_duet_not_solo_tt:
Both Caudillos will increase their influence with Interest Groups within The National Duet.
They will prioritize winning back support of groups aligned with the other Caudillo.
strings.IBR_duet_not_solo_caetano_addendum_tt: If Caetano is the more influential Caudillo, him and his faction will gain influence. Otherwise, they will lose influence.
strings.IBR_legislative_project_tt: We will unlock a new legislative project.
strings.IBR_healthcare_legislation_desc: Our National Healthcare Programs have been suffering from a myriad of problems ever since the Union's founding during the 50s. As the Iberian Government begins to make strides in standardizing the Union, tackling the issue of health security should be one of our biggest priorities, however it requires a delicate hand. This legislation aims to bridge the gap until that day comes. It includes the expansion of funding and start of an auditing process to ensure funds are allocated and used properly.
strings.IBR_salazar_military_decision_tt: Salazar will try to sway the military to his side.
strings.IBR_franco_morocco_decision_tt: Franco will try to sway the colonial settlers and natives to his side.
strings.IBR_salazar_church_decision_tt: Salazar will try to sway the Church to his side.
strings.IBR_franco_business_decision_tt: Franco will try to sway the businessmen to his side.
strings.IBR_salazar_intellectuals_decision_tt: Salazar will try to sway the intellectuals to his side.
strings.IBR_franco_bureaucrat_decision_tt: Franco will try to sway the bureaucrats to his side.
strings.IBR_salazar_settlers_generic_desc: In order to improve the Portuguese side of the Union's standing with the settlers, plans will be executed to improve the conditions of settlers living in our sub-Saharan colonial holdings. These will come via the form of subsidies both to individuals and private entities meant to boost living conditions and economic growth.“
strings.IBR_salazar_natives_generic_desc: Across our colonial holdings there exist brave locals which help ensure our rule becomes as stable and efficient as possible. Whether they be policemen, bureaucrats or fulfilling any other job, such individuals must be rewards for their services, ensuring that will boost our standing with the natives and incentivize further collaboration.
strings.IBR_salazar_military_generic_desc: The Federal Conscription Efforts have their own series of problems that worsen the quality of our armed forces, something that must be solved given the growing storms in our interest zones. Even applying band-aid fixes will help us and any effort taken in this regard is sure to boost the initiator's standing with the armed forces.
strings.IBR_salazar_bureaucrats_generic_desc: Auditing private enterprises is the best way to ensure industrial regulations are followed, sadly the Union's ability to perform in this regard suffers from the same woes other aspects of administration suffers from. Acting to fix this as quickly as possible would be a must before the situation deteriorates further, the fact our bureaucrats would be overjoyed by this plan is an extra boon.
strings.IBR_salazar_foreign_generic_desc: Streamlining certain aspects of our immigration and customs process is sure to win us the favour of foreigners by making it easier for them to visit Iberia.
strings.IBR_salazar_church_generic_desc: The Concordat Portugal signed with the Vatican permits the establishment of Catholic schools across the country, a matter which is still applicable now that they are part of the Iberian Funding. Providing subsidies to such institutions will increase the quality of the services they provide and put the Portuguese side of the Union in the good graces of the Church.
strings.IBR_salazar_businessmen_generic_desc: The Portguese side of the Union is renowned for its tungsten it provides to the global market, helping businesses that are part of this economic process, be it mining, logistics or exporting will surely prove a lucrative venture. Of equal importance is the fact it will boost our standing with the businessmen.
strings.IBR_franco_settlers_generic_desc: In order to improve the Franco's standing with the settlers, efforts will be undertaken to improve policing in the colonies. Making the settlers feel safe will increase the efficiency of all other colonial affairs.
strings.IBR_franco_natives_generic_desc: Those willing to collaborate with us in upholding our law and order across our colonial holdings must be rewarded, yes, but the best way to ensure this would be to simply pay them more. After all, if the best paying jobs are those that benefit the Union, then collaboration becomes the most profitable option.
strings.IBR_franco_military_generic_desc: The Federal Armed Forces suffer from several deficiencies in their trainning process which could be fixed if given enough time and resources. While a full reform would be preferable, these smaller changes may still save lives of our soldiers should they end up on the battlefield.
strings.IBR_franco_bureaucrats_generic_desc: The Union's income taxation system is plagued by administrative inefficiencies that have existed since the funding of the Union and the Spanish side of the Union has come forth with solutions. Working to remove such flaws from our system will surely put the good graces of our bureaucrats and boost the popularity of the reform's initiators.
strings.IBR_franco_foreign_generic_desc: The simplest way to win the favour of other nations is to prove Iberia is a power that can provide, and there is nothing more important to provide than a show of force, or in this case, of wealth.
strings.IBR_franco_church_generic_desc: Across Iberia there exist many abbeys that suffer from a lack of funding which hampers their activities and results in buildings with rich historical legacies deteriorating under the strain of time. Allocating funds to these holy buildings will permit reconstruction efforts, allow better care of their surrounding lands and more importantly, it will put us in the good graces of the Church.
strings.IBR_franco_businessmen_generic_desc: Our current tariff regulation for imports causes stirs among the Union's business circles due to problems such as inefficiency and corruption. Working to fix such issues, alongside offering help to our local manufacturers will surely win us the favor of businessmen from across the Union.
strings.IBR_pp_post_trium_get_tt:
The entire Union will suffer from the Collapse.

A new course needs to be charted...

We will unlock £decision_icon_small Decisions in which Franco will attempt to deal with the problems facing Iberia.
strings.IBR_pp_foreign_get_tt: This will unlock £decision_icon_small Decisions in which Salazar will attempt to deal with Iberia's foreign policy.
strings.IBR_pp_terrorism_get_tt: This will unlock £decision_icon_small Decisions in which Franco will attempt to deal with terrorism in Iberia.
strings.IBR_pp_economics_get_tt: This will unlock £decision_icon_small Decisions in which Salazar will attempt to deal with Iberia's economic problems.
strings.IBR_pp_stability_get_tt: This will unlock £decision_icon_small Decisions in which Franco will attempt to deal with political instability in Iberia.
strings.IBR_pp_post_trium_category_desc:
The dissolution of the Triumvirate has been a wake-up call for Iberia, with the government scrambling to keep the Union afloat. In the wake of its collapse, Caudillo Franco has taken it upon himself to lead the effort in making long overdue changes to improve Iberia's internal stability, as well as strengthening her position in the Mediterranean.

Despite being sorely needed, making these decisions will doubtless make Franco new enemies across Iberian society.
Were Franco's popularity to fall significantly during this trying time, the stability of the nation could be in jeopardy when he is needed the most.
strings.IBR_post_trium_military_decision_desc: Complacent yes-men and careerists are leading several of our garrisons. They must be reassigned.
strings.IBR_post_trium_church_decision_desc: The men of the Opus Dei should be compensated for their aid to Iberia, despite much of the population's skepticism.
strings.IBR_post_trium_intellectuals_decision_de: Our influence in Academia is waning; embedding favorable representatives there is crucial.
strings.IBR_post_trium_settlers_decision_desc: If there is to be peace in our colonies, the most ardent Portuguese settlers must be neutered.
