strings.IBR_post_trium_natives_decision_desc: There can be no discussion of dissolution. This is all Iberian land.
strings.IBR_post_trium_foreign_decision_desc: We will let the Italians know that we condemn their aggressive posturing in Algeria.
strings.IBR_post_trium_majority_decision_desc: In order to make the Union run smoothly, some national quirks must be sidelined.
strings.IBR_post_trium_regional_decision: Uphold the Status of Spanish and Portuguese
strings.IBR_post_trium_regional_decision_desc: All citizens of Iberia must know that there are only two languages of the land.
strings.IBR_post_trium_regional_decision_tt: This action will have grave consequences down the line.
strings.IBR_pp_foreign_category_desc:
With the Algeria situation behind her, Iberia is ready to step onto the world stage, with Caudillo Salazar leading initiatives overseas. His greatest focus lies in reaching out to former colonies in attempts to reach mutually beneficial partnerships, but Iberia's current colonies also require additional attention.

Despite the fact that Iberia's standing in the world could be greatly strengthened, making these decisions will doubtless make Salazar new enemies across Iberia, her colonies, and around the world.
Were Salazar's popularity to fall significantly during this trying time, the stability of the nation could be in jeopardy when he is needed the most.
strings.IBR_foreign_military_decision: Decide the Fate of Equatorial Guinea
strings.IBR_foreign_military_decision_desc: The garrison left in Central Africa is weak, and is draining our resources. We cannot, as a self-respecting power, let this show be run by the natives. Reinforcements will be sent and further investments in the region will be made.
strings.IBR_foreign_military_decision_tt: This action will unlock a new Development Project in Equatorial Guinea.
strings.IBR_foreign_bureaucrat_decision: Reorganize the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
strings.IBR_foreign_bureaucrat_decision_desc: There are far too many conflicting cliques vying for power in the ministry. There no longer will be.
strings.IBR_foreign_church_decision_desc: We cannot keep prioritizing relations with Catholic nations, when it is clearly in our interests to do otherwise.
strings.IBR_foreign_businessmen_decision: Impose New Tariffs on Foreign Goods
strings.IBR_foreign_businessmen_decision_desc: Strategically placed tariffs will help us pressure the governments we need to work with us.
strings.IBR_foreign_intellectuals_decision: Undermine Unhelpful Foreign Policy Think Tanks
strings.IBR_foreign_intellectuals_decision_desc: There is no room for such treasonous activism, which seeks to undermine Iberian interests.
strings.IBR_foreign_settlers_decision: Deemphasize Our Colonialism on the World Stage
strings.IBR_foreign_settlers_decision_desc: Our overseas provinces are natural extensions of Iberia; we shall make it clear that people there are treated well.
strings.IBR_foreign_natives_decision_desc: Why would we not further increase the revenue from our most profitable overseas province?
strings.IBR_foreign_foreign_decision: Stand by Claims on Angola and Mozambique
strings.IBR_foreign_foreign_decision_desc: These core parts of our very spirit were ripped from us by the Germans. It will be made abundantly clear that they are ours.
strings.IBR_foreign_foreign_decision_tt: This action may affect us in the future.
strings.IBR_foreign_majority_decision: Host Expensive Banquets with Foreign Leaders
strings.IBR_foreign_majority_decision_desc: These seemingly superfluous expenses are in fact some of the greatest investments that can be made.
strings.IBR_foreign_regional_decision: Join Anti-Separatist Efforts Across the World
strings.IBR_foreign_regional_decision_desc: Nations across the world can have something to learn from our ways in combatting separatism.
strings.IBR_foreign_regional_decision_tt: This action will surely aid us in combating such groups.
strings.IBR_pp_terrorism_category_desc:
In the wake of the bloody Battle of Barcelona, the very core of Iberia has been shaken. Emboldened by the bloodshed, separatism across the Union is strengthening. Further carnage and destruction must be stopped at all costs, and Caudillo Franco is prepared to take decisive action to crush separatism in Spain and quell nationalist sentiment in Portugal.

Despite being critical for keeping the Union together, rooting out terrorism and lessening separatist tensions will doubtless make Franco new enemies across Iberian society.
Were Franco's popularity to fall significantly during this trying time, the stability of the nation could be in jeopardy when he is needed the most.
strings.IBR_terrorism_military_decision: Divert Special Military Resources to the AAS
strings.IBR_terrorism_military_decision_desc: The military will have to take some short-term cuts to provide critical aid to the Axencia.
strings.IBR_terrorism_bureaucrat_decision: Remove Corrupt Spanish Officials in Portugal
strings.IBR_terrorism_bureaucrat_decision_desc: Those officials who have become the greatest objects of the Portuguese ire must be removed.
strings.IBR_terrorism_church_decision_desc: It is essential to keep strong ties with Basque religious community leaders, particularily in rural areas.
strings.IBR_terrorism_businessmen_decision: State Job Programs in Catalan Cities
strings.IBR_terrorism_businessmen_decision_desc: If the restless youth of Catalonia get to work, perhaps they will be less inclined to do us harm.
strings.IBR_terrorism_intellectuals_decision_des: The disgusting apologia of terrorism in our universities must be stamped down ruthlessly.
strings.IBR_terrorism_settlers_decision_desc: Our elite anti-insurgency units in North Africa are more urgently needed on the peninsula.
strings.IBR_terrorism_natives_decision_desc: We cannot let opportunists in the parts of Africa under Iberia see weakness as we face terrorism at home.
strings.IBR_terrorism_foreign_decision_desc: Certain governments will support the scum of the earth to see us fail. We will do everything in our power to stop them.
strings.IBR_terrorism_majority_decision_desc: A few token measures could ease tensions among the broader regional populations.
strings.IBR_terrorism_regional_decision: Expand Guardia Civil in Minority Regions
strings.IBR_terrorism_regional_decision_desc: There must be an unprecedented expansion of police presence in the areas where separatism is brewing.
strings.IBR_pp_economics_category_desc:
With the AAS corruption scandal behind us, Caudillo Salazar is working on directing the nation's collective focus towards restructuring its ever-struggling economy. In conjunction with the broader economic measures that will be taken in the future, the plan is to restructure failing bureaucracies and implement targeted austerity measures in anticipation for the greater reforms that are coming.

Despite the fact that Iberia's economy will be helped In the short term, making these decisions will doubtless make Salazar new enemies across Iberian society.
Were Salazar's popularity to fall significantly during this trying time, the stability of the nation could be in jeopardy when he is needed the most.
strings.IBR_economics_military_decision_desc: Our military has become bloated and excessive. Some cuts can easily be made without much risk to the nation.
strings.IBR_economics_bureaucrat_decision_desc: The Iberian bureaucracy is in some areas completely out of control, and must be tamed.
strings.IBR_economics_church_decision_desc: Organizations masquerading as religious groups should not be propped up, when they in reality profit from faith.
strings.IBR_economics_businessmen_decision_desc: Those businesses which willfully avoid taxes shall find fewer loopholes when these new measures are in place.
strings.IBR_economics_intellectuals_decision_des: Those who choose to study less worthwhile subjects, should not receive equal support.
strings.IBR_economics_settlers_decision_desc: The economic problems yet plaguing our Union require drastic measures. May the settlers forgive us for such an injustice.
strings.IBR_economics_natives_decision_desc: After all, what's the harm that an extra 4% on a ledger could do?
strings.IBR_economics_foreign_decision_desc: Iberia cannot afford to spend as much as we previously have, sending money overseas. The money is best spent here.
strings.IBR_economics_majority_decision_desc: Farmers in Iberia will do just fine with a small cut to their subsidies. No more whining.
strings.IBR_economics_regional_decision_desc: We see great promise among Spanish companies which recently have moved in to Catalonia. They deserve some support.
strings.IBR_this_is_madness: We have sufficiently lost our minds to pursue such a course of action.
strings.IBR_this_is_madness_blocked: We have sufficiently lost our minds to pursue such a course of action.
strings.IBR_pp_stability_category_desc:
In this critical time for the Union, in which the final decision regarding the Council's status is approaching, it is essential that political stability is ensured. Caudillo Franco has begun work on anti-corruption task forces, as well as pushing programs to restructure previously disloyal and mismanaged parts of the government.

Despite being critical for the Union's stability, going after powerful people and interest groups will doubtless make Franco new enemies across Iberian society.
Were Franco's popularity to fall significantly during this trying time, the stability of the nation could be in jeopardy when he is needed the most.
strings.IBR_stability_military_decision_desc: The nepotism and incompetence in the higher echelons of the military must be reduced.
strings.IBR_stability_bureaucrat_decision_desc: Corrupt bureaucrats across Iberia should be afraid if they have siphonined taxpayer money.
strings.IBR_stability_church_decision_desc: The culture of corruption in our churches is pervasive, and must be dealth with harshly.
strings.IBR_stability_businessmen_decision_desc: We will the owners of capital know that at the end of the day, we are in charge. Their profits are secondary.
strings.IBR_stability_intellectuals_decision_des: Iberia will not prosper if the halls of intelligentsia are not determined by merit. Investigations will ensue.
strings.IBR_stability_settlers_decision_desc: The money pits that are our overseas administrations are not economically nor politically sustainable.
strings.IBR_stability_natives_decision_desc: Further restrictions to the natives in our overseas provinces are neded to uphold Iberian stability at this time.
strings.IBR_stability_foreign_decision_desc: Our foreign policy must be run by those with utmost loyalty to the state, even if it means breaking a few established eggs.
strings.IBR_stability_majority_decision_desc: We have reason to believe that certain favorites of the public harbor unacceptable views. Their removal is necessary.
strings.IBR_stability_regional_decision: Restrict Local Governments in Minority Regions
strings.IBR_stability_regional_decision_desc: The special freedoms of these local governments can be revoked at any time, and this critical time is one of them.
strings.IBR_terrorism_category_desc:
Following the bloodbath in Barcelona, support for separatism is growing across Iberia. Militant groups are simultaneously growing in size and becoming more active, with the Axencia Anti-Separatista uncovering an increasing amount of new terror cells across the Union. All resources necessary, material and economic, must be diverted to support the AAS in their fight against those who would want to see Iberia burn.

Terrorism is combated from the Political Screen next to Iberia's ministers.
strings.IBR_AAS_Funding_decision_low_pp_tt: Due to lack of political power:
strings.IBR_AAS_decision_budget_cuts: Creating exceptions to our ongoing austerity program makes this more politically costly.
strings.IBR_AAS_CNT_offensive_decision_desc: Due to the critical situation in Catalonia, the army is standing by for a full assault against the DI.
strings.IBR_AAS_CNT_offensive_decision_tt:
The offensive will decrease DI Activity, Supplies, and Support by 4 each, but can only lower each value to 2.
The bloody clashes will lower Iberia's stability by [?IBR_AAS_offensive_decision_ticker_temp|Y0%%]!
strings.IBR_AAS_ETA_offensive_decision_desc: Due to the critical situation in the Basque Country, the army is standing by for a full assault against ETA.
strings.IBR_AAS_ETA_offensive_decision_tt:
The offensive will decrease ETA Activity, Supplies, and Support by 4 each, but can only lower each value to 2.
The bloody clashes will lower Iberia's stability by [?IBR_AAS_offensive_decision_ticker_temp|Y0%%]!
strings.IBR_AAS_FSLP_offensive_decision_desc: Due to the critical situation in Portugal, the army is standing by for a full assault against the BR.
strings.IBR_AAS_FSLP_offensive_decision_tt:
The offensive will decrease BR Activity, Supplies, and Support by 4 each, but can only lower each value to 2.
The bloody clashes will lower Iberia's stability by [?IBR_AAS_offensive_decision_ticker_temp|Y0%%]!
strings.IBR_AAS_BTA_offensive_decision_desc: Due to the critical situation in Asturias, the army is standing by for a full assault against the BTA.
strings.IBR_AAS_BTA_offensive_decision_tt:
The offensive will decrease BTA Activity, Supplies, and Support by 4 each, but can only lower each value to 2.
The bloody clashes will lower Iberia's stability by [?IBR_AAS_offensive_decision_ticker_temp|Y0%%]!
strings.IBR_yves_war_algeria_category_desc: The state of affairs in Algeria was always meant to be a temporary one, or so we planned, plans change however and we cannot tolerate losing such a valuable region to irresponsible governance.
strings.IBR_yves_war_mission: End the Illusion of Algerian Self-Determinism
strings.IBR_yves_war_mission_desc: We have a limited window of opportunity to topple new regime in Algiers before the threat of foreign intervention will force us to back out.
strings.IBR_emergency_reforms_desc:
The Collapse of the Triumvirate has badly wounded our economy, which has created a rather unfavourable situation.
It is time the Union attends to its duties and ensure the welfare of its population.
We cannot allow our economic malaise to worsen, the time has come to act.
strings.IBR_army_increase_tt: This will surely increase our Military's Ability to act in the case of a Crisis.
strings.IBR_Army_Upgrades_Effect: Due to our previous efforts to improve our Military, we will gain additional rewards.
strings.IBR_Army_Upgrades_Barcelona: Due to our previous efforts to improve our Military, they shall perform better against this uprising.
strings.IBR_repeatable_project_tt: This decision can be taken more than once.
strings.IBR_once_project_tt: This decision can only be taken once.
strings.IBR_twice_project_tt: This decision can only be taken twice.
strings.IBR_DP_unlocked_tt: New Development Projects will become available.
strings.IBR_DP_passages: Refurbish the Inner Moroccan Road Network
strings.IBR_DP_rif: Invest in the Reconstruction and Expansion of the Rif
strings.IBR_DP_canary: Increase Army Presence in the Canary Islands
strings.IBR_DP_A_metro: Construct Administrative Offices in Mainland Iberia
strings.IBR_DP_B_metro: Construct Military Bases in Mainland Iberia
strings.IBR_agri_reform_category_desc:
One of the many side effects of the Economic Malaise is that the Peninsula's agricultural production has remained sluggish and underperforming. Our production is based on outdated equipment and practices. The Caudillos sought to address the issue by starting a five-year modernization program in 1960 and setting up a Commission to manage fund allocation. However, the program also suffered from the effects of economic stagnation, which continues to plague Iberia, and insufficient progress has been made.

With the deadline approaching and rural discontent growing, it is imperative that the Union pursue this matter for the economic and political gains that success would bring.

Current Yearly Mechanization Budget: [?IBR.IBR_agri_subsidies_misc_costs_var|Y3] B USD
strings.IBR_Agri_Reform_Active_tt: We must complete the Agricultural Modernization Program before its deadline.
strings.IBR_agri_warning_tt: Should the Program fail to achieve its goal in time, it will simply be shed and the Union will bear the burden of its consequences.
strings.IBR_Agri_Reform_Success_tt:
The success of the Modernization Program will undoubtedly lend us goodwill with Iberia's rural population, calming tensions and restoring faith in the Federal Government.
Furthermore, it will nullify the costs of our Modernization Program.
strings.IBR_CD_victory_category_desc:
With a victory in the polls, the £IBR_party_CD CD will now govern the Union until a constitution is written and approven by the Iberian people. £IBR_party_CD Centro Democrático is made up of several parties, ranging from moderate social democrats to conservatives and as such the government will have to either balance this ideological big tent or give into one of the sides, which will determine the form of the coalition in the next elections.

While there is no risk of the government collapsing, it is still important to keep the faith of the Iberian people in the constitutional process, as their faith will determine the fate of the constitution.

strings.IBR_CD_move_to_right_tt: The Democractic Center will move to the right
strings.IBR_CD_move_to_left_tt: The Democractic Center will move to the left
strings.IBR_AP_move_to_right_tt: The People's Alliance will move to the right
strings.IBR_AP_move_to_left_tt: The People's Alliance will move to the left
strings.IBR_increase_belief_in_transition_tt: People's belief in the transition process will increase
strings.IBR_decrease_belief_in_transition_tt: People's belief in the transition process will decrease
strings.IBR_in_crisis: Iberia is going through a crisis
strings.IBR_in_crisis_tt: Iberia is going through a crisis
strings.IBR_divorce_decision_flag: The Caudillos are willing to accept the dissolution of the Iberian Union
strings.IBR_SAF_support: Iberian Support in the South African War
strings.IBR_claims_africa: Reasserted Their Claims on Angola and Mozambique
strings.IBR_claims_africa_really_mad: Reasserted Their Claims on Angola and Mozambique
strings.IBR_road.1.d:
With the turn of the year, the time is finally rife for us to unveil our new infrastructure expansion plans. The beginning will be marked only by minor improvements to create the foundational framework for larger, more comprehensive plans for our new economic structure in the Union. With the highlight of this year's project being the construction of a new semi-major road in outer Madrid, Caudillo Franco has taken a surprising amount of interest in the construction. Reportedly he has been visiting different sites and inspecting work regularly with keen attention.

Optimistic Union officials seem to have missed the ensuing grumble that gripped parts of Portuguese society at the news of the plans. Many regions in the country are in dire need of repair, so financing roadworks hundreds of miles away seems ineffectual at best, and neglectful at worst. However, those involved in the project remain daily confident that its completion will not have any hindrances due to large security contingents being posted to specifically watch for separatist terrorists. Even more importantly, they recognize the potential the start of this project could have for the infrastructure of the whole Union.
strings.IBR_road.2.d: Unsurprisingly, the new flagship infrastructure plan has hit the same filter of survival that most policy proposals hit once both halves of the ever-bickering Union have access to information regarding them. Angry invoices and incessant phone calls to the Ministry of the Interior in Madrid were all of the same nature, a rejection of the plan to start construction on the proposed highway outside of the Spanish capital because of another trivial matter. The matter of the tools being used not being exactly proportional in terms of national origin. This obstacle has the potential to freeze the Iberian domestic arm of the government if not truly addressed; thus, we have two options to consider for going forward.
strings.IBR_road.2.a: Use more construction equipment of Portuguese make.
strings.IBR_road.2.b: Propose a matching road in Lisbon.
strings.IBR_road.3.d: The planning phase for the new infrastructure project has again halted at an early point in the resource stage due to a dispute that begun after a rather sharp Portuguese civil servant noticed diverging Portuguese and Spanish material regulations on asphalt mixtures. There is the possibility that this may ruin the road if further work continues without any intervention. Considering that this will be a coordinated effort between both Union members it is important for propaganda reasons that this is done right. Then again it only is a road, the bigger projects are on the horizon afterwards and will be far better at helping to stabilise Iberian unity. How should we proceed on this issue?
strings.IBR_road.3.a: This is Spanish soil, so Spanish laws must be put in place.
strings.IBR_road.3.b: Appeal for federal laws on road construction material.
strings.IBR_road.3.c: Who needs regulations? Use what we brought along.
strings.IBR_road.4.d: The Iberian government has approved using the asphalt mixtures and road measurements standardized in Spanish law for the Outer Madrid road.
strings.IBR_road.5.d:
The small motorcade of Portuguese officials meandering through Madrid's old roads carried with it another message bound to cause disarray. Their national government has very foolishly decided to veto our request to use Spanish law instead of Portuguese laws when determining the acceptable mixture of asphalt for the construction of the outer Madrid road.

Their decision is supposedly based on technical difficulties with the sand and gravel mixtures but any politically savvy individual could clearly see that it is rather another attempt to defy Iberian centralization with lesser Portuguese characteristics, even on a small matter such as this. They would have us work less efficiently and with a higher cost rather than swallow their pride and admit that other parts of the Union might just have better laws! To remedy the construction deadlock this will create we will have to find a way around this ruling. There is always a loose screw or a bad apple in the bunch, and if we can find them and “convince” them to look the other way, then we will still end up saving a very good amount of time, money, and effort. We will just have to make sure that these less savory actions are not discovered by anyone else.
strings.IBR_road.6.d: The less experienced labourers at the road construction site this morning were surprised to see all machines that had used the concrete mixture were in a state beyond repair. The older, arguably more wiser men shook their heads in knowing disbelief. It seems the Portuguese machines that we were mandated to use apparently are incompatible with the required paving mixture, and have suffered numerous mechanical failures. They must be swapped out if we are to finish this project.
strings.IBR_road.7.d: A surprise inspection has discovered that we have not been obeying established regulations regarding the asphalt mixture to be used on the road. The Iberian government has fined us for said mistake, stating that only the best and agreed upon quality was allowed to persist in any further construction work. Why government employed workers were being fined by the government for I competency outside their pay grade was still to be found out.
strings.IBR_road.8.d:
With the asphalt mixture problem resolved and the investigation underway, we have been given the go-ahead to start our project. State sanctioned contractors are beginning to arrive in droves, already making great progress as they begin to tear out defunct infrastructure to implement the new great works. Both foreign and domestic journalists gasp in awe when they get their allotted time to visit the construction sites; a process requiring a great deal of effort and delay on our part as everything has to be prepared accordingly in advance.

On one such visit everything changed however, time coming to a freezing halt as a blood curdling scream tears down the perfect visage we created.

An explosion of asphalt ruptures the now trembling earth, exposing cracks within the hardly setting concrete. Swathes of road cratered in after tons of dynamite were preemptively detonated in the foundations of an interchange, reducing days of toil into rubble and ash. Large stockpiles of resources and machinery are lost in the horrific mess. Emergency services were deployed within minutes, tending to wounds and attempting to pull grasping, bloodied hands out of the charred piles of ruin. We have confirmed four deaths and over three hundred workers injured, adding costly medical bills to the already colossal repairs we need to immediately address.

After the cry of “Bietan jarrai!” was reported during the chaos, we have strong evidence supporting the notion that Basque separatists belonging to socialist organizations are directly responsible for the attacks, based off reports of similar terrorist activities that have plagued other government sponsored public works. The SECED has begun an investigation to address our suspicions, but in the meantime, we need to figure out how to amend or adjust our budget to deal with this shortfall. How should we recover from this disaster?
strings.IBR_road.8.a: Ask for a grant of Spanish tax money.
strings.IBR_road.8.b: Ask for a grant of Iberian tax money.
strings.IBR_road.8.c: Cut corners - we can save material here and there.
strings.IBR_road.9.d: Our request to the Spanish regional government for tax money to be used for repairing the road has been accepted. This means we are finally free to get back to work and finish this cursed project.
strings.IBR_road.10.d: The Spanish regional government has denied us funding, stating that the project is solely in the federal domain and that any move to bring it out of said sphere will result in internal bickering between regional governments. We must seek alternate sources of funding.
strings.IBR_road.11.d: Our request for more federal tax money to be used for repairing the road has been finally been accepted by officials both in Madrid and Lisbon. Our constructions can now hopefully continue and eventually finish without any further delay.
strings.IBR_road.12.d: The federal Iberian government has denied more funding to road building, stating that the project has been given more than enough funding to ensure its completion. This comes despite their extensive knowledge of the disastrous bombing attack. We must seek alternate sources of funding.
strings.IBR_road.13.d:
After the bureaucratic nightmare that was finding the necessary funds for the desperately-needed repairs, it seems as if we may at last proceed. The many confused workmen were finally allowed back onsite, the immense amount of resources again made available, and the heavy machinery was driven out of storage.

If only it were so simple.

In the early hours of the first morning of official repairs, the construction site was suddenly swarmed with mysterious men in dark suits, who quickly cordoned off the area and hustled several of the foremen into black vans before ordering the workers to vacate the site immediately. When the regional governor's office received a phone call from one of the contractors explaining what had happened, he was furious. However, that tone was dampened by the arrival of several SECED agents bringing... less-than-ideal news.

They had already identified the people responsible for the bombings: a group of radicalized Basque students-turned-separatists with leftist leanings. Their ringleader was one Iñigo Núñez, cousin of Alfredo Núñez... one of the foremen for a contractor hired on the project. SECED has reasons to believe that Alfredo may have aided his cousin's terrorist cell in organizing the bombing, and that he was not the only one operating on the inside. They have obtained an official warrant to fully investigate and audit all the contractors we have hired, in order to vet them for any other associates of Alfredo who may share his separatist ideology. In the meantime, all road work must be halted for the duration of the investigation, effective immediately to make sure no further damage can be inflicted on the already controversy stricken project.
strings.IBR_road.13.a: Are you really- are you KIDDING ME?!
strings.IBR_road.14.d: Despite the numerous setbacks facing it, the Outer Madrid road project has been deemed a safe and law-abiding enterprise. It is a good example to all of Iberia in how the rest of the planned infrastructure overhauls should be organised.
strings.IBR_road.15.d: The investigation into the Outer Madrid road project has found several suspicious practices, including fraud, bribery, and a neglect of proper vetting procedures for employees. A heavy fine is being drafted for the road-building company to try to minimize mitigating damage to the government. The issue of further dragging the project on is hardly even being considered at this point.
strings.IBR_road.16.d: The investigation into the Outer Madrid road project has found many suspicious practices, including bribing officials and a foreman with active ties to Basque separatists. The Guardia Civil have raided the site and arrested the suspect.
strings.IBR_road.17.d: The investigation into the Outer Madrid road project has found many suspicious practices, the most notable of which is finding out that one of the companies involved was a front for a southern Italian-based organized crime family. Considering the initial benign nature of the investigation it is surprising to now see the Iberian government having a minor international incident on their hands.
strings.IBR_road.17.a: How did they get away with it?
strings.IBR_road.18.d:
The project should've been simple. It should've just been a two lane road going from point A to point B. Yet sadly nothing can be that simple, these are turbulent times for Iberia, a political union where the building of a road is vastly outdone in effort just by the timescale of getting everything about said road approved with multiple administrations. Every little thing must bear with it fifty clauses and a hundred subsections, as though the mix of the pavement itself could potentially spark an inter-ethnic conflict were it not for corpulent bureaucracy that keeps us moving at a snail's pace.

The government in Madrid has now become involved in the construction of the road, and with it comes an entirely other magnitude of legislature and administration. The bombing of the road has forced us to create an extra-wide shoulder to be able to actually get equipment around the crater left by said attack. Madrid is now demanding that we turn this shoulder into an entirely new lane. They either have no idea what they're asking for, or, more likely, they don't care.

This is a case for the federal government. You would have to file a pile's worth of appeal paperwork asking for a permit to actually alter the road we're working on, and then of course there's a lengthy waiting period all just so a committee of pencil pushers and nepotists can take a quick glance at the paperwork and grant or deny your requests on what feels like a whim. Madrid's ignorance of the realities in the ground are mind-numbing. We can't just turn a larger than average shoulder into an entirely new lane! The shoulder would have to be expanded, the budget would have to be reconsidered, and we'd just fall once more into the seemingly endless abyss of bureaucracy we've been dealing with for the past months.
strings.IBR_road.18.a: Accept the request, and appeal to the federal government.
strings.IBR_road.18.b: Decline the request, to hell with the city government.
strings.IBR_road.19.d: The proposed alteration to our construction permit has been accepted by the federal government, and we are once again cleared to begin work. The new road will now have the desired amount of lanes wanted by the Madrid city administration.
strings.IBR_road.20.d: The Spanish national government has declined our request to alter the construction permit, stating that the city government has no right to make requests that would fundamentally change the new flagship union project. We will not be able to expand the lanes.
strings.IBR_road.21.d: The Portuguese government has unfortunately decided to deny our request to alter the construction permit to fit more lanes onto the current flagship infrastructure project outside of Madrid. They claim that a municipal government such as ours has neither the ability nor the right to make these kinds of major changes to a project that so clearly falls under federal jurisdiction. This not only means that there will not be any lane expansions but it also sets a decidedly chilly mood for future negotiations on the project. Despite our proximity to the infrastructure and therefore the heightened fallout whether positive or negative for us, we can now only hope that they will be more reasonable in the future when it comes to the project, as it seems any further involvement on our part is being opposed at high government levels.
strings.IBR_road.22.d: The city government of Madrid, after having their request declined, has denied construction teams a permit to move construction equipment through the city. Thankfully, the federal government is already moving to overturn this, but this still means there will be a significant delay in continuing further construction.
strings.IBR_road.23.d: After a long period of bureaucratic delays and general pitfalls it seems that the construction of the outer Madrid road is finally proceeding smoothly. Senior contractors and civil servants have created multiple detailed models which all currently project it to all be finished in several months allowing us to finally move onto other, more grand parts of our infrastructure overhaul project.
strings.IBR_road.23.a: Let's hope it's really several months.
strings.IBR_road.24.d: Finally, after many incidents and delays, the proposed road in outer Madrid is now usable. This will be the first stepping stone in providing Iberia with a logistical infrastructure system that will bring the half-peninsula the capabilities to flex its eager muscles on the international market. One question remains however... who will open it, and who will it be named after? This may not be an easy issue to solve.
strings.IBR_road.25.d: Planned years ago in 1962, the Lisbon Infrastructure Plan has finally been completed. Lisbon now possesses a sister road to the one in Madrid.
strings.IBR_germany.1.d:
Sánchez Herrera arrived in La Jonquera, the Pyrenees border town between France and Spain, at the bequest of his cousin, the local mayor, Raúl Herrera. Raúl welcomed Sánchez to his house, drawing him to the parlour where a cool drink awaited him, alongside a small pile of documents. “Sánchez, long time no see. How've you been?”

“Just fine, cousin.” Sánchez grabbed a chair and a glass. “We've never been ones for social calls - what's this about?

”Well, my dear cousin, I know how hard the search for work can be for a convicted man, and you know I'm a generous spirit,, so I'm offering you a proposition. I've heard that with that craziness in Malta, some Madrid fellows decided Iberia will begin expanding trade with the Pakt, and a beautiful border village like La Jonquera is in prime position to benefit, if local entrepreneurs were to develop for the kind of roadside businesses that cater for major trade routes the world over.. I'd just need someone to head the business side of things.“ As Raúl spoke, he slid across the documents across the table towards Sánchez.. ”All you'd have to do is rubberstamp some proposals. I've already expedited zoning plans and a wealth fund for these projects. Need be, we can take out federal loans and personal ones. Practically no risk.“

Sánchez flipped through the pages in front of him - planning permissions, floorplans, projected earnings charts promising the moon. ”It's a little different to the kind of books I was running before; restaurants, brothels and gas stations for all these new German patrons, huh?

“Yes, my dear Sánchez, there's that sharp business brain! I knew you'd see a gap in the market when it appears! A gap in the market practically waiting to be exploited by the Herreras! Imagine, cousin, the wealth of Europe rolling through our sleepy town, right into our pockets! Ha!”
strings.IBR_germany.1.a: The ink couldn't dry fast enough.
strings.IBR_germany.2.d:
Yet another toast was raised in the Herrera house, this one for a French hotel magnate opening a branch in La Jonquera. It was a night dedicated to Iberia's European neighbors and the success they had brought to the sleepy canton on the French border, which was now experiencing triple the usual traffic. As businessmen mingled with each other and celebrated their recent successes, new deals were shaken over champagne.

Curled anti-socially into an armchair, Sánchez saw easy lines of credit throughout the room; the cousins had, as they had planned, exploited the market opportunity at the ripe time, and the pace of expansion was practically exhausting. Even tonight he wasn't safe from some rosy-cheeked German telling him his gas stations should stock the number one whiskey in Thuringia. There was nothing wrong with making money, but something stunk to high heaven.

“...Which is why,” Sánchez heard Raúl say, “we are proud to announce our most ambitious expansion yet. Very soon, gentlemen, we will be breaking ground on the La Jonquera industrial and distribution center!”

Sánchez winced at the applause that broke out. Something like that would need real money; no doubt he'd have to secure the loans needed while Raúl dipped into the municipal treasury. Still drunk, he almost absent-mindedly said aloud, “You know, there's already a fine distribution hub in Girona we'd be competing with.”

There was a smash above Sánchez' head. Bolting upright, he looked with surprise at the shattered fragments of his cousin's glass which fell around him, and then up at Raúl, staring daggers into him. “Then our hub will be better than fine!” Raúl yelped at his ungrateful cousin. “It'll be great! It'll be the only place to be! We'll make a place that dwarfs Girona!” The mayor paused briefly, having become aware his outburst may have somewhat lost the room.
strings.IBR_germany.2.a: “On my mother's life, I swear I'll make every man in this room rich as a prince!”
strings.IBR_germany.3.d:
Beneath a dead oak tree on the Spanish hillside, Mayor Raúl Herrera overlooked the valley where a crude concrete outpost sat inert by the road. The site of his industrial and development hub for La Jonquera died a sudden death as traffic stopped flowing in, payments were missed, financiers vanished overnight, and contractors simply stopped showing up. The trouble up north skewered Raúl's plans, and now the only activity between the quarter-finished structures were the furtive movements of German and French refugees, who darted beneath the tarpaulin...

With the sun hanging high over the Pyrenees, Raúl realized that Sánchez wasn't going to meet him here as they agreed. Wily as a fox, his cousin had probably hit the brothels and gas stations, grabbed what he could from each safe and slipped out in the early morning - he was probably in Barcelona right now, getting in touch with his old contacts. Raúl wanted to be angry with Sánchez, but he didn't feel anything. He wondered if he had perhaps spent all of himself in the mad greed of the recent past. That greed had left the mayor with a lot of debt, and Raúl didn't want to be in La Jonquera when the debtors inevitably arrived.

After finally putting out the nub that was left of his Reemtsma and turned back to the dirt road where he parked his Volkswagon, a gift from some jolly German businessman who disappeared in the first days of the Kampfzeit. Raúl had prepared that morning also, and packed enough clothes and pesetas to make it to Galicia, and then Argentina.

As Raúl pulled away he gave a deep chuckle, somehow finding it impossible to feel sorry for himself. He saw a gap in the market and filled it, that was it. Eventually, when things calm down, the trucks will roll through again, the brothels will pick up. Some other ass will take a bite out of a place like this eventually. It's just the nature of things. Cycles of boom and bust, plenty and poverty. In a sense, Raúl wasn't really responsible at all.
strings.IBR_germany.3.a: Poverty and plenty, that's all it is.
strings.IBR_germany.4.d:
We have received an urgent message from the Mayor of Llívia. Following the Burgundian invasion, thousands of terrified Frenchmen have fled southwards. Llívia, with a population of only a few hundred, has been inundated with no fewer than 4000 refugees. Border officials in Girona have opted to 'contain' refugees in the exclave until receiving orders to either admit them into Iberia proper or deny them entry.

Smaller groups of migrants have appeared at other border towns and isolated cases of illegal crossings of the Pyrenees have been reported. Immigration to Iberia is virtually unheard of, and Border Customs are not in any shape to handle a sudden crisis of this magnitude.

Immediate action is needed, and it will be taken as an emergency expansion of existing immigration protocols. Regulations and procedures for the handling of high-volume, single-region immigration will be drafted and presented to the legislature in short order. This issue, affecting all Iberians, is also an excellent first major issue for the Council's involvement.

With its diversified membership, all perspectives can be presented and incorporated into the solution, and with the immediacy of the issue, its organization and speed can be tested. All that remains is to call the delegates to the table, and begin deliberations. They will move quickly. They must.
strings.IBR_germany.4.a: Time to see the Council in action.
strings.IBR_germany.10.t: Speer Wins the German Civil War!
strings.IBR_germany.10.d: An official news broadcast from a ruined but now hopeful Germania was picked up on waiting Iberian airwaves today, both Caudillo Salazar and Franco waiting together for the past few hours for the statement from the Reichstag to finally be pronounced. Speer, the liberal and idol of Germany's youth, has won the German Civil War, a huge sigh of relief could almost be heard coming from all freedom loving peoples of this wretched earth. The Nazi reformer now becoming Führer was seen as a much appreciated shift away from the current dark paradigm that Europe has had to suffer for the last 20 years, conquest and economic ruin being its defining hallmarks. In Iberia this view was shared by the vast majority of the populace, even both Caudillos could for once agree that this was the best possible outcome of that terrible conflict, an outcome with a future that may not have to involve further war and death. The possibility of regained prosperity from trade, bettering of diplomatic relations, finally the chance for Europe to come closer together. After brief celebrations and a short meeting with other senior government officials, the two Caudillos parted ways for now, Salazar leaving with a secretive, yet buoyant grin. If everything went accordingly now and Speer kept to his reformist promises, the Iberian Union may become defunct as a necessary measure of unity against an external threat. Portugal could become independent again, sovereign again, reigned just by the pragmatist, regaining its lost glory. His daydream was almost too perfect, to be free of Franco and his split, mismanaged country. Whether Speer would be able to actually change Europe's oppressive, dark dynamic was yet to be seen, but for once Salazar could finally entertain the idea of hope.
strings.IBR_influence_tt_7: Speer's victory after choosing to support him will increase the Council's influence.
strings.IBR_germany.11.t: Once an Enemy, Always an Enemy
strings.IBR_germany.11.d:
While the public was still mostly celebrating and looking forward to a brighter future, the machinations of the never-resting Iberian state did not relax. Its view of a peaceful Europe, one without German domination and therefore threat, was not yet envisioned, even with Speer's victory. The new Führer is still a national socialist, formerly a devoted, close acolyte of Hitler, one who may talk sense but still by blood a barbaric German.

The idea that Iberia could now relax, possibly even devolve, as Salazar hoped for an idealistic future, was not one rooted in the still-grotesque reality they had to endure. After initial jubilance, even the Portuguese Caudillo became rooted again, adopting his usual composure at the next Council meeting. Invited military and economic analysts began to give estimates, derived from close analysis of Germany's material reality and Speer's proposed policies, of how long it would take Germany to rebuild and what sort of military capabilities the Iberians would need to prepare for in a worst-case scenario.

Caudillo Franco, unusual for the aging fighter, was very invested in this meeting, interrupting regularly to ask specific questions on military matters. Salazar, spotting Franco taking charge of the situation in a way he did not appreciate in the slightest, began to make equally valid statements on the political and diplomatic motivations Speer had.

While Franco raged on with an aggressive rhetoric, Salazar attempted to mitigate any pushes for Iberian military expansion, viewing it as an unjustified move that may produce a negative reaction from the Germans. Underneath his open reasoning, he was motivated to try to reduce the further integration of the two nations this expansion would create. Surprisingly, the Council took Franco's side in this matter and began preparing for a worst-case possibility, to better be safe than sorry. Salazar retched internally once he left the meeting.
strings.IBR_germany.12.t: Naval Maneuvers in the Gulf of Vizcaya
strings.IBR_germany.12.d:
A lone seagull, high up in the pure sea of white clouds, listened to its primal instincts and dove further down to try to spot some possible prey. Instead it was greeted with the unusual sight of a rather large contingent of the Iberian navy, both Portuguese and Spanish ships conducting a large scale exercise, a show of strength personally overseen by Caudillo Franco from the shore. The brutish Spaniard had secured this personal vanity project out of his Portuguese counterpart in the recent debate over the Iberian response towards the victory of the liberal reformer Speer in the German Civil War.

Salazar, quite fond of the his navy himself, had quickly recognized that the Germans would take little notice of this waste of precious fuel, their attention mainly focused inwards at this moment, any of their little foreign policy decision being in regards to their subjects around the world, and therefore granted his fellow Caudillo's request without much opposition. He needed Franco grateful and ready to compromise with him on more important issues regarding the new diplomatic scene of Europe, but the training also showed him the Portuguese naval capacity, which he also inspected closely from his comfortable viewing platform standing next to Franco. It after all was vital to rebuild the empire he had lost to the marauding Teutons, who it seems now might be finally tamed from their destructive nature.
strings.IBR_germany.13.d:
The Pyrenees Mountains, an immense, natural defensive line that once had split the peninsula from the feared French, now divided Iberia away from a Europe ruled by a far greater evil. Or so it would seem for anyone watching the sunburnt manual labourers and military men toiling away endlessly, using man's great ingenuity to further expand the large fortifications that lined the beautiful mountain range on the southern French border.

Again the Iberian Council had voted for Franco's gruffly made proposal that had led to the constructions, to the deep and bitter chagrin of Salazar who was getting more impatient with Franco's defensive demands each new meeting. The Spaniard did not seem to run out of ideas. So far the intelligence services had reported nothing that could suggest Speer had untoward desires when it came to Iberia and its peoples. Whether that would change with each new military venture that Franco departed on was yet to be seen.

In all honesty, Salazar was not entirely against the fortress installations being built, yet for different reasons to the Spanish Caudillo. He saw a great threat emitting from the former German puppet of Burgundy, the secretive SS state. Any kind of defense against this ominous threat was a welcome one indeed. He therefore has not vetoed this idea either.
strings.IBR_germany.14.d:
In the ever worsening personal conflict between the two contrasting Caudillos over the official Iberian government policy towards the new Reich, the traditional statesman and politician Salazar had finally been able to wrangle a significant concession out of the aging former general.

Drawing upon all the previous plans and projects from the Spanish Caudillo that he had not vetoed for the sake of an opportunity like this, the old Portuguese convinced the Spaniard that even if the government's policy will follow one of caution toward the wobbling European hegemon, we should not allow the Germans to see any aggression in our handling of state affairs.

Following another debate, this time more of a monologue as Franco had lost interest, it was decided that diplomacy would be initiated with the new regime in Germania, diplomacy on mutual necessity. In other words trade and commerce. It would allow a channel of communication in the possibility of crisis. Through this change in policy it might also be possible to expand the intelligence network we are still building in the ruined country, to ascertain the direction and working of the German government, but for Salazar more importantly it could allow a thawing of previously frozen relations between the two European nations.

Like usual, Franco had not been able to object to the ascetic statesman when he had begun his rant. He saw no real danger in pursuing what Salazar proposed but deemed it not useful enough for Iberia, the nation needed a threatening external force to unite against. Looks like he might have to create a new enemy.
strings.IBR_germany.15.t: Bormann Wins the German Civil War!
strings.IBR_germany.15.d:
After years of fighting and bloody deadlock, the end of the German Civil War has finally come. The victor is Martin Bormann, a staunch conservative and the man most expected by several international observers to be the final victor.

As the new Nazi leader begins to pick up the pieces and return to unsteady normalcy in his nation, there is ample time to implement several defense plans that were intended to go into effect earlier in the year. As Bormann has shown no desire to change German foreign policy, the Caudillos and Iberian Council are convinced that the previous plans are still effective, and that there is ample time to implement them.
strings.IBR_influence_tt_8: Speer's defeat after choosing to support him will decrease the Council's influence.
strings.IBR_germany.16.d:
Bormann is a staunch conservative, and this means that his methods shall be predictable and based on Germany's previous exploits. One of the most notable of these was their aerial bombing operations, which legendarily crippled the industrial capacity of any nation that drew their ire. The fearful capabilities of the Luftwaffe can be seen in the desolation of Western Africa following the Second World War, and the bombing operations that turned Russia from a respectable power into an anarchic wasteland. Thus, in order to avoid meeting this fate ourselves, a means of protecting our civilians is necessary.

This shall come in the form of the humble air raid siren. While not capable of directly protecting our industry, they would give ample time to our citizens to get to shelters, and for various cities' garrisons to get anti-aircraft systems online. Until we can revolutionize our air force and meet the modern standards demanded by our potential opponents, this stopgap measure will have to do.
strings.IBR_germany.17.d:
For too long our border fortifications with the French State have been neglected. However, with the clear violation of Vichy France by Burgundy, we can no longer trust the Germans to take a sane route in dealing with the French. We must renew the old Pyrenees Line immediately. In order to do so, we will initiate several inspections along the line, replace built-in artillery, and ensure that the logistical problems involved with running heavy artillery and armor in the mountains are maximized for a potential threat, yet minimized for our purposes.

If the Germans come, we will be ready for them.
strings.IBR_germany.18.d:
Our small Equatorial African colony has been in jeopardy for some time now, due to the heavy German presence in its area. While Müller is slightly more reasonable than the Reichskommissars that seized the Portuguese colonies in southern Africa, he still presents the same mortal threat that any agent of the Reich does, simply by existing on our borders.

Additionally, with the formation of the Afrika-Schild and the South African War, it is extremely evident that the Reichskommissars will not hestitate to expand wantonly into any territory that takes their fancy. Therefore, our at-risk colony must be fortified as quickly and as thoroughly as possible. While its risky position and the appalling state of our economy will present challenges in this sector, there's nothing that a few honeyed words, promises of freedom, and 'volunteer' labor cannot solve, when it comes to the field of construction. Hopefully, when the endeavor is over, the Reichskommissars will choose a different target, and kindly leave us alone.
strings.IBR_germany.19.d:
Now that our more urgent preparations are complete, it is time to finally put an end to Bormann's sabre-rattling... by rattling our own sabre back! We shall hold an enormous military exercise in the far western Pyrenees, simulating a potential German invason from the French border. While the plans for this exercise existed before, it has been heavily altered to reflect the loss of the Triumvirate as dependable allies in wartime. Still, even without Italian naval support, armored divisions, and supplemental airpower, the display is sure to be enough to make Bormann turn his head towards a weaker neighbor.

The festivities shall occur over a week-long period, and be attended personally by both Caudillos. Elements from every wing of the Iberian armed forces shall be present, from the federal army, to the Portuguese Army, to the Spanish Army, to Guardia Civil units being used as reserves. Two full tank divisions, the majority of Iberia's armor corps, shall be deployed in advanced maneuvers in the foothills of the Pyrenees, while split elements of the Spanish and Portuguese armies shall serve as the federal army's opposing force in the mountains themselves. To prevent foreign interference, a massive deployment of military policemen and elements of the AAS shall stand in support.

As a bonus, since the exercise is occuring within the Basque-populated region of Iberia, it could serve to shock the problematic ETA into lying low for a while...
strings.IBR_starting.1.d:
A dossier after another, corruption scandals, forgotten grudges, treacherous elements; the clock ticks into dusk through the sounds of bussing carriages still wide awake. Just as the relentless, grinding engines rattling on the pavement of Lisbon, António de Oliveira Salazar soldiers into one more sleepless night with his pen tightly gripped. No tiredness can slip through his work, for any sign of weakness is fruit for traitors who know no better than to rob Portugal of her prosperous fate.

Soon enough, Lisbon finally turned quiet. It was about the time of night when the bustling should end abruptly, as if a dying man taking his final gasp before it all turned dark. The scribbling Caudillo was nonetheless interrupted again, even in this absolute silence, by a gentle pull on the stool he rested upon. An incredible pain struck Salazar's knees in a sharp note, taking its sweet time to remind him of the long-darkened horizons and turning his attention away from his voracious note-taking. As it had appeared, the sixteenth consecutive hour of work finally took its well-deserved toll, a late one at that. No matter, there are only very few more to read over; it was time to ring in the secretary.

Salazar never once permitted entrance to the study during any such long hauls; still, the two-page briefers he had always left for the fortunate one performing the clean-up afterwards tend to be specific enough to make chaos a non-factor. But how can the giant just unceremoniously leave for a rest when the world, as a whole, has still not bent to his sense of order?
strings.IBR_starting.1.a: Time to clean the garden as well.
strings.IBR_starting.2.d:
“...and why am I still, still, having to sit by and watch this pestilential dance we play with the Yanquis again and again?” This had been a decent portion of that same afternoon, listening to Francisco Franco sounding off at the injustice (according to him) of it all. “Do they have absolutely zero consideration for our ever ephemeral security in Europe?

The motor boat sat idle in the lake, fishing rods resting static off the sides of them. Vice-Admiral Pedro Nieto Antúnez learned over the side ”There is a lot to be s-“

”Surely, they actually read whatever pseudo-academic babbling the Führer has to say in the press on any given day?“ This had been a large part of that morning too, Franco continued. ”Anyone with eyes knows that the Reich is just a ticking time bomb with a border.“

The lures bobbed gently on the surface of the water, a healthy bounty of fish for the catching. ”Do we-“

”But the Japanese!“ Franco hissed irritably, this was looking to be a bigger piece of that evening too. ”It is only God's grace that the home islands do not sink into the sea for how they fatten themselves on the riches of the east!“

Franco was suddenly silenced by the rattling of his fishing rod, the Vice-Admiral was taken aback as well. A few gentle winds later and the line arose from the waters; A decently-sized Lucio, somewhat smaller for a Black Bass, but a good catch all the same. The thing writhed aggressively for only a moment before Franco slammed it hard on the boat, an audible crack silencing his catch. A small measure of satisfaction rolled over Franco's face, the Caudillo raising his eyebrow curiously.
strings.IBR_starting.2.a: “In the end, the little fish is not the one who gets caught!”
strings.IBR_starting.3.d:
They lifted the glasses over their heads: “Salute!” they said in unison, the men of the National Business Council finally had their day.

“We all knew Franco and Salazar would see sense!” one man said. Madrid and Lisbon had buckled at last, the primacy of Corporatism giving way to the private sector.

“That needle got a nice nap in, but it was only ever going to move eventually.” For once in what felt like forever, the Business Council would become relevant again. The second man continued. “Maybe we could-”

“Has anyone seen that damn letter!?” A third voice rose up indignantly. “The one about the agreeme- Oh! There it is!” The man rifled through his desk.

“What's your hurry?” The first man said, the news of the government's reforms had only broken that day.

The third held up a stack of papers. “Meeting with the Ministry of the Economy, investment ideas, a kind of jam session.”

The second man almost didn't believe what he was hearing. “That fast? They got you in the door that quickly? How?”

The third man grinned mightily. “My nephew! He works at the Ministry, got the word to me two weeks ago, arranged the meeting himself.”

A fourth man, gripping the martini in his hand, scowled at him. “And you made sure to keep that to yourself?” The third man looked back only shrugged and walked away, folder in hand.
strings.IBR_starting.3.a: Corruption didn't disappear when the system did, it just bided its time.
strings.IBR_starting.4.d:
So, this was the view that the strongmen of Europe found so appealing? The veranda offered a charitable view of Lisbon as well as the crowd below, a throng of cheering onlookers as Guanabara governor Carlos Lacerda waved to them. This was not the first diplomatic mission from Brazil to the mother country in Europe and certainly not for Lacerda personally. Indeed, this was but one of many new 'friendship flights' between Lisbon and many other Brazilian cities.

Lacerda's speech began: “On some days, when I am home with my family, there are times I look out the window and marvel at the truly great nation my people have built. When our aircraft finally flies in and overlooks this grand city, I am reminded that such majesty has a continuity, for what other nation would be so bold as to chart a course to uncover such a wondrous place if not one as beautiful as yours?”

Prolonged applause followed, Lacerda continued: “But your nation and mine no longer exist in a world defined by Kings or Emperors and perhaps this world would be much safer if the aggressor nations of the world would accept this as well.” A spattering of boos arose, clearly aimed at those whose vile names need not be uttered.

“In truth, the Americas are not blind to the plight of Iberia. Yes, this most-storied lands of Old Europe are in a constant struggle with the machinations of the mercurial polity of their northern neighbors. It is an existential battle for self-preservation and national sovereignty that my people know all too well.” A noticeable number of murmurs in the crowd spoke to the implications behind Lacerda's words.

“It is for these reasons, for the determinism of an independent Iberia and an independent Brazil, that your nation and ours should embark on the establishment of a new and fruitful relationship on the world stage! United in the bosom of almighty God and the great history of the pioneers of old, the proud peoples of Iberia and Brazil shall chart a new course for a fairer and even greater future!
strings.IBR_starting.4.a: One wonders what else he sees that he likes so much?
strings.IBR_starting.5.t: It Ends With a Door Being Closed...
strings.IBR_starting.5.d:
“BY ORDER OF THE CAUDILLO OF PORTUGAL AND THE PARTY LEADERSHIP OF THE ESTADO NOVO, UNDER INVESTIGATION FOR INFILTRATION OF COMMUNIST ELEMENTS, THIS RESERVED SPACE WILL REMAIN CLOSED FOR THE DURATION IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE RULE OF LAW AND THE SECURITY AND CONTINUED PROSPERITY OF THE IBERIAN UNION OF SPAIN AND PORTUGAL.”

Government decrees found their way into Sancho's vision with such regularity that it was truly obnoxious. Sancho was not all that shocked to learn that his student association had been shut down by the regime. He was a pragmatist and a realist. It came with the territory. The government signage reflected mutedly off his glasses.

“Well, what now?” Paula leaned listlessly against the lockers lining the wall, her study papers resting in her school bag.

“Nothing,” Sancho replied.

“What did we do?” João held a red ball in his hand, bouncing it off the door to what had been their meeting place, catching it, chucking it. “Is Salazar still jumping at ghosts? Why bother us? We've done nothing.”

 Seeing the ball bounce gave Sancho an idea. “I... think I know where we could move to. There's a room downstairs, in a bar near where my father works. I know people there we can talk to. I'll explain on the way.” Some of the more... eclectic students spent time there too. It was very odd, having candid conversations with his peers about the PCP of all people. But seeing their meeting place shuttered like this, maybe he was open to hear what they had to say after all.
strings.IBR_starting.6.d:
The Ministry of Information and Tourism had come alive in a way it had not in years.

Civil servants dashed with commands and tasks in its offices, reports and guidelines being written on typewriters hot from the pace of typing. Data hung upon walls, testimonies and research overflowing upon the desks they clung to. The new Minister had promised a revolution in tourism and few could doubt that he was making good the promise. The tourists would come, and he had made it clear they would come quickly.

Above it all was the Minister himself, his office the antithesis of the chaos that clutched the rest of the Ministry. Manuel Fraga sat behind his desk in a silent office, a half written letter before him. His next mandate would require explanation to the highest authority, a mere telegram would not suffice. The Caudillos were owed a personal correspondence before he was indisposed on his planned Andalusia tour. How to summarise?

“Perception. The word that controls the flow of tourism just as it does a government. If the tourist feels oppressed in their leisure, that the culture they view is manufactured, they will not come. It brings stability, yes, at the cost of potentially huge revenues, easier access to foreign currency, and endless opportunities to improve our international perception.”

“My ministry will focus on tourism as our measure of policy. Iberian values must be maintained, but we can have some tolerance for those who are not Iberian but come to benefit us with their money. Small allowances can be made for them in the interests of the greater good. Further, censorship rules will be reviewed to ease the touch of the State upon broadcasting and publishing, particularly in the Press, to create a guided but not controlled society conducive to positive perception. Iberian Values will remain central and protected, with bountiful new funds with which to do it.”
strings.IBR_starting.6.a: Caudillo and civil servant alike raised eyebrows at Fraga, but knew better than to obstruct.
strings.IBR_starting.7.t: The Rugged Character of the Frontier
strings.IBR_starting.7.d:
José never came to this region of Extremadura. Arid, rocky, all year around nothing but difficult terrain and bipolar weather - unbearably hot in the summer and washed out in the winter. It was one of the most difficult regions of Iberia, and as an agent of the National Institute of Colonization he truly felt able to make such an assessment.

He had driven through winding valleys and barely existent roads to reach this village, Génesis, near the old Portugal border. The file had made for curious reading, a ten year project to create a new town in the region. It was positioned close to major roads - on maps at least - and fields suitable for agriculture; a fine base from which to tame the area.

As José stepped out of the car, it took him all of a second to determine how successful the efforts had been.

It was little more than a shanty, run down pre-fabs aged terribly in the sun. Animals milled in small pens where a central road had been expected, meanwhile the few residents quietly shuffled in their errands around the exhausted structures. A man, youngish but with clothes and features worn and hanging, ran out of one of the buildings. “Hola Señor, you are the NIC man, yes? I'm the Mayor you spoke to on the phone!” José gave him a shrewd nod, his attention more occupied by the poverty as the Mayor dashed to him.

José spared no time on pleasantries. “This place does not meet the project's projections. You were given a mandate to foster population growth. What on earth have you been doing?” The Mayor gave him merely a sheepish look.

José doubled his focus, holding a severe glare upon the man. “Why haven't you attracted a population, this town looks smaller than the listed starting population while you receive Institute money. It looks like a damn gypsy encampment!”
strings.IBR_starting.7.a: The Mayor's dry mouth quivered. “Señor... what money? We have to work the fields by hand.”
strings.IBR_starting.8.d:
Francisco Franco and António Salazar, even to their detractors, were not men to be considered lightly. They had risen from humble origins to become among the most significant human beings to grace their respective countries in generations, even rivaling Spanish and Portuguese royals of old. Yet for all the magnanimity assigned to them, as much born from heavy propaganda as their very real credentials as heads of state, they were both easily dwarfed by the behemoth before them.

Up until that point, the tour of the facility had been fairly straightforward. The hardhats worn by either leader was mostly for show, everything else was just business along lengthy walks down sterile corridors to the whirring of the press cameras. The lead engineer spouted off technical specifications of Iberia's second experimental nuclear power plant and its contributions to ongoing research to the candid, if rehearsed curiosity of the Caudillos. This all changed when they reached the marquis of the tour, the center of the complex where the engine of this massive machine awaited.

Staring into the mass of the Arbi Reactor was something akin to staring into the mouth of heaven or hell or both. Flickering lights, labyrinthine readouts and switchboards that seemed to line the walls around them like locusts, all well beyond the imagination of military men like either Caudillo. The heart of the Iberian Union's nuclear power program loomed over them, the weight of the occasion by no means lost on either man.

Franco held his fist over his mouth, tracing the length of the thing upwards with his eyes. At times, Salazar had to consciously close his mouth to hide that he was in fact speechless. Neither of them spoke, the genial difference between the Caudillo of Spain and Portugal melted away at the sight of the thing, the two of them considering the moment pensively.

At the end of the tour, Nuclear Energy Board Director Armando Durán was approached by Franco and Salazar, the former with a singular inquiry in mind.
strings.IBR_starting.8.a: “Are there any plans for a commercial reactor?”
strings.IBR_starting.9.d:
When the engineers finally dragged the last bit of cable through the maintenance corridor to the control center, there was nothing left to delay them, the light primary colors and almost medical appearance of the control room contrasting with the weight of the moment. Franco and Salazar had already come and gone, the other advisers and press functionaries all given the run down. There was nothing else to be done, nothing left to prepare. It was time, they had all waited for this.

With the reactor finally connected to the power grid proper, the lead engineer flipped the big red switch, they needed only to stand back and watch the history of their nation change right in front of their faces. 0%, 5%, 10%, the numbers began to tick. 15%, 20%, 25%, the machinery around them began to whirr, fists began to clinch, air caught in men's throats.

28%, 32%, 37%, men's brows began to furrow, the numbers climbed, but slowly, almost savoring the moment as much as they were. 41%, 44%, 49%, from a murmur to a growl, the reactor clawed to life. 53%, 57%, 61%, a hand clutching at their chest, beads of sweat trickling down the face.

The floor, the walls, the ceiling, the whole room almost shook from the noise. 66%, 70%, 75%, a hand over the hot phone, the direct line to emergency control, almost expecting a horrific twist behind the numbers. 79%, 83%, 89%, all eyes pointed upwards, hearts in their throats, their minds afire. 90%, 91%, 92%, 93%, 94%, a prayer to God, a lifetime buried in study, the life's work of some of the brightest minds that Spain and Portugal combined had ever produced. 96%, 97%, 98% The reactor thundered, their souls soared.

99%...100%. No words were left that could be said, no human sound could even be heard even without the cacophony of the reactor from the far end of their instruments. Silence was all they had, until that silence broke. A roar of cheers erupted from the control room, men wept freely as they embraced. The Iberian Union's first commercial nuclear power plant had finally sprung to life and in the eyes of the men working tirelessly to make this project a reality were all the words they could not say.
strings.IBR_starting.9.a: An atomic sun rises over Iberia as one of Europe's most historic regions is brought into the modern age.
strings.IBR_starting.10.d:
Khadidiatou was no stranger to bandit raids. It had not been this bad even just a few years ago, but ever since the Amadou Gang had acquired trucks, the Mauritanian border had been a low-grade war zone. Militiamen now guarded the outskirts of the town of Aleg. Years of raids had turned the Aleg Militia larger and more experienced. Usually the Amadous picked easier targets.

Patrols were scarce in this remote corner of the Iberian Empire, and Khadidiatou preferred it that way. The Europeans were thieving taxmen, no more than another gang of bandits too numerous and well armed for the militia to dare resist. Not that they would want to resist--after all it was the Iberians who supplied the militiamen with weapons and imported luxuries.

A convoy of trucks appeared on the horizon. Iberians, of course, but why were they here? This was not a scheduled ammunition delivery or tax collection, and the convoy was twice as long as any Khadidiatou had ever seen. Dozens of European men, many armed with semi-automatic rifles, stepped out and began unloading cargo. Why were they here? Security? Aleg already had security! Sure, the occasional raid still took place, but at this point bandits stole less from the townspeople than the militiamen themselves.

And if the Iberians are here because they think they can take out the bandit gangs...
strings.IBR_starting.10.a: They are going to need a lot more guns...
strings.IBR_starting.11.d:
Sand dunes have a bad habit of burying things. The roads crossing the western parts of the Sahara must constantly be maintained, carefully monitored for any signs of a sandfall. Just about the only thing more difficult than maintaining desert roads is laying them down. Pablo and his fellow surveyors laid down steel markers as they plotted the course for a new road. Officially, this was to promote regional commerce. As they moved further south, Pablo noticed a most unusual rock. There were many large rocks out here, but this one was much flatter than the others, an ever so slightly green-tinted color, and... was that rust? Was that cracked glass?

“That's not a rock.” Pablo said. “Oh my God, that's not a rock.”

As Pablo approached the truck, near completely buried by the sand, he shuddered to think of what he might see inside. Hand shaking, he brushed away the dust that obscured the window. There he found bodies. Sickly brown tissue clung tightly to dust-covered bones. Empty eye sockets and teeth almost forming smiles brought disquieting humanity to the emaciated husks before him. They were holding hands when they died, husband and wife surely. On the floor of the passenger seat rested a smaller corpse. Its skull was disarticulated from a torso wearing the tattered remnants of baby clothes.

Who is to say what doomed this family to die here? A flat tire, an empty fuel tank, a failed ignition. There were many ways to get lost out here but no way to call for help.
strings.IBR_starting.11.a: The dunes consume all in their path.
strings.IBR_starting.12.t: The Medieval Fortress of Aïn Chaïr
strings.IBR_starting.12.d:
The weather in Morocco could surprisingly be quite pleasant. Alfonso had gotten used to the temperate mornings on his commute to the office. How glad he was to enumerate the census at this time of year, rather than under the oppressive heat of the African summer sun. For 4 hours he drove his van southwards, into the heart of the Sahara. There were no roads here, only miles of indistinguishable dunes. Dunes could blur together, it was easy to lose your bearings here.

That was what Zdan was there for. He had grown up in this desert and, more importantly, he was a native Tamazight. These were truly remote lands, nearly untouched since ancient times, few spoke any other language, not even Arabic. “Over there!” Zdan yelled, spotting through binoculars a stone tower peeking above the dunes. Pulling closer they found an old walled village: Aïn Chaïr, its sandstone buildings seeming more like something out of medieval times than today.

As the Iberians approached, a small band of pastoralists prepared to depart the city. Their eyes widened at the sight of the mysterious machine now before them, the rhythm of its engine coming to a halt as Alfonso and Zdan stepped out. Trucks were unheard of out here, and most knowledge of Europe came by the tales of traders.

An elderly man approached the vehicle, turning to Alfonso and asking “Vous français?” It really had been a long time since any Europeans were out here. Zdan chuckled and said something to the man in Tamazight. The man looked confused and responded in Arabic. Zdan asked questions and relayed them to Alfonso. The band was a tribe of 46 men, women, and children. Most spoke only 'Tabaldit', a language that neither Alfonso nor Zdan had ever heard of, a few of the men spoke Arabic or Tamazight to trade at the oases. It had been many years since any of them had met a European in person; they had not even heard that the French had left Morocco. Alfonso tallied every man, woman, and child, in the band that day. No matter how far away from the roads, no matter the climate, no matter what the language: all would be counted in the 1962 Colonial Census.
strings.IBR_starting.13.d:
Colonial slavery began with Portugal. The first Portuguese settlements in Guiné became the first large slave depots for European colonists. For four centuries, tens of thousands of Africans were shipped every single year from Guiné to the colonies of the New World in chains. Colonial slavery also ended with Portugal. Portuguese merchants sailing from Guiné sent the final slaves to Brazil when that country abolished the trade.

Portuguese administrators struggled to find alternative uses for the colony, ultimately coming to rely on modestly profitable peanut farms used to produce cooking oil. On the eve of the unification, Guiné was an economic burden. Peanut prices had fallen dramatically, and most farmers had returned to subsistence rice farming. The cost of maintaining control of Guiné far exceeded its profits. Businessman António Silva had owned successful cashew orchards in Goa, but his fortunes there dashed by the Indian invasion in 1947, he began to build a new cashew empire in Guiné.

In the 1950s, Silva successfully lobbied for high tariffs on foreign-grown cashews. He launched an extensive advertising campaign for his cashews across Iberia, and in 1956 turned his first annual profit. Enticed, various investors pitched in, and the cashew orchards greatly expanded by the end of the decade. Now, as the second generation of cashew trees grow tall enough to produce fruit, in 1962, cashews are becoming cheaper and more widely available throughout Iberia.

After consideration by the Colonial Budget Committee, it is agreed that native land may be expropriated for the development of new orchards, and Africans may have their sentences commuted by choosing to serve a half-length sentence in the cashew orchards.
