”Acknowledged. Hammer, Anvil, we go in on both sides in ten, make sure there's no stragglers. Watch your corners and your targets. Out.“

The sniper counted down the seconds, and right on cue they moved. A battering ram slammed down the door, shouts of ”AAS, nobody move!“ penetrating even to his vantage point. The man in the window attempted to stir, an ambition stopped with a single shot from the sniper. Within the first 20 seconds he heard more shots from deeper inside, a break of a few moments and then sporadic bursts. He saw the flashes of discharge in the upstairs rooms, likely from doors open outside of his view. Intel had said maybe even a dozen armed men were on site.

Within a minute, the radio buzzed again.
strings.IBR_terror.12.a: “Overlook, building is secure. Basement is a goldmine, maintain watch and signal the cavalry.”
strings.IBR_terror.13.t: AAS Botches Raid on DI Cell
strings.IBR_terror.13.d:
As he had done many times before, the Axencia sniper, in his second career after the military, maintained the perimeter around the building. Supposedly occupied by the DI, the raid upon it was being efficiently executed.

He listened on his radio as the raid progressed, with each room cleared and more supposed terrorists captured. He listened - and watched carefully through his rifle - as the radio chatter grew more and more concerned with the lack of evidence found. And, when a face flashed in an upper-story window, holding what he was certain was a gun, he did not hesitate.

That first shot heralded an apocalypse, as dozens of other agents opened fire as well. By the time it was all over and the building fully cleared, a number of bodies were discovered, all with Axencia bullets within them. What was not found was evidence. Or any confirmed members of the DI. Recriminations started immediately.

It quickly became clear that the intelligence had been faulty. That the building had not been a DI hideout. That those killed had been ordinary Catalans. And that the 'gun' that the sniper had seen had, in fact, been an entrepà sandwich. Chorizo.

Such a disaster could not be hidden, but the Axencia did its best to blunt the questions and obfuscate the particulars. And the sniper found himself immediately reassigned to the office in Faro.
strings.IBR_terror.14.d:
Case Number: 583209{year}

Reporting Officer: Paco Ortega

Details of Incident: Met with informant, codename Torre, at the arranged meeting point. The location was clean and thoroughly observed by two agents for two hours prior to the meeting. At the arranged time, Torre revealed themselves to agents and discussed recent developments.

Torre's condition was poor, assessment quickly being reached that they were fatigued and exhibiting paranoia. Torre was unduly nervous for the length of the exchange despite being under AAS protection for the duration, frequently interrupting both themselves and agents seeking clarification on pre-meeting security, potential moles within the agency, and an assortment of other fears. Torre was searched for illicit substances, however none were found.

Torre relayed that they had been approached, by virtue of their role in the {redacted} organisation, to a meeting. At said meeting, they and the representatives of a variety of minor dissident groups were invited to partner with a new unified socialist organisation agitating for an independent, socialist Portugal. Torre claims that this group showed clear evidence of being behind the recent increases in separatist activity in the region, were well organised and called themselves the Brigadas Revolucionárias, a socialist front for Portuguese liberation. This name, and Torre's description of their symbol, matches many of the new literature starting to be seized in Lisbon, however concerningly it appears they may not be a localised organisation as was suspected.

Torre reports all groups in attendance of the meeting accepted annexation into the Front. They also reported suspected surveillance by non-AAS individuals. Torre stated that they believe they are suspected as an informant.
strings.IBR_terror.15.d:
It had taken months to arrange this meeting. Not since the Civil War had leaders of the Spanish Socialist Workers' Party, General Union of Workers, Syndicalist Party, and Basque Nationalist Party, all been together in the same room. This would be an uneasy meeting, to say the least. Ideological divides threatened any hope at a united opposition.

Nine men sat at a quiet private residence in Belém, Brazil. 4 were Iberian dissidents that had been quietly smuggled out of Cádiz. The others were exiles, 3 Portuguese and 2 Spanish, that had not seen Iberia in many years. All saw the rising discontent that had created Iberia's terrorist movements as an opportunity for reform.

The tension in the room slowly dissipated as the men discussed which content to include in their manifesto. Democratic rights and the legalization of opposition parties were obvious. But were there any parties too extreme to legalize? Should the Iberian Union be dissolved or maintained? Should the culturally distinct regions of Iberia be granted full autonomy?

To many of the underground dissidents in Iberia, the Belém Manifesto was hardly inspirational. It was too vague in its goals and too unclear in how they hoped to achieve them, and it tried to ignore the obvious question of whether Iberia should be a socialist state. But others saw something else: A consensus between liberal and leftist activists in Iberia, whose differences had previously prevented cooperation. Its calls for increasing the rights of workers to organize and working to improve the wellbeing of citizens through increased state intervention, struck a compromise between the calls for revolution and the call for more limited reform.
strings.IBR_terror.16.d:
I got a commendation for the port bust, though reading the report was more like reading a description gone three sheets to the wind. Apparently we took out a major supply drop, I personally incapacitated a resisting dissident. Damn thing didn't even say who we supposedly stopped getting the guns. I hope the chief got his congratulatory phone call from the Caudillo, all I got was a fake inky nod.

But between me and the commendation, it's hard to say I'm not getting paranoid. Leaving my apartment, I see shapes in the sides of my vision. Wisps that vanish as soon as I look. Cars seem to repeat, I see the same eyes over and over. At the station, my kids' school, the bar and the apartment - all seem watched.

They're young, twins barely ten, Rosa and Carlos. Were it just me I'd shake it off, not the first time the shakes have gotten to me over work, but it's the first time since their mother died. I can't get a security detail over something so silly as thinking I saw the same car a few times, but I could at least put the school on alert, just in case.

Walking out of my kids' school, I almost thank my onset paranoia. The receptionist is a cutie, though getting involved with the staff is probably a bad idea. At least it gave a little distraction from the day, playing with our words for a few minutes before heading back to the fight. It was a grey day, and the fight today was just reports and documents. Anything to delay that inevitability. Making sure the school knows not to accept anyone except me calling for them makes me feel a bit better at least.

I look at the windows of the school, trying to see my kids' classroom. Second floor, far left of the building... and there they are. The twins give a wave. I chuckle as I reach my car, no doubt the teacher is chewing them out for idling. But why shouldn't they wave Pa goodbye? I get in the car and turn the key.
strings.IBR_terror.16.a: I don't hear the explosion, or the screams from the classroom. I don't hear anything anymore.
strings.IBR_terror.17.d:
The Palace of the Cortes was on high alert. Soldiers in full uniform, armed with DUX submachine guns, guarded every entrance to the Palace, preventing any civilian from approaching. Such were the measures that now had to be taken as the terrorist threat escalated.

With so few men on the Council, it would be obvious if anyone were missing, and even more obvious if an unfamiliar face were to appear. And so, as Manuel Fraga entered the chamber, he could feel dozens of curious and suspicious eyes moving over him. Franco rose from his seat and began to speak. “Gentlemen, I am pleased to welcome Minister of Information Manuel Fraga to brief the Council. Salazar and I have tasked Fraga with leading a remewed, more organized effort to combat extremist propaganda. Several smaller bureaus in the present Ministry of Education and Ministry of Labor will be reorganized under Fraga's supervision, to ensure a consistent, hard-hitting effort against propagandists across the nation. I give the floor to Don Fraga.”

“Thank you, my Caudillo,” began Fraga, “Good evening, gentlemen. As we attempt to bring an end to terrorism in Iberia, the terrorists have adapted new tactics, and new strategies to win over those vulnerable to their messages. In Girona last week, a group of DI members briefly hijacked the city's largest radio station, preaching absurd anti-government conspiracies to thousands of people. Our battle against terrorism is just as much a battle against propaganda, and if we are to succeed in our mission we need to organize and expand our own media outreach efforts. The terrorists' propaganda is specifically designed to inflame regional tensions, and speak primarily to disaffected young men.”

“If we are to succeed against terrorism, we need to target their recruiting grounds. The Ministry of Information will devote the majority of its efforts to the regions and cities where terrorists are most active, with media messaging focused on reminding people of the great things the Caudillos have done for them, instilling fear in anyone who would think to oppose our security forces, and removing the 'mystique' of terrorist groups, turning them from subjects of fear and fascination into subjects of disgust and mockery.”
strings.IBR_terror.17.a: “How do you think youths would react to photos of awkward, scrawny insurgents on magazine covers?”
strings.IBR_terror.18.d:
When he was a professor at the University of Duesto, Cecilio Mariñelarena never would have imagined himself having a political career. As the only Basque economist on the Iberian Council, Mariñelarena had frequently involved himself in discussions regarding the growth of terrorist activity in the region. He held the controversial belief that, though the Basque Country overall was among the wealthiest regions in Iberia, the rapid economic changes in the past decade were nonetheless significant factors in the growth of separatist extremism. As Councilor Herrero Tejedor concluded his introductory remarks, he listened carefully to hear the full details of the bill Manuel Fraga, Minister of Information, was about to introduce.

“Gentlemen, I am pleased to report that in just this past week, the Axencia Anti-Separatista uncovered and destroyed a large ETA weapons cache near Vitoria, and arrested 12 terrorist plotters in Tarragona.” Fraga paused while his audience cheered. “Though the seizure of weapons and arrest of conspirators are vital to the Union's security and these recent victories are significant, our media efforts are just as critical. A cache of ten thousand guns means nothing without as many terrorists to hold them, which is why I am putting forth a bill to increase funding to the AAS Information Office by 50%, to enable the AAS to purchase radio and television ad-space at greatly a reduced price, and to initiate a thorough review of the history textbooks used in secondary and tertiary schools to identify and remove separatist-sympathetic content.” Even before Fraga gave the specific details of this bill, the loud applause made it obvious to everyone in the chamber that it would pass overwhelmingly. In the end, only five councilors of the 480 present voted Nay: All hardline conservatives objecting to what they perceived as a 'soft' and useless method to combat terrorism.

Mariñelarena joined the applause, and voted in favor of the bill. But though he both publicly and privately supported the bill's aims, he was frustrated. He already had to worry about paranoid conservatives suspecting that he was sympathetic to the separatists on account of his origin. There was only so much he could feel comfortable suggesting that Iberia's economic policy contributed to radicalization.
strings.IBR_terror.18.a: Is this really enough to end the violence?
strings.IBR_terror.100.d:
For over thirty years, the DI has been one of our Union's most intractable enemies. They have bombed, assassinated, and sown terror across Catalonia and Iberia, and caused deep divisions in our nation. And now, finally, they are defeated.

Through countless hours of investigation, through innumerable raids and arrests, and through the blood of not a small number of brave agents, the Axencia has broken their armed wing, crushing the last few holdouts and leaving what scattered remnants might exist leaderless and disarmed. It has not been easy, but they, and we, have triumphed.

Though we can be certain that anarcho-syndicalism is in no way dead as an ideology, it has been beaten into submission for the time being. Catalonia in general, and Barcelona in particular, have proven themselves as tenacious and enduring foes in their support of that movement, and we will need to be vigilant to ensure it does not return. The Axencia certainly plans to embody that vigilance and will maintain its extensive intelligence network across the region.

Resources can now be diverted elsewhere, against other enemies of the state, as we march forward towards a day, not far away, when the state reigns supreme, and those who would see it dismembered are brought low.
strings.IBR_terror.101.d:
Case Number: 136452{year}

Reporting Officer: Fermín Canez

Details of Incident: At approximately 1915 hours on the Carrer de Rera Palau, César Izquierdo, local Falange party treasurer, was assaulted by two men, Valentín Marcial, a local barber, and Federico Arcos, an itinerant from Terrassa. Following a verbal altercation, the perpetrators began striking César, knocking him to the ground and kicking him. This incident was seen immediately by Officer Canez, who responded with a verbal warning for the men to cease immediately and surrender themselves. Arcos lunged to attack Officer Canez, who was able to subdue the perpetrator without difficulty. Marcial attempted to flee, but was tripped by a local resident who witnessed the altercation and attempted to assist Officer Canez.

The assault is believed to be politically motivated, as both perpetrators were observed to be shouting political epithets relating to Izquierdo's political affiliation with the Falange. Both men also uttered anarchist slogans associated with Defensa Interior (DI), a known anarchist terror movement. Both men have admitted to being anarchists, though it is unknown if this assault is part of a larger campaign or merely a crime of opportunity or passion.

Izquierdo was admitted to the Hospital del Mer and diagnosed with minor injuries to the chest, abdomen, and groin. He is not expected to have any permanent injury and will make a full recovery. Members of the Falange have been notified to exercise additional caution. Arcos and Marcial have been arrested, Marcial's home is being searched for information relating to DI, and fellow transients in Terrassa are being investigated for possible terror links.
strings.IBR_terror.101.a: Every mighty oak begins from a humble acorn.
strings.IBR_terror.102.d:
Pastor Fleitas was a warrior. He fought with a well-trimmed mustache, a sharp tailored suit, a touch of gray in his hair to lend him an extra sort of paternal gravitas, and a voice that projected confidence no matter what he spoke. His dragons were fear and ignorance. He was a newsman, and he was who the people depended on when they were afraid of what was and what could be.

“Good evening, I am Pastor Fleitas and you're listening to EFE, Iberia's most reliable and trusted name in news. In Madrid today, the Vicar-General's office was targeted by two explosive devices which exploded overnight. No one was present at the site and no injuries were reported.”

“The attack was claimed by a group calling themselves the Defensa Interior, an anarchist group whose statement decried the Iberian military and security apparatus. In their statement, they called for the dismantlement of the Iberian government, the establishment of self-governing communes, and the prosecution of the Caudillos for crimes against the Iberian people.”

“Police sources have no leads at the present time but stress that it is early in the investigation. Madrid's Police Commissioner Conrado Canizares made a statement today assuring the public that they do not believe any further attacks are forthcoming and that the perpetrators will be brought to justice swiftly. We eagerly await further development in this case and hope for a speedy resolution.”
strings.IBR_terror.102.a: The best armor against fear is the confidence that you are safe, given to you every evening.
strings.IBR_terror.103.d:
Pastor Fleitas, the trusted face of EFE, felt a sense of deja vu as he sat behind the desk, his teleprompter starting to scroll with news of the latest DI attack.

“Another bombing today. Two bombs exploded in the Iberia airline offices at Sevilla this morning before working hours, destroying much of the office and littering the street below with broken glass. There were no injuries owing to the early hour when the bombs detonated, but the attack has still rattled the city and its townspeople.”

“The motivation for the attack was made apparent at the scene. Leaflets against tourism were found at the scene claiming that tourists exploited Iberian workers and the airline had facilitated this crime against the working class, decrying it as an artery bringing tainted blood. Statements of this nature had been previously attributed to the Defensa Interior terrorist organization, causing analysts to believe that DI was responsible for the bombing. Only a few hours later, this was proven correct as they claimed credit for the act in a statement delivered to local EFE station in Sevilla. They have threatened more attacks to come until such time as they believe that Iberia has been liberated from the quote, fascist yoke and foreign interlopers, end quote.”

Another bombing, another message by the Defensa Interior. It was a carefully considered move, a bombing of the Iberia airline offices in Sevilla. The bombs were larger and of better manufacture. For a moment, Pastor's unflappable anchorman calm broke and his hand trembled.
strings.IBR_terror.103.a: Doubt can creep into the strongest armor.
strings.IBR_terror.104.d:
Pastor Fleitas steeled his gaze and looked straight into the camera. He was the face of the Iberian news agency EFE, the man people trusted to tell them what had happened, when, and what to do. He knew he needed to look the part, confident and strong in his features and gestures, to project a powerful aura and reassure the people back home. The Defensa Interior was on everyone's mind, and if they could not count on the steely eyes of Pastor Fleitas, what could they rely on?

“Top story today is the brazen day-time robbery of the Banc del Sol in Zaragoza. Shortly after noon today, four masked men armed with pistols entered the Banc del Sol and made off with an as-yet undeclared total of money. The entire robbery took less than five minutes from entry to escape. The identities of the perpetrators are currently unknown. The bank manager was injured in the robbery, shot in the leg to demand compliance. He is currently at the hospital and his injuries are believed to not be life-threatening.”

“Witnesses report that the perpetrators did not appear to have money as their primary goal, as two of the bombers were observed to spend two minutes placing a bomb near the entry of the bank. This bomb, which exploded before police arrived on the scene, was of crude manufacture and exploded without causing injury. The masked suspects were observed shouting anarchist slogans and are believed to be members of the notorious terror group Defensa Interior.”

“Police have stated that the culprits were last seen driving a dark blue VIASA van, plate number M-4573-MJ that had been reported stolen yesterday. Citizens who see the van are advised to call police as the suspects are believed to be armed and dangerous.”
strings.IBR_terror.104.a: Fear begets fear, as does its inverse.
strings.IBR_terror.105.d:
Case Number: 400836{year}

Reporting Officer: Rodolfo Campillo

Details of Incident: At 1445 hours, a convoy of light military equipment was hijacked and its two drivers kidnapped near Santa Maria de l'Avall. According to Private Agapito Villaseñor, one of the drivers, his vehicle was flagged down by an unknown male asking for help with his vehicle which had broken down. When the two men exited their vehicle to render assistance, they were ambushed by five masked gunmen, who forced them out of the truck. Private Villaseñor attempted to resist but was struck on the side of his head with a rifle butt. The two privates were robbed, stripped, and tied to a nearby telephone pole with rope and chains. The two men had minor injuries relating to the robbery and low levels of dehydration.

The truck was found abandoned in a field approximately a kilometer southwest of the hijacking location. The cargo, which consisted of rifles, pistols, body armor, helmets, radios, optics, and other infantry equipment were all missing. Defensa Interior leaflets were left inside, calling on Iberians to “end militarism.” Tire tracks in the field suggest that the kidnappers escaped with the stolen cargo in two trucks of unknown make and manufacture.

The unknown male who stopped the shipment was described as slightly heavyset with dark hair and appeared to be a manual laborer due to his dirty clothing and calloused hands. Investigation is ongoing. All police and military drivers will be instructed not to stop for any civilian, no matter their state of distress.
strings.IBR_terror.105.a: No good deed goes unpunished, and virtue is oft the first coin spent.
strings.IBR_terror.106.d:
Case Number: 824403{year}Reporting Officer: Alphonso San Román

Details: At 1850 hours, a bomb exploded in the town hall of Castellfollit de la Roca in Catalonia. The bomb appeared to have been planted in a lavatory trash can. A communique issued by Defensa Interior claimed responsibility for the attack, offering several details about the explosion that could have only been known by the perpetrators including the location of the bomb. It was initially believed to have targeted Caudillo Franco, who had visited the town several days prior, with the bomb's trigger mechanism failing to detonate. The bomb was small in size but caused significant interior devastation, suggesting that professionally manufactured explosives were used instead of an improvised explosive device. No injuries were reported as the explosion occurred after business hours. Investigators currently have no suspects and fear that DI's sophistication as an organization possesses more capability than hoped. Informants do not have any suspects as to who has planted the bomb and early investigation has not produced credible leads.

The final paragraph of the issued communique contained a direct threat. It reads as follows: “Our bomb was detonated intentionally to send a message. Franco, we know where you are. We are coming for you. Run if you like. We are everywhere. You will not escape us.”
strings.IBR_terror.106.a: DI has been elevated to a priority one threat.
strings.IBR_terror.107.d:
Case Number: 136742{year}

Reporting Officer: Miguel Herrera

Details of Incident: At 0436 in the Sarrià-Sant Gervasi district in Barcelona, a munitions plant was destroyed following several explosions from within the plant. Officer Miguel Herrera, who had been patrolling nearby, arrived first on the scene through the north access road. In the dark, he spotted two unidentified individuals running away from the scene of the blast, carrying large bags. When confronted by Officer Herrera, both individuals fled into a wooded area, where visual contact was then lost.

Officer Herrera reported that small, initial explosions could be heard from the plant prior to the large explosion that eventually destroyed the entire factory. Considering Factory Number F-7 had been specifically designated to produce artillery ordinance, it is likely that small bombs had been planted from within the factory that went on to create a chain reaction to detonate unsecured shells. Given the status of the individuals injured in the explosion, testimony cannot be taken at the current moment.

In the aftermath of the explosion, responding personnel recovered a makeshift explosive device from the north access road. The device bore no markings; however, the materials used and pattern of assembly were indicative of the previous devices used by the terrorist group, Defensa Interior (DI), suggesting that, at the very least, they had supplied these perpetrators.

The political ramifications remain to be seen. It is possible that materials and munitions had been stolen from the facility prior to the explosion. What's worse is that this attack may embolden other terrorist groups to execute more dangerous raids and attacks, knowing that the government cannot defend a munitions complex.
strings.IBR_terror.107.a: A catalyst to spark two more explosions.
strings.IBR_terror.108.d:
Pastor Fleitas sat in his chair, waiting for the cue from the cameraman to begin speaking, and in his mind he felt a strong feeling of deja vu. How many times had he sat at this desk reporting another incident from Defensa Interior? How many times had he reassured the public and how long would it be before they stopped believing him? He quieted his mind when he saw he was on, and he was back to being himself.

“Pure pandemonium today in Madrid after a 10 AM bombing of the DGS passport offices. Officials have stated that 30 persons were injured due to shrapnel, smoke inhalation, and second-degree burns, three of them in a critical state. According to police statements, the bombs appear to have been planted overnight in the office's main reception area. Police are currently investigating for the culprit or culprits but do not have a suspect at this time.

”Defensa Interior took credit for the bombing in a statement delivered to this news station earlier today, claiming that the strike was meant as an attack against police. While two of the injured were police officers assigned to security detail in the passport office, the majority of the victims were employees of the passport bureau and Iberian citizens attempting to have their passports renewed.“

”We wish the injured a speedy recovery and hope the perpetrators can be brought to justice soon. We at EFE will keep you updated on this breaking matter as more information becomes available.“
strings.IBR_terror.108.a: A fire burns. It does not care what.
strings.IBR_terror.109.t: The Siege of San Andrés de Palomar
strings.IBR_terror.109.d:
Case Number: 548014{year}

Reporting Officer: Teo Montero

Details of Incident: The San Andrés de Palomar crisis can be considered concluded, the week long occupation of buildings within the Barcelona neighbourhood by DI insurgents ending with their neutralization. Of the 74 DI insurgents believed to have been involved, 37 have been confirmed dead, 35 hospitalized and the remainder arrested. The prospect that some insurgents successfully fled means the total number cannot be definitively confirmed.

The DI seized a number of buildings around the neighbourhood, centered around the Plaça de les Palmeres. As previous reports noted, the DI publicly made their presence known via loudspeaker and a public execution of missing AAS Agent Hugo Jofré. The area was subsequently evacuated.

Early attempts to dislodge them led to the Plaça de les Palmeres debacle, where Police, Guardia Civil and supporting AAS combat teams were caught in a crossfire as the DI revealed positions in multiple buildings forming a crossfire. The DI insurgents remained highly mobile, having collapsed walls between buildings, and well armed with a variety of Italian and German weapons of unknown origin. They made frequent use of improvised explosives both hidden and utilised as grenades. Details on all operations are available in Appendices 1-9.

The decision to deny a military response likely contributed to the length of the siege. Attrition tactics between counter-terrorism teams and insurgents forced their eventual surrender. The siege motive remains unknown and arrested insurgents have provided none. That the Agency was provoked and the siege's highly public nature gives us our current hypothesis; that this was an operation designed solely as a show of force.
strings.IBR_terror.200.d:
Case Number: 421362{year}

Reporting Officer: Jorge Herrera

At 2346, AAS operatives successfully conducted an assault upon the last known Euskadi Ta Askatasuna (ETA) mountain hideout across the Basque Country. This particular outpost was reported to be host to the group's “Zuba”, or directional committee, and its removal will prove a major blow to ETA's organizational capabilities.

It is believed that all active terrorist personnel within the base have either been killed or effectively apprehended for questioning. Bereft of headquarters and with fractured leadership, we expect surviving cells scattered around the region to either eventually lay down arms or lack the cohesion to pose any significant threat to our conventional military forces.

While a cause for rejoice, securing this victory came at the cost of numerous casualties on our side as well, with ETA militias offering unexpectedly fierce resistance despite their numerical disadvantage, quickly organizing into a rather effective defense force even in the face of surprise.

Their training, and above all, worrying supply of equipment raises further concern about the source of their material support, which, lacking more than meager backing among most of the Basque civilian populace, can only be accounted to external means.

Until our investigations into the guerrillas' mysterious purported benefactors bear fruit, this operation should still, as of yet, be considered the most significant accomplishment in our efforts to liberate our country from the separatist threat.
strings.IBR_terror.201.d:
Case Number: 295163{year}

Reporting Officer: Gualtiero Camino

Details of Incident: At 2025 hours, two men were arrested near a rail line just outside of Bilbao. The two men were spotted acting suspiciously by railroad employees, detained after a brief verbal confrontation and turned over to local authorities. The two men, Marcelo Mancilla and Vinicio Ignacio, were caught with picks and shovels and appeared to be damaging the rail line in an attempted sabotage.

After a brief interrogation, both men admitted to being members of Euskadi Ta Askatasuna (ETA) and hoped to sabotage the rail line to stoke unrest and damage the legitimacy of the Iberian government in the hopes of furthering the cause of Basque independence. Neither man was known to police sources as expressing anti-government sentiment or advocating for Basque nationalism, suggesting the size of ETA may be larger than initially theorized. Interrogation remains ongoing.

Security officials at railways and dockyards in Basque regions are instructed to have heightened vigilance until the scope of the threat to Iberian infrastructure becomes clear. It is clear that a train derailment would have been a significant disaster with a large loss of life and materiel.
strings.IBR_terror.202.d:
Case Number: 677230{year}

Reporting Officer: Isandro Castrejon

Details of Incident: At 2130, 16 members of the Iberian Police engaged in a brief firefight with 5 members of the Euskadi Ta Askatasuna (ETA) at a warehouse in the industrial district of Donostia-San Sebastián. The 16 members were part of a task force investigating a lead that the warehouse was used as an armory by the ETA. After the task force entered the building, they discovered five ETA members located in a room located in the rear of the facility armed with pistols. The task force issued an order for the men to lay down their arms and surrender; the ETA responded by opening fire. Officer Tercero Borquez was shot in the hip in the initial exchange of gunfire, while Sergeant León Vega was injured in the eye attempting to pull Officer Borquez into cover; police medics believe he was struck by a ricocheting projectile. After a short exchange of gunfire, officers reiterated their demand for the ETA members to surrender and that the building was surrounded. When the ETA members retreated into their armory, Lieutenant Isandro Castrejon, task force leader, ordered the use of riot gas grenades. The grenades were deployed successfully and the ETA members were successfully subdued and arrested.

The armory contained rifles, pistols, bulletproof vests, optics, and other related equipment sufficient to equip approximately sixty persons (see attached form 8-A for complete inventory). The equipment was commonly older models of German and French manufacture, suggesting illicit purchases on the black market. Also found in the warehouse were Iberian Armed Police and Iberian Armed Forces uniforms, potentially indicating future false flag attacks against Iberian personnel or attempts to compromise security checkpoints at police or army facilities.

Interrogation of the five ETA members is ongoing. Investigation into possible sympathizers who may have authorized the ETA to use the warehouse as an armory has been determined to be a top priority. Sergeant Vega has been recommended for a commendation following his actions to rescue his subordinate while under fire.
strings.IBR_terror.202.a: Operation has been deemed a success.
strings.IBR_terror.203.d:
Pastor Fleitas, the face of the Iberian news, looked out upon the carcass of the decimated building. For a moment, Pastor thought it looked like a crabshell after a dinner, an open gap that once held meat within. The smell got to Pastor most of all, a disgusting blend of machine oil and ink that caused him to gag when he first made it to the site. Once the camera crew was ready though, he had to be the journalist that Iberia depended on. He suppressed his disgust, looking straight into the camera, and gave the people the news they depended on him for.

“Pastor Fleitas coming to you from Navarro. A bomb exploded at the printing offices of El Pensamiento Navarro in the early morning hours. No injuries were reported, but several printing presses were damaged. The terrorist group Euskadi Ta Askatasuna claimed responsibility for the act, calling for the destruction of any organizations affiliated with Don Javier de Borbón as a critical step in establishing a robust, independent Basque Country separate from the Iberian Union and the shackles of the past.”

“Bajardo Campano, the chief editor of the El Pensamiento Navarro, issued a statement. 'While we are most grateful to Almighty God that no one was harmed in the explosion, our facility and equipment suffered significant damage. It is unfortunate, but we must reduce our publication schedule to one issue per week until we can repair or replace the damaged printing presses. We thank our subscribers for their patience as we work to restore ourselves to full functionality and can deliver them the publication that we are famous for.”

“Police investigations are in the earliest stages, but their leadership have expressed confidence that the perpetrator or perpetrators will be caught soon. Individuals with information relating to the case should contact their local authorities.”
strings.IBR_terror.203.a: A movement cannot speak without its tongue.
strings.IBR_terror.204.d:
Pastor Fleitas looked over at the body language of the people in the studio, noticing that they had appeared much more relaxed than usual. Good news had a palpable energy to it.

“The issue of businessman Gaspar Valladolid has been brought to its conclusion, much to the relief of his family, as he was discovered alive today in the outskirts of Guernica. Valladolid's kidnapping last week made national headlines, with the terror group Euskadi Ta Askatasuna claiming credit and issuing a ransom demand that, in the interests of maintaining the family's privacy, was not made public. The family had announced that they intended to pay the ransom after ETA threatened to kill Valladolid this past Saturday if the ransom was not delivered. It appears that the ransom was paid and Gaspar was rushed to Guernica General. While he was suffering from dehydration and appeared to have been drugged, doctors report that he had no life-threatening injuries and expects to make a full recovery in the immediate future.”

“While it is known that the ETA committed the kidnapping, the suspect or suspects are currently unknown at this time. Valladolid was kidnapped by at least three masked men driving a red panel van who ambushed him in the parking garage outside his workplace. He was blindfolded and driven for a significant length of time, so he was unable to provide a significant description of his abductors. Police investigations are currently ongoing.”
strings.IBR_terror.204.a: One man is saved at the cost of many more.
strings.IBR_terror.205.d:
Case Number: 320670{year}

Reporting Officer: Eurico Sigüenza

Details of Incident: At 1530 hours, Captain Eugenio Campoy was shot by two unidentified gunmen in the city square of San Sebastián. Captain Campoy was departing from a social function at City Hall when a motorcycle pulled up near him, with one driver and one passenger directly behind. The passenger identified Captain Campoy by his first name to solicit his attention. After Captain Campoy approached the motorcycle to speak with the passenger, the driver pulled a small-caliber pistol and fired directly into Captain Campoy's abdomen. After firing, the motorcycle sped off, with the pistol being discarded at the scene.

Captain Campoy was rushed to Our Lady of Mercy Hospital, and after two hours of emergency surgery was declared in stable condition. Captain Campoy sustained damage to his stomach and kidneys, but is expected to make a full recovery. Lieutenant Rafael Calzada will assume his duties until Captain Campoy is medically cleared for duty.

Witnesses were unable to clearly identify either the driver or the passenger of the motorcycle, as both wore helmets that fully obscured their facial features. The motorcycle's license plate was tracked to a motorcycle stolen from Bilbao approximately seven months ago. The armed militant group Euskadi Ta Askatasuna claimed responsibility for the attack, claiming that Captain Campoy, as a captain of the Iberian Police, represented the threat of Iberian tyranny and the face of colonial oppression.
strings.IBR_terror.206.d:
Case Number: 204363{year}

Reporting Officer: Eberardo Giraldo

Details of Incident: At 1345 hours, a bomb exploded outside of the police station at Plaza del Castilo. The bomb appeared to have been planted in the trunk of a pale green SEAT 600 parked outside the station about one hour before detonation. There are approximately thirteen injured in the blast, mostly officers and pedestrians outside of the police station at the time of the blast. There were zero fatalities, but four men remain in critical condition. All thirteen medical reports are attached for more detailed review.

No group has claimed responsibility as of the time of reporting, but Euskadi Ta Askatasuna (ETA) is strongly suspected to have carried out the attack. Five members of ETA were held at the police station, detained on charges of weapons trafficking, robbery and terror charges temporarily while arrangements were made to transfer to a maximum-security facility; their transfer was successfully completed two days ago. While there is no confirmation of ETA involvement, the timing and location of the bombing is unlikely to be coincidental and this remains the primary focus of the investigation.

The bombing did significant damage to the car and has complicated identification efforts to trace the original owner. The license plate was captured on CCTV and was traced to a vehicle belonging to Wilfredo Baca, resident of Pamplona and aviation engineer. His vehicle was discovered in a parking garage with its license plate missing. Baca has been cooperative and is unsuspected of being involved in this crime.
strings.IBR_terror.206.a: A message not unheard by its intended listeners.
strings.IBR_terror.207.d:
It was a uniquely Navarrese trait that bestowed the gift to transcend the puny lobster into something that only could suitably be described as a form of art. Few things held more truth in Jesús Larrainzar Yoldi's mind; just as the fact that it was one to be consumed in duly temperate and tastefully-spaced occasions, which made each of his visits to the Eskalera all the more precious when they did occur.

But beyond bold statements of culinary delights, the lavish seafood restaurant, solely catering to the Pamplona elite, also provided the aging Governor an even dearer escape from the worries outside: into a fortress of brick and exquisite scents that neither the Madrid vultures nor the chaos further south could breach. Hell, even the Basque vermin stood locked away from his usual concern this evening, or so he cared to make known to the many socialites gathered to schmooz and mingle within the latest instance of his chronic parties.

Of course, the stellar recent successes of the local Guardia Civil had no small part to play in buying him this peace of mind. And if he wished they'd have drawn just a bit more from the lastly-caught rat before its untimely passing, he had every faith that his boys' occasional lapses in restraint would prove more than welcome as they scoured the curfewed streets to find its peers before any more could imagine threatening his solace.

Indeed. In this instant, any and all that mattered to him stood within these confines. Right here with him, and anyone deserving of note within generous reach. And all would bear witness to the clock as it rang ten, though less so to the muffled click it would hide. Nor to the silent progress of a fuze lit underneath the floorboards of a rampaging class that knew only of feast. Or the tiniest crackling of sparks from one final serving of those upon which they gorged.

But not a single one would miss the light.
strings.IBR_terror.207.a: And there would never be anything else.
strings.IBR_terror.208.d:
Even hours after the incident, Pastor Fleitas could smell that sickly scent of blood in the air of the latest bombing site. It smelled like old, wet copper that stuck in the back of the throat. The cleaning crews may have covered up the sight of it but the smell lingered in the tile floors, just as the memory of the attack would persist in the people who experienced it long after the flash and noise were gone. He made sure to look his best and stare directly in the camera - the people of Iberia demanded nothing less.

“Pastor Fleitas and the EFE speaking to you live and on scene in the capital. The Cafetería Rolando was a favorite restaurant for many at the Puerta del Sol in Madrid; every day of the week countless passersby would stop by for a bite to eat morning, noon, or night. That daily scene turned to horror today as a bomb exploded in the main dining area just past noon. According to latest reports, twelve people are dead and fifty-nine are wounded, primarily from shrapnel and debris propelled by the explosion. Several of the injured remain in critical condition in nearby hospitals.”

“No group has officially claimed credit for the attack, and police emphasize that this is still in the initial stages of the investigation and more information will be forthcoming in the future. However, police sources believe that the militant group Euskadi Ta Askatasuna, or ETA, was responsible for the blast and they believe they know the motive. Cafeteria Rolando was believed to be targeted because it is frequented by officers of the Directorate of General Security, whose headquarters are located nearby, as a favored spot for their lunch breaks. Therefore, ETA was hoping to conduct an attack on DGS personnel. Police sources consider ETA to be a significant threat to national security and have stressed that the perpetrators will face swift justice in the near future.”

Pastor didn't know what else he could do other than report it, so that everyone in Iberia knew exactly what had happened.
strings.IBR_terror.208.a: A fast way to make a statement, and invite a response.
strings.IBR_terror.209.d:
Case Number: 234552{year}

Reporting Officer: Leo Sastre Lagos

At 0324, several explosive incidents were reported in numerous infrastructure landmarks across the Basque Country, all in near-simultaneous occurrences.

Targets of significant note include critical railway links between the city of Bilbao and several key logistical sites, including major weapons, ammunition, and material depots.

Presently recorded casualties remain limited, and it appears the attacks were intended to focus exclusively on military targets, with the suggested aim of paralyzing troop movement capacity as well as the means to supply presumedly deployed forces.

Encounters between our rapid response personnel and apprehended suspects fleeing the bombing sites have resulted in two instances of light-intensity skirmishes, both resulting in death; one of which due to the subject allegedly taking their own life. Bodies attest with near-certainty the Basque-nationalist terrorist group referred to as “Euskadi Ta Askatasuna” to be the author of these strikes. As of writing, no enemy operative has successfully been captured alive.

It is not currently possible to confirm whether the goal of these strikes is to prepare the ground for a full uprising coordinated by the separatist cells or simply provide a distraction to allow for a more comprehensive set of attacks.

We affirm that every effort is being made into investigating the security flaws that allowed these acts to proceed in the first place, and the hunt for any remaining escapees remains of the utmost priority for our local field agents.
strings.IBR_terror.209.a: So many wheels, with so many wedges left to fit.
strings.IBR_terror.300.d:
Hugo had always imagined a glorious end, filled with glorious defiance against the fascists. He'd never deluded himself to their chances of winning, of an independent Asturias finally breaking the chains of oppression. His fate had always been just to carry the torch as far as he could. As he gazed at the antique revolver in his hands as he sat on the side of his bed, he pondered. Had he stumbled in that duty?

He was far from his native Asturias now, instead some small town in the middle of Andalusia posing as a travelling university student with the help of an old ID. He'd been lucky enough to beg this spare room from the night, a grotty little room consisting of a rusted bed and a barren red closet, the grey bricks of the walls looking like they hadn't been cleaned since Napoleon's men passed through. He couldn't stay in Asturias, he couldn't fulfil his oath as a BTA member anymore. There was no BTA left.

Things had been bad for a while. Arrests and discovered caches, but few had been truly concerned. They were an insurgency, crackdowns were inevitable. Then, in the space of a week, the entire organisation fell apart. Military raids destroyed headquarters, leaders shot or arrested. By the time Hugo had fled, he was hard pressed to name any fellow BTA members that hadn't fallen victim to Franco's forces.

A knock at the door to the room. Firm, three strikes upon the old wood. Hugo froze, his body tensing as though he were rendered to stone. The only part that moved was his heart, which painfully pounded. Senora Alfaguara said she would be gone all day yet it was barely past noon. He hadn't heard the door open. He had heard distant sirens however, perhaps...

He tried to raise his revolver, his last tool of resistance, to the door as the door knocked again. No call of identification came from the other side. It simply kept pounding, this time not stopping.
strings.IBR_terror.300.a: Hugo's terrified eyes aimed the shaking weapon at the door, unsure of whether to fire.
strings.IBR_terror.301.d:
Case Number: 732355{year}

Reporting Officer: Patricio Pelaez

Details of Incident: At 1545 hours, an eight-man task force led by Sergeant Patricio Pelaez was tasked with closing an illegal printing press calling itself “The Worker's Voice” discovered in the outskirts of Gijón via a confidential police informant. Sergeant Pelaez led Officers Sofronio Gonzalo and Simón Esquilin to issue a warning, dismantle the printing press, and shut down the illegal publication. When Officer Esquilin radioed for an engineer to dismantle the printing press, Jacobo Vilchez, a 28-year old man who identified himself as the author of numerous articles for “The Worker's Voice” became agitated and combative. Officer Gonzalo ordered Vilchez to stand away from the machinery, repeating his demand three times. During this time, Officer Gonzalo acted professionally, refusing to be baited by Vilchez nor any of the other staff members. After the third time, Vilchez complied, moving away while Officer Esquilin continued to make his radio request.

While Esquilin was occupied and Gonzalo and Pelaez observed the staff, Vilchez grabbed a wrench and struck Officer Gonzalo on the head. Sergeant Pelaez responded immediately, grabbing his baton and subduing Vilchez while Esquilin shielded Gonzalo. No other members joined in the altercation, and Officer Gonzalo was able to stand on his own two feet.

Vilchez was arrested and the printing press was successfully dismantled. The other members of the staff professed no knowledge of Vilchez's attempt to assault Officer Gonzalo and were arrested at the scene for the lesser charge of publishing seditious material. During interrogation, Vilchez identified himself as a member of the Batallones de Trabajadores Asturianos, a known terror group active in the Asturias region.
strings.IBR_terror.301.a: The new procedure going forward is that all suspects on scene are to be cuffed before destroying equipment.
strings.IBR_terror.302.d:
Case Number: 349002{year}

Reporting Officer: Santiago Davila

A small-scale brawl occurred on the grounds of Oviedo University just after noon. Campus security alerted local Oviedo police that two groups appeared to be engaging in fisticuffs. When police arrived, Officer Santaigo Davila secured the scene and utilized security assets to arrest those who had participated in the brawl. Overall, nine people were detained on charges of simple assault and disorderly conduct.

According to eyewitnesses, members of the Falange were performing a public rally with their youth corps, for which their student organization was able to produce legal permits from the university They were approached by members of an unknown group who attempted to intimidate them into stopping their meeting, shouting and attempting to surround them. When the Falange refused to yield their ground, members of the second group became enraged, shoving them and telling them to leave the campus grounds. The Falangists continued to refuse, and after that, Anibal Dorado, leader of the second group, attempted to punch one of the Falangists, igniting the brawl.

The second group was later identified to be members of the Batallones de Trabajadores Asturianos (BTA) who had either attended the university or lived near its campus grounds. Anibal Dorado, the leader of the BTA group, will be charged with aggravated assault and incitement to riot in addition to simple assault and disorderly conduct for his role in leading. Police investigators will comb over the footage and testimony of the incident to see if the Falangist group members, who had acted in self-defense, will have their charges reduced or dropped entirely.
strings.IBR_terror.303.d:
“Oviedo was rocked by an explosion today in the late afternoon after an explosive device detonated at the Falange party headquarters in the city center today. Police sources state that at about half-past three a bomb exploded on the north side of the building, causing structural damage to the building but no injuries were reported due to the low explosive yield of the device and the building's stone construction. Explosives experts for the Iberian Police searched the building and found no other explosive devices present, and they have concluded that this was a bombing of opportunity rather than one part of a larger coordinated campaign and do not believe the public to be in imminent danger of another bombing.”

“Police sources stated that the bombing was politically motivated due to fresh graffiti placed near the site where the bomb was placed proclaiming 'Death to Fascism. Death to Fascists.' Eyewitnesses believe that they had seen a man wearing dark sunglasses enter the alley where the bomb was planted with a bag on his shoulder, believed to be the bomb, about ten minutes before the bomb detonated. Police sources caution Iberians everywhere to be suspicious of abandoned bags or packages, and report them to police if they are discovered unattended. From Oviedo, this has been Pastor Fleitas with EFE, bringing you the latest news from Iberia and beyond.”

***

Later that night, what Pastor had said really weighed upon him as he took a sip of his after-dinner coffee. The last thing he wanted to do was fearmonger the people of Iberia to have them see phantom bombs in every forgotten suitcase. But if it saved a life, perhaps a little dose of fear could save someone a lifetime of heartbreak. Resolute, Pastor knew all he could do was continue.
strings.IBR_terror.303.a: Sometimes it's the little things. Sometimes it's the little sins.
strings.IBR_terror.304.d:
“Residents of several villages in Eastern Asturias were left without power today after a bomb exploded at the power plant outside of Llanes. Several people were injured in fires stemming from this blast, but no fatalities have been recorded. Multiple villages reported being without power following this bombing, with blackouts lasting up to four hours in the villages. Remote areas are still experiencing some disruption. The resulting blackouts left one elderly woman requiring medical care, but her condition has been stabilized and doctors predict a full recovery.”

“The terror group Batallones de Trabajadores Asturianos claimed responsibility for the attack, and have promised more bombings to come. Emergency crews have been working to restore the grid to full functionality and this bombing has raised amongst local officials questions of redundancy in the power grid to ensure functionality and reserve capacity in the event of another bombing or natural disaster. That's the latest news from Iberia and around the world. This is Pastor Fleitas for EFE, signing off.”

“We're clear, good work Signor Fleitas,” the camera crewman, who couldn't have been older than 20, gave him a nod.

For a second, Pastor wondered, what was even the point of BTA bombing a power station. How did it advance their cause? How did it win the sympathy of the Iberian people? There were hundreds of boys just like his crewman in eastern Asturias. How many of them feared for fires in their homes, or their sick grandmothers without electricity? Was he a fool for trying to find the logic of it, or was it simply lost on him?
strings.IBR_terror.304.a: Pastor grimaced for a second, unnoticed for all save for a single camera crewman.
strings.IBR_terror.305.d:
Case Number: 826749{year}

Reporting Officer: Desi Del Cid

Details of Incident: At 0955 hours, a bomb exploded in Gijón port damaging the cargo vessel Alberini as it sat in port awaiting unloading. The bomb was planted in cargo bay 3 and appeared to have been planted on the exterior of a cargo container, suggesting that the bomb was loaded either by a member of the crew or a longshoreman at the previous port of call. The ship was searched thoroughly and was declared to be free of explosive devices at 1630 hours.

The yield of the bomb was insufficient to rupture the hull, and the ship is in no immediate danger of sinking. No deaths were reported but 14 people were injured in the bombing primarily from the lateral and rotational shock provided by the explosion. This resulted in injuries from personnel falling and striking bulkheads or being struck by falling equipment. Repair crews have been dispatched to repair damage to the internal walls and structures; an assessment of how long repair efforts are forthcoming.

There are currently no suspects that have been identified. The crew members of the Alberini have not been founded to harbor any ties to militant groups either foreign or domestic. Gijón does have pockets of Batallones de Trabajadores Asturianos (BTA) sentiment; lead investigator Desi Del Cid suspects that the bomb may have been planted by a dockworker during their initial cargo inspection. If a BTA member is among the port employees, they would be well-suited to conduct such a terror attack. Investigation remains ongoing.
strings.IBR_terror.305.a: One of the longshoremen will know something, question them until they crack.
strings.IBR_terror.306.d:
The anchorman steeled his gaze, keeping his jaw firm and his gaze sharp, as he began the broadcast. “Good evening, I am Pastor Fleitas with EFE. The small town of Langreo was rocked by an explosion this afternoon after a bomb exploded at the offices of Reales Minas de Langreo. No deaths were reported, but several office workers were wounded in the explosion and are currently being treated for shrapnel and burns resulting from the bombing.”

“The Batallones de Trabajadores Asturianos claimed responsibility for the attack today, issuing a statement that this bombing was to strike back at Reales Minas de Langreo corporate leadership for their controversial layoffs of 20 miners last week without severance and that the BTA stands in solidarity with the working people of Asturias. RML's chief executive, Valerio Camino, condemned the bombing, reassuring the public that all appropriate measures are being taken to safeguard the health and welfare of all its employees. Signor Camino also stated that the mines will remain open and that business operations will not be disrupted by the bombing.”

“Initial analysis has suggested that the bomb was planted inside of the building but it is currently unknown how the perpetrators managed to enter the building and plant the bomb unnoticed. The current suspect appears to be a man in his thirties identified as Carlos Manso, a deliveryman who was seen in the building shortly before the bomb detonated. However, police sources have stressed that the investigation is only in the preliminary stages, and have asked anyone with information on the perpetrators to contact them immediately.”

Pastor kept looking forward as the cameras began to stop rolling, but he couldn't help but think - what if a bomb had hit these offices? Would he still be able to look at the camera, back straight, diction perfect, when it was people he knew covered in burns and debris? Or would he crumple as easily as the first draft he discarded this morning?
strings.IBR_terror.306.a: Distance makes the heart grow harder.
strings.IBR_terror.307.t: BTA Assasination Attempt on Oviedo Governor
strings.IBR_terror.307.d:
Case Number: 589112{year}

Reporting Officer: Emilio Medina

Details of Incident: The Civil Governor of the Oviedo province, José Manuel Mateu de Ros, is currently hospitalized following an attempt on his life by the Batallones de Trabajadores Asturianos yesterday evening. Leaving his office at 21:44, security observed him entering his vehicle at 21:46 before fire enveloped it it. The Governor was able to escape the burning vehicle before a final detonation occurred. He is currently suffering from a multitude of second and third degree burns. First response was on the scene by 21:54, AAS agents by 22:00.

The offices have been closed and staff relocated to a temporary location while examination of the vehicle remains continue. It is apparent that the device malfunctioned in some way, giving the governor a timeframe in which to escape, though the exact cause has not yet been conclusively determined. It is suspected that the bomb had insufficient explosive force to penetrate the metal plate underneath the driver's seat of the car.

The BTA have already claimed responsibility for the attack via a pirate broadcast that briefly hijacked Oviedo broadcasting at 08:19 this morning. We suspect the broadcast was pre-recorded, as it states that the Governor was killed rather than wounded. Staff at the broadcasting station and any staff members present in the Governor's office's car park are being questioned for further information on both incidents.
strings.IBR_terror.307.a: Examination of the vehicle continues, and results will be reported as they appear.
strings.IBR_terror.308.d:
The Oviedo Regional Council Building looked like it had been hit with nothing short of a storm without water. Desks bolted to the ground had been ripped from their fixtures and toppled like great beached whales. At this scene, Pastor Fleitas, the trusted face of EFE, stood with his faithful cameraman ready to film the devastation.

“Pastor Fleitas in Oviedo tonight, and this is EFE. A dagger has been struck into the very heart of the region as a bomb exploded in the Diputación de Oviedo building. The bomb exploded roughly one half-hour after the Diputación had adjourned for the day, but some of the members had remained behind, either to do paperwork in their offices or hold committee meetings to discuss affairs of regional governance. No deaths were reported, but there are at least thirty people injured, including at least three Councilmen.”

“The terror group Batallones de Trabajadores Asturianos took credit for the bombing, issuing a statement where they decried the Diputación as instruments of the Iberian oppressors and traitors to their fellow countrymen. BTA continued on in their statement, expressing that all collaborators are hereby notified that they will be considered foreign threats and treated accordingly.”

“Police sources are currently investigating the bombing, but have not announced any suspects. A Diputación spokesman has stated that BTA is a threat to all Iberians and that all terrorists will be dealt with to the fullest extent of the law possible. They have urged all members of the public with information regarding any member of BTA to come forward as a matter of both public safety and patriotic civic duty.
strings.IBR_terror.308.a: Asturias has been found to be full of kindling.
strings.IBR_terror.309.d:
The blazing sirens and the roaring inferno made the night red with heat and noise, the thunderous roars of the water bursting towards the building creating an orchestra of flame. Sweat poured down the faces of the firefighters clinging to the hoses, hot and sticky beneath their uniforms. The fire continued unabated, it was unquenchable in its hunger for food. The Iberian Historical Archive burned, and despite their best efforts it would not abate.

It was difficult to surround the building. Built off the Calle de Serrano, it was surrounded by other tall official buildings. An observatory, the Research Council building, their only real access had been the once well kept lawn before it, now churned and muddy from the trucks and hoses. A small car park around the back offered some access, but they couldn't access a large swathe of the building's rear; exactly where the flames seemed to originate from.

Behind the contact line of the firefighters, with the command unit, stood two conspicuous men. They wore lean and cheapsuits, patiently watching the inflamed archive as men moved around them. None spoke to them. None seemed to recognise their presence.

“Can't lie, the tip off was accurate. It is being reduced to embers.” One of the men spoke, hands in his pockets.

“Tip offs don't mock, or arrive just as fires start. Someone did this, and they want us to know it was on purpose.” The other man crossed his arms. “We need to know when this fire will be out, we need to find some trace of who did this.”

He began to walk to the command desk beside the trucks before his colleague spoke. “Who do you think did this one?”

A solemn look at the flames, and then at his partner. “Let's find out.”
strings.IBR_terror.400.d:
“Now, are we absolutely certain that they are there?”

“I identified them myself before you arrived, they're there. Torre delivered perfectly; they all came. So, shall we begin?”

Paulo Costa and Paco Ortega, AAS agents, sat upon the hill overlooking the shack. The ramshackle building was in a valley, a small wood around it. A single dirt road led back to civilization, winding through the hills around them. They were hidden by mere bushes but the risk had been more than worth it to see the proud meeting place of the leaders of the BR. It was hard to believe this collapsing shack had been the source of so much trouble.

Paulo sighed, before nodding. “We should go back and get things started, Torre was ordered to keep them talking. Shouldn't be an issue for them at all. You verified the army set things up correctly, right?” He took another look through his binoculars, seeing only wood and grass.

Paco spoke with a glee Paulo hadn't heard since they began their work together. “Mortars set up, road's blocked around the bend and there's snipers and response teams surrounding the entire valley. No escapes this time. On the signal, they'll turn this place into a moon crater. We can stroll in and mop up after.”

“Good,” Paulo moved up into a crouch and started to ascend the hill as Paco followed, “but it's a shame about Torre.”

“You want to attempt an extraction? We have the means, I guess.”

Paulo stopped, placing his hand and knee on the ground as he bent in contemplation. After a moment he shook his head. “We can't risk it, it's almost over” he muttered, as both men continued up.
strings.IBR_terror.400.a: Over the hill they gave the signal, and so ended the story of the Brigadas Revolucionárias.
strings.IBR_terror.401.d:
“I need you to think very hard about last night, Señor Gallo. Was there anything out of the usual?”

AAS Agent Paulo Costa before the remains of the Faro factory with its owner. Police and firefighters bumbled around, performing their busywork, but none dared bother him nor his conversation partner. They sat upon a low brick wall, backs to the road, Paulo watching as Gallo red, damp eyes bore into the dirt below them. On the ground before the factory a message had been smeared. “SPANISH SCUM”. A common calling card of the Brigadas Revolucionárias.

“I moved here from Valencia just after the Civil War you know...” he muttered, voice strained from private tears. “I did everything I could to be a good employer. Fair wages, an open door policy to complaints, I even put on a Christmas party out of pocket. Now?” he motioned at the bones of the building that remained. “Theres nothing left.”

Paulo bristled internally, eager to finish the reminiscing. He could see his partner Paco rambling through the ruins achieving little of substance too. “I understand Señor, anything you can tell me about last night could help.”

Gallo looked morosely at the dirt again, long enough for Paulo to start summoning curses within his mind, before finally speaking. “Not last night, but last week. There was an unannounced safety inspection team from the city. Had all the right documents, said they were going through all the local factories, though no one I spoke to after had ever heard of them. They insisted on having a copy of the master key to the doors, to smooth over the inspection.”

Paulo blinked. “Are you certain they weren't forgeries?”

“Absolutely not, I've grown very adept at spotting those.”
strings.IBR_terror.401.a: Paulo stood up from the wall. “Paco, get over here. We got something!”
strings.IBR_terror.402.d:
Traffic coming into Lisbon has been jammed as a result of the latest antics of the Portuguese separatists. At approximately 1 pm, what was once a rather busy road was blasted into bits of asphalt by a crudely made bomb, leaving a giant crater in the middle of a four lane highway and sending the city into a state of emergency.

While fortunately, no fatalities have been reported, this attack by the BR shows an increase in competence in the terrorist group, as they are now willing to harm innocent people for the sake of their goals. The Guardia Civil has acted quickly and arrests have been made, but the ringleaders remain elusive as usual, and it is clear from recent statements that the terrorists only plan to continue hindering our nation in whatever way they can.
strings.IBR_terror.403.d:
Paco Ortega, AAS agent, reached the site first and swore as he did, seeing the swarm of Lisbon Police Department drones no doubt contaminating the crime scene. It had been barely even dawn when his phone rang, telling him of the explosion as to get there as soon as he could. He'd apologized to his wife for waking her, prayed the kids hadn't heard, before he had run out of the house in yesterday's suit which was still thrown by the side. The long hours meant he hadn't even gotten home until nearly midnight, he hadn't the energy for standards.

He burst out of his car, shouting for the nearest officer while flashing his badge. “Is Paulo here?”

“Who?”

The passion of irritance left little sympathy for the officer within Paco. “AAS, has any other AAS agents turned up.” A shake of the head served as his answer. He abandoned the officer and moved further up the road to the crater that had remained. It was large, the bomb that had done this must have been sizable, and off-centered to the left. Windows were shattered around, nervous faces looking down through their frames. Bomb must have been hidden under one of the car wrecks that lingered around the crater. He looked around; this area would have been busy come rush hour, it was a well known commuting route.

“What do you think?” A voice came from behind Paco, cutting through the sirens and noise of the crime scene. Paulo stood, in equally as dishevelled a state as Paco was.

“Bomb, probably supposed to go off during rush hour. Take out a car or too, maybe get a pileup. Luckily all it is now is a bill to the city.”

Paulo fumbled in his coat for a cigarette, offering one to Paco, before lighting it. His lighter illuminated tired, grey eyes. “BR work?”
strings.IBR_terror.403.a: Paco lit his cigarette. “Who the fuck else could it be?”
strings.IBR_terror.404.d:
The last thing Alejandro had ever heard was the grenade rolling across the cold stone floor of his quarters. He heard no cries. He heard no gunfire. Only an explosion followed by blood-soaked pillows.

His bunk had taken most of the shrapnel. His roommates were not as fortunate. Alejandro grabbed his pistol and fired at the first shadow that entered his room. He only tasted the gunpowder residue firing from his gun.

Another entered. Another shot. Another fell. A grenade rolled in without a pin. Without hesitation, Alejandro jumped off his bunk and threw it back outside. He only smelled the sulphuric powder rising into the air, mingling with the metallic blood.

Some of his roommates lay unconscious — or had already passed. Others were too injured to get up. Alejandro slowly made his way out of the room, checking both sides of the hallway. A boy, no older than seventeen, lay lifeless next to him. He could only feel his feet squelching against his lain out guts.

Alejandro pushed through the halls. Each corner was rounded meticulously. But there were no attackers. Just bodies of his fellow officers, lying alongside Brigadas Revolucionárias terrorists. If either of them were alive, he could not tell. He could only see masses of bodies clogging the hall.

Then a tap came from behind. Alejandro turned around with a pistol in hand, ready to fire, before realizing it was his commanding officer. His lips moved, but he could not hear the words coming out of his mouth. He could not hear the absence of gunfire. He could not hear the chirping of birds outside as the sun rose over Lisbon.
strings.IBR_terror.404.a: He tried to speak, but he could not hear his own self.
strings.IBR_terror.405.d:
Paulo sat in the car, and for a moment he debated turning the ignition and driving away. He was tired, dog tired. He hadn't slept properly in weeks - he couldn't believe he was looking back on his PIDE days with rose-colored glasses. Back then, working long days then coming home to an empty apartment had seemed like a nadir. At least back then he'd been able to go back to an apartment. Now he spent more nights under a desk or in his car than in a be-

A knock on the window disturbed his rumination. Paco looked at him from outside, exhausted eyes looking on in something between sympathy and resignation. Paulo shook his head and slapped his cheeks before opening the door. They had a job to do.

He stepped out of the car and together they moved into the mass of emergency vehicles and personnel. Neither men spoke, neither needed to. They had seen it all before. A BR bombing, some new tragedy they had to stare at and assure officers that all was under control. Another list of damages and casualties to add to their file to serve as little more than context to their eventual report. Today was an apartment block, and as they reached the far side of the Police cordon both men stared impassively at what remained of it.

The blast had clearly been from one of the central apartments. A hole was gouged into it, reaching into a dozen rooms. If they squinted they could see corpses, or at least parts of them, in the blasted rooms no doubt considered too unstable to touch.

“Not a single Spanish person lived here, Paulo.” Paco said. His voice carried no sorrow nor horror. He spoke matter of factly, coarse voice commenting as if it were the weather.

“These apartments were expensive. Rich, educated, maybe just lucky from mom and dad. I'm sure the BR had some crime it could pin on them.”
strings.IBR_terror.405.a: Both men stood before the ruin, shoulders low as it began to rain.
strings.IBR_terror.406.d:
“Ladies and Gentleman, I won't take up much of your time. Our message is simple, and we want you to think on our words.”

A man dressed in black, a sack with eyeholes upon his face, spoke from the RTP News Anchor's seat. He was shouting, his words garbled through the sack, but subtitled upon the screen. All across Portugal, people stared at their TV's in silent horror. Gone were the friendly faces upon the news desk calmly informing them on the world. Those people sat bound and gagged before the desk, weeping and terrorised, as masked men roamed the set.

“We are the Brigadas Revolucionárias. Your leaders have tried to hide our existence from you; let this be the end of that charade. We strike where we choose, we go where we please, and victory shall be ours. The Iberian abomination will be destroyed. A free Portugal shall be restored. The capitalist and fascist torments to which it has been subjected will be eradicated. We shall drive out the Caudillos and all who support them.”

His reading was emotionless and cold, clearly rehearsed as he read from the paper in his hands. He seemed motionless on most screens, nearly impossible to see where he was looking. More masked men absently waded through the foreground before the news desk, stepping through the sitting employees. Each flinched, desperate not to impede them. They brandished their modern weapons, clearly making sure the camera saw them too.

“If you love Portugal, then your loyalty is to us. Try to fight us, and you will be left in a ditch for our dogs to eat.”

The man got up and walked away. Within moments the feed filled with a cacophony of desperate grunts and obstructed cries as the gagged hostages were dragged away out of the shot. The feed cut to black, and Portugal exploded into panic.
strings.IBR_terror.406.a: As Officers Costa and Ortega reached the room minutes later, both hostage and terrorist were gone.
strings.IBR_terror.407.d:
Case Number: 142271{year}

Reporting Officer: Altair Melo

Details of Incident: At 1231, the Portuguese Axencia Anti-Separatista (AAS) headquarters in northern Portugal was attacked by the Brigadas Revolucionárias (BR) terrorist group. The commanding officer, Altair Melo, immediately mobilized all units stationed in the headquarters to retaliate against the ambush. An attack of such scale at their own base of operations was not anticipated by the AAS, and consequently, casualties were heavier than expected.

Fortunately, the complex had been designed with pre-built fortifications that allowed the AAS to fend off the separatists. In spite of that, many of the BR terrorists fought to the very end, unwilling to surrender themselves to the AAS even after some of them ran out of ammo and resorted to charging into gunfire.

The assault on the AAS regional headquarters in northern Portugal reveals many vulnerabilities in our intelligence network. Not only were the terrorists able to source high-grade weaponry, some more advanced than ours, but they were also able to hide it from our watchful eyes.

Even more troubling was that this attack served as merely a diversion. A turncoat allowed elements of the BR to sneak into our facilities and make it out with records, munitions, and intelligence. It is likely that more AAS depots and strongholds in the region will be raided with their newfound intelligence and resources. While the AAS is busy finding its mole from within, northern Portugal remains vulnerable to terrorist attacks and is in dire need of resources.
strings.IBR_terror.407.a: How many more will die before we get our shit together?
strings.IBR_terror.408.d:
Case Number: 142314{year}

Reporting Officer: Raul Vieira

Details of Incident: On {date}, a large attack has occurred across the Union. A series of stabbings, shootings, and mail bombs has been directed at Iberian officials. A close examination of the cases revealed that all victims were all Spanish officials involved in the Iberian administration.

This follows the modus operandi of the Brigadas Revolucionárias (BR), a Portuguese separatist group willing to separate Portugal from its union with Spain. In the past, they have been problematic in their raids against anti-separatist facilities, but these attacks have revealed critical vulnerabilities in our intelligence capabilities. The fact that they were able to conduct so many attacks across the Union with such ease and such coordination is telling of how underequipped the Axencia Anti-Separatista (AAS) is in dealing with groups like the BR.

Although the culprits have been narrowed down and justice will be swiftly delivered, the damage and destruction — both physical and psychological — will scar the nation. Many Spanish officials — and civilians — remain in fear that they may be next in one of the BR's attacks. Some officials have already resigned from their positions. Governmental efficiency has been hampered, and it is imperative that new domestic security and counterterrorist measures be taken in order to ensure a day as dark as this one will not happen again.
